words.enDefinition: two people who seem well suited to each other as partners

examples.en: Our friends thought we were a good match because we liked the same quiet places.
examples.zh: 朋友觉得我们是「合适的一对」，因为我们都喜欢同样的安静地方。

examples.en: They wondered whether they were a good match once their different plans became clear.
examples.zh: 各自的计划明朗后，两人想知道他们是否是「合适的一对」。

collocations: be a good match for each other

words.enDefinition: a willingness to listen patiently and sympathetically to someone

examples.en: My neighbour offered a listening ear when I was worrying about a family decision.
examples.zh: 我正为家里的决定担心时，邻居「愿意听我倾诉」。

examples.en: I didn't need advice, but it helped to have a listening ear after class.
examples.zh: 我不需要建议，下课后有人「愿意听我倾诉」就很有帮助。

words.enDefinition: a small gift referred to in a casual or modest way

examples.en: I brought a little something for you from the bookshop near my campus.
examples.zh: 我在学校附近的书店给你带了「一点小心意」。

examples.en: My classmate left a little something at the door before heading home.
examples.zh: 同学回家前在门口留了「一点小心意」。

words.enDefinition: a small amount of food offered when someone might be hungry

examples.en: Would you like a little something to eat now, or shall we wait until dinner?
examples.zh: 你现在想来「一点吃的」吗？还是等到晚饭？

examples.en: My friend fixed me a little something to eat when my train arrived late.
examples.zh: 我的火车晚点了，朋友给我弄了「一点吃的」。

collocations: get a little something to eat
offer a little something to eat
make a little something to eat

words.enDefinition: a formal title that refers to someone's academic role or qualification

examples.en: I checked the academic title on the biography before introducing our guest speaker.
examples.zh: 介绍来宾发言人前，我查看了简介上的「学术头衔」。

examples.en: The invitation listed the speaker's academic title beneath her name and photo.
examples.zh: 邀请函在发言者的姓名和照片下方列了她的「学术头衔」。

words.enDefinition: unfair assumptions based on the way someone pronounces a language

examples.en: The workshop discussed accent bias using feedback from students who had presented projects.
examples.zh: 工作坊用做过项目汇报的同学收到的反馈，讨论了「口音偏见」。

examples.en: We looked at how accent bias can affect whose ideas get noticed.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「口音偏见」如何影响谁的想法能得到关注。

words.enDefinition: to connect with your account on a social networking service

examples.en: Can I add you on social media so I can send you the photos later?
examples.zh: 我能「在社交平台加你」吗？这样之后能把照片发给你。

examples.en: I wanted to add you on social media after our chat at the art table.
examples.zh: 在美术摊位聊过之后，我想「在社交平台加你」。

collocations: can I add you on social media
happy to add you on social media
ask before I add you on social media

words.enDefinition: a language someone learns in addition to the ones they already use

examples.en: I use an additional language for classes and my first language at home.
examples.zh: 我上课用「另外学的一门语言」，在家用第一语言。

examples.en: The student wrote about making friends while studying in an additional language.
examples.zh: 那名学生写了自己用「另外学的一门语言」上课时交朋友的经历。

words.enDefinition: A calendar with daily openings or surprises counting down to Christmas.

examples.en: My roommate put an Advent calendar with tiny chocolate shapes on the kitchen shelf.
examples.zh: 室友把一份装有小块造型巧克力的「圣诞倒数日历」放在厨房架子上。

examples.en: We noticed a reusable Advent calendar with little drawers in the window near campus.
examples.zh: 我们在校园附近的橱窗里看到一份有小抽屉、可重复使用的「圣诞倒数日历」。

words.enDefinition: The period of preparation before Christmas in many Christian traditions.

examples.en: The chapel displayed a special notice about Advent beside its regular weekly schedule for students.
examples.zh: 校园礼拜堂在面向学生的每周日程旁贴了一则关于「将临期」的专门通知。

examples.en: My roommate explained how her family marks Advent while we walked past the chapel.
examples.zh: 经过礼拜堂时，室友介绍了她家如何度过「将临期」。

words.enDefinition: A wreath with candles used to mark the weeks before Christmas in some Christian traditions.

examples.en: The chapel placed an Advent wreath beside a note explaining the meaning of its candles.
examples.zh: 礼拜堂摆了一只「将临期花环」，旁边的说明讲了蜡烛的含义。

examples.en: We saw an Advent wreath on the table while helping with the winter exhibition.
examples.zh: 我们帮忙筹备冬季展览时，看见桌上有一只「将临期花环」。

collocations: a candle on the Advent wreath

words.enDefinition: to decide together to start again without carrying a previous dispute into the future

examples.en: They chose to agree to a fresh start after clearing up the old misunderstanding.
examples.zh: 说开旧误会后，两人选择「同意重新开始相处」。

examples.en: We could agree to a fresh start once we both felt ready to talk.
examples.zh: 等两人都准备好谈一谈，我们就可以「同意重新开始相处」。

collocations: decide to agree to a fresh start
be ready to agree to a fresh start
choose to agree to a fresh start

words.enDefinition: the time everyone has agreed an activity will begin

examples.en: I arrived before the agreed start time so we could begin together.
examples.zh: 我在「约好的开始时间」之前到了，这样大家可以一起开始。

examples.en: We moved the agreed start time after checking with everyone in the group.
examples.zh: 确认过所有小组成员的情况后，我们改了「约好的开始时间」。

collocations: a change to the agreed start time
be there by the agreed start time

words.expression: all the best for the move
words.lemma: all the best for the move
words.enDefinition: a friendly wish that someone's upcoming move goes well
acceptedEnVariants: all the best for the move
all the best with the move

examples.en: “All the best for the move,” he wrote on the card from our flat.
examples.zh: 他在我们公寓的卡片上写道：“「祝你搬家顺利」。”

examples.en: We said all the best for the move before her taxi left for the station.
examples.zh: 她的出租车开去车站前，我们说：“「祝你搬家顺利」。”

collocations: wish someone all the best for the move
a message saying all the best for the move
all the best for the move next week

words.enDefinition: a gathering where former students of a university or school meet again

examples.en: I registered for the alumni reunion after finding out my old roommate was coming.
examples.zh: 得知老室友也会来后，我报名参加了「校友聚会」。

examples.en: The campus tour at the alumni reunion included the library we used every weekend.
examples.zh: 「校友聚会」的校园参观包括我们以前每周末都去的图书馆。

words.enDefinition: the United States holiday on the fourth Thursday in November

examples.en: I first experienced American Thanksgiving with a friend's family in Ohio.
examples.zh: 我第一次过「美国感恩节」是在俄亥俄州，和一个朋友的家人一起过的。

examples.en: My friends in the States were planning their American Thanksgiving trip in November.
examples.zh: 我在美国的朋友正在筹备十一月「美国感恩节」的出行。

words.enDefinition: the end of a romantic relationship without hostility between the people involved

examples.en: They had an amicable breakup and stayed on friendly terms at their campus club.
examples.zh: 两人「和平分手」，在校园社团里仍能友好相处。

examples.en: An amicable breakup made it easier for them to share friends in the department.
examples.zh: 两人「和平分手」后，更容易继续和系里共同的朋友来往。

collocations: remain friendly after an amicable breakup

words.enDefinition: at a distance approximately equal to the length of an arm

examples.en: We stood an arm's length away from each other during the rehearsal.
examples.zh: 排练时，我们彼此「相隔一臂远」。

examples.en: The photographer asked me to stand an arm's length away from the chair.
examples.zh: 摄影师让我站到和椅子「相隔一臂远」的地方。

collocations: stay about an arm's length away

words.enDefinition: A casual question about someone's plans before suggesting a weekend activity.

examples.en: I asked “Any plans for the weekend?” before suggesting a picnic by the river.
examples.zh: 我先问了「周末有什么安排吗」，然后才提议去河边野餐。

examples.en: Do you have any plans for the weekend now that your last exam is over?
examples.zh: 你最后一门考试已经考完了，「周末有什么安排吗」？

collocations: ask about any plans for the weekend
have any plans for the weekend
check if someone has any plans for the weekend

words.enDefinition: A phrase offering any time once the relevant class has finished.

examples.en: I can meet any time after class, so choose a time that suits the others.
examples.zh: 「下课后什么时候都行」，你选个其他人方便的时间吧。

examples.en: My roommate said we could start any time after class, since her shift was canceled.
examples.zh: 室友说她不用上班了，我们「下课后什么时候开始都行」。

collocations: be free any time after class
come by any time after class

words.enDefinition: An informal question asking whether additional people will attend an activity.

examples.en: Do you know if anyone else is coming before I ask for a larger table?
examples.zh: 我去要更大的桌子前，你知道「还有谁会来」吗？

examples.en: Maya asked “Anyone else coming?” while she was trying to count how many seats we needed.
examples.zh: 玛雅在算需要几个座位时问「还有谁会来」？

collocations: know if anyone else is coming
is anyone else coming to the picnic
ask if anyone else is coming

words.enDefinition: An informal opener asking if anyone wants to join a proposed activity.

examples.en: I wrote “Anyone up for a picnic?” after seeing the forecast for Saturday afternoon.
examples.zh: 看到星期六下午的天气预报后，我发消息问「有人想一起野餐吗」？

examples.en: Leo asked “Anyone up for coffee after class?” while we were putting away our notebooks.
examples.zh: 我们收笔记本时，利奥问「下课后有人想一起喝咖啡吗」？

collocations: anyone up for a short walk

words.enDefinition: the activity of gathering apples directly from trees at an orchard

examples.en: The students went apple picking together on the first cool Saturday of term.
examples.zh: 学期里第一个凉爽的周六，大家一起去「摘苹果」。

examples.en: I tried apple picking with my roommate's family during a visit home.
examples.zh: 室友回家时我跟着去做客，和他们一家体验了「摘苹果」。

words.enDefinition: asks whether your visit is preventing someone from going to bed

examples.en: Are we keeping you up? I didn't realise it was already past eleven o'clock.
examples.zh: 「我们耽误你睡觉了吗」？我没意识到已经十一点多了。

examples.en: My roommate asked, "Are we keeping you up?" when our friend started to yawn.
examples.zh: 朋友开始打哈欠时，室友问：「我们耽误你睡觉了吗」？

collocations: sorry, are we keeping you up
are we keeping you up too late
wait, are we keeping you up

words.enDefinition: Asks whether an activity scheduled for a time or day is still happening.

examples.en: Are we still on for Friday even though our afternoon lecture has been moved online?
examples.zh: 虽然星期五下午的讲座改成线上了，「那天的安排还照旧吗」？

examples.en: Are we still on for coffee after class now that your shift starts earlier?
examples.zh: 你上班时间提前了，「下课后还照原计划去喝咖啡吗」？

collocations: are we still on for Friday
are we still on for coffee
ask are we still on for Saturday

words.enDefinition: asks whether someone only recently arrived or joined a place

examples.en: Are you new here, or were you at the first welcome session last week?
examples.zh: 「你是刚来的吗」？还是上周也参加了第一场迎新活动？

examples.en: The person in line asked, "Are you new here? I moved in on Tuesday."
examples.zh: 排队时，一个人问：「你是刚来的吗」？我周二搬进来的。

collocations: are you new here or just visiting

words.enDefinition: checks whether a visitor feels comfortable around dogs

examples.en: Are you okay with dogs? Ours usually sleeps near the chairs in the living room.
examples.zh: 「你介意家里有狗吗」？我家狗平时睡在客厅椅子旁。

examples.en: My neighbour asked, "Are you okay with dogs?" before inviting me into the garden.
examples.zh: 邻居请我进花园之前问：「你介意家里有狗吗」？

collocations: are you okay with dogs in the room
ask if they're okay with dogs
are you okay with dogs being here

words.expression: are you okay with me posting this
words.lemma: are you okay with me posting this
words.zhGloss: 你介意我把这个发出去吗
words.enDefinition: Asks permission to share something online, such as a photo of the group.
acceptedZhAnswers: 你介意我把这个发出去吗
acceptedEnVariants: are you okay with me posting this

examples.en: Are you okay with me posting this photo from our picnic on my page?
examples.zh: 「你介意我把这张野餐照片发到我主页上吗」？

examples.en: Are you okay with me posting this video from the game in our class chat?
examples.zh: 「你介意我把这段游戏视频发到班级群里吗」？

collocations: ask are you okay with me posting this
text are you okay with me posting this
say are you okay with me posting this

words.enDefinition: an informal question asking if someone is currently dating another person

examples.en: My friend asked, “Are you seeing anyone at the moment, or are you single?”
examples.zh: 朋友问：“「你现在在和人交往吗」，还是单身？”

examples.en: “Are you seeing anyone these days?” she asked while we waited for our drinks.
examples.zh: 等饮料时她问：“「你最近在和人交往吗」？”

collocations: are you seeing anyone at the moment
are you seeing anyone these days
ask if someone is seeing anyone

words.enDefinition: a question checking whether someone is finished before clearing their place

examples.en: “Are you still eating?” I asked before picking up my classmate's plate.
examples.zh: 我端走同学的盘子前问「你还在吃吗？」

examples.en: A student volunteer asked, “Are you still eating?” when she reached our table.
examples.zh: 一名学生志愿者来到我们桌旁，问「你还在吃吗？」

collocations: “Are you still eating, or may I take your plate?”

words.enDefinition: to get to a place shortly before the planned time

examples.en: I tried to arrive a few minutes early so I could find a seat.
examples.zh: 我尽量「提前几分钟到场」，好先找个座位。

examples.en: The organiser asked us to arrive a few minutes early for the rehearsal.
examples.zh: 组织者请我们「提前几分钟到场」参加排练。

collocations: plan to arrive a few minutes early
be asked to arrive a few minutes early
arrive a few minutes early to settle in

words.enDefinition: to come after an activity has already begun

examples.en: The theatre asked anyone who might arrive after the start to wait outside.
examples.zh: 剧场请可能「在活动开始后到场」的人先在外面等。

examples.en: I knew I'd arrive after the start, so I checked the late entry policy.
examples.zh: 我知道会「在活动开始后到场」，便先查了迟到入场规定。

collocations: expect to arrive after the start
be likely to arrive after the start
guests who arrive after the start

words.enDefinition: to reach a place at or before the stated time

examples.en: Our invitation asked us to arrive by six for the student awards evening.
examples.zh: 学生颁奖晚会的邀请函请我们「最迟六点到」。

examples.en: The coordinator said I should arrive by noon to help with seating.
examples.zh: 协调员说，我应该「最迟中午到」，帮忙安排座位。

collocations: ask guests to arrive by noon

words.enDefinition: to reach a place before it is convenient for you to be there

examples.en: I didn't want to arrive too early while the volunteers were setting up.
examples.zh: 志愿者还在布置现场，我不想「到得太早」。

examples.en: We agreed not to arrive too early because the hall doors were still locked.
examples.zh: 礼堂门还锁着，我们商量好别「到得太早」。

collocations: try not to arrive too early
arrive too early for a meeting

words.enDefinition: to ask one more question based on someone's previous answer

examples.en: I wanted to ask a follow-up after she mentioned the campus radio station.
examples.zh: 她提到校园电台后，我想「接着追问一句」。

examples.en: You can ask a follow-up if their story reminds you of something similar.
examples.zh: 对方的经历让你想起类似的事时，你可以「接着追问一句」。

collocations: ask a follow-up about the story

words.zhGloss: 打电话前先问方不方便
words.enDefinition: to check that someone is ready to take a call before calling
acceptedZhAnswers: 打电话前先问方不方便

examples.en: My study partner asked me to ask before calling during her lab shift.
examples.zh: 学习伙伴请我在她实验室值班时「打电话前先问方不方便」。

examples.en: We agreed to ask before calling anyone in the group late at night.
examples.zh: 我们约好，深夜要给群里的人打电话时「先问方不方便」。

collocations: ask before calling late at night

words.zhGloss: 分享号码前先征求同意
words.enDefinition: to get permission before giving someone's phone number to others
acceptedZhAnswers: 分享号码前先征求同意

examples.en: Our group agreed to ask before sharing a number with another club.
examples.zh: 我们小组约定，把成员号码给别的社团前要「先征求同意」。

examples.en: The organiser reminded us to ask before sharing a number from the contact list.
examples.zh: 组织者提醒，分享通讯录里的号码前要「先征求同意」。

collocations: remember to ask before sharing a number
ask everyone to ask before sharing a number
agree to ask before sharing a number

words.enDefinition: to get permission before linking another person's account to a post

examples.en: The club asked us to ask before tagging someone in a public photo.
examples.zh: 社团请我们在公开照片里「标注别人前先问一声」。

examples.en: I try to ask before tagging someone in any image from a meeting.
examples.zh: 会议照片里如果要「标注别人，我尽量先问一声」。

collocations: remember to ask before tagging someone
agree to ask before tagging someone
ask before tagging someone in a photo

words.enDefinition: to ask what to do to join an unfamiliar activity

examples.en: I waited for a pause to ask how to take part in the dance.
examples.zh: 我等活动暂停下来，才「问怎么加入这支舞」。

examples.en: My roommate encouraged me to ask how to take part before the workshop began.
examples.zh: 室友鼓励我在工作坊开始前「问一下怎么参加」。

collocations: feel free to ask how to take part
go over to ask how to take part
encourage someone to ask how to take part

words.enDefinition: to ask questions that invite fuller answers than yes or no

examples.en: Our tutor encouraged us to ask open-ended questions during the cultural exchange interviews.
examples.zh: 导师鼓励我们在文化交流访谈中「问开放式问题」。

examples.en: The host took time to ask open-ended questions about how the custom had changed.
examples.zh: 主持人花时间就习俗如何演变「问了开放式问题」。

collocations: encourage people to ask open-ended questions

words.enDefinition: to ask about something instead of treating a guess as fact

examples.en: I chose to ask rather than assume what my guest meant by the phrase.
examples.zh: 对于客人那句话的意思，我选择「先问清楚再判断」。

examples.en: Our facilitator suggested we ask rather than assume what the unfamiliar picture meant.
examples.zh: 引导员建议，对不熟悉的图像含义要「先问清楚再判断」。

collocations: choose to ask rather than assume
remember to ask rather than assume
learn to ask rather than assume

words.enDefinition: unable to think of anything to say at a particular moment

examples.en: I was briefly at a loss for words after she asked what I liked about campus.
examples.zh: 她问我喜欢学校的哪些地方，我「一时不知道说什么」。

examples.en: We were both at a loss for words until the tutor asked us about our hometowns.
examples.zh: 我们俩都「一时不知道说什么」，直到老师问起我们的家乡。

collocations: be at a loss for words
momentarily at a loss for words
leave someone at a loss for words

words.expression: at my school, we used to
words.lemma: at my school, we used to
words.zhGloss: 在我以前的学校，我们常常
words.enDefinition: a phrase introducing a repeated practice from one's own school
acceptedZhAnswers: 在我以前的学校，我们常常
acceptedEnVariants: at my school, we used to

examples.en: At my school, we used to write notes to the next graduating class.
examples.zh: 「在我以前的学校，我们常常」给下一届毕业生写便条。

examples.en: At my school, we used to spend Friday afternoons showing each other projects.
examples.zh: 「在我以前的学校，我们常常」在周五下午和同学互相展示项目。

collocations: “At my school, we used to share our work”
“At my school, we used to do it differently”
“At my school, we used to start later”

words.enDefinition: A Scots song widely sung at gatherings to mark the start of a new year.

examples.en: Some neighbors sang Auld Lang Syne after midnight in the courtyard of our apartment building.
examples.zh: 过了午夜，几位邻居在公寓楼的庭院里唱起了「《友谊地久天长》」。

examples.en: A Scottish classmate recognized Auld Lang Syne when the choir began singing it near midnight.
examples.zh: 临近午夜，合唱团一开口，一位苏格兰同学就听出了是「《友谊地久天长》」。

collocations: a recording of Auld Lang Syne

words.enDefinition: to keep from standing where others cannot see past you

examples.en: I took off my tall hat to avoid blocking the view behind me.
examples.zh: 我摘下高帽子，「避免挡住后面人的视线」。

examples.en: We crouched for the photo to avoid blocking the view from the back row.
examples.zh: 拍照时我们蹲低了一些，「避免挡住最后一排的视线」。

collocations: try to avoid blocking the view
avoid blocking the view of other people
move to avoid blocking the view

words.enDefinition: to refrain from making asides while someone else has the floor

examples.en: The moderator asked us to avoid side comments during the student readings.
examples.zh: 学生朗读期间，主持人请我们「别在旁边插话评论」。

examples.en: We were reminded to avoid side comments while the guest answered a question.
examples.zh: 来宾回答问题时，有人提醒我们「别在旁边插话评论」。

collocations: ask attendees to avoid side comments
avoid side comments during the discussion

words.enDefinition: to remain neutral when people you know are in a disagreement

examples.en: I tried to avoid taking sides because I cared about both of my friends.
examples.zh: 我在乎两个朋友，所以尽量「避免偏向任何一方」。

examples.en: The club organiser chose to avoid taking sides in a disagreement about the venue.
examples.zh: 在关于场地的分歧中，社团组织者选择「避免偏向任何一方」。

words.enDefinition: to leave seats marked for other people available to them

examples.en: The usher asked guests to avoid using the reserved seats in the front row.
examples.zh: 引座员请来宾「不要坐前排预留的座位」。

examples.en: We decided to avoid using the reserved seats even while the room was empty.
examples.zh: 即便房间空着，我们也决定「不要坐预留的座位」。

collocations: ask guests to avoid using the reserved seats
avoid using the reserved seats near the stage
signs asking people to avoid using the reserved seats

words.enDefinition: a brief silence that feels uncomfortable during a conversation

examples.en: There was an awkward pause before I remembered how we had met.
examples.zh: 我想起我们是怎么认识的之前，出现了一阵「尴尬的停顿」。

examples.en: After an awkward pause, I asked what classes everyone was taking.
examples.zh: 出现「尴尬的停顿」后，我问了问大家都选了什么课。

words.enDefinition: To decide not to take part in something after previously agreeing to join.

examples.en: I had to back out of the plan when my supervisor changed my Saturday shift.
examples.zh: 主管调整了我星期六的班次，我只得「退出已经约好的活动」。

examples.en: She didn't want to back out of the plan after everyone had already bought tickets.
examples.zh: 大家都已经买了票，她不想再「退出已经约好的活动」。

collocations: have to back out of the plan
decide to back out of the plan
back out of the plan at the last minute

words.enDefinition: a social gathering in someone's backyard with food cooked on a grill

examples.en: Our neighbour invited us to a backyard barbecue when the semester finished in June.
examples.zh: 六月学期结束时，邻居邀请我们去参加「后院烧烤聚会」。

examples.en: I brought a salad to the backyard barbecue at my classmate's house on Saturday.
examples.zh: 周六我带了一份沙拉去同学家的「后院烧烤聚会」。

words.enDefinition: A New Year's Eve ceremony in which a large illuminated ball is lowered toward midnight.

examples.en: We watched the ball drop in Times Square on a screen at our neighbor's apartment.
examples.zh: 我们在邻居家用屏幕看了纽约时报广场的「跨年灯球降落仪式」。

examples.en: My roommate asked why the ball drop was part of the New Year's Eve broadcast.
examples.zh: 室友问，跨年夜转播为什么包含「跨年灯球降落仪式」。

collocations: a livestream of the ball drop

words.enDefinition: A square parcel of glutinous rice and savory filling wrapped in leaves, associated with Tết.

examples.en: My classmate shared bánh chưng with us at the Vietnamese New Year gathering on campus.
examples.zh: 校园越南新年聚会上，同学跟我们分享了「越南方形糯米粽」。

examples.en: The exhibit displayed bánh chưng beside a photo showing how it looks when sliced.
examples.zh: 展览展出了「越南方形糯米粽」，旁边有一张照片展示它切开后的样子。

words.enDefinition: A cylindrical leaf-wrapped glutinous rice cake associated with Tết, especially in southern Vietnam.

examples.en: Our neighbor brought bánh tét to the winter gathering and shared slices with our study group.
examples.zh: 邻居带了「越南长筒形糯米粽」来参加冬季聚会，切片分给了我们自习小组。

examples.en: The student presenter used a photo of bánh tét to explain a tradition from southern Vietnam.
examples.zh: 做展示的同学用一张「越南长筒形糯米粽」的照片来讲越南南方的一项习俗。

collocations: cut a slice of bánh tét

words.enDefinition: a UK weekend extended by a nearby bank holiday

examples.en: We took the train to visit my sister over the bank holiday weekend.
examples.zh: 「公众假日连休周末」期间，我们坐火车去看了姐姐。

examples.en: The university kept its park open throughout the bank holiday weekend for local families.
examples.zh: 「公众假日连休周末」期间，学校的公园一直向当地家庭开放。

words.enDefinition: playful remarks exchanged between people who are joking together

examples.en: The friendly banter made me less nervous about joining the table.
examples.zh: 几句「善意的玩笑话」让我坐过去时没那么紧张了。

examples.en: There was a little banter about whose timetable looked the busiest.
examples.zh: 大家说了几句「善意的玩笑话」，主题是谁的课表看起来最满。

words.enDefinition: to feel pleased about another person's good news or success

examples.en: It's possible to be happy for someone while still feeling disappointed about your own result.
examples.zh: 即使对自己的结果感到失望，你也可以「为别人感到高兴」。

examples.en: My friend reminded me that I could be happy for someone facing a different opportunity.
examples.zh: 朋友提醒我，可以「为获得不同机会的人感到高兴」。

collocations: learn to be happy for someone

words.enDefinition: to have an ongoing romantic relationship with another person

examples.en: You don't have to be in a relationship to enjoy the campus film festival.
examples.zh: 不一定得「有恋爱对象」才能享受校园电影节。

examples.en: He didn't want to be in a relationship while adapting to the new course.
examples.zh: 他适应新课程时不想「谈恋爱」。

collocations: want to be in a relationship
choose to be in a relationship
be in a relationship with someone

words.enDefinition: to be facing the same problem or uncertainty as someone else

examples.en: It's easier to speak up when you be in the same boat as the others.
examples.zh: 知道自己和其他人「处境相同」时，开口就容易些。

examples.en: I felt less nervous when I realised we seemed to be in the same boat.
examples.zh: 发现大家似乎都「处境相同」之后，我就没那么紧张了。

collocations: all be in the same boat
realise you'll be in the same boat
know you will be in the same boat

words.enDefinition: to be romantically interested in a person, in informal speech

examples.en: I didn't expect to be into someone from my study group at all.
examples.zh: 我完全没想到会「喜欢上学习小组里的人」。

examples.en: You can be into someone and still decide a relationship isn't right for you.
examples.zh: 你可能「喜欢某个人」，同时觉得建立恋爱关系不适合自己。

words.enDefinition: to enjoy the same activities or subjects as someone else

examples.en: I didn't expect us to be into the same things after that quiet first meeting.
examples.zh: 第一次见面没说几句话，我没想到我们后来发现「喜欢相同的东西」。

examples.en: It's nice to be into the same things when you're trying to find new friends.
examples.zh: 想认识新朋友时，发现彼此「喜欢相同的东西」挺好的。

collocations: seem to be into the same things
turn out to be into the same things
be into the same things as classmates

words.enDefinition: to have a pleasant relationship with someone you know

examples.en: It's nice to be on friendly terms with the people next door already.
examples.zh: 这么快就能和隔壁的人「关系友好」，真不错。

examples.en: I didn't expect to be on friendly terms with so many classmates after one week.
examples.zh: 没想到才过一周，我就能和这么多同学「关系友好」。

collocations: be on friendly terms with neighbours
seem to be on friendly terms
be on friendly terms with everyone

words.enDefinition: to be unaware of what a group has been discussing or doing

examples.en: I felt I might be out of the loop after missing three group calls.
examples.zh: 错过三次群组通话后，我觉得自己可能「没跟上大家的近况」。

examples.en: She didn't want to be out of the loop while studying at another campus.
examples.zh: 她在另一个校区读书时，不想「没跟上大家的近况」。

collocations: seem to be out of the loop
not want to be out of the loop
friends who might be out of the loop

words.expression: be part of each other's lives
words.lemma: be part of each other's lives
words.enDefinition: to remain involved in what happens to another person over time
acceptedEnVariants: be part of each other's lives

examples.en: We wanted to be part of each other's lives after moving to separate cities.
examples.zh: 搬到不同城市后，我们还是想「参与彼此的生活」。

examples.en: Sharing our small successes helped us be part of each other's lives from afar.
examples.zh: 分享小小的成就，让我们即使相隔很远，也能「参与彼此的生活」。

collocations: continue to be part of each other's lives
find ways to be part of each other's lives
want to be part of each other's lives

words.enDefinition: to start returning somewhere often enough to be recognised

examples.en: I wanted to become a regular at the neighbourhood repair café that term.
examples.zh: 那一学期，我想「成为社区维修咖啡馆的常客」。

examples.en: It didn't take long to become a regular at the Saturday library group.
examples.zh: 没多久，我就「成了周六图书馆小组的常客」。

collocations: become a regular at a meeting

words.enDefinition: to become the friend of someone, often someone new or alone

examples.en: My roommate made an effort to befriend the student upstairs.
examples.zh: 室友主动试着「和楼上的同学交朋友」。

examples.en: I wanted to befriend someone who also liked making short films.
examples.zh: 我想「和同样喜欢拍短片的人交朋友」。

words.expression: belong in more than one place
words.lemma: belong in more than one place
words.zhGloss: 在不止一个地方有归属感
words.enDefinition: to feel connected to several different places at once
acceptedZhAnswers: 在不止一个地方有归属感
acceptedEnVariants: belong in more than one place

examples.en: My classmate said she could belong in more than one place at once.
examples.zh: 同学说，她可以同时「在不止一个地方有归属感」。

examples.en: I started to believe I could belong in more than one place.
examples.zh: 我开始相信自己可以「在不止一个地方有归属感」。

collocations: feel that you belong in more than one place
learn you can belong in more than one place
understand how people belong in more than one place

words.enDefinition: living with experiences shaped by two cultural settings

examples.en: She wrote about growing up between two cultures in a student magazine.
examples.zh: 她在学生杂志上写了自己「在两种文化之间」长大的经历。

examples.en: I heard different stories about moving between two cultures at the workshop.
examples.zh: 我在工作坊听到不同的人讲自己怎样「在两种文化之间」来回切换。

words.enDefinition: shaped by or familiar with two different cultural settings

examples.en: My classmate described herself as bicultural when she shared her family photographs.
examples.zh: 同学分享家庭照片时，说自己「受两种文化影响」。

examples.en: He said his bicultural upbringing helped him see why the two groups disagreed.
examples.zh: 他说自己「受两种文化影响的」成长经历，让他明白两组人为什么意见不合。

words.enDefinition: a printed or digital document giving event information in two languages

examples.en: The bilingual handout helped my friend check how the game was played.
examples.zh: 「双语讲义」帮朋友看懂这个游戏是怎么玩的。

examples.en: I used the bilingual handout to follow the discussion with my classmate.
examples.zh: 我用「双语讲义」和同学一起跟上了讨论。

words.enDefinition: a gift someone receives to mark their birthday

examples.en: I dropped off a birthday present for my classmate after the workshop.
examples.zh: 实训课后，我顺路给同学送了份「生日礼物」。

examples.en: My roommate saved her birthday present until we were all home.
examples.zh: 室友把「生日礼物」留到我们都在家才打开。

words.enDefinition: seating in which people sit on blankets instead of chairs

examples.en: The show offered blanket seating on the lawn in front of the main stage.
examples.zh: 演出允许观众在主舞台前的草坪上「铺毯席地而坐」。

examples.en: I picked the blanket seating area because our group wanted to sit together.
examples.zh: 我们这组想坐在一起，所以我选了「铺毯席地坐席」的区域。

words.enDefinition: to combine elements of more than one custom in the same activity

examples.en: My roommates decided to blend traditions when planning their end-of-term dinner together.
examples.zh: 室友们筹划期末聚餐时，决定「把不同传统结合起来」。

examples.en: The students found a way to blend traditions in the decorations for their table.
examples.zh: 同学们想出办法，在餐桌装饰上「把不同传统结合起来」。

words.zhGloss: 见面前互不相识的约会
words.enDefinition: a romantic meeting arranged for two people who have never met each other
acceptedZhAnswers: 见面前互不相识的约会

examples.en: My flatmate set up a blind date for me with someone from her course.
examples.zh: 室友安排我和她课上的一名同学来一次「见面前互不相识的约会」。

examples.en: He was nervous about the blind date until they started talking about their classes.
examples.zh: 开始聊各自的课之前，他一直对这次「见面前互不相识的约会」有些紧张。

collocations: meet someone on a blind date

words.enDefinition: To keep the whole afternoon free for a planned activity.

examples.en: I told my roommate to block out the afternoon because the picnic might run long.
examples.zh: 我让室友「腾出整个下午」，因为野餐可能比预想久。

examples.en: Could you block out the afternoon for our group walk if the weather stays clear?
examples.zh: 如果天气一直晴朗，你能「腾出整个下午」跟我们一起散步吗？

collocations: block out the afternoon on your calendar
ask people to block out the afternoon
block out the afternoon for a picnic

words.enDefinition: a social gathering for neighbours on the same city block, especially in North America

examples.en: The neighbours organised a block party with tables outside both apartment buildings that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，邻居们办了场「街坊聚会」，在两栋公寓楼外都摆了桌子。

examples.en: I met three students from nearby flats at the block party near our residence.
examples.zh: 我在宿舍附近的「街坊聚会」上认识了三个住在旁边公寓的学生。

words.enDefinition: a game of catching floating apples with your mouth

examples.en: Our hall played a game of bobbing for apples at its autumn party.
examples.zh: 我们宿舍楼的秋季派对玩了「用嘴捞苹果游戏」。

examples.en: I had never seen bobbing for apples before the fall festival on campus.
examples.zh: 在学校办秋季庆典前，我没见过「用嘴捞苹果游戏」。

collocations: play a game of bobbing for apples

words.enDefinition: to grow closer through something that two people share

examples.en: We began to bond over our love of cheap science fiction novels.
examples.zh: 两个人因为都爱看便宜的科幻小说而开始「拉近关系」。

examples.en: It's easy to bond over a familiar song when you're far from home.
examples.zh: 在离家很远的地方，人们很容易「因为共同熟悉的歌而拉近关系」。

words.enDefinition: To reserve seats next to each other so friends can stay together.

examples.en: Can we book seats together for the afternoon film before the middle rows fill up?
examples.zh: 下午的电影能不能赶在中间几排坐满前，「预订相邻的座位」？

examples.en: We tried to book seats together, but only one pair was left near the front.
examples.zh: 我们想「预订相邻的座位」，但只剩前面有两个挨着的位置。

collocations: book seats together for the screening
ask if we can book seats together

words.enDefinition: A reservation recorded using the speaker’s name.

examples.en: There is a booking under my name for our group at seven this evening.
examples.zh: 今天晚上七点有「用我名字订的位置」，是给我们小组的。

examples.en: I told Kai to ask for the booking under my name when he arrived first.
examples.zh: 凯先到，我让他问一下「用我名字订的位置」。

collocations: find the booking under my name
check the booking under my name

words.enDefinition: a group of flowers arranged together to give or display

examples.en: I took a bouquet of flowers to the neighbour who hosted our dinner.
examples.zh: 我带了「一束花」给请我们吃晚饭的邻居。

examples.en: My flatmate put the bouquet of flowers I brought in a tall jug.
examples.zh: 室友把我带来的「一束花」插进了一个高水壶。

collocations: give someone a bouquet of flowers

words.enDefinition: The day following Christmas Day, observed in the UK and some other countries.

examples.en: The British student in our flat went for a long walk on Boxing Day.
examples.zh: 我们公寓的那位英国同学在「节礼日」出去走了很久。

examples.en: The shopping center near our Canadian campus posted shorter opening hours for Boxing Day.
examples.zh: 我们加拿大校区附近的购物中心贴了告示，「节礼日」营业时间较短。

words.enDefinition: to form small groups containing people from different backgrounds or teams

examples.en: We were asked to break into mixed groups with students from other clubs.
examples.zh: 我们被请去和其他社团的同学「分成背景多样的小组」。

examples.en: The organiser invited us to break into mixed groups for the story exercise.
examples.zh: 组织者邀请我们「分成背景多样的小组」，做讲故事的练习。

collocations: ask people to break into mixed groups
agree to break into mixed groups
break into mixed groups for a discussion

words.enDefinition: to do something that causes someone no longer to trust you

examples.en: Sharing a private message can break someone's trust even if it was a mistake.
examples.zh: 即使是无意分享私信，也可能「辜负对方的信任」。

examples.en: He didn't mean to break someone's trust when he repeated what he had heard.
examples.zh: 他复述听来的话时，本没想「辜负对方的信任」。

collocations: never want to break someone's trust
avoid doing something that may break someone's trust

words.enDefinition: to decide to stop dating someone or end the relationship

examples.en: She chose to break things off before they applied to universities in different cities.
examples.zh: 在两人申请不同城市的学校之前，她选择「结束这段恋情」。

examples.en: He didn't know how to break things off without making their shared seminar awkward.
examples.zh: 他不知道怎样「结束这段恋情」，又不让两人一起上的研讨课变尴尬。

collocations: try to break things off gently

words.enDefinition: to make communication or relationships feel closer despite physical distance

examples.en: Weekly calls helped bridge the distance after we moved to three separate countries.
examples.zh: 我们搬到三个不同国家后，每周的电话帮助我们「拉近彼此的距离」。

examples.en: The shared album was another way to bridge the distance between old university friends.
examples.zh: 共享相册也能帮助大学老友「拉近彼此的距离」。

collocations: find ways to bridge the distance
use video calls to bridge the distance

words.expression: bring a bit of home with me
words.lemma: bring a bit of home with me
words.zhGloss: 把一点家乡的感觉带在身边
words.enDefinition: to take something familiar that makes a new place feel more personal
acceptedZhAnswers: 把一点家乡的感觉带在身边
acceptedEnVariants: bring a bit of home with me

examples.en: I chose a small photo album to bring a bit of home with me.
examples.zh: 我挑了本小相册，「把一点家乡的感觉带在身边」。

examples.en: “I wanted to bring a bit of home with me,” she said, showing her notebook.
examples.zh: 她给大家看了笔记本，说「我想把一点家乡的感觉带在身边」。

collocations: choose to bring a bit of home with me
try to bring a bit of home with me
want to bring a bit of home with me

words.enDefinition: to take spare clothes for changing into when staying somewhere

examples.en: I'm going to bring a change of clothes in case I stay the night.
examples.zh: 万一我要留宿，我打算「带一身换洗衣服」。

examples.en: My neighbour told me to bring a change of clothes for the next morning.
examples.zh: 邻居叫我「带一身换洗衣服」，第二天早上穿。

collocations: remember to bring a change of clothes
tell someone to bring a change of clothes
need to bring a change of clothes

words.enDefinition: to contribute some food that others at the meal can try

examples.en: Guests at Friendsgiving could bring a dish to share if they wanted to contribute.
examples.zh: 参加朋友感恩节聚餐的人想出份力，可以「带道菜和大家分享」。

examples.en: My roommate offered to bring a dish to share instead of bringing another bottle of juice.
examples.zh: 室友主动提出「带道菜和大家分享」，省得再带一瓶果汁。

collocations: ask everyone to bring a dish to share
offer to bring a dish to share
choose to bring a dish to share

words.enDefinition: To come to an event with an additional friend.

examples.en: The invitation said I could bring a friend to the picnic after our seminar.
examples.zh: 邀请上写着，研讨课结束后的野餐我可以「带一位朋友来」。

examples.en: I asked if I could bring a friend to the screening in Maya's building.
examples.zh: 我问能不能「带一位朋友来」参加玛雅那栋楼里的放映活动。

collocations: be allowed to bring a friend
ask if you can bring a friend
invite someone to bring a friend

words.enDefinition: to bring your own food and supplies to eat outdoors

examples.en: The concert notice said we could bring a picnic to the park that evening.
examples.zh: 音乐会通知说，那晚我们可以「自带野餐食物」去公园。

examples.en: I asked the others whether to bring a picnic or buy food there.
examples.zh: 我问大家是「自带野餐食物」，还是到那里再买。

collocations: bring a picnic to the event
visitors are welcome to bring a picnic

words.enDefinition: to cause someone to remember something from their own past

examples.en: Certain songs bring back memories of our first few weeks at university together.
examples.zh: 有些歌会「唤起我们刚上大学那几周的回忆」。

examples.en: The meal seemed to bring back memories for everyone who lived in that flat.
examples.zh: 对曾住那套公寓的人来说，这顿饭似乎会「唤起回忆」。

words.enDefinition: To bring food, drinks, or supplies for people to use or enjoy together.
acceptedEnVariants: bring something for everyone to share

examples.en: Everyone said they could bring something to share when we planned lunch on the lawn.
examples.zh: 计划在草坪吃午饭时，大家都说可以「带点东西来分给大家」。

examples.en: I offered to bring something to share because Mina was already carrying the picnic blanket.
examples.zh: 米娜已经带着野餐毯了，我就主动提出「带点东西来分给大家」。

collocations: ask people to bring something to share
bring something to share with the group
bring something to share at the picnic

words.enDefinition: to begin talking about something that may make people uncomfortable

examples.en: I decided not to bring up a sensitive topic while everyone was eating.
examples.zh: 我决定大家吃饭时不「提起敏感话题」。

examples.en: Our facilitator asked us to check before we bring up a sensitive topic.
examples.zh: 引导员请我们在「提起敏感话题」前先问问大家。

collocations: avoid bringing up a sensitive topic
choose when to bring up a sensitive topic
ask before you bring up a sensitive topic

words.enDefinition: an event notice asking attendees to provide their own seat

examples.en: The summer concert poster said bring your own chair near the entrance information.
examples.zh: 夏季音乐会海报在入场信息旁写着「请自备座椅」。

examples.en: I saw bring your own chair on the notice before deciding what to carry.
examples.zh: 决定带什么之前，我在告示上看到了「请自备座椅」。

words.enDefinition: A request for each person attending an activity to supply snacks for themselves.

examples.en: The note said “Bring your own snacks” because the screening room did not sell food.
examples.zh: 放映室不卖吃的，通知上写着「自带零食」。

examples.en: Mina wrote “Bring your own snacks” at the top of the group chat message.
examples.zh: 米娜在群聊消息的开头写了「自带零食」。

collocations: a sign saying bring your own snacks
a note reading bring your own snacks
bring your own snacks to the screening

words.enDefinition: to develop regular connections with people in an area

examples.en: I started volunteering to build ties with the community beyond our campus.
examples.zh: 我开始做志愿服务，想「和校外的当地社区建立联系」。

examples.en: The student garden helped us build ties with the community around the university.
examples.zh: 学生花园帮我们「和大学周边的社区建立了联系」。

collocations: volunteer to build ties with the community
help build ties with the community
find ways to build ties with the community

words.enDefinition: to settle an old quarrel and get on better with someone

examples.en: The two friends agreed to bury the hatchet before their classmates visited that weekend.
examples.zh: 周末同学来访前，那两位朋友同意「结束长期争执」。

examples.en: I thought it was time to bury the hatchet after months of awkward silence.
examples.zh: 尴尬地不说话好几个月后，我觉得该「结束长期争执」了。

words.enDefinition: To cancel the activity that had been planned for that evening.

examples.en: We may need to call it off for tonight if the common room stays closed.
examples.zh: 如果公共休息室继续关闭，我们可能得「取消今晚的安排」。

examples.en: Let's call it off for tonight and try again when more friends are around.
examples.zh: 「取消今晚的安排」吧，等更多朋友有空再试。

collocations: decide to call it off for tonight
have to call it off for tonight
call it off for tonight and try again

words.enDefinition: Asks whether people in another part of the space can hear clearly.

examples.en: Can everyone hear from there, or should we bring the speaker a little closer?
examples.zh: 「大家在那里听得清吗」？要不要把音箱再拿近一点？

examples.en: I asked “Can everyone hear from there?” before starting the film in our lounge.
examples.zh: 在休息室放电影前，我问了句「大家在那里听得清吗」？

collocations: ask can everyone hear from there
check by saying can everyone hear from there
can everyone hear from there before we start

words.expression: can I get you anything to drink
words.lemma: can i get you anything to drink
words.enDefinition: offers to fetch a drink for a visitor
acceptedEnVariants: can I get you anything to drink

examples.en: Can I get you anything to drink while we wait for my roommate to get back?
examples.zh: 等我室友回来的时候，「给你拿点喝的吗」？

examples.en: My friend's dad asked, "Can I get you anything to drink?" and held up two clean glasses.
examples.zh: 朋友爸爸举起两个干净杯子，问：「给你拿点喝的吗」？

collocations: can I get you anything to drink first
can I get you anything to drink while we wait
before we start, can I get you anything to drink

words.expression: can I help with the dishes
words.lemma: can i help with the dishes
words.enDefinition: offers to help wash dishes after sharing a meal
acceptedEnVariants: can I help with the dishes

examples.en: Can I help with the dishes before we leave to catch the train back home?
examples.zh: 我们去坐火车回家前，「我能帮忙洗碗吗」？

examples.en: I asked, "Can I help with the dishes?" when my friend started filling the sink.
examples.zh: 朋友开始往水槽里放水时，我问：「我能帮忙洗碗吗」？

collocations: can I help with the dishes after we eat
can I help with the dishes before I go
ask if I can help with the dishes

words.zhGloss: 我能把其他人也约上吗
words.enDefinition: Asks permission to invite additional people to an existing plan.
acceptedZhAnswers: 我能把其他人也约上吗

examples.en: Can I invite the others from our seminar if there's room on the lawn?
examples.zh: 如果草坪上还有地方，「我能把研讨课的其他人也约上吗」？

examples.en: Can I invite the others before I tell Maya how many people are coming?
examples.zh: 在告诉玛雅有多少人来之前，「我能把其他人也约上吗」？

collocations: ask can I invite the others
can I invite the others from class
can I invite the others next time

words.enDefinition: A question asking if it is okay to arrive or take part after others begin.

examples.en: Can I join later if my class finishes after you've already ordered your coffees?
examples.zh: 如果你们点完咖啡我才下课，「我晚点能加入吗」？

examples.en: Can I join later once I've dropped my bag off at the residence hall?
examples.zh: 我先把包放回宿舍，「晚点能加入吗」？

collocations: can I join later after class
can I join later this evening

words.enDefinition: asks whether the giver wants you to open a gift now

examples.en: Can I open it now, or would you like everyone else to see it too?
examples.zh: 「我现在能打开吗」？还是你想让其他人也看到？

examples.en: I asked, "Can I open it now?" while my classmates waited for our tutor to arrive.
examples.zh: 等老师来时，我问在场的同学：「我现在能打开吗」？

collocations: can I open it now or later
can I open it now with you here
ask if I can open it now

words.enDefinition: offers to take a visitor's coat and put it away

examples.en: Can I take your coat? There are some hooks just behind the front door.
examples.zh: 「要我帮你挂外套吗」？大门后面有几个挂钩。

examples.en: My classmate asked, "Can I take your coat?" and hung it next to her own.
examples.zh: 同学问：「要我帮你挂外套吗」？随后把它挂在自己的外套旁。

collocations: here, can I take your coat
can I take your coat for you
can I take your coat while you find a seat

words.enDefinition: asks permission to use the bathroom in another person's home

examples.en: Can I use your bathroom before we leave to catch the last bus downtown?
examples.zh: 坐末班公交去市中心之前，「我能用一下洗手间吗」？

examples.en: I put down my bag and asked, "Can I use your bathroom for a moment?"
examples.zh: 我放下包问：「我能用一下洗手间吗」？

collocations: can I use your bathroom before I go
can I use your bathroom for a minute
ask if I can use your bathroom

words.expression: can we talk about where this is going
words.lemma: can we talk about where this is going
words.zhGloss: 我们能谈谈关系接下来怎么走吗
words.enDefinition: a question asking to discuss how the relationship might develop in the future
acceptedZhAnswers: 我们能谈谈关系接下来怎么走吗
acceptedEnVariants: can we talk about where this is going

examples.en: At the café I asked, “Can we talk about where this is going before next term?”
examples.zh: 我在咖啡馆问：“下学期开学前，「我们能谈谈关系接下来怎么走吗」？”

examples.en: “Can we talk about where this is going?” he asked on the walk back from class.
examples.zh: 下课往回走时，他问：“「我们能谈谈关系接下来怎么走吗」？”

collocations: can we talk about where this is going tonight
can we talk about where this is going sometime
can we talk about where this is going next term

words.expression: can you send me the address
words.lemma: can you send me the address
words.enDefinition: A question asking someone to send the address of a meeting place.
acceptedEnVariants: can you send me the address

examples.en: Can you send me the address before I get on the bus to the picnic?
examples.zh: 我坐公交车去野餐之前，「你能把地址发给我吗」？

examples.en: Can you send me the address so I can check which entrance faces the park?
examples.zh: 「你能把地址发给我吗」？我想看看哪个入口朝着公园。

collocations: can you send me the address again
text can you send me the address
ask can you send me the address

words.enDefinition: Canada's national holiday, celebrated on July first

examples.en: We watched musicians perform outdoors on Canada Day with friends from our exchange programme.
examples.zh: 「加拿大国庆日」那天，我们和交换项目认识的朋友一起看了户外音乐表演。

examples.en: The community centre listed several activities for Canada Day on a board near reception.
examples.zh: 社区中心在前台旁的板上列出了几项「加拿大国庆日」的活动。

words.enDefinition: a day celebrating the diversity and contributions of Canada's cultural communities

examples.en: I joined a panel discussion about languages on Canadian Multiculturalism Day at the college.
examples.zh: 「加拿大多元文化日」那天，我在学院参加了一场讨论语言的专题活动。

examples.en: The town held a series of community performances for Canadian Multiculturalism Day that summer.
examples.zh: 那年夏天，镇上为「加拿大多元文化日」办了几场社区演出。

words.enDefinition: the Canadian holiday on the second Monday in October

examples.en: Our Toronto neighbours invited us to dinner for Canadian Thanksgiving in October.
examples.zh: 十月，多伦多的邻居邀请我们一同吃「加拿大感恩节」晚餐。

examples.en: I marked Canadian Thanksgiving on my calendar when I moved to Ottawa.
examples.zh: 搬到渥太华时，我在日历上标出了「加拿大感恩节」。

words.enDefinition: A blessing said on an occasion when ceremonial candles are lit.

examples.en: At the Hanukkah event, a student explained the candle-lighting blessing before people gathered downstairs.
examples.zh: 光明节活动中，大家下楼集合前，一位同学先介绍了「点烛祝祷」。

examples.en: A booklet for visitors included a translation of the candle-lighting blessing used that evening.
examples.zh: 访客手册上有当晚所用「点烛祝祷」的译文。

words.enDefinition: a bowl filled with sweets for people to take

examples.en: We put a candy bowl next to the pumpkin by the door.
examples.zh: 我们在门口的南瓜旁边放了个「装糖果的碗」。

examples.en: I refilled the candy bowl after a large group of children left.
examples.zh: 一大群小孩走后，我又往「装糖果的碗」里添了些糖。

words.enDefinition: a sweet shaped like a corn kernel, associated with Halloween

examples.en: My roommate put a bowl of candy corn beside the welcome sign.
examples.zh: 室友在欢迎牌旁边摆了一碗「玉米粒形糖果」。

examples.en: I'd never seen candy corn until our floor held its costume party.
examples.zh: 我们这层楼办化装派对的时候，我才第一次见到「玉米粒形糖果」。

words.enDefinition: a large amount of candy collected while trick-or-treating

examples.en: The kids dumped their candy haul on the floor after coming home.
examples.zh: 孩子们一回家，就把「讨到的一大堆糖果」倒在地上。

examples.en: My neighbour's son showed me his candy haul before heading inside.
examples.zh: 邻居家的孩子进屋前，给我看了他「讨到的一大堆糖果」。

words.enDefinition: a whole apple covered in caramel, often served on a stick

examples.en: I bought a caramel apple from a stall at the harvest festival.
examples.zh: 我在丰收庆典的一个摊位买了个「裹焦糖的苹果」。

examples.en: My host family's children shared a caramel apple after leaving the corn maze.
examples.zh: 寄宿家庭的孩子们走出玉米地迷宫后，分吃了一个「裹焦糖的苹果」。

words.enDefinition: to do most of the work of keeping people talking

examples.en: At first I had to carry the conversation because everyone was still nervous.
examples.zh: 一开始大家还很紧张，我只好一个人「独力维持聊天」。

examples.en: I relaxed when I realised I didn't have to carry the conversation on my own.
examples.zh: 意识到不用我独自「独力维持聊天」之后，我就放松了。

collocations: feel obliged to carry the conversation
expect someone to carry the conversation

words.enDefinition: to cut decoration into a pumpkin, often for Halloween

examples.en: Our host offered to show us how to carve a pumpkin after lunch.
examples.zh: 午饭后，寄宿家庭主人主动说要给我们示范怎么「雕刻南瓜」。

examples.en: We planned to carve a pumpkin in the shape of a smiling owl.
examples.zh: 我们打算「雕刻南瓜」，把它刻成一只微笑的猫头鹰。

words.enDefinition: to cut a cooked whole turkey into portions for serving

examples.en: Our host asked her brother to carve the turkey once everyone sat down.
examples.zh: 大家坐好后，主人请自己的兄弟「把火鸡切片分给大家」。

examples.en: My classmate offered to carve the turkey while the rest of us brought plates.
examples.zh: 我们其他人拿餐盘时，同学主动提出「把火鸡切片分给大家」。

collocations: learn how to carve the turkey
ask someone to carve the turkey

words.enDefinition: a template used to transfer a design onto a surface for carving

examples.en: I used a carving stencil to make a neat owl on mine.
examples.zh: 我用「雕刻描图模板」在自己的南瓜上做了只轮廓整齐的猫头鹰。

examples.en: The club printed a carving stencil with the outline of our campus bell.
examples.zh: 社团印了一张带校园钟轮廓的「雕刻描图模板」。

words.enDefinition: going on dates without agreeing to a committed relationship

examples.en: They both preferred casual dating while getting used to their new university schedules.
examples.zh: 在适应大学的新课表时，两人都更倾向于「非正式交往」。

examples.en: She explained what casual dating meant to her before they made any plans together.
examples.zh: 两人一起做任何安排前，她说清楚了「非正式交往」对她意味着什么。

words.enDefinition: informal dating slang for starting to feel romantic affection, often unexpectedly

examples.en: I didn't think I'd catch feelings after meeting him for coffee on campus twice.
examples.zh: 在学校和他喝了两次咖啡，我没想到自己会「开始动心」。

examples.en: She told her roommate she might catch feelings if they kept spending weekends together.
examples.zh: 她跟室友说，如果两人继续一起过周末，她可能会「开始动心」。

words.enDefinition: a phone call to hear someone's news since you last spoke

examples.en: We had a catch-up call on Friday after I finished my afternoon classes.
examples.zh: 周五，我上完下午的课后打了通「聊近况的电话」。

examples.en: Our first catch-up call after graduation lasted longer than either of us expected.
examples.zh: 毕业后第一次「聊近况的电话」比我们两人预想的都久。

words.enDefinition: a time set aside to exchange news after a period without seeing each other

examples.en: We planned a catch-up session after the lecture for people from our old project.
examples.zh: 讲座后我们给以前项目组的人安排了一个「专门聊近况的聚会」。

examples.en: The catch-up session lasted until the café turned off the music that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚，这次「专门聊近况的聚会」一直持续到咖啡馆关掉音乐。

words.enDefinition: to mark an achievement made by one of your friends

examples.en: We brought cake to celebrate a friend's success after she passed her final interview.
examples.zh: 朋友通过最后一轮面试后，我们带了蛋糕去「庆祝她取得成功」。

examples.en: It felt right to celebrate a friend's success at the end of a difficult year.
examples.zh: 艰难的一年结束后，应该「庆祝朋友取得成功」。

collocations: get together to celebrate a friend's success
plan to celebrate a friend's success
take time to celebrate a friend's success

words.enDefinition: A change to what the group previously agreed to do.

examples.en: There was a change of plans after we found out the courtyard would be closed.
examples.zh: 得知庭院会关闭后，「安排有变」。

examples.en: I sent a quick message about a change of plans before anyone left their residence hall.
examples.zh: 大家还没从宿舍楼出发，我赶紧发消息说「安排有变」。

collocations: message everyone about a change of plans

words.enDefinition: a large inflatable figure in the shape of a recognisable character

examples.en: The first character balloon I saw in the parade looked like a duck.
examples.zh: 我在游行上看到的第一个「卡通角色形气球」长得像只鸭子。

examples.en: My little cousin pointed to a character balloon above the marching band.
examples.zh: 我的小表亲指着行进乐队上方的一个「卡通角色形气球」。

words.enDefinition: to ask whether sharing a message with others is acceptable

examples.en: My friend reminded me to check before forwarding her message to the committee.
examples.zh: 朋友提醒我，把她的消息转给委员会之前「先征求同意」。

examples.en: The class group agreed to check before forwarding photos from the session.
examples.zh: 班级群商定，活动照片「转发前先征求同意」。

collocations: ask people to check before forwarding
check before forwarding a private message

words.enDefinition: to contact a friend to find out whether they are all right

examples.en: I went upstairs to check in on a friend after she missed our usual coffee.
examples.zh: 朋友没来和我们像平时那样喝咖啡，我就上楼「问候朋友是否安好」。

examples.en: It's worth making time to check in on a friend during a busy exam week.
examples.zh: 考试周虽然忙，也可以抽点时间「问候朋友是否安好」。

collocations: take time to check in on a friend
remember to check in on a friend
call to check in on a friend

words.zhGloss: 问问伴侣的想法和情况
words.enDefinition: to contact your partner to see how they feel or how things are going
acceptedZhAnswers: 问问伴侣的想法和情况

examples.en: Try to check in with your partner before promising your whole weekend to friends.
examples.zh: 把整个周末都答应给朋友前，先「问问伴侣怎么想」。

examples.en: She said it's helpful to check in with your partner when your timetable changes.
examples.zh: 她说，课表变了时，「问问伴侣的想法和情况」会有帮助。

collocations: remember to check in with your partner
regularly check in with your partner
take time to check in with your partner

words.enDefinition: to encourage someone while they try to do something difficult or competitive

examples.en: I went to the track to cheer someone on during the last student race.
examples.zh: 最后一场学生赛跑时，我去了跑道边「给参赛者加油助威」。

examples.en: I stayed to cheer someone on through the last song of the campus contest.
examples.zh: 校园比赛唱到最后一首歌时，我还留在场边「给参赛者加油助威」。

collocations: cheer someone on from the sidelines
cheer someone on during a race

words.enDefinition: a flower from a cherry tree, often enjoyed in spring

examples.en: A cherry blossom landed on my notebook while I was studying outdoors after class.
examples.zh: 我下课后在户外学习，一朵「樱花」落在了笔记本上。

examples.en: My host family showed me a photo of a cherry blossom from their garden.
examples.zh: 寄宿家庭给我看了他们花园里一朵「樱花」的照片。

words.enDefinition: a public event celebrating the flowering of cherry trees

examples.en: The cherry blossom festival offered guided walks through the garden beside campus on Sunday.
examples.zh: 周日的「樱花节」在校园旁的花园安排了导览散步。

examples.en: I went to a cherry blossom festival with my classmates during our spring visit.
examples.zh: 春季参访时，我和同学去参加了一场「樱花节」。

words.enDefinition: the period when cherry trees in an area are generally flowering

examples.en: I planned my visit for cherry blossom season so we could walk by the river.
examples.zh: 我把探访安排在「樱花花期」，这样我们可以到河边走走。

examples.en: The university's garden stayed open later during cherry blossom season for visitors.
examples.zh: 「樱花花期」期间，学校花园为访客延长了开放时间。

words.enDefinition: to keep your lips closed while chewing food

examples.en: The short table manners guide said to chew with your mouth closed at dinner.
examples.zh: 那份简短的餐桌礼仪指南说，用晚餐时要「闭着嘴咀嚼」。

examples.en: Our tutor used “Chew with your mouth closed” in a lesson about polite reminders.
examples.zh: 导师讲礼貌提醒时，举了「闭着嘴咀嚼」这个例子。

collocations: remember to chew with your mouth closed
a reminder to chew with your mouth closed
please chew with your mouth closed

words.enDefinition: A traditional Chinese craft using cut paper to make patterns, often for festivals.

examples.en: The museum included Chinese paper cutting in its display of Lunar New Year window decorations.
examples.zh: 博物馆在农历新年的窗饰展览里展示了「中国剪纸」。

examples.en: A student demonstrated Chinese paper cutting at the craft table next to our exhibition.
examples.zh: 一位同学在我们展览旁的手工桌上演示了「中国剪纸」。

collocations: an example of Chinese paper cutting

words.enDefinition: A Chinese cycle of twelve animals used to represent years and other time divisions.

examples.en: The campus exhibit included a diagram showing the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.
examples.zh: 校园展上有一张图，展示了「中国生肖体系」里的十二种动物。

examples.en: My neighbor explained the Chinese zodiac while we looked through her collection of festival stamps.
examples.zh: 我们翻看邻居收藏的节日邮票时，她介绍了「中国生肖体系」。

collocations: a display about the Chinese zodiac

words.enDefinition: To contribute part of the money for something a group is buying.

examples.en: We decided to chip in for pizza after the film ran longer than expected.
examples.zh: 电影比预想的长，我们决定「一起出钱买」比萨。

examples.en: Would everyone chip in for a larger bag of popcorn to share during the film?
examples.zh: 大家愿不愿意「一起出钱买」一大袋爆米花，看电影时一起吃？

collocations: ask everyone to chip in for snacks

words.enDefinition: to contribute some money to a present shared with others

examples.en: Three of us offered to chip in toward a gift for the person hosting dinner.
examples.zh: 我们当中三个人提出「凑钱合送一份礼物」给晚饭的主人。

examples.en: I was happy to chip in toward a gift even though I couldn't be there.
examples.zh: 虽然没法到场，我也很乐意「凑钱合送一份礼物」。

collocations: agree to chip in toward a gift
ask who can chip in toward a gift
offer to chip in toward a gift

words.enDefinition: to add a brief remark to an existing conversation

examples.en: I waited for a pause so I could chip in with my own story.
examples.zh: 我等到话头停了一下，才「插话补充」自己的经历。

examples.en: The student by the window decided to chip in with a comment about housing.
examples.zh: 窗边的同学决定「插话补充」一句，说说住宿。

words.enDefinition: informal conversation about everyday things of little importance

examples.en: The chitchat before our seminar made the room feel more relaxed.
examples.zh: 研讨课开始前的「闲聊」让教室里的气氛放松了些。

examples.en: We had a bit of chitchat while waiting for the lift.
examples.zh: 等电梯时，我们「闲聊」了几句。

words.enDefinition: Foil-wrapped chocolate coins often given or used in games during Hanukkah.

examples.en: My flatmate brought chocolate gelt to the common room along with a small wooden top.
examples.zh: 室友带了「光明节巧克力金币」和一个小木陀螺到公共休息室。

examples.en: We found chocolate gelt in the campus market beside a sign explaining the holiday.
examples.zh: 我们在校园集市看到了「光明节巧克力金币」，旁边有牌子介绍这个节日。

words.enDefinition: to decide what amount of personal information to tell others

examples.en: The session leader said we could choose how much to share in the group.
examples.zh: 活动负责人说，在小组里可以「自己决定分享多少」。

examples.en: I liked being able to choose how much to share during the exercise.
examples.zh: 我喜欢在练习中能「自己决定分享多少」。

collocations: let people choose how much to share
feel free to choose how much to share
allow everyone to choose how much to share

words.enDefinition: to decide which familiar customs you want to continue

examples.en: Moving gave me a chance to choose what to keep from my old routine.
examples.zh: 搬家让我可以「选择旧习惯里哪些继续保留」。

examples.en: My friends said I could choose what to keep as I tried new traditions.
examples.zh: 朋友们说，我在尝试新传统的同时，也可以「选择哪些继续保留」。

collocations: take time to choose what to keep
choose what to keep from an old routine
be free to choose what to keep

words.enDefinition: A Christian festival marking Jesus's birth, also celebrated through many cultural traditions.

examples.en: My flatmate invited me to spend Christmas with her family while campus was quiet.
examples.zh: 学校里人少的时候，室友邀请我和她家人一起过「圣诞节」。

examples.en: We asked classmates how they celebrate Christmas, and several described very different family traditions.
examples.zh: 我们问同学怎么过「圣诞节」，几个人讲的家庭习俗各不相同。

words.enDefinition: A traditional song sung during the Christmas season.

examples.en: The campus choir sang a Christmas carol during its winter performance in the main hall.
examples.zh: 校园合唱团在大厅举行冬季演出时，唱了一首「圣诞颂歌」。

examples.en: I recognized a Christmas carol playing quietly while we waited at the bus stop.
examples.zh: 我们在公交站等车时，我听出轻轻播放的是一首「圣诞颂歌」。

words.enDefinition: A wrapped paper novelty used at Christmas meals in Britain and elsewhere, often containing a paper crown or small gift.

examples.en: There was a Christmas cracker beside each plate at the community center's holiday lunch.
examples.zh: 社区中心举办节日午餐时，每个盘子旁都有一个「圣诞拉炮」。

examples.en: My British flatmate showed me the paper crown that came from her Christmas cracker.
examples.zh: 我的英国室友给我看了她的「圣诞拉炮」里附的纸王冠。

collocations: a joke from a Christmas cracker
a Christmas cracker at each place

words.enDefinition: The calendar day on which a community celebrates Christmas.

examples.en: The residence desk posted different opening hours for Christmas Day and the weekend after it.
examples.zh: 宿舍前台公布的「圣诞节当天」开放时间和随后那个周末的不一样。

examples.en: Some of us went for a walk on Christmas Day before sharing lunch together.
examples.zh: 「圣诞节当天」，我们几个人先去散步，然后一起吃了午饭。

words.enDefinition: The evening or calendar day immediately before Christmas Day.

examples.en: We picked up pastries on Christmas Eve because our usual cafe would be closed the next day.
examples.zh: 「平安夜」那天，我们买了些酥点，因为常去的咖啡馆第二天不开门。

examples.en: My neighbor spent Christmas Eve singing with a choir at the local community center.
examples.zh: 邻居在当地社区中心跟合唱团一起唱歌，度过了「平安夜」。

words.enDefinition: Decorative lights displayed around Christmas, often on trees, homes, or public streets.

examples.en: We went to see the Christmas lights downtown after our group finished its presentation.
examples.zh: 小组完成展示后，我们去市中心看了「圣诞彩灯」。

examples.en: The Christmas lights in our neighbor's window made the courtyard feel cheerful during the break.
examples.zh: 放假期间，邻居窗户上的「圣诞彩灯」让庭院更热闹了。

words.enDefinition: A public event to turn on a town's Christmas lights, especially in British usage.

examples.en: We stopped at the Christmas lights switch-on after a classmate finished work at the cafe.
examples.zh: 同学在咖啡馆下班后，我们顺路看了「圣诞彩灯点亮仪式」。

examples.en: A student choir was listed on the program for the town's Christmas lights switch-on.
examples.zh: 镇上「圣诞彩灯点亮仪式」的节目单上列出了一个学生合唱团。

collocations: a poster for the Christmas lights switch-on

words.enDefinition: A market selling seasonal food, decorations, or goods in the period before Christmas.

examples.en: We walked through the Christmas market after our last lecture and bought hot drinks.
examples.zh: 我们上完最后一节课后逛了「圣诞集市」，还买了热饮。

examples.en: The Christmas market near campus had several stalls run by local makers and student groups.
examples.zh: 校园附近的「圣诞集市」有几个由本地手工艺者和学生团体经营的摊位。

collocations: a stall at the Christmas market

words.enDefinition: A decorative object usually hung on a Christmas tree.

examples.en: I made a Christmas ornament from recycled paper at the craft table in our lounge.
examples.zh: 我在休息室的手工桌上用再生纸做了一个「圣诞树挂饰」。

examples.en: The Christmas ornament shaped like a small book came from a stall near the library.
examples.zh: 那个像一本小书的「圣诞树挂饰」是从图书馆附近的摊位买的。

words.enDefinition: A family stage show, often based on a fairy tale, performed around Christmas in Britain.

examples.en: A British classmate suggested seeing a Christmas pantomime at the small theater near our university.
examples.zh: 一位英国同学提议去学校附近的小剧院看「英式圣诞喜剧」。

examples.en: The local theater advertised its Christmas pantomime on a poster beside our campus bus stop.
examples.zh: 当地剧院在校园公交站旁的海报上宣传「英式圣诞喜剧」。

words.enDefinition: A dense fruit dessert traditionally served at Christmas in Britain and some other places.

examples.en: My flatmate brought Christmas pudding to the lounge and explained what her family puts in it.
examples.zh: 室友把「圣诞布丁」带到休息室，讲了她家都用些什么做。

examples.en: One table at the winter fair offered Christmas pudding alongside other desserts chosen by students.
examples.zh: 冬季集市有一桌供应「圣诞布丁」，也有同学们挑的其他甜点。

words.enDefinition: A large decorative sock hung at Christmas to hold small gifts.

examples.en: My neighbor's Christmas stocking had her name sewn on it in bright red thread.
examples.zh: 邻居的「圣诞袜」上用鲜红的线绣了她的名字。

examples.en: The language club displayed a Christmas stocking beside examples of traditions from other winter holidays.
examples.zh: 语言社摆了一只「圣诞袜」，旁边展示了其他冬季节日的习俗。

collocations: a Christmas stocking by the fireplace

words.enDefinition: A natural or artificial evergreen tree displayed and decorated at Christmas.

examples.en: The residents put up a Christmas tree in the lounge before the last week of term.
examples.zh: 学期最后一周前，住户们在休息室里摆了一棵「圣诞树」。

examples.en: Our small Christmas tree fit on the windowsill beside the plants my roommate looks after.
examples.zh: 我们的小「圣诞树」刚好能放在窗台上，挨着室友照料的植物。

words.enDefinition: A circular decoration displayed at Christmas, often made with greenery.

examples.en: Our neighbors hung a Christmas wreath on their door before leaving for the winter break.
examples.zh: 邻居们放寒假离开前，在门上挂了一个「圣诞花环」。

examples.en: I noticed a Christmas wreath with dried orange slices in the community center lobby.
examples.zh: 我在社区中心大厅看到一个带干橙片的「圣诞花环」。

collocations: a Christmas wreath on the door

words.enDefinition: A Vietnamese greeting wishing someone a happy new year.

examples.en: We wrote “Chúc mừng năm mới” on a card for our Vietnamese neighbors.
examples.zh: 我们在给越南邻居的卡片上写了「越南语的新年快乐」。

examples.en: A banner saying “Chúc mừng năm mới” hung above the student society table.
examples.zh: 学生社团的桌子上方挂着横幅，写的是「越南语的新年快乐」。

collocations: a sign reading Chúc mừng năm mới
write Chúc mừng năm mới on a card

words.enDefinition: a place where apples are pressed and made into cider

examples.en: The cider mill let us watch the apples go into the press.
examples.zh: 「苹果汁作坊」让我们观看苹果被送进压榨机的过程。

examples.en: We stopped at a cider mill on our way back to campus.
examples.zh: 我们回学校时，顺路去了家「苹果汁作坊」。

words.enDefinition: an organized meeting of people who attended the same school class or graduating year

examples.en: The class reunion gave us a chance to hear where everyone had ended up.
examples.zh: 「同学聚会」让我们有机会了解大家后来都去了哪里。

examples.en: I saw three friends from my first year at the class reunion that summer.
examples.zh: 那年夏天的「同学聚会」上，我见到了三个大一时的朋友。

words.enDefinition: To remove used cups so a space is tidy again after a gathering.

examples.en: Could you clear away the cups while I fold the blanket after our picnic?
examples.zh: 野餐完我来叠毯子，你能「把杯子收走」吗？

examples.en: Mina offered to clear away the cups while we returned the chairs to the lounge.
examples.zh: 我们把椅子放回休息室时，米娜主动提出「把杯子收走」。

collocations: offer to clear away the cups
clear away the cups from the table

words.enDefinition: to discuss a disagreement or misunderstanding so that tension eases

examples.en: I wanted to clear the air after my joke came across badly in the group chat.
examples.zh: 我在群里开的玩笑被误解后，想「消除彼此间的误会」。

examples.en: They met for coffee to clear the air before the campus festival that weekend.
examples.zh: 周末校园节庆之前，两人见面喝咖啡，好「消除彼此间的误会」。

words.enDefinition: to remove used dishes and utensils from where you sat

examples.en: The sign said to clear your place before leaving the dining hall.
examples.zh: 牌子写着，离开餐厅前要「收拾自己用过的餐具」。

examples.en: The volunteer said, “Please clear your place and leave the cups by the sink.”
examples.zh: 志愿者说「请收拾自己用过的餐具」，并把杯子放在水槽旁。

words.enDefinition: to touch drinking glasses together as a sign of celebration

examples.en: We stopped talking to clink glasses when the club finished the last performance.
examples.zh: 社团完成最后一场演出后，我们停下闲聊，「碰杯庆祝」。

examples.en: The students waited to clink glasses until everyone had a drink.
examples.zh: 学生们等每个人都拿到了饮料，才「碰杯」。

words.enDefinition: a group whose members know each other well and support one another

examples.en: Our year abroad turned four strangers into a close-knit group by the final month.
examples.zh: 到最后一个月，那一年的留学经历让四个陌生人成了「关系紧密的群体」。

examples.en: It took time to feel at home in such a close-knit group of friends.
examples.zh: 在这样一个「关系紧密的」朋友圈里，我花了些时间才感觉自在。

words.enDefinition: to shut a door without making much noise

examples.en: Could you close the door quietly while the group next door is recording?
examples.zh: 隔壁小组在录制，你能「轻轻把门关上」吗？

examples.en: The usher held a sign asking people to close the door quietly.
examples.zh: 引座员举着牌子，请大家「轻轻把门关上」。

collocations: remember to close the door quietly
ask someone to close the door quietly

words.enDefinition: to organise and run an event together with another person or group

examples.en: The language clubs agreed to co-host an event for anyone interested in storytelling.
examples.zh: 几个语言社团约好「共同主办活动」，欢迎对讲故事感兴趣的人参加。

examples.en: Our society offered to co-host an event with the neighbourhood arts group.
examples.zh: 我们社团提出和社区艺术团体「共同主办一场活动」。

collocations: co-host an event with another group

words.enDefinition: switching between languages or language varieties in a conversation

examples.en: My classmate used code-switching when quoting her aunt's words during the interview.
examples.zh: 访谈中，同学引用姨妈的话时用了「语码转换」。

examples.en: We noticed code-switching in the recording after the speaker changed to a local dialect.
examples.zh: 发言者转用当地方言后，我们从录音中听出了「语码转换」。

words.enDefinition: an informal romantic meeting over coffee or a similar drink

examples.en: I suggested a coffee date because we only had an hour between our classes.
examples.zh: 我们两节课之间只有一个小时，我就提议来一次「喝咖啡的约会」。

examples.en: Their coffee date turned into an afternoon walk around the university's botanical garden.
examples.zh: 他们的「喝咖啡的约会」后来变成了下午在大学植物园散步。

words.enDefinition: powder containing colour, used in some festivities such as Holi

examples.en: The photos showed clouds of coloured powder above the crowd at the Holi event.
examples.zh: 照片上，胡里节现场人群上方扬起一团团「节庆彩色粉末」。

examples.en: My friend still had coloured powder on her sleeve when we took the bus home.
examples.zh: 我们坐公交回家时，朋友的袖子上还留着「节庆彩色粉末」。

words.enDefinition: to make other people see you in a particular way

examples.en: I worried I might come across as quiet because I didn't say much.
examples.zh: 我没怎么说话，担心「给人的印象是」不爱开口。

examples.en: People who listen carefully can come across as interested without saying very much.
examples.zh: 认真听的人就算话不多，也能「给人的印象是」对话题感兴趣。

words.enDefinition: to give an impression of being impolite, whether intended or not

examples.en: I worried that my short reply might come across as rude in writing.
examples.zh: 我担心回复太短，写出来会「让人觉得没礼貌」。

examples.en: She didn't mean to come across as rude when she left the table.
examples.zh: 她离开餐桌时，并不想「让人觉得没礼貌」。

collocations: worry you'll come across as rude

words.expression: come and go as you please
words.lemma: come and go as you please
words.enDefinition: To arrive and leave at any time you choose during an informal event.
acceptedEnVariants: come and go as you please
come and go as you like

examples.en: You can come and go as you please while we share snacks in the lounge.
examples.zh: 我们在休息室一起吃零食时，大家「随时来去都可以」。

examples.en: The notice said “Come and go as you please” below the picnic start time.
examples.zh: 告示在野餐开始时间下方写着「随时来去都可以」。

collocations: feel free to come and go as you please
a message saying come and go as you please
tell friends to come and go as they please

words.enDefinition: A request to join the speaker's group at the place they indicate.

examples.en: Come find us by the window when you finish speaking with the tutor upstairs.
examples.zh: 你在楼上跟导师聊完后，「到窗边来找我们」。

examples.en: I told her to come find us once she had picked up her own coffee.
examples.zh: 我叫她拿到自己的咖啡后就「过来找我们」。

collocations: tell them to come find us
come find us by the window

words.enDefinition: To visit or join someone informally to have coffee together.

examples.en: Do you want to come for coffee after you finish your shift at the library?
examples.zh: 你在图书馆下班后，要不要「来喝杯咖啡」？

examples.en: Mina asked us to come for coffee when our morning lecture finished earlier than expected.
examples.zh: 上午的讲座提前结束，米娜请我们「来喝杯咖啡」。

collocations: invite someone to come for coffee
ask someone to come for coffee

words.enDefinition: to arrive at an event wearing clothes that form a costume

examples.en: We were invited to come in costume for the evening's pumpkin painting event.
examples.zh: 主办方邀请我们「穿化装服来」参加当晚的南瓜彩绘活动。

examples.en: I didn't plan to come in costume until my roommate offered me a cape.
examples.zh: 我本来没打算「穿化装服来」，后来室友说可以借我一件披风。

collocations: encourage guests to come in costume
ask everyone to come in costume

words.expression: come in out of the rain
words.lemma: come in out of the rain
words.enDefinition: invites a visitor to come indoors to avoid getting wet
acceptedEnVariants: come in out of the rain

examples.en: Come in out of the rain while I grab a towel for your wet backpack.
examples.zh: 「快进来避避雨」，我去拿条毛巾擦擦你的湿书包。

examples.en: When my neighbour saw me outside, she said, "Come in out of the rain and have some tea."
examples.zh: 邻居见我在外面，就说：「快进来避避雨」，喝点茶吧。

collocations: please come in out of the rain
hurry and come in out of the rain
come in out of the rain first

words.enDefinition: a friendly spoken invitation for a visitor to enter

examples.en: When my friend opened the door, she said, "Come on in. It's chilly outside."
examples.zh: 朋友打开门说：「快请进」，外面挺冷的。

examples.en: Come on in while I move these shoes away from the front door.
examples.zh: 「快请进」，我把门口这几双鞋挪开。

collocations: come on in and sit down
come on in out of the cold

words.enDefinition: to show such intense interest that it may make another person uncomfortable

examples.en: He worried he might come on too strong by suggesting another date before leaving.
examples.zh: 他担心离开前就提下次约会，会「一上来表现得太热切」。

examples.en: I didn't want to come on too strong when we had only talked once.
examples.zh: 我们只聊过一次，我不想「一上来表现得太热切」。

collocations: try not to come on too strong
worry about coming on too strong
seem to come on too strong

words.enDefinition: An informal invitation allowing someone to arrive at any convenient time.

examples.en: We're staying in the lounge all afternoon, so come whenever you finish your assignment.
examples.zh: 我们整个下午都在休息室，你写完作业「随时来都行」。

examples.en: Mina said we could come whenever, since the picnic didn't have an official start time.
examples.zh: 野餐没有正式的开始时间，米娜说我们「随时来都行」。

words.enDefinition: to express an opinion about how another person looks

examples.en: I felt it wasn't the right moment to comment on someone's appearance.
examples.zh: 我觉得那时候不适合「评论别人的外表」。

examples.en: The workshop discussed when it might be unwelcome to comment on someone's appearance.
examples.zh: 工作坊讨论了哪些情况下「评论别人的外表」可能让人不舒服。

collocations: choose whether to comment on someone's appearance
hesitate to comment on someone's appearance
try not to comment on someone's appearance

words.zhGloss: 有明确承诺的恋爱关系
words.enDefinition: an ongoing romantic relationship both people have agreed to value and maintain
acceptedZhAnswers: 有明确承诺的恋爱关系

examples.en: She wasn't sure she wanted a committed relationship during her year studying abroad.
examples.zh: 她不确定留学这一年里是否想进入「有明确承诺的恋爱关系」。

examples.en: They talked about what a committed relationship would mean while living in different cities.
examples.zh: 两人谈了异地居住时，「有明确承诺的恋爱关系」会意味着什么。

words.enDefinition: ordinary consideration people show each other in everyday situations

examples.en: My roommate picked up the dropped scarf as a matter of common courtesy.
examples.zh: 室友顺手捡起掉在地上的围巾，觉得这是「基本礼貌」。

examples.en: The notice described returning the chairs after the session as a common courtesy.
examples.zh: 通知说，活动结束后把椅子归位，是一种「基本礼貌」。

words.enDefinition: the usual way a person expresses themselves and responds to others

examples.en: I asked what communication style felt most natural for our partner in the project.
examples.zh: 我问合作伙伴，哪种「交流方式」对他来说最自然。

examples.en: My communication style changed when I moved from voice notes to written messages.
examples.zh: 我从发语音改为发文字后，「交流方式」也变了。

words.enDefinition: a local event held to raise money for a shared project or cause

examples.en: We helped sell plants at a community fundraiser beside the student library in June.
examples.zh: 六月，我们在学生图书馆旁边的「社区筹款活动」上帮忙卖植物。

examples.en: The community fundraiser paid for new picnic tables at the garden near campus.
examples.zh: 「社区筹款活动」为校园附近的花园筹到了购买新野餐桌的钱。

collocations: community fundraiser for a local project

words.enDefinition: a local organisation working with a group on a shared project

examples.en: A community partner helped our class put together an exhibition about local stories.
examples.zh: 一家「社区合作方」帮我们班策划了一个关于当地故事的展览。

examples.en: I met the community partner at the public library before the workshop.
examples.zh: 工作坊开始前，我在公共图书馆见了「社区合作方」。

words.enDefinition: a holiday meal organised for people in a local community

examples.en: I helped set tables for the community Thanksgiving meal at our local centre.
examples.zh: 我在社区中心帮忙为「社区感恩节聚餐」摆桌。

examples.en: Our class was invited to the community Thanksgiving meal near the new library.
examples.zh: 我们班受邀参加新图书馆附近的「社区感恩节聚餐」。

collocations: serve at a community Thanksgiving meal

words.enDefinition: to look at different people's calendars to find suitable shared times

examples.en: We needed to compare calendars before setting a date for our next group call.
examples.zh: 定下一次群组通话的日期前，我们得「对一对各自的日程」。

examples.en: I suggested we compare calendars after everyone had received their new timetables for spring.
examples.zh: 大家都收到春季新课表后，我建议「对一对各自的日程」。

words.enDefinition: a card sent to celebrate someone's achievement or happy occasion

examples.en: I left a congratulations card for my neighbour after she finished her degree.
examples.zh: 邻居完成学位后，我给她留了张「祝贺卡」。

examples.en: We passed the congratulations card around the flat so everyone could sign it.
examples.zh: 我们在公寓里传阅这张「祝贺卡」，好让大家签名。

words.enDefinition: a comment or question that helps people begin talking

examples.en: The pins on her backpack were a conversation starter at the welcome fair.
examples.zh: 在迎新集市上，她背包上的徽章成了「打开话题的引子」。

examples.en: Asking about local food was a good conversation starter in my group.
examples.zh: 在我们那组，问问附近有什么好吃的，是个「打开话题的好办法」。

words.enDefinition: an outdoor gathering with food cooked outside, especially in North American usage

examples.en: The residence held a cookout at the park after exams were over that Friday.
examples.zh: 那周五考试结束后，宿舍在公园办了一场「户外烧烤聚餐」。

examples.en: I signed up to bring drinks to the cookout with my host family.
examples.zh: 我报名了寄宿家庭的「户外烧烤聚餐」，负责带饮料。

words.enDefinition: a network of paths cut through a field of corn
