examples.en: We took the short route through the corn maze before it rained.
examples.zh: 下雨前，我们选了穿过「玉米地迷宫」的短路线。

examples.en: My roommate laughed when we got lost in the corn maze again.
examples.zh: 我们又在「玉米地迷宫」里迷路时，室友笑了起来。

collocations: find your way through a corn maze
get lost in a corn maze

words.enDefinition: small extras used to complete the look of a costume

examples.en: I borrowed costume accessories from the drama society instead of buying a costume.
examples.zh: 我从戏剧社借了「化装服配件」，省得买一套服装。

examples.en: The shop kept its costume accessories in a small box by the register.
examples.zh: 店家把「化装服配件」放在收银台旁边的小盒子里。

words.enDefinition: a competition that awards prizes for the costumes people wear

examples.en: My roommate entered the costume contest dressed as a tiny library cart.
examples.zh: 室友扮成一辆小图书推车参加了「化装比赛」。

examples.en: The costume contest took place after the last song of the evening.
examples.zh: 当晚最后一首歌结束后，举行了「化装比赛」。

words.enDefinition: a covering worn over the face as part of an outfit

examples.en: I made a costume mask that looked like a fox for the party.
examples.zh: 我为派对做了一个狐狸样子的「化装面具」。

examples.en: He lifted his costume mask so I could recognise him in the photograph.
examples.zh: 他掀起「化装面具」，好让我能在照片里认出他。

words.enDefinition: indicates that people may attend without wearing a costume

examples.en: The invite said "Costume optional," so I wore my usual clothes and boots.
examples.zh: 邀请上说「可不穿化装服」，所以我穿了平时的衣服和靴子。

examples.en: I was glad to see "Costume optional," since my costume hadn't arrived.
examples.zh: 看见「可不穿化装服」我很高兴，因为我的化装服还没到。

words.enDefinition: an organised walk in which participants show what they are wearing

examples.en: The evening began with a costume parade through the main residence hall.
examples.zh: 晚上的活动从穿过主宿舍楼的「化装游行」开始。

examples.en: I watched the costume parade from the steps with two other students.
examples.zh: 我和另外两个同学在台阶上看了「化装游行」。

words.enDefinition: a social gathering where people wear costumes instead of everyday clothes

examples.en: I borrowed a friend's hat for the costume party in our building.
examples.zh: 我借了朋友的帽子，准备参加楼里的「化装派对」。

examples.en: We left the costume party early to catch the last campus bus.
examples.zh: 为了坐上末班校园公交，我们提前离开了「化装派对」。

words.enDefinition: a service that lends costumes for payment for a limited time

examples.en: We looked for costume rental after deciding our matching outfits would cost too much.
examples.zh: 我们觉得买配套服装太贵，就去找「化装服租赁」服务。

examples.en: The drama society offers costume rental from its collection of old stage outfits.
examples.zh: 戏剧社拿珍藏的旧戏服提供「化装服租赁」。

words.enDefinition: an event where people exchange costumes they no longer use

examples.en: Our hall held a costume swap so students could reuse last year's outfits.
examples.zh: 我们宿舍办了场「化装服交换活动」，让同学能再利用去年的服装。

examples.en: I traded an old hat for a cloak at the costume swap.
examples.zh: 我在「化装服交换活动」上用一顶旧帽子换了件斗篷。

collocations: bring a costume to a costume swap

words.enDefinition: a hairpiece worn to look like a character or someone else

examples.en: The red costume wig gave my roommate an entirely different look.
examples.zh: 那顶红色「化装假发」让室友看起来像是完全变了个人。

examples.en: I borrowed a costume wig from the drama department for the student party.
examples.zh: 我从戏剧系借了顶「化装假发」，准备参加学生派对。

words.enDefinition: A question asking to move a shared activity to a different day.

examples.en: Could we do another day for coffee if your class ends too late this evening?
examples.zh: 如果你今晚下课太晚，喝咖啡「能改天吗」？

examples.en: Could we do another day when more people are free to see the film?
examples.zh: 「能改天吗」？找个有更多人有空看电影的日子。

collocations: ask could we do another day
could we do another day for coffee
could we do another day this week

words.enDefinition: An informal reply saying you may attend but cannot commit yet.
acceptedEnVariants: put me down as a maybe

examples.en: Please count me as a maybe until I get my shift schedule for next weekend.
examples.zh: 下周末的排班出来前，请「先把我算作待定」。

examples.en: For the picnic, count me as a maybe until my cousin confirms her travel plans.
examples.zh: 野餐「先把我算作待定」吧，我表亲还没确认她什么时候来。

collocations: count me as a maybe for now
count me as a maybe for Sunday
count me as a maybe until tomorrow

words.enDefinition: to remember and appreciate the good things in your life

examples.en: My grandmother says it's good to count your blessings once in a while.
examples.zh: 奶奶说，时不时「想想值得感恩的事」挺好的。

examples.en: The prompt said "Count your blessings," so I wrote about my friends here.
examples.zh: 提示写着「想想值得感恩的事」，所以我写了在这儿交的朋友。

collocations: take time to count your blessings

words.enDefinition: a US community event typically featuring local exhibits, competitions, and attractions

examples.en: We went to the county fair after a friend recommended its local produce exhibits.
examples.zh: 朋友推荐了当地农产品展，我们就去逛了「美国县集市」。

examples.en: My host brother volunteered at a county fair near his town during summer break.
examples.zh: 寄宿家庭的哥哥暑假在镇子附近的一场「美国县集市」做志愿者。

collocations: take part in a county fair

words.enDefinition: in British university usage, a student taking the same degree course as you

examples.en: A coursemate recognised me by the badges on my laptop cover.
examples.zh: 一位「同专业同学」认出了我笔记本保护壳上的徽章。

examples.en: My coursemate and I both chose the same optional module this term.
examples.zh: 这学期，我和一位「同专业同学」选了同一门选修课。

words.expression: cover your mouth when you cough
words.lemma: cover your mouth when you cough
words.enDefinition: to put something in front of your mouth when coughing
acceptedEnVariants: cover your mouth when you cough

examples.en: The waiting room notice said to cover your mouth when you cough.
examples.zh: 等候室的通知说要「咳嗽时遮住嘴」。

examples.en: I saw “Cover your mouth when you cough” near the shared kitchen sink.
examples.zh: 我在共用厨房的水槽旁看到「咳嗽时遮住嘴」。

collocations: remember to cover your mouth when you cough
a reminder to cover your mouth when you cough
please cover your mouth when you cough

words.enDefinition: a stand set up for displaying, selling, or making handmade objects

examples.en: My classmates decorated their craft booth with pieces they had made during term.
examples.zh: 同学们用学期中做的作品装饰了他们的「手工艺品摊位」。

examples.en: I stopped at a craft booth to buy a card for my host family.
examples.zh: 我在一个「手工艺品摊位」停下，给寄宿家庭买了张卡片。

words.enDefinition: an event where makers exhibit or sell handmade objects

examples.en: We bought two small bowls at the craft fair outside the university gallery.
examples.zh: 我们在大学美术馆外的「手工艺品集市」买了两只小碗。

examples.en: I helped a friend set out her handmade cards for the craft fair.
examples.zh: 我帮朋友把手工卡片摆好，准备在「手工艺品集市」出售。

words.enDefinition: to sleep for the night on someone's sofa as a temporary arrangement

examples.en: I had to crash on the couch after missing the last train home.
examples.zh: 我没赶上回家的末班车，只能「临时在沙发上过夜」。

examples.en: My friends said I could crash on the couch if it got too late.
examples.zh: 朋友说，如果时间太晚，可以「临时在沙发上过夜」。

collocations: let someone crash on the couch
offer to let someone crash on the couch
need to crash on the couch

words.enDefinition: cool fresh air that is typical of an autumn day

examples.en: We walked back through campus to enjoy the crisp fall air before dark.
examples.zh: 我们穿过校园走回去，趁天黑前享受一下「清爽的秋日空气」。

examples.en: A long walk in the crisp fall air woke me up before class.
examples.zh: 上课前，我在「清爽的秋日空气」里走了很久，人也清醒了。

collocations: walk in the crisp fall air

words.enDefinition: to go beyond what someone considers socially acceptable

examples.en: The student said a joke can cross a line even among friends.
examples.zh: 那名学生说，朋友之间开的玩笑也可能「超出分寸」。

examples.en: I thought posting the private photo would cross a line in our group.
examples.zh: 我觉得在我们群里发那张私人照会「超出分寸」。

collocations: feel that something would cross a line
cross a line with a joke
be about to cross a line

words.enDefinition: a small stand presenting objects, stories or activities from a community

examples.en: At our cultural booth, visitors could listen to songs people grew up hearing.
examples.zh: 来我们的「文化展示摊位」，参观者可以听到不同的人从小听的歌。

examples.en: I spent an hour helping at the cultural booth near the library entrance.
examples.zh: 我在图书馆入口旁的「文化展示摊位」帮了一个小时。

words.enDefinition: the shared background that helps people interpret words or actions

examples.en: The note gave enough cultural context to explain why the audience laughed.
examples.zh: 说明提供了足够的「文化语境」，解释观众为什么发笑。

examples.en: We discussed the cultural context before comparing how our families used the phrase.
examples.zh: 我们先谈了「文化语境」，再对比各自家里是怎么用那个说法的。

collocations: interpret something in its cultural context

words.enDefinition: a way of interpreting experiences shaped by one's cultural background

examples.en: I realised I was reading her story through my own cultural lens.
examples.zh: 我意识到，自己在用自己的「文化视角」理解她讲的事。

examples.en: The class looked at the same illustration through more than one cultural lens.
examples.zh: 全班从不止一种「文化视角」看了同一幅插图。

collocations: see something through a cultural lens
look through a different cultural lens

words.enDefinition: a repeated activity or way of doing something shared within a cultural setting

examples.en: Our project focused on a cultural practice my neighbour had taught me.
examples.zh: 我们的项目关注我邻居曾教给我的一种「文化惯例」。

examples.en: The volunteer described the cultural practice through examples from her own childhood.
examples.zh: 志愿者用自己童年的例子介绍了这种「文化惯例」。

words.enDefinition: a mention that relies on knowledge of a shared cultural detail

examples.en: I had to look up the cultural reference in the student film.
examples.zh: 学生拍的短片里有个「文化典故」，我得去查一下。

examples.en: My friend caught the cultural reference as soon as the actor named the song.
examples.zh: 演员一说出歌名，我朋友马上就听懂了那个「文化典故」。

words.enDefinition: cultural influences inherited from one's family or community

examples.en: The recording project encouraged my classmates to talk about their cultural roots.
examples.zh: 这个录音项目鼓励同学谈谈自己的「文化根脉」。

examples.en: I learned more about my cultural roots when my uncle explained the song.
examples.zh: 舅舅解释那首歌后，我对自己的「文化根脉」了解得更多了。

words.enDefinition: an event where people present arts, practices or stories from their communities

examples.en: Our cultural showcase included recordings collected by students from their own families.
examples.zh: 我们的「文化展示活动」播放了同学们从自己家里收集的录音。

examples.en: I chose to explain a game at the cultural showcase this year.
examples.zh: 今年的「文化展示活动」上，我选择介绍一种游戏。

collocations: take part in a cultural showcase

words.zhGloss: 对某一文化的刻板印象
words.enDefinition: an oversimplified belief about people associated with a particular culture
acceptedZhAnswers: 对某一文化的刻板印象

examples.en: The class discussed why the film's joke depended on a cultural stereotype.
examples.zh: 全班讨论了为什么电影里的笑话建立在「对某一文化的刻板印象」上。

examples.en: My classmate challenged a cultural stereotype by describing her own mixed experiences.
examples.zh: 同学讲了自己的多种经历，对「有关某一文化的刻板印象」提出了质疑。

words.zhGloss: 与特定文化密切相关的
words.enDefinition: closely tied to the practices or knowledge shared in one cultural setting
acceptedZhAnswers: 与特定文化密切相关的

examples.en: The joke was culturally specific, so I asked what I was missing.
examples.zh: 这个笑话「依赖特定文化背景」，我就问自己没听懂的是哪一部分。

examples.en: We replaced a culturally specific example with one everyone in the room understood.
examples.zh: 我们把一个「依赖特定文化背景」的例子换成了在场的人都懂的例子。

words.enDefinition: a statement noting that practices do not always stay the same

examples.en: “Customs change over time,” the speaker said, holding up two old photographs.
examples.zh: 发言者举着两张老照片说「习俗会随时间变化」。

examples.en: We talked about how customs change over time after comparing our family stories.
examples.zh: 对比各家的故事后，我们谈到了「习俗会随时间变化」。

collocations: discuss how customs change over time
show how customs change over time
recognise that customs change over time

words.enDefinition: to divide off a single portion of a pie for serving

examples.en: I offered to cut a slice of pie for my neighbour while she poured the tea.
examples.zh: 邻居倒茶时，我主动帮她「切一块派」。

examples.en: Could you cut a slice of pie for me while you have the plate nearby?
examples.zh: 盘子就在你手边，能帮我「切一块派」吗？

collocations: offer to cut a slice of pie
cut a slice of pie for a guest
ask someone to cut a slice of pie

words.enDefinition: an evening a couple sets aside to spend time together

examples.en: We moved date night to Thursday because my partner had an essay due Friday.
examples.zh: 伴侣周五要交论文，所以我们把「两人专门约会的晚上」改到了周四。

examples.en: Our date night was just homemade pizza and a movie in the living room.
examples.zh: 我们的「两人约会之夜」只是在客厅吃自制披萨、看电影。

words.enDefinition: a place people like to go for a romantic meeting

examples.en: We found a quiet date spot near campus that stayed open after lectures.
examples.zh: 我们在校园附近找到一个安静的「适合约会的地点」，下课后还营业。

examples.en: My friend suggested a date spot within walking distance of our residence.
examples.zh: 朋友推荐了一个「适合约会的地点」，从宿舍走路就能到。

words.enDefinition: the yearly date when a couple marks the start of their dating relationship

examples.en: On our first dating anniversary, we went back to the cinema where we first met.
examples.zh: 第一次过「交往纪念日」时，我们回了最初见面的那家电影院。

examples.en: She remembered their dating anniversary after seeing an old photo from that weekend.
examples.zh: 看到那周末的一张旧照片后，她想起两人的「交往纪念日」。

words.enDefinition: an app people use to meet potential romantic partners

examples.en: We first spoke on a dating app while studying at different universities nearby.
examples.zh: 我们在附近不同大学读书时，最先是在「约会交友应用」上开始聊天的。

examples.en: Maya deleted the dating app after deciding she wanted a break from meeting people.
examples.zh: 玛雅决定暂停认识新人后，删除了「约会交友应用」。

words.enDefinition: the qualities or circumstances someone looks for in people they might date

examples.en: I adjusted my dating preferences after moving closer to the main university campus.
examples.zh: 搬到离主校区更近的地方后，我调整了「约会偏好」。

examples.en: They talked about dating preferences with friends on their way home from the film.
examples.zh: 看完电影回家的路上，他们和朋友聊了「约会偏好」。

words.enDefinition: the page describing a person to others on a dating service

examples.en: My dating profile says I like quiet cafés and walks near the river.
examples.zh: 我的「约会交友资料」写着，我喜欢安静的咖啡馆和河边散步。

examples.en: I updated my dating profile after I moved to a new part of town.
examples.zh: 搬到城里新的片区后，我更新了「约会交友资料」。

words.enDefinition: the people, places, and social habits involved in dating in a particular setting

examples.en: My friend was curious about the dating scene after moving to a smaller university town.
examples.zh: 朋友搬到较小的大学城后，很好奇当地的「交友约会圈」怎么样。

examples.en: We talked about the dating scene while walking back from the student film night.
examples.zh: 我们从学生电影之夜走回来时聊了「当地交友约会圈」。

collocations: get back into the dating scene

words.enDefinition: something important enough to make someone decide against a relationship or agreement

examples.en: Being unable to agree on where to live might be a deal-breaker for them.
examples.zh: 无法就住在哪里达成一致，对他们来说可能是「无法接受的条件」。

examples.en: She thought very different plans after graduation could become a deal-breaker in their relationship.
examples.zh: 她觉得毕业后的计划差别太大，可能会成为恋爱里「让人无法接受的条件」。

words.enDefinition: to talk explicitly about what kind of romantic relationship two people have

examples.en: She wanted to define the relationship before committing to plans for the summer holidays.
examples.zh: 落实暑假计划前，她想「说清双方是什么关系」。

examples.en: They finally agreed to define the relationship after dating for most of the term.
examples.zh: 他们约会了大半个学期，最终同意「说清双方是什么关系」。

collocations: talk about whether to define the relationship

words.enDefinition: checks whether something you just said or repeated was correct

examples.en: I repeated her name and asked, "Did I get that right? It's new to me."
examples.zh: 我复述了她的名字，问：「我说对了吗」？这个名字我第一次听。

examples.en: You said your family name comes first. did I get that right, or did I misunderstand?
examples.zh: 你说你的姓在前面，「我说对了吗」，还是我理解错了？

collocations: did I get that right this time
just checking, did I get that right
did I get that right now

words.expression: did you find the place okay
words.lemma: did you find the place okay
words.enDefinition: asks a visitor whether they had trouble reaching the location
acceptedEnVariants: did you find the place okay

examples.en: Did you find the place okay? Some of the house numbers are hidden behind the trees.
examples.zh: 「这个地方好找吗」？有些门牌号被树挡住了。

examples.en: Our host asked, "Did you find the place okay?" and took our wet umbrellas at the door.
examples.zh: 主人在门口接过我们的湿雨伞，问：「这个地方好找吗」？

collocations: so did you find the place okay
did you find the place okay in the rain
ask if they found the place okay

words.enDefinition: a statement that different practices can continue in the same group

examples.en: Our facilitator said different customs can coexist, even in a single shared kitchen.
examples.zh: 引导员说，即使在同一间共用厨房里，「不同习俗也可以共存」。

examples.en: The photo project showed how different customs can coexist in the same neighbourhood.
examples.zh: 摄影项目展示了「不同习俗怎样在同一社区共存」。

collocations: recognise that different customs can coexist
show how different customs can coexist
find a place where different customs can coexist

words.enDefinition: tells guests that their meal is ready to eat

examples.en: Our host called "Dinner is served!" as we finished taking the group photo.
examples.zh: 我们拍完合影时，做东的人喊了声「开饭了」！

examples.en: We heard "Dinner is served!" and put our cards away before heading inside.
examples.zh: 我们听见有人说「开饭了」，就把牌收起来，进了屋。

words.enDefinition: the degree to which words state their point without hinting

examples.en: The directness of his reply surprised me until we talked about the wording.
examples.zh: 他的回复那么「直白」，让我吃了一惊，后来我们聊了措辞。

examples.en: We had different ideas about directness when giving feedback on each other's drafts.
examples.zh: 我们对互相改稿时表达该「多直白」有不同想法。

words.enDefinition: shared expectations for how a group will conduct a discussion

examples.en: We agreed on discussion ground rules before sharing experiences from our hometowns.
examples.zh: 大家聊家乡经历之前，先商量了「讨论基本规则」。

examples.en: The handout put the discussion ground rules above the first group question.
examples.zh: 资料把「讨论基本规则」列在第一道小组讨论题的上面。

words.enDefinition: to deliberately reduce how closely you spend time or communicate with a friend

examples.en: She said it can be hard to distance yourself from a friend you still admire.
examples.zh: 她说，要「主动和自己仍欣赏的朋友拉开距离」可能很难。

examples.en: My tutor asked what it meant to distance yourself from a friend without being rude.
examples.zh: 导师问，「主动和朋友拉开距离」而又不失礼，是怎样一回事。

collocations: choose to distance yourself from a friend
start to distance yourself from a friend
find it difficult to distance yourself from a friend

words.expression: do you mind if I join you
words.lemma: do you mind if i join you
words.enDefinition: politely asks to become part of what someone is doing
acceptedEnVariants: do you mind if I join you

examples.en: Do you mind if I join you? I recognised you two from the welcome session this morning.
examples.zh: 「介意我加入吗」？我认出你们是早上参加迎新活动的那两位。

examples.en: She asked, "Do you mind if I join you for lunch? The people I know are in class."
examples.zh: 她问：「介意我加入你们一起吃午饭吗」？我认识的人都在上课。

collocations: do you mind if I join you for lunch
do you mind if I join you here
do you mind if I join you all

words.expression: do you mind if I open a window
words.lemma: do you mind if i open a window
words.enDefinition: asks whether opening a window would bother another person
acceptedEnVariants: do you mind if I open a window

examples.en: Do you mind if I open a window while we're eating, or would it make you too cold?
examples.zh: 我们吃饭时，「介意我开扇窗吗」？会不会让你觉得冷？

examples.en: I asked, "Do you mind if I open a window?" because the room was getting rather warm.
examples.zh: 房间慢慢变得挺热的，我问：「介意我开扇窗吗」？

collocations: do you mind if I open a window a little
do you mind if I open a window in here
ask if I can open a window

words.expression: do you still do that now
words.lemma: do you still do that now
words.enDefinition: a question asking whether an earlier habit continues into the present
acceptedEnVariants: do you still do that now

examples.en: “Do you still do that now?” I asked after hearing about her childhood meals.
examples.zh: 听她讲完小时候怎么吃饭，我问「你现在还这样做吗？」

examples.en: He described his family's old routine, so I asked, “Do you still do that now?”
examples.zh: 他讲了家里以前的日常做法，我就问「你现在还这样做吗？」

collocations: ask “Do you still do that now?”
“Do you still do that now that you live here?”
“I wonder whether you still do that now”

words.enDefinition: a question asking if a practice differs between areas

examples.en: “Does it vary by region?” I asked after hearing two names for the bread.
examples.zh: 听到这种面包有两种叫法后，我问「各地叫法一样吗？」

examples.en: Our tutor asked, “Does it vary by region?” when the students compared their stories.
examples.zh: 同学们对比各自讲的事时，导师问「各地做法有差别吗？」

collocations: “Does it vary by region where you live?”

words.enDefinition: a request for permission to be sought before adding you to a group

examples.en: “Don't add me without asking,” my flatmate said after I mentioned the chat.
examples.zh: 我说起那个群聊后，室友说「加我进群前先问一声」。

examples.en: I wrote, “Don't add me without asking,” after leaving the study group chat.
examples.zh: 我退出学习群后写道「加我进群前先问一声」。

words.enDefinition: an informal request to stay in contact or visit again after leaving

examples.en: “Don't be a stranger,” my old tutor said as I left the department.
examples.zh: 我离开系里时，以前的导师说：“「以后别断了联系」。”

examples.en: My friend waved and said, “Don't be a stranger when you're back in town.”
examples.zh: 朋友挥手说：“回来时记得来找我，「别断了联系」。”

collocations: don't be a stranger after graduation
don't be a stranger when you're nearby

words.enDefinition: a request to leave room for people to pass through a door

examples.en: “Don't block the doorway,” the usher said as the crowd moved in.
examples.zh: 人群进来时，引座员说「别挡住门口」。

examples.en: The volunteer held up a sign saying “Don't block the doorway” after the talk.
examples.zh: 讲座结束后，志愿者举起写着「别挡住门口」的牌子。

collocations: a sign reading “Don't block the doorway”

words.expression: don't feel you owe me anything
words.lemma: don't feel you owe me anything
words.enDefinition: tells someone that you do not expect anything in return
acceptedEnVariants: don't feel you owe me anything

examples.en: Don't feel you owe me anything. I already had a copy, and I know you collect these.
examples.zh: 「不用觉得欠我什么」。我已经有一本了，也知道你在收藏这些。

examples.en: My neighbour said, "Don't feel you owe me anything. I just thought you'd like this."
examples.zh: 邻居说：「不用觉得欠我什么」。我只是觉得你会喜欢。

collocations: please don't feel you owe me anything
really, don't feel you owe me anything
tell them don't feel you owe me anything

words.enDefinition: asks someone to keep a cat from leaving the home

examples.en: Don't let the cat out when you bring your bag in through the back door.
examples.zh: 你从后门拿包进来时，「别让猫跑出去」。

examples.en: My classmate's only house rule was, "Don't let the cat out when you open the door."
examples.zh: 同学家就一个规矩，开门时「别让猫跑出去」。

collocations: please don't let the cat out
remember, don't let the cat out
don't let the cat out when you leave

words.enDefinition: lets someone know they need not worry about disturbing your sleep

examples.en: Don't worry about waking me if you need to leave for the station early.
examples.zh: 如果你要早早去车站，「不用怕把我吵醒」。

examples.en: My host said, "Don't worry about waking me when you make breakfast in the morning."
examples.zh: 主人说：「早上你做早餐时，不用怕把我吵醒」。

collocations: really, don't worry about waking me
please don't worry about waking me
don't worry about waking me up

words.enDefinition: money given to a cause as a gesture honouring you

examples.en: We made a donation in your name to the community garden you told us about.
examples.zh: 我们给你提过的社区菜园「以你的名义捐了款」。

examples.en: This card tells you about a donation in your name for your graduation.
examples.zh: 这张卡片是想告诉你，我们为庆祝你毕业「以你的名义捐了款」。

collocations: make a donation in your name
let you know about a donation in your name
send a card about a donation in your name

words.enDefinition: going from one house or building to the next

examples.en: The club planned door-to-door trick-or-treating for the afternoon before the costume party.
examples.zh: 换装派对那天下午，社团安排了「挨家挨户」讨糖的活动。

examples.en: We stayed in the courtyard instead of joining the door-to-door group.
examples.zh: 我们留在院子里，没跟着那组人去「挨家挨户」讨糖。

words.enDefinition: Having made two commitments for the same time.

examples.en: I realized I was double-booked when my roommate reminded me about our cinema tickets.
examples.zh: 室友提醒我电影票的事，我才发现自己「同时有两个安排」。

examples.en: Maya was double-booked for Sunday afternoon and couldn't stay for the whole picnic after all.
examples.zh: 玛雅星期天下午「同时有两个安排」，所以最后没能全程参加野餐。

words.enDefinition: a date on which two couples go somewhere together

examples.en: We planned a double date with my roommate and her boyfriend after exams.
examples.zh: 考试后，我们安排了和我室友及她男朋友「两对人一起约会」。

examples.en: Our double date ended with four of us sharing chips outside the cinema.
examples.zh: 「两对人一起约会」的最后，我们四人在电影院外分吃了一份薯条。

collocations: invite someone on a double date

words.enDefinition: to put a bitten piece of food back into a shared dip

examples.en: My flatmate reminded me not to double-dip in the bowl we were sharing.
examples.zh: 室友提醒我，公用酱碗里的酱，食物「咬过后别再蘸」。

examples.en: The student café put up a sign asking customers not to double-dip.
examples.zh: 学生咖啡馆挂了块牌子，请顾客不要「咬过后再蘸公用酱」。

collocations: don't double-dip in a shared bowl

words.enDefinition: a title used in academic contexts before a doctorate holder's name

examples.en: The coordinator introduced Dr Chen before she began speaking about the community project.
examples.zh: 协调员介绍了陈「博士」，随后她开始谈那个社区项目。

examples.en: I used Dr Malik on the programme because that was their request.
examples.zh: 我按对方的要求，在活动手册上写了马利克「博士」。

words.enDefinition: A traditional performance in which a team moves a long dragon figure in coordinated patterns.

examples.en: We watched the dragon dance curve past the community center during the festival procession.
examples.zh: 节庆巡游时，我们看着「舞龙」队伍蜿蜒经过社区中心。

examples.en: My classmate pointed out the dragon dance team waiting near the entrance to the fair.
examples.zh: 同学指给我看在集市入口旁等候的「舞龙」队。

words.enDefinition: to encourage a quiet person to take part in an ongoing discussion

examples.en: A simple question can draw someone into the conversation without putting them on the spot.
examples.zh: 一个简单的问题能「把人带进话题」，用不着当场给对方压力。

examples.en: Our mentor knew how to draw someone into the conversation by asking about their interests.
examples.zh: 学长知道怎么通过问对方的兴趣「把人带进话题」。

collocations: try to draw someone into the conversation
use a question to draw someone into the conversation
draw someone into the conversation gently

words.enDefinition: A four-sided top with Hebrew letters used in a traditional Hanukkah game.

examples.en: A student showed us a wooden dreidel at the activity table in the library.
examples.zh: 一位同学在图书馆的活动桌上给我们看了一个木制「光明节四面陀螺」。

examples.en: We watched the dreidel spin across the table while our classmate explained the Hebrew letters.
examples.zh: 同学介绍上面的希伯来字母时，我们看着「光明节四面陀螺」转过桌面。

words.enDefinition: to put on clothing that makes you look like someone or something

examples.en: My desk mate wanted to dress up as a librarian from a novel.
examples.zh: 同桌想「装扮成」一部小说里的图书馆管理员。

examples.en: We might dress up as characters from an old cartoon for the dance.
examples.zh: 舞会上，我们可能会「装扮成」一部老动画里的角色。

collocations: dress up as someone from a film

words.expression: drop by when you're in town
words.lemma: drop by when you're in town
words.enDefinition: an informal invitation to visit when the other person is nearby
acceptedEnVariants: drop by when you're in town

examples.en: “Drop by when you're in town next week,” she said after the reunion.
examples.zh: 聚会结束后，她说：“下周「进城时顺道过来」。”

examples.en: I wrote, “Drop by when you're in town, and we'll get dinner together.”
examples.zh: 我写道：“「进城时顺道过来」，我们一起吃晚饭。”

collocations: feel free to drop by when you're in town
do drop by when you're in town
drop by when you're in town next

words.enDefinition: a person who visits without first arranging a particular time

examples.en: I had just put the kettle on when a drop-in visitor arrived.
examples.zh: 我刚烧上水，就来了一位「没预约就上门的访客」。

examples.en: Our group didn't mind a drop-in visitor joining us for tea sometimes.
examples.zh: 我们不介意偶尔有「没预约就上门的访客」加入，一起喝茶。

words.enDefinition: to go briefly to leave a present with someone

examples.en: I stopped by to drop off a gift for my neighbour after her exam.
examples.zh: 邻居考完试后，我「顺路把礼物送去」了。

examples.en: We planned to drop off a gift after class instead of mailing it.
examples.zh: 我们打算下课后「顺路把礼物送去」，就不寄了。

collocations: offer to drop off a gift
stop by to drop off a gift
arrange to drop off a gift

words.enDefinition: to contact someone briefly in writing, in informal speech

examples.en: You can drop someone a line if you want to ask how they are.
examples.zh: 想问对方过得怎样，可以「给某人发个简短消息」。

examples.en: It was easy to drop someone a line between classes on my new campus.
examples.zh: 在我现在的校区，两节课之间「给人发个简短消息」很方便。

collocations: remember to drop someone a line
drop me a line when you arrive

words.enDefinition: humour delivered with a serious manner and little obvious emotion

examples.en: I finally caught her dry humour after listening to a few stories.
examples.zh: 听了几个故事后，我终于听懂了她那种「一本正经的幽默」。

examples.en: His dry humour took me by surprise when we first worked together.
examples.zh: 刚开始一起做事时，他那种「一本正经的幽默」让我意外。

words.enDefinition: a UK bank holiday normally observed in early May

examples.en: The UK calendar showed the Early May bank holiday before the weekend we had chosen.
examples.zh: 英国日历显示，「英国五月初公众假日」在我们选的那个周末之前。

examples.en: We made lunch plans for the Early May bank holiday because neither of us had class.
examples.zh: 我们俩那天都没课，于是约在「英国五月初公众假日」吃午饭。

collocations: over the Early May bank holiday
Early May bank holiday opening hours
closed for the Early May bank holiday

words.enDefinition: to become someone another person can trust through your behaviour over time

examples.en: It often takes small promises kept over time to earn someone's trust in a friendship.
examples.zh: 朋友间往往要长期信守小承诺，才能「赢得对方的信任」。

examples.en: She thought listening carefully was one way to earn someone's trust after they had met.
examples.zh: 她觉得相识后认真听对方说话，是「赢得对方信任」的一种方式。

collocations: take time to earn someone's trust

words.enDefinition: to begin talking gradually until the exchange feels more natural

examples.en: It was easier to ease into a conversation while we both shelved the books.
examples.zh: 我们一边把书摆上架，一边更容易「慢慢聊开」。

examples.en: I tried to ease into a conversation instead of asking lots of questions immediately.
examples.zh: 我试着「慢慢聊开」，一上来没有连问好几个问题。

collocations: ease into a conversation with a question
help someone ease into a conversation
take time to ease into a conversation

words.enDefinition: a basket filled with eggs, sweets, or other items for Easter

examples.en: My younger cousin carried an Easter basket while looking for eggs in the garden.
examples.zh: 年纪较小的表亲提着「复活节礼篮」在花园里找彩蛋。

examples.en: We filled the Easter basket with small chocolates from the shop near the station.
examples.zh: 我们用车站附近商店的小块巧克力装满了「复活节礼篮」。

words.enDefinition: a decorated hat traditionally worn for some Easter events

examples.en: My neighbour was making an Easter bonnet for her daughter's school parade that weekend.
examples.zh: 邻居正在给女儿做一顶「复活节装饰帽」，准备周末学校游行戴。

examples.en: She pinned a paper flower to the Easter bonnet just before leaving home.
examples.zh: 临出门时，她在「复活节装饰帽」上别了一朵纸花。

words.enDefinition: a meal between breakfast and lunch held to mark Easter

examples.en: We brought fruit to Easter brunch at my flatmate's aunt's house that Sunday.
examples.zh: 那天周日，我们带着水果去室友姨妈家吃「复活节早午餐」。

examples.en: The student café advertised Easter brunch for people staying near campus over the weekend.
examples.zh: 学生咖啡馆为周末留在校园附近的人宣传「复活节早午餐」。

words.enDefinition: an imaginary rabbit said to bring Easter eggs or gifts to children

examples.en: The library invited someone dressed as the Easter Bunny to its afternoon story session.
examples.zh: 图书馆请了一位扮成「复活节兔子」的人参加下午的故事会。

examples.en: My niece drew the Easter Bunny beside a basket on the card she made.
examples.zh: 外甥女在自己做的卡片上画了一只「复活节兔子」，旁边还有个篮子。

collocations: a picture of the Easter Bunny

words.enDefinition: a decorated egg or egg-shaped sweet associated with the Easter holiday

examples.en: My nephew left an Easter egg on the table for me when I visited.
examples.zh: 我去做客时，外甥在桌上给我留了一个「复活节彩蛋」。

examples.en: The children each painted an Easter egg before the picnic began in the garden.
examples.zh: 花园里的野餐开始前，孩子们各涂了一个「复活节彩蛋」。

words.enDefinition: an activity where people look for hidden eggs or egg-shaped sweets

examples.en: Our neighbours invited us to their Easter egg hunt in the small park.
examples.zh: 邻居邀请我们参加在小公园举办的「复活节寻蛋活动」。

examples.en: The Easter egg hunt ended when the last child found a chocolate egg under a bench.
examples.zh: 最后一个孩子在长椅下找到一枚巧克力蛋后，「复活节寻蛋活动」结束了。

words.enDefinition: an Easter activity in which people roll eggs along the ground

examples.en: The museum held an Easter egg roll on the lawn for visiting families.
examples.zh: 博物馆在草坪上为到访家庭举办了「复活节滚彩蛋活动」。

examples.en: I volunteered at the Easter egg roll and helped put signs on the path.
examples.zh: 我去「复活节滚彩蛋活动」做志愿者，帮忙在小路上放指示牌。

words.enDefinition: a Christian holiday celebrating the resurrection of Jesus, also marked by seasonal customs

examples.en: My aunt invited us to stay with her over Easter near the coast.
examples.zh: 姨妈邀请我们在「复活节」期间到她沿海的住处留宿。

examples.en: I asked my flatmate how her family usually spent Easter when she was young.
examples.zh: 我问室友小时候家里通常怎么过「复活节」。

words.enDefinition: the Monday immediately after Easter Sunday

examples.en: The library will open later on Easter Monday because the staff timetable is different.
examples.zh: 由于值班安排不同，图书馆在「复活节星期一」会晚些开门。

examples.en: We came back to campus on Easter Monday after spending the weekend with friends.
examples.zh: 周末和朋友待在一起后，我们在「复活节星期一」回了学校。

words.enDefinition: a Christian worship gathering held for Easter

examples.en: A friend asked whether I wanted to attend an Easter service at her church.
examples.zh: 朋友问我要不要去她的教堂参加「复活节礼拜」。

examples.en: The choir practised a new song for the Easter service on Sunday morning.
examples.zh: 合唱团为周日早上的「复活节礼拜」排练了一首新歌。

words.enDefinition: the Sunday on which Easter is celebrated in a Christian calendar

examples.en: We met for lunch on Easter Sunday at my friend's house outside the city.
examples.zh: 「复活节星期日」那天，我们在朋友城外的家里一起吃午饭。

examples.en: The church displayed the times of its services for Easter Sunday on the noticeboard.
examples.zh: 教堂在公告栏上贴出了「复活节星期日」的礼拜时间。

words.enDefinition: making others feel comfortable talking to or confiding in you

examples.en: I found my new neighbour easy to talk to even when I paused a lot.
examples.zh: 我经常说到一半停下来，但觉得新邻居还是很「好聊」。

examples.en: The tutor was easy to talk to, so I stayed after class to chat.
examples.zh: 老师很「好聊」，所以我课后留下来聊了会儿。

collocations: find someone easy to talk to

words.enDefinition: to eat without trying to match how quickly others finish

examples.en: My friend said, “Eat at your own pace,” when I checked the time.
examples.zh: 我看时间时，朋友说「按自己的速度吃」。

examples.en: “You can eat at your own pace,” the host told us at the buffet.
examples.zh: 主持人告诉大家，自助餐可以「按自己的速度吃」。

collocations: feel free to eat at your own pace
eat at your own pace during the break
a reminder to eat at your own pace

words.enDefinition: a present made of food that the recipient can eat

examples.en: The jam I brought was an edible gift from my hometown.
examples.zh: 我带来的果酱是份家乡的「可以吃的礼物」。

examples.en: My cousin likes getting an edible gift instead of more kitchen items.
examples.zh: 比起收到更多厨房用具，表姐更喜欢「可以吃的礼物」。

words.enDefinition: the activity of painting or otherwise decorating eggs, often for Easter

examples.en: The residence office set out brushes for egg decorating in the common room.
examples.zh: 宿管办公室在公共休息室摆出了「彩蛋装饰活动」用的画笔。

examples.en: I tried egg decorating with my friends after our last class before the holiday.
examples.zh: 放假前最后一节课结束后，我和朋友一起做了「彩蛋装饰活动」。

words.enDefinition: A rich drink made with eggs and dairy, often served around Christmas in North America.

examples.en: We tried nonalcoholic eggnog at the gathering in our Canadian residence before the break.
examples.zh: 放假前，我们在加拿大宿舍的聚会上尝了无酒精的「节庆蛋奶饮」。

examples.en: My roommate had a cup of eggnog while we looked through the winter fair stalls.
examples.zh: 我们在冬季集市逛摊位时，室友喝了一杯「节庆蛋奶饮」。

words.enDefinition: an event marking the close of the summer season

examples.en: The college held an end-of-summer celebration for students finishing their short courses that week.
examples.zh: 学院为那周结课的短期课程学生举办了「夏末庆祝活动」。

examples.en: My neighbours brought fruit to the end-of-summer celebration at the small community garden.
examples.zh: 邻居带了水果来参加小社区花园的「夏末庆祝活动」。

words.enDefinition: A gathering or event held to mark the end of the year.

examples.en: Our residence held an end-of-year celebration before students began heading home for the winter break.
examples.zh: 同学们开始陆续回家过寒假前，宿舍办了一场「年末庆祝活动」。

examples.en: We saw neighbors from across the area at the end-of-year celebration in the park.
examples.zh: 我们在公园的「年末庆祝活动」上见到了附近各处的邻居。

words.enDefinition: a person with whom someone formerly had a romantic relationship

examples.en: My ex-partner and I still say hello when we meet outside the library.
examples.zh: 我和「前任伴侣」在图书馆外遇到时还是会打招呼。

examples.en: She asked her ex-partner to return the books they had bought for their course.
examples.zh: 她请「前任伴侣」还回两人为课程买的那些书。

words.enDefinition: a romantic relationship whose partners agree not to date other people

examples.en: They discussed an exclusive relationship before deciding how to introduce each other to friends.
examples.zh: 他们先讨论了是否建立「排他性恋爱关系」，再决定怎么向朋友介绍彼此。

examples.en: I wasn't ready for an exclusive relationship after only a few meetings in town.
examples.zh: 我们只在城里见了几次，我还没准备好进入「排他性恋爱关系」。

words.enDefinition: to tell the people you are eating with that you need to leave

examples.en: Our host said you could excuse yourself from the table if needed.
examples.zh: 主持人说，如果有需要，可以「打声招呼暂时离席」。

examples.en: In our practice dinner, you could excuse yourself from the table between courses.
examples.zh: 模拟聚餐时，可以在两道菜之间「打声招呼暂时离席」。

collocations: remember to excuse yourself from the table
quietly excuse yourself from the table
excuse yourself from the table between courses

words.enDefinition: to think that people are coming to visit you

examples.en: We didn't expect company, so there were books all over the couch.
examples.zh: 我们「没想到会有客人来」，所以沙发上到处都是书。

examples.en: I told my roommate we might expect company after the afternoon seminar.
examples.zh: 我告诉室友，下午研讨课后可能「有客人要来」。

words.enDefinition: to clarify the background behind something mentioned in a conversation

examples.en: My teammate paused to explain the reference before finishing the story.
examples.zh: 队友停下来「解释提到的典故」，然后才讲完故事。

examples.en: I asked my roommate to explain the reference to an old television show.
examples.zh: 我请室友「解释她提到的那部老电视节目的典故」。

collocations: ask someone to explain the reference
take a moment to explain the reference
explain the reference to a song

words.enDefinition: room at a meal for one person beyond the expected group

examples.en: My tutor said there was an extra seat at the table if I was staying in town.
examples.zh: 老师说，如果我留在镇上，「餐桌上还有个额外座位」可以给我。

examples.en: Our host arranged an extra seat at the table when my roommate asked to come too.
examples.zh: 室友问能不能也来时，做东的人在「餐桌上加了一个座位」。

collocations: offer an extra seat at the table
find an extra seat at the table
arrange an extra seat at the table

words.enDefinition: colouring applied to the skin for decoration or a costume

examples.en: I used blue face paint to match the sleeves of my costume.
examples.zh: 我用了蓝色的「面部彩绘颜料」，和化装服的袖子相配。

examples.en: She borrowed some face paint to draw spots on her own cheeks.
examples.zh: 她借了点「面部彩绘颜料」，在自己脸颊上画斑点。

words.enDefinition: A red inscription bearing New Year wishes, known as fai chun in Cantonese.

examples.en: We saw a display of fai chun written by Hong Kong students in the library.
examples.zh: 我们在图书馆看见香港同学书写的「挥春」展品。

examples.en: My classmate explained the wishes on the fai chun in her family's holiday photograph.
examples.zh: 同学给我解释了她家节日照片里「挥春」上的祝福。

collocations: display fai chun at the door

words.enDefinition: an area where a fair with stalls, games, or rides takes place

examples.en: The bus stopped near the fairground where we planned to meet our classmates.
examples.zh: 公交停在「游艺集市场地」附近，我们计划在那里和同学碰头。

examples.en: I could hear music from the fairground while walking to my summer job.
examples.zh: 我走去暑期打工的地方时，能听到「游艺集市场地」传来的音乐。

words.enDefinition: short games at a fair where people try to win prizes or have fun

examples.en: We tried two fairground games before my friend's little brother wanted to go home.
examples.zh: 朋友的小弟弟想回家前，我们玩了两个「游艺集市小游戏」。

examples.en: The fairground games were set up behind the tents where food was sold.
examples.zh: 「游艺集市小游戏」设在卖食物的帐篷后面。

words.enDefinition: a moving amusement attraction people ride at a fair

examples.en: We watched our friends try a fairground ride before looking for the picnic area.
examples.zh: 我们先看朋友玩了一个「游乐设施」，才去找野餐区。

examples.en: The programme showed a height limit for each fairground ride beside its picture.
examples.zh: 节目册在每张图片旁标出了对应「游乐设施」的身高限制。

collocations: height limit for a fairground ride

words.enDefinition: decorative material made to look like webs spun by spiders

examples.en: We hung fake cobwebs over the bookshelf before our Halloween film night.
examples.zh: 万圣节电影之夜前，我们在书架上方挂了「假蜘蛛网」。

examples.en: Someone left fake cobwebs on the common room windows after the party.
examples.zh: 聚会结束后，有人把「假蜘蛛网」留在了公共休息室的窗上。

collocations: cover a doorway with fake cobwebs

words.enDefinition: a short pause in university classes during the autumn term

examples.en: I stayed in town over fall break and explored the nearby trails.
examples.zh: 「秋季假期」我留在镇上，去附近的步道逛了逛。

examples.en: Our fall break was short, so my neighbour took a day trip.
examples.zh: 我们的「秋季假期」很短，所以邻居就出门玩了一天。

collocations: stay on campus over fall break

words.enDefinition: an event celebrating autumn with seasonal activities or local goods

examples.en: The fall festival on our campus had live music and a pumpkin display.
examples.zh: 校园的「秋季庆典」有现场音乐，还展出了南瓜。

examples.en: We bought tickets for the fall festival near my roommate's hometown.
examples.zh: 我们买了室友老家附近「秋季庆典」的门票。

words.enDefinition: the leaves that change colour and create autumn scenery

examples.en: We took the train north to see the fall foliage along the river.
examples.zh: 我们坐火车往北走，去看河边的「秋叶景色」。

examples.en: The residence newsletter suggested a hike with good views of fall foliage.
examples.zh: 宿舍简报推荐了一条能看到好看「秋叶景色」的徒步路线。

words.enDefinition: to begin to feel strong romantic affection for someone

examples.en: I never expected to fall for someone during my first summer away from home.
examples.zh: 我没想到第一次离家过暑假时会「爱上某人」。

examples.en: It's possible to fall for someone after knowing them as a friend for years.
examples.zh: 认识多年的朋友也有可能让你「爱上对方」。

words.enDefinition: to stop feeling romantic love for someone you previously loved

examples.en: I never thought we would fall out of love while living in the same city.
examples.zh: 我从没想到，我们住在同一座城市也会「渐渐不再爱了」。

examples.en: People sometimes fall out of love without either person doing anything particularly wrong.
examples.zh: 有时双方都没有做错什么，还是会「渐渐不再爱了」。

collocations: begin to fall out of love
fall out of love with someone

words.enDefinition: a ring of seasonal materials used as an autumn decoration

examples.en: Our hall made a fall wreath out of dried leaves and ribbon.
examples.zh: 我们宿舍楼用干叶子和丝带做了一个「秋季装饰花环」。

examples.en: I saw an orange fall wreath on the door of my friend's house.
examples.zh: 我在朋友家门上看见一个橙色的「秋季装饰花环」。

words.enDefinition: a quarrel that makes an established relationship unfriendly

examples.en: Their falling-out started over a small misunderstanding after the group moved flats.
examples.zh: 那群人搬家后，一点小误会让他们「闹翻」了。

examples.en: They had a falling-out early that year but still shared several friends on campus.
examples.zh: 那年年初他们「闹翻」了，但在校园里还有几个共同的朋友。

words.enDefinition: someone you recognise from having seen them before

examples.en: The person by the coffee machine was the only familiar face there.
examples.zh: 咖啡机旁边那个人是现场唯一一个我「眼熟的人」。

examples.en: I spotted a familiar face as I walked into the crowded common room.
examples.zh: 我走进挤满人的公共休息室，看到了一个「眼熟的人」。

collocations: see a familiar face in the crowd

words.enDefinition: an event with informal activities intended for families of different ages

examples.en: I volunteered at the family fun day in the park next to the library.
examples.zh: 我在图书馆旁公园举行的「家庭趣味活动日」做了志愿者。

examples.en: The family fun day offered short games and music at the community centre on Saturday.
examples.zh: 周六的「家庭趣味活动日」在社区中心安排了小游戏和音乐。

words.enDefinition: a custom shared and maintained within a particular family

examples.en: Making a photo album each year is a family tradition for my roommate.
examples.zh: 室友每年做一本相册，那是他们的「家庭传统」。

examples.en: We wrote down one family tradition each for the class display board.
examples.zh: 我们每人写下一项「家庭传统」，展示在班级展板上。

collocations: a family tradition passed down over time

words.enDefinition: a designated area with facilities or activities intended for families at an event

examples.en: The festival volunteers showed me the family zone near the shaded picnic tables.
examples.zh: 节庆志愿者给我指了荫凉野餐桌旁的「亲子活动区」。

examples.en: My neighbour waited in the family zone while her children finished making paper flowers.
examples.zh: 邻居在「亲子活动区」等孩子们做完纸花。

words.enDefinition: to feel romantically attracted to someone, especially in informal British English

examples.en: I didn't expect to fancy someone from my course after spending so much time together.
examples.zh: 相处这么长时间后，我没想到会「对同一门课的人有好感」。

examples.en: My flatmate joked that you can fancy someone before learning their name or course.
examples.zh: 室友开玩笑说，还不知道名字或专业，也可能「对一个人有好感」。

words.enDefinition: a written or spoken message wishing someone well as they leave

examples.en: We recorded a farewell message for a friend who couldn't attend our dinner.
examples.zh: 我们为没法来聚餐的朋友录了一段「告别留言」。

examples.en: My classmate left a farewell message in the notebook we'd been sharing all year.
examples.zh: 同学在那本我们共用了一整年的笔记本里留了段「告别留言」。

words.enDefinition: a gathering held to say goodbye to someone who is leaving

examples.en: We organized a farewell party for our flatmate before her flight back home.
examples.zh: 室友乘机回家前，我们为她安排了一场「送别聚会」。

examples.en: My old study group met for a farewell party in the common room.
examples.zh: 我原来的学习小组在公共休息室办了一场「送别聚会」。

words.enDefinition: a day honouring fathers and other paternal figures

examples.en: My brother and I planned a video call for Father's Day while I studied abroad.
examples.zh: 我在国外读书时，和哥哥约好「父亲节」打视频电话。

examples.en: The community café advertised a family lunch for Father's Day near the park.
examples.zh: 公园附近的社区咖啡馆宣传「父亲节」有家庭午餐活动。

words.enDefinition: a holiday recognized by the US federal government

examples.en: The student handbook listed the federal holiday alongside the campus's own scheduled break.
examples.zh: 学生手册把「美国联邦假日」与学校自己安排的假期都列了出来。

examples.en: We checked whether the local office would open on the federal holiday next week.
examples.zh: 我们查了当地办事处下周「美国联邦假日」那天会不会开门。

words.enDefinition: to feel comfortable and free from worry in a situation

examples.en: It helped me feel at ease when she said she was also new.
examples.zh: 她说自己也是新来的，我就「觉得自在」多了。

examples.en: I began to feel at ease once we found a topic we both liked.
examples.zh: 找到双方都喜欢的话题之后，我开始「觉得自在」了。

words.enDefinition: to feel pressured between people who are disagreeing with each other

examples.en: I began to feel caught in the middle when both friends wanted my opinion.
examples.zh: 两个朋友都问我的看法，我开始「觉得夹在双方中间」。

examples.en: She told me it's easy to feel caught in the middle when flatmates argue.
examples.zh: 她跟我说，室友吵架时很容易「觉得夹在双方中间」。

collocations: start to feel caught in the middle
often feel caught in the middle
try not to feel caught in the middle

words.expression: feel free to use the kitchen
words.lemma: feel free to use the kitchen
words.enDefinition: gives a guest permission to use the host's kitchen
acceptedEnVariants: feel free to use the kitchen

examples.en: Feel free to use the kitchen if you get back later than us this evening.
examples.zh: 今晚如果你回来得比我们晚，「厨房可以随便用」。

examples.en: My neighbour said, "Feel free to use the kitchen," and showed me where she kept the mugs.
examples.zh: 邻居说：「厨房可以随便用」，还告诉我她平时把杯子放在哪儿。

collocations: please feel free to use the kitchen
feel free to use the kitchen in the morning
tell guests to feel free to use the kitchen

words.enDefinition: to feel that others are treating you as part of their group

examples.en: They asked what I thought, and that helped me feel included.
examples.zh: 他们问我怎么看，这让我「感到被接纳」。

examples.en: It's easier to feel included when people remember your name and face.
examples.zh: 别人记得你的名字和长相时，你更容易「感到被接纳」。

words.enDefinition: to feel that others acknowledge who you are or what you experience

examples.en: Hearing a story like mine helped me feel seen at the gathering.
examples.zh: 聚会上有人讲的经历跟我的类似，让我「觉得自己被看见」。

examples.en: My classmate said she began to feel seen when our group mentioned her language.
examples.zh: 同学说，小组提到她使用的语言时，她开始「觉得自己被看见」。

words.zhGloss: 在两个选择间左右为难
words.enDefinition: to have conflicting feelings about two people, places or choices
acceptedZhAnswers: 在两个选择间左右为难

examples.en: I sometimes feel torn between spending breaks here and going back home.
examples.zh: 放假的时候，我有时在留在这边和回老家之间「左右为难」。

examples.en: I started to feel torn between keeping my old routines and trying new ones.
examples.zh: 我开始在沿用以前的生活习惯和尝试新习惯之间「左右为难」。

collocations: feel torn between two ways of doing things

words.enDefinition: someone who attends the same school or university as you

examples.en: A fellow student helped me find the room for my first seminar.
examples.zh: 一位「同校学生」帮我找到了第一堂研讨课的教室。

examples.en: I met a fellow student who lived in the building across from mine.
examples.zh: 我认识了一位「同校学生」，住在我那栋楼对面。

words.enDefinition: a person attending a public festival

examples.en: A festival-goer asked whether we knew where the second entrance to the park was.
examples.zh: 一名「节庆活动参加者」问我们知不知道公园的第二个入口在哪儿。

examples.en: I met another festival-goer from my university while waiting for the evening bus.
examples.zh: 等晚间公交时，我遇到另一位同校的「节庆活动参加者」。

words.enDefinition: the area set aside for a festival and its activities

examples.en: We reached the festival grounds by walking through the park behind our residence.
examples.zh: 我们穿过宿舍后面的公园，到达了「节庆会场区域」。

examples.en: The map of the festival grounds showed a quiet area near the far entrance.
examples.zh: 「节庆会场区域」的地图标出了靠远端入口的一处安静区域。

words.enDefinition: a schedule listing a festival's events, times, and locations

examples.en: I checked the festival programme to see which performance followed the outdoor dance show.
examples.zh: 我查看了「节庆活动节目单」，想知道户外舞蹈后面是哪场演出。

examples.en: The festival programme included a short introduction to each of the student groups performing.
examples.zh: 「节庆活动节目单」简要介绍了每个登台的学生团体。

words.enDefinition: an unpaid person who helps carry out work at a festival

examples.en: A festival volunteer handed me a map at the entrance to the garden.
examples.zh: 在花园入口，一位「节庆志愿者」给了我一张地图。

examples.en: My flatmate worked as a festival volunteer during the weekend after our exams.
examples.zh: 考试结束后的那个周末，室友去做了「节庆志愿者」。

collocations: sign up as a festival volunteer

words.enDefinition: a wristband used to show a person has entry to a festival

examples.en: The volunteer checked my festival wristband when I returned from the bus station.
examples.zh: 我从车站回来时，志愿者检查了我的「节庆入场腕带」。

examples.en: I kept my festival wristband in a notebook after the summer market ended.
examples.zh: 夏季集市结束后，我把「节庆入场腕带」放进了笔记本留作纪念。

words.enDefinition: strings of small flags used as decoration for a celebration

examples.en: The organisers hung festive bunting between the stalls before the market opened on Sunday.
examples.zh: 周日集市开门前，组织者在摊位之间挂上了「节庆挂旗」。

examples.en: My flatmate helped take down the festive bunting after the street party had ended.
examples.zh: 街头联欢结束后，室友帮忙拆下了「节庆挂旗」。

words.enDefinition: to discover ordinary things that feel reassuring in a new setting

examples.en: I could find familiar comforts at the market, including snacks my aunt used to buy.
examples.zh: 在市场上我能「找到熟悉的慰藉」，包括姨妈以前常买的小吃。

examples.en: Our first shared meal helped me find familiar comforts in the unfamiliar kitchen.
examples.zh: 第一次一起做饭，帮我在陌生的厨房里「找到了熟悉的慰藉」。

collocations: look around to find familiar comforts
be glad to find familiar comforts
find familiar comforts in a new city

words.enDefinition: Asks someone to meet or locate the speaker once a performance finishes.

examples.en: Find me after the show and we can get coffee near the bus stop.
examples.zh: 「演出结束后来找我」，咱们可以去公交站附近喝咖啡。

examples.en: I wrote “Find me after the show” on the note I left with Maya.
examples.zh: 我给玛雅留的纸条上写着「演出结束后来找我」。

collocations: tell them to find me after the show
please find me after the show
say find me after the show

words.enDefinition: to become comfortable and confident in a new situation

examples.en: It can take a few weeks to find your feet in a new city.
examples.zh: 在一个新城市「逐渐适应下来」可能要花几周。

examples.en: She said meeting people helps you find your feet in your first term.
examples.zh: 她说，结识一些人有助于你在第一学期「逐渐适应下来」。

collocations: take time to find your feet

words.enDefinition: to meet people who accept you and share your interests

examples.en: It takes time to find your people when you're new to campus.
examples.zh: 刚来学校时，要花点时间才能「找到志趣相投的人」。

examples.en: The art society might be where you find your people this term.
examples.zh: 这学期你也许会在美术社「找到志趣相投的人」。

collocations: take time to find your people

words.enDefinition: to speak the remaining words before the other person has finished

examples.en: I sometimes rush to finish someone's sentence when I think I know the answer.
examples.zh: 有时我以为知道答案，就「抢着替人把话说完」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked us not to finish someone's sentence during the group exercise.
examples.zh: 导师请我们在小组练习时别「抢着替人把话说完」。

collocations: try not to finish someone's sentence
resist the urge to finish someone's sentence

words.enDefinition: an organized show of fireworks for people to watch

examples.en: We watched the fireworks display from the grass behind the community centre that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚我们在社区中心后面的草地上观看了「烟花表演」。

examples.en: The town moved the fireworks display to Saturday because rain was expected on Friday.
examples.zh: 预计周五有雨，镇上把「烟花表演」改到了周六。

words.enDefinition: the final part of a fireworks show, usually its most impressive section

examples.en: We stayed by the river long enough to see the fireworks finale together.
examples.zh: 我们一起在河边等到看完「烟花表演的压轴」。

examples.en: The programme listed a fireworks finale after the last song by the local band.
examples.zh: 节目单写着，本地乐队演完最后一首歌后是「烟花表演的压轴」。

words.enDefinition: the first romantic meeting between two people

examples.en: Our first date was at the little café opposite the campus bookshop last spring.
examples.zh: 去年春天，我们的「第一次约会」是在校园书店对面的小咖啡馆。

examples.en: She suggested a walk for their first date because both of them liked being outdoors.
examples.zh: 她建议两人的「第一次约会」去散步，因为他们都喜欢户外。

words.enDefinition: anxiety or uneasiness before or during a first romantic date

examples.en: My first-date nerves faded once we started talking about films near the library.
examples.zh: 在图书馆旁聊起电影后，我「第一次约会时的紧张」渐渐消失了。

examples.en: She went for a walk beforehand to settle her first-date nerves that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，她事先散了会儿步，缓解「第一次约会时的紧张」。

words.enDefinition: A Scottish New Year custom centered on the first visitor to a home after midnight.

examples.en: A Scottish neighbor explained first-footing while showing us photos from her family's New Year gathering.
examples.zh: 一位苏格兰邻居一边给我们看她家新年聚会的照片，一边介绍「苏格兰新年首访习俗」。

examples.en: We read about first-footing in a booklet at the community center's winter traditions display.
examples.zh: 我们在社区中心的冬季习俗展上，从一本小册子里读到了「苏格兰新年首访习俗」。

words.enDefinition: the first occurrence of frost in autumn in a particular place

examples.en: Our garden group took pictures of the first frost before class.
examples.zh: 上课前，我们园艺小组拍了「初霜」的照片。

examples.en: The first frost arrived while the pumpkins were still on our porch.
examples.zh: 降「初霜」的时候，南瓜还摆在我们的门廊上。

words.enDefinition: indicating that a person has never visited a place before

examples.en: It's my first time here, so I don't know where everyone usually sits.
examples.zh: 我「第一次来这里」，还不知道大家通常坐哪儿。

examples.en: I told the person beside me that it was my first time here.
examples.zh: 我告诉旁边的人，这是我「第一次来这里」。

collocations: realise it is someone's first time here
ask if it's their first time here

words.enDefinition: a small light made to resemble a candle without a flame

examples.en: I put a flameless candle inside the pumpkin that sat in my window.
examples.zh: 我在窗台上的南瓜里放了一支「无焰蜡烛」。

examples.en: The desk handed out a flameless candle to each student who painted a pumpkin.
examples.zh: 服务台给每位画南瓜的同学都发了一支「无焰蜡烛」。

words.enDefinition: to act playfully in a way that suggests romantic interest

examples.en: He used to flirt with her by making silly jokes during our coffee breaks.
examples.zh: 我们课间喝咖啡时，他以前总爱逗她，跟她「调情」。

examples.en: I couldn't tell whether she meant to flirt or was just being friendly.
examples.zh: 我分不清她是有意「调情」，还是单纯友好。

words.enDefinition: playfully showing that you may be romantically interested in someone

examples.en: His message sounded flirty to me, but my roommate read it differently.
examples.zh: 我觉得他的消息「带有调情意味」，室友却有不同的理解。

examples.en: They exchanged flirty jokes while waiting for the outdoor film to start that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚等露天电影开场时，他们互相开了些「带有调情意味」的玩笑。

words.enDefinition: a circular arrangement of flowers worn on the head

examples.en: A friend made a flower crown at the craft stall for her sister.
examples.zh: 朋友在手工摊位上为姐姐做了一个「花环头饰」。

examples.en: She wore a flower crown in the photograph from the spring celebration beside campus.
examples.zh: 校园旁的春季庆典照片里，她戴着一个「花环头饰」。

words.enDefinition: a prediction of where and when autumn leaves will change colour

examples.en: We checked the foliage forecast before choosing which park to visit.
examples.zh: 选去哪座公园之前，我们看了看「秋叶观赏预报」。

examples.en: The foliage forecast mentioned two nearby trails where leaves were already changing.
examples.zh: 「秋叶观赏预报」提到，附近有两条步道的树叶已经开始变色了。

words.enDefinition: to take another person's example as a guide for your actions

examples.en: It's fine to follow someone's lead when you're unsure which seats are reserved.
examples.zh: 拿不准哪些座位被预留了，可以先「照着别人的做法来」。

examples.en: I thought I'd follow someone's lead instead of guessing where to put my coat.
examples.zh: 我想「照着别人的做法来」，不自己猜外套该放哪儿。

collocations: be ready to follow someone's lead

words.enDefinition: to continue the practice that has personal or family meaning for you

examples.en: The host explained that you could follow your own tradition at this gathering.
examples.zh: 主持人解释说，在这次聚会上可以「按自己的传统来」。

examples.en: Our club said, “Follow your own tradition if you want to mark the occasion.”
examples.zh: 社团说「想纪念这一天的话，可以按自己的传统来」。

collocations: choose to follow your own tradition
be welcome to follow your own tradition
continue to follow your own tradition

words.enDefinition: an event bringing several mobile food trucks together at one location

examples.en: We went to a food truck rally after the outdoor concert behind the library.
examples.zh: 图书馆后面的户外音乐会结束后，我们去了一场「餐车集会」。

examples.en: The food truck rally had picnic tables where we could sit with other students.
examples.zh: 「餐车集会」摆了野餐桌，方便我们和其他学生坐在一起。

words.enDefinition: done to remember or enjoy something associated with a shared past

examples.en: We ordered our old favourite snack for old times' sake after the campus tour.
examples.zh: 参观完校园后，我们点了以前最喜欢的小吃，「为了重温旧日时光」。

examples.en: I suggested sitting in the old study room for old times' sake before leaving.
examples.zh: 离开前，我建议去老自习室坐一坐，「为了重温旧日时光」。

collocations: do something for old times' sake
go back for old times' sake

words.enDefinition: an uncommon clover with four leaflets, widely regarded as a sign of good luck

examples.en: My classmate found a four-leaf clover beside the path on our walk to campus.
examples.zh: 我们走去学校时，同学在路边发现了一株「四叶草」。

examples.en: She pressed the four-leaf clover inside a notebook to keep it from getting crushed.
examples.zh: 她把「四叶草」夹在笔记本里，免得弄坏。

words.enDefinition: a set of experiences or ideas used to interpret something

examples.en: Her example came from a frame of reference I didn't share yet.
examples.zh: 她的例子来自一种我还不熟悉的「理解问题的参照框架」。

examples.en: The same event made sense once I understood my friend's frame of reference.
examples.zh: 弄懂朋友「理解问题的参照框架」后，我才明白同一件事为何在她看来很合理。

words.enDefinition: a student who has just started university in Britain

examples.en: As a fresher in York, I knew nobody in my building.
examples.zh: 我刚在约克上大学，是个「大学新生」，同楼的人一个都不认识。

examples.en: A fresher from Wales helped me find the welcome lunch in Bristol.
examples.zh: 一位来自威尔士的「大学新生」帮我在布里斯托找到了迎新午餐的地点。

words.enDefinition: the patterns in how members of a group of friends interact

examples.en: The move changed our friend group dynamics because two of us lived farther apart.
examples.zh: 搬家改变了「朋友圈里的相处模式」，因为我们中有两个人住远了。

examples.en: She noticed different friend group dynamics after several classmates joined the weekly club meeting.
examples.zh: 几个同学开始参加每周的社团聚会后，她注意到「朋友圈里的相处模式」变了。

collocations: notice changes in friend group dynamics

words.enDefinition: a person whose presence makes a place feel more welcoming

examples.en: There was a friendly face near the door when I arrived alone.
examples.zh: 我一个人到场时，门边有个「让人感到亲切的人」。

examples.en: After a difficult first morning, I was glad to see a friendly face.
examples.zh: 第一天上午不太顺利，见到一个「让人感到亲切的人」，我很开心。

collocations: offer a friendly face to newcomers

words.enDefinition: a small movement of the head used as a warm greeting

examples.en: She gave me a friendly nod when I walked past her table.
examples.zh: 我从她那桌旁经过时，她「友好地点了点头」。

examples.en: I responded with a friendly nod because the speaker had already started.
examples.zh: 主讲人已经开始讲话，我就「友好地点头」回应。

collocations: acknowledge someone with a friendly nod

words.enDefinition: friends who live in places with different local times

examples.en: My friends across time zones agreed on a call before our classes started again.
examples.zh: 我和「身处不同时区的朋友」约好开课前打一次电话。

examples.en: It took a while to find a regular meeting time for friends across time zones.
examples.zh: 给「身处不同时区的朋友」找到固定碰面的时间花了好一阵。

collocations: stay close to friends across time zones
make time for friends across time zones

words.enDefinition: friends from the place where someone lived before moving away

examples.en: I called my friends from back home the evening before my first university lecture.
examples.zh: 大学第一节课前一晚，我给「老家的朋友们」打了电话。

examples.en: My friends from back home kept asking to see pictures of the new city.
examples.zh: 「老家的朋友们」一直让我发新城市的照片给他们看。

collocations: hear from friends from back home

words.enDefinition: a Thanksgiving-style meal or celebration shared among friends

examples.en: We held Friendsgiving because several roommates were staying in town.
examples.zh: 因为好几个室友留在镇上，我们办了场「朋友感恩节聚餐」。

examples.en: The international student club invited everyone to Friendsgiving in the lounge.
examples.zh: 国际学生社团邀请大家到休息室参加「朋友感恩节聚餐」。

words.enDefinition: a bracelet given or exchanged as a symbol of friendship

examples.en: My former flatmate sent me a friendship bracelet after she moved abroad to study.
examples.zh: 以前的室友出国读书后，寄给我一条「友谊手链」。

examples.en: I found our friendship bracelet while looking through photos from my first year.
examples.zh: 翻看大一照片时，我找到了我们那条「友谊手链」。

words.enDefinition: the ending of a close friendship, sometimes as a deliberate choice

examples.en: She found the friendship breakup harder to explain than moving to a different campus.
examples.zh: 她觉得「友情破裂」比转到另一个校区更难向别人解释。

examples.en: A friendship breakup changed who I talked to after our weekly seminar that year.
examples.zh: 那年一次「友情破裂」改变了我每周研讨课下课后会和谁聊天。

words.zhGloss: 朋友之间固定的小习惯
words.enDefinition: a small, repeated practice that a group of friends uses to stay connected
acceptedZhAnswers: 朋友之间固定的小习惯

examples.en: Our last coffee before each term break became a friendship ritual that everyone looked forward to.
examples.zh: 每次放假前喝最后一杯咖啡，成了大家盼着做的「朋友之间固定的小习惯」。

examples.en: Sending a photo from the station became a friendship ritual on our way home.
examples.zh: 每次回家路上从车站互发照片，成了「朋友之间固定的小习惯」。

words.enDefinition: indicates a gift is being given jointly by several people

examples.en: This is from all of us, since everyone wanted to thank you for hosting.
examples.zh: 这是「我们大家一起送的」，大家都想谢谢你的招待。

examples.en: The note said the book was from all of us, including my absent roommate.
examples.zh: 留言写着，那本书是「我们大家一起送的」，没到场的室友也有份。

collocations: a little something from all of us
say it's from all of us
a present from all of us

words.enDefinition: an amusing or unexpected detail about you to share with others

examples.en: The worksheet asked you to include a fun fact about yourself alongside your name.
examples.zh: 练习纸要求你在姓名旁写「关于自己的一件趣事」。

examples.en: It's hard to think of a fun fact about yourself when everyone is listening.
examples.zh: 大家都在听的时候，很难想出「关于自己的一件趣事」。

collocations: share a fun fact about yourself
think of a fun fact about yourself
tell us a fun fact about yourself

words.enDefinition: to come together beside a table, usually to share a meal

examples.en: We usually gather around the table only after everyone has arrived for the holiday.
examples.zh: 我们一般等过节的人到齐了，才「围坐到餐桌旁」。

examples.en: Our hosts asked us to gather around the table before they brought out dessert.
examples.zh: 主人请我们先「围坐到餐桌旁」，他们再端出甜点。

collocations: ask everyone to gather around the table
gather around the table for dinner
wait for friends to gather around the table

words.enDefinition: to draw a broad conclusion based on one case alone

examples.en: The tutor asked us not to generalise from one example about family traditions.
examples.zh: 导师请我们别根据一个家庭传统的例子「以偏概全」。

examples.en: I tried not to generalise from one example in our campus interviews.
examples.zh: 我尽量不从校园访谈的一个例子「以偏概全」。

collocations: be careful not to generalise from one example
easy to generalise from one example

words.expression: get a rough idea of numbers
words.lemma: get a rough idea of numbers
words.enDefinition: To find out approximately how many people are likely to come to an event.
acceptedEnVariants: get a rough idea of numbers

examples.en: We need to get a rough idea of numbers before choosing which courtyard to use.
examples.zh: 选在哪个庭院之前，我们得先「估一下人数」。

examples.en: I started a poll to get a rough idea of numbers for Friday's drawing session.
examples.zh: 我发起了投票，为星期五的绘画活动「估一下人数」。

collocations: try to get a rough idea of numbers
get a rough idea of numbers for the picnic
ask around to get a rough idea of numbers

words.enDefinition: to find a chance to speak while others are talking

examples.en: Everyone was talking at once, so it was hard to get a word in.
examples.zh: 大家同时开口，很难「插得上话」。

examples.en: I finally managed to get a word in when they stopped to check the map.
examples.zh: 他们停下来查看地图时，我终于「插得上话」了。

collocations: hard to get a word in
let someone get a word in

words.enDefinition: to meet and learn basic things about each other

examples.en: We had a few minutes to get acquainted before our first workshop.
examples.zh: 第一场实训开始前，我们有几分钟「互相认识」。

examples.en: The walking tour helped the new students get acquainted with each other.
examples.zh: 步行参观帮新同学们「开始互相认识」。

collocations: use an activity to get acquainted

words.enDefinition: to contact someone again after a period without communication

examples.en: We decided to get back in touch after realising we lived in the same city.
examples.zh: 发现住在同一座城后，我们决定「重新联系上」。

examples.en: An old classmate wanted to get back in touch after seeing a graduation photograph.
examples.zh: 一位老同学看到毕业照后想「重新联系上」。

collocations: try to get back in touch
decide to get back in touch
get back in touch with someone

words.enDefinition: to become a couple again after a romantic breakup

examples.en: They decided to get back together after spending the summer in different places.
examples.zh: 在不同地方过完暑假后，两人决定「复合」。

examples.en: I didn't expect them to get back together when they returned for their final year.
examples.zh: 我没想到他们回来读最后一学年时会「复合」。

words.enDefinition: to begin talking informally, often without planning to

examples.en: We started comparing our schedules and managed to get chatting before the session.
examples.zh: 我们先是对了对课表，活动开始前就「聊起来」了。

examples.en: It's easy to get chatting with people while waiting outside the seminar room.
examples.zh: 在研讨课的教室外等候时，很容易和人「聊起来」。

words.enDefinition: to start feeling relaxed when a particular person is nearby

examples.en: It can take a while to get comfortable around someone after a shy introduction.
examples.zh: 拘谨地互相介绍之后，可能要过一阵子才能「和对方相处得自在」。

examples.en: One good conversation helped me get comfortable around someone I had found hard to approach.
examples.zh: 那人一开始让我觉得不好接近，好好聊过一次后，我就能「和对方相处得更自在」了。

collocations: take time to get comfortable around someone
start to get comfortable around someone
manage to get comfortable around someone

words.enDefinition: to stop feeling upset about a person after a relationship or interest ends

examples.en: It took a while to get over someone I still saw in class every week.
examples.zh: 我每周上课还会见到对方，花了好一阵才「走出那段感情」。

examples.en: My friend said it was harder to get over someone when all their friends overlapped.
examples.zh: 朋友说，两人的朋友都是同一拨人时，更难「走出对某人的感情」。

collocations: take time to get over someone

words.enDefinition: to begin treating a romantic relationship as more committed

examples.en: They didn't plan to get serious until they knew where they'd be living in summer.
examples.zh: 在弄清楚暑假会住哪里之前，他们没打算「开始认真交往」。

examples.en: I asked what would change if we chose to get serious after the semester.
examples.zh: 我问如果学期结束后决定「开始认真交往」，会有哪些变化。

words.enDefinition: to make someone notice you so that you can communicate

examples.en: We discussed how to get someone's attention without interrupting the speaker at the front.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了怎样「引起别人的注意」而不打断台上的发言者。

examples.en: The volunteer explained how to get someone's attention without speaking across the room.
examples.zh: 志愿者解释了怎么不隔着房间喊，就能「引起某人的注意」。

words.enDefinition: a present meant to cheer up someone who is ill

examples.en: We left a get-well gift with my friend's family during our visit.
examples.zh: 去看朋友时，我们给朋友家人留了一份「慰问病人的礼物」。

examples.en: My classmate sent a get-well gift when I missed class that week.
examples.zh: 那周我没去上课，同学寄来一份「慰问病人的礼物」。

words.enDefinition: a frightening story about a ghost or other unexplained events

examples.en: Our roommate told a ghost story about the oldest building on campus.
examples.zh: 室友讲了个校园里最老那栋楼的「鬼故事」。

examples.en: Nobody could finish the ghost story without laughing at the sound effects.
examples.zh: 音效太搞笑了，谁都没法忍住笑把「鬼故事」讲完。

words.enDefinition: suddenly stopping all communication with someone without explaining why

examples.en: My friend thought it was ghosting when the conversation stopped immediately after their date.
examples.zh: 两人约完后对话突然中断，朋友觉得对方是「突然断联」了。

examples.en: They talked about ghosting when someone in the group mentioned a date that went quiet.
examples.zh: 小组里有人提到约会对象忽然没了消息，大家便聊起「突然断联」。

words.enDefinition: the amount of money someone sets aside to spend on presents

examples.en: We set a gift budget before choosing anything for our host.
examples.zh: 给主人挑东西之前，我们先定了「送礼预算」。

examples.en: My friend said she could not go over her gift budget that month.
examples.zh: 朋友说，她那个月不能超出自己的「送礼预算」。

words.enDefinition: a present carried from the place you consider your home

examples.en: My host smiled when I handed her a gift from home after dinner.
examples.zh: 饭后，我把「从家乡带来的礼物」递给主人，她笑了。

examples.en: I brought a gift from home for the flatmate who picked me up.
examples.zh: 我给来接我的室友带了份「从家乡带来的礼物」。

collocations: give someone a gift from home

words.enDefinition: a collection of gifts arranged together in a basket or box

examples.en: My friends put together a gift hamper with tea and local jam.
examples.zh: 朋友们做了个「礼篮」，里面放了茶和本地果酱。

examples.en: The gift hamper arrived while my cousin was away visiting her family.
examples.zh: 表姐回家探亲的时候，「礼篮」送到了。

words.enDefinition: a list of requested gifts shared with people attending an event

examples.en: I checked their gift registry before choosing a present for the wedding.
examples.zh: 我先看了他们的「礼品登记清单」，再挑结婚礼物。

examples.en: Our friends had a small gift registry for people who asked what they needed.
examples.zh: 我们朋友准备了一份简短的「礼品登记清单」，给问他们缺什么的人看。

words.enDefinition: A small model house made from gingerbread and decorated with icing or sweets.

examples.en: The residents decorated a gingerbread house with white icing at the winter craft session.
examples.zh: 冬季手工活动中，住户们用白色糖霜装饰了一个「姜饼屋」。

examples.en: Our department displayed a gingerbread house made by students beside the reception desk in December.
examples.zh: 十二月，我们院系在接待处旁展出了同学们做的一个「姜饼屋」。

words.enDefinition: to say goodbye to someone in a friendly or celebratory way as they leave

examples.en: Our study group met to give a warm send-off to two exchange students.
examples.zh: 我们学习小组碰面「热情送别」两名交换生。

examples.en: The club planned to give a warm send-off to its graduating members that evening.
examples.zh: 社团打算那晚给即将毕业的成员「热情送行」。

collocations: give a warm send-off to friends
gather to give a warm send-off
plan to give a warm send-off

words.enDefinition: to name the creator when passing their work on to others

examples.en: We agreed to give credit when sharing the diagrams made by other students.
examples.zh: 我们约好，分享其他同学做的图示时要「注明出处」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to give credit when sharing anyone else's photos.
examples.zh: 导师请我们在分享别人拍的照片时「注明出处」。

collocations: remember to give credit when sharing
ask members to give credit when sharing

words.enDefinition: an informal invitation to contact you when the other person wants or needs to

examples.en: “Give me a shout when you're back on campus,” my friend said on Sunday.
examples.zh: 周日朋友说：“回到校园后「联系我一声」。”

examples.en: “Give me a shout if you need help with the move next weekend.”
examples.zh: “下周末搬家需要帮忙的话，「就联系我」。”

collocations: give me a shout if you need help
give me a shout when you're free

words.enDefinition: to pass on a polite greeting from the speaker to someone else

examples.en: “Please give my regards to your parents,” I said after our campus tour.
examples.zh: 参观完校园后，我说：“请「代我问候」你的父母。”

examples.en: I asked her to give my regards to the classmates I had not seen.
examples.zh: 我请她「代我问候」那些我还没见到的同学。

collocations: give my regards to your family

words.enDefinition: to hand sweets to children or visitors at an event

examples.en: I volunteered to give out candy while my housemates decorated the porch.
examples.zh: 室友们装饰门廊时，我自告奋勇去「分发糖果」。

examples.en: Families who wanted to give out candy set chairs by their doors.
examples.zh: 想「分发糖果」的人家把椅子放到了门边。

collocations: give out candy at the door

words.enDefinition: to let someone try again after a mistake or disappointment

examples.en: It can be hard to give someone a second chance after a broken promise.
examples.zh: 承诺被违背后，要「再给对方一次机会」并不容易。

examples.en: She felt ready to give someone a second chance after hearing both accounts.
examples.zh: 听了双方的说法后，她愿意「再给对方一次机会」。

collocations: decide to give someone a second chance
be willing to give someone a second chance
choose to give someone a second chance

words.enDefinition: to greet a person by moving your raised hand

examples.en: There was just time to give someone a wave before the next talk began.
examples.zh: 下一场讲座快开始了，只来得及「朝别人挥手打个招呼」。

examples.en: I try to give someone a wave if I recognise them in the crowd.
examples.zh: 在人群里认出对方，我会尽量「朝对方挥手打个招呼」。

collocations: remember to give someone a wave
give someone a wave across the hall
give someone a wave from the doorway

words.enDefinition: to allow someone time or privacy without pressing them to interact

examples.en: It's easier to give someone space when they tell you what they need.
examples.zh: 对方说清自己需要什么后，更容易「给对方一些独处空间」。

examples.en: She decided to give someone space after hearing that they needed some quiet time.
examples.zh: 听说对方需要安静一会儿后，她决定「给对方一些独处空间」。

words.enDefinition: to give a gift in response to someone else's gift

examples.en: She said there was no need to give something in return just because she brought biscuits.
examples.zh: 她说，不用因为她带了饼干就「回送点东西」。

examples.en: I hoped to give something in return the next time my neighbours invited me over.
examples.zh: 我想下次邻居请我过去时，「回送点东西」。

collocations: feel you ought to give something in return
offer to give something in return
no need to give something in return

words.enDefinition: to express appreciation for good things or other people

examples.en: Our group took a moment to give thanks before we started eating.
examples.zh: 开饭前，我们这组人花了一点时间「表达感恩」。

examples.en: We decided to give thanks for the help we'd received that year.
examples.zh: 我们决定为这一年受到的帮助「表达感恩」。

collocations: take a moment to give thanks

words.enDefinition: to make another attempt at a relationship after difficulties or a breakup

examples.en: They decided to give things another try after discussing what had gone wrong last term.
examples.zh: 他们谈过上学期出了什么问题后，决定「再试着交往一次」。

examples.en: She wondered whether to give things another try when he reached out over the summer.
examples.zh: 暑假他主动联系她时，她犹豫要不要「再试着交往一次」。

collocations: agree to give things another try
decide to give things another try
ready to give things another try

words.enDefinition: a narrow tube that gives off light when activated

examples.en: The volunteers gave each child a glow stick at the Halloween event.
examples.zh: 万圣节活动上，志愿者给每个小孩发了一根「荧光棒」。

examples.en: She held a green glow stick so we could find her easily.
examples.zh: 她拿着一根绿色的「荧光棒」，这样我们就容易找到她。

words.enDefinition: encourages someone to open a present they have been given

examples.en: Go ahead and open it if you're curious about what's inside the little brown box.
examples.zh: 要是好奇棕色小盒子里装的是什么，「现在就打开吧」。

examples.en: My flatmate said, "Go ahead and open it. I want to see what you think."
examples.zh: 室友说：「现在就打开吧」。我想看看你喜不喜欢。

collocations: please go ahead and open it
go ahead and open it now
go ahead and open it while we're here

words.enDefinition: A request to let the group start or continue without the speaker taking part.

examples.en: Go ahead without me if my class runs over and you want to order.
examples.zh: 要是我上课拖堂，而你们又想点单了，「你们不用等我」。

examples.en: You can go ahead without me because I don't know when my shift will finish.
examples.zh: 我不知道什么时候下班，「你们不用等我」。

collocations: tell them to go ahead without me
go ahead without me if I'm late
go ahead without me and order

words.enDefinition: to let each person seated at a table speak in turn

examples.en: We decided to go around the table and share one thing we appreciated.
examples.zh: 我们决定「按座位轮流说」，每人分享一件感激的事。

examples.en: Our host asked if we could go around the table to introduce ourselves.
examples.zh: 主人问，我们能不能「按座位轮流说」，做一下自我介绍。

collocations: go around the table before dinner
take a moment to go around the table
ask if we can go around the table

words.enDefinition: to be known by an informal name instead of your full name

examples.en: My art class is small, so I usually go by a nickname there.
examples.zh: 我上的美术班人少，所以在班里我一般「用昵称」。

examples.en: I asked her whether she liked to go by a nickname outside class.
examples.zh: 我问她平时在课堂之外是否喜欢「用昵称」。

collocations: go by a nickname at school
prefer to go by a nickname
