words.enDefinition: To go out with others to sing Christmas songs in public or to neighbors.

examples.en: Some students planned to go caroling with the choir at a nearby community center.
examples.zh: 有些学生计划和合唱团一起去附近的社区中心「唱圣诞颂歌」。

examples.en: My neighbor asked whether I wanted to go caroling with her group after class.
examples.zh: 邻居问我下课后愿不愿跟她们那群人一起去「唱圣诞颂歌」。

words.enDefinition: to make less noise so others are not disturbed

examples.en: Please go easy on the noise if you come back after our roommates are asleep.
examples.zh: 如果回来时我们的室友已经睡了，请「声音轻一点」。

examples.en: My neighbour asked us to go easy on the noise when we moved the chairs.
examples.zh: 我们挪椅子时，邻居请我们「声音轻一点」。

collocations: ask guests to go easy on the noise
remember to go easy on the noise
try to go easy on the noise

words.enDefinition: To share a cost equally with one other person.

examples.en: My roommate offered to go halves on the picnic supplies because we were shopping together.
examples.zh: 我和室友一起采购，她提出野餐用品「各付一半」。

examples.en: Could we go halves on the larger bag of popcorn if you're sharing it too?
examples.zh: 你也吃的话，我们能「各付一半买」大袋爆米花吗？

collocations: go halves on a bag of snacks
offer to go halves on something
go halves on the picnic supplies

words.enDefinition: To enter a building or venue at the same time as a group.

examples.en: We agreed to go in together so the usher could see all our tickets at once.
examples.zh: 我们说好「一起进去」，这样引座员能一次看完所有人的票。

examples.en: Do you want to go in together when the rest of our group gets here?
examples.zh: 等我们小组其他人到了，你想「一起进去」吗？

collocations: go in together once everyone arrives

words.enDefinition: to meet someone socially with a possible romantic interest

examples.en: I hadn't planned to go on a date during the first week of term.
examples.zh: 我本来没打算在开学第一周「去约会」。

examples.en: Leo asked whether I wanted to go on a date after our seminar ended.
examples.zh: 利奥问我，研讨课结束后想不想「去约会」。

collocations: ask someone to go on a date
go on a date with someone

words.enDefinition: to have an ongoing romantic relationship with someone

examples.en: I didn't expect to go out with someone from my own course this year.
examples.zh: 我没想到今年会「和同一门课的人交往」。

examples.en: She said she didn't want to go out with someone who lived far away.
examples.zh: 她说不想「和住得很远的人交往」。

collocations: decide to go out with someone
go out with someone for months
go out with someone from class

words.enDefinition: to let other people know about a previously private romantic relationship

examples.en: They waited until graduation to go public with a relationship they had kept private all year.
examples.zh: 他们等到毕业才「公开了一整年都保密的恋爱关系」。

examples.en: I didn't want to go public with a relationship while we were still figuring things out.
examples.zh: 两人的想法还没理清时，我不想「公开恋爱关系」。

collocations: choose to go public with a relationship
decide when to go public with a relationship
ready to go public with a relationship

words.enDefinition: to share a number of difficult or important experiences over time

examples.en: Friends can go through a lot together during the final year of a demanding course.
examples.zh: 一门很难的课程最后一年，朋友们可能「一起经历很多事」。

examples.en: We knew we'd go through a lot together when our placements began in different places.
examples.zh: 我们知道，实习在不同地方开始后，两人会「一起经历很多事」。

collocations: go through a lot together at university
friends who go through a lot together
expect to go through a lot together

words.enDefinition: to visit homes in costume asking for Halloween treats

examples.en: My host family's kids invited me to go trick-or-treating with them.
examples.zh: 寄宿家庭的孩子邀请我和他们一起「挨家挨户讨糖」。

examples.en: Some children on our street go trick-or-treating before it gets dark.
examples.zh: 我们街上有些小孩在天黑前就去「挨家挨户讨糖」了。

words.enDefinition: to approach someone in order to begin speaking to them

examples.en: I wasn't sure how to go up to someone at such a crowded event.
examples.zh: 活动人太多，我不知道该怎么「走过去找人攀谈」。

examples.en: It's easier to go up to someone when they are standing on their own.
examples.zh: 对方一个人站着时，「走过去找对方攀谈」会容易些。

collocations: decide to go up to someone
feel able to go up to someone
go up to someone and say hello

words.enDefinition: to have known each other for a long time, in informal speech

examples.en: My cousin and I go way back with the neighbours who used to live downstairs.
examples.zh: 我和表亲都跟以前住楼下的邻居「很早就认识了」。

examples.en: You can tell they go way back from the stories they share over dinner.
examples.zh: 听两人晚饭时讲的那些故事，就知道他们「很早就认识了」。

words.enDefinition: To choose the option preferred by most people in the group.

examples.en: We said we'd go with the majority when choosing between the two films tonight.
examples.zh: 我们说好，今晚两部片子只能选一部时就「按多数人的选择来」。

examples.en: Let's go with the majority because everyone has had a chance to choose.
examples.zh: 大家都有机会选过了，「咱们就按多数人的选择来」吧。

collocations: decide to go with the majority
agree to go with the majority
go with the majority if the votes differ

words.enDefinition: A Mandarin New Year greeting wishing someone prosperity.

examples.en: A card reading “Gong Xi Fa Cai” stood above the sweets at the student fair.
examples.zh: 学生集市的糖果上方有张卡片，写着「恭喜发财」。

examples.en: My classmate showed us how to pronounce “Gong Xi Fa Cai” for the New Year event.
examples.zh: 同学教我们在新年活动上怎么念「恭喜发财」。

collocations: a card that reads Gong Xi Fa Cai

words.enDefinition: the Friday before Easter Sunday, observed by Christians in memory of Jesus's death

examples.en: My friend checked the train schedule for Good Friday before booking her ticket home.
examples.zh: 朋友订回家车票前，查了「耶稣受难日」当天的火车时刻表。

examples.en: The church notice listed a service on Good Friday in the early evening.
examples.zh: 教堂的告示写着，「耶稣受难日」当天傍晚有场礼拜。

words.enDefinition: a person who pays close attention when others speak

examples.en: I realised that my new roommate was a good listener over dinner.
examples.zh: 晚饭时，我发现新室友是个「善于倾听的人」。

examples.en: You don't have to talk much to be a good listener here.
examples.zh: 在这里，想当个「善于倾听的人」用不着说很多话。

words.enDefinition: a friendly expression used when speaking to someone you have missed

examples.en: “It's good to hear your voice again,” she said when our call finally connected.
examples.zh: 电话终于接通了，她说：“再次「听到你的声音真好」。”

examples.en: I said, “It's good to hear your voice,” before asking about her new flat.
examples.zh: 我说：“「听到你的声音真好」。”然后问起了她的新公寓。

collocations: so good to hear your voice
it's good to hear your voice again
good to hear your voice after so long

words.enDefinition: To get a quick, light bite after a planned activity.

examples.en: Do you want to grab a snack afterward if the film finishes before nine?
examples.zh: 如果电影九点前结束，你想「之后去吃点东西」吗？

examples.en: We decided to grab a snack afterward at the shop next to our residence hall.
examples.zh: 我们决定「之后去宿舍楼旁的店里吃点东西」。

collocations: want to grab a snack afterward
suggest we grab a snack afterward
grab a snack afterward near campus

words.enDefinition: a chain of paper strips containing notes of appreciation

examples.en: We added a link to the gratitude chain after our Friendsgiving meal.
examples.zh: 朋友感恩节聚餐后，我们给「感恩纸链」又接了一环。

examples.en: The gratitude chain included messages about friendship, family, and finding a home.
examples.zh: 「感恩纸链」上写着有关友情、家人和找到归属感的话。

collocations: add a link to a gratitude chain

words.enDefinition: a small pouring container used to serve gravy at meals

examples.en: I passed the gravy boat to the student sitting next to me.
examples.zh: 我把「船形肉汁壶」递给了坐在旁边的同学。

examples.en: A little gravy boat sat between the bread basket and the flowers.
examples.zh: 面包篮和鲜花中间放着一个小小的「船形肉汁壶」。

words.enDefinition: an informal term for a sign that someone may be a considerate partner

examples.en: For me, listening carefully when someone disagrees is a green flag in a relationship.
examples.zh: 对我而言，遇到不同意见时能认真倾听，是恋爱中「值得肯定的信号」。

examples.en: She saw it as a green flag when her date respected the change of plans.
examples.zh: 约会对象尊重了她更改计划的决定，她认为这是个「值得肯定的信号」。

collocations: see something as a green flag

words.enDefinition: A reservation made together for several people attending the same activity.

examples.en: We made a group booking for the screening because everyone wanted to sit together.
examples.zh: 我们做了放映活动的「团体预订」，因为大家想坐在一起。

examples.en: Maya checked the group booking before telling everyone which entrance to use on Saturday.
examples.zh: 玛雅查了「团体预订」信息，才通知大家星期六走哪个入口。

words.enDefinition: ways of messaging considerately in a shared chat

examples.en: Our society added a page about group chat etiquette to its welcome notes.
examples.zh: 社团在迎新资料里加了一页「群聊礼仪」。

examples.en: We discussed group chat etiquette after the messages kept arriving through the night.
examples.zh: 晚上消息接连不断，我们便讨论了「群聊礼仪」。

words.enDefinition: a costume theme shared by several people dressing up together

examples.en: Our history class planned a group costume based on an old painting.
examples.zh: 我们历史课的同学照着一幅老油画，策划了个「多人配套化装」。

examples.en: The group costume worked because everyone borrowed something in the same colour.
examples.zh: 大家借来的东西都是同一个颜色，所以「多人配套化装」的效果不错。

collocations: take part in a group costume

words.enDefinition: a present bought or prepared together by several people

examples.en: We decided on a group gift after finding a book everyone liked.
examples.zh: 找到一本大家都喜欢的书后，我们决定把它作为「大家合送的礼物」。

examples.en: The cookbook was a group gift from all four of her flatmates.
examples.zh: 那本菜谱是她的四个室友「合送的礼物」。

words.enDefinition: an informal occasion when several people spend time together

examples.en: The afternoon turned into a group hangout after two classmates stopped by the café.
examples.zh: 两位同学来咖啡馆坐坐后，那个下午变成了「一帮朋友的休闲聚会」。

examples.en: I booked the common room for a group hangout before everyone left for summer.
examples.zh: 大家放暑假走之前，我订了公共休息室办「一帮朋友的休闲聚会」。

words.enDefinition: A picture taken of several people together at the same time.

examples.en: We took a group photo on the steps before everyone left for the bus.
examples.zh: 大家离开去坐公交前，我们在台阶上拍了张「合照」。

examples.en: Mina asked for a group photo while there was still enough light in the courtyard.
examples.zh: 庭院里的光线还够，米娜提议拍张「合照」。

words.enDefinition: An informal outdoor meal or get-together planned for a group.

examples.en: We arranged a group picnic by the lake after most people finished their final exams.
examples.zh: 大多数人考完期末后，我们在湖边安排了一次「集体野餐」。

examples.en: I brought an extra blanket to the group picnic because the benches were already taken.
examples.zh: 长椅已经有人了，所以我给「集体野餐」多带了一条毯子。

collocations: bring something to a group picnic

words.enDefinition: A poll sent to a group to find out what its members prefer.

examples.en: I made a group poll so everyone could vote on which evening worked for them.
examples.zh: 我发起了「群内投票」，让大家选自己方便的晚上。

examples.en: The group poll ended in a tie between Friday evening and Saturday afternoon this week.
examples.zh: 本周星期五晚上和星期六下午在「群内投票」中得票相同。

words.enDefinition: A list of the people invited to a gathering or event.

examples.en: Maya checked the guest list before asking whether we needed another table for the evening.
examples.zh: 玛雅查看了「宾客名单」，再问晚上要不要多摆一张桌子。

examples.en: My roommate asked me to add his sister to the guest list for the picnic.
examples.zh: 室友请我把他妹妹加到野餐的「宾客名单」里。

collocations: add someone to the guest list

words.enDefinition: a room in a home where visitors can sleep

examples.en: My friend's parents offered me their guest room when the trains stopped.
examples.zh: 列车停运时，朋友的父母留我睡他们的「客房」。

examples.en: We moved two boxes out of the guest room before she arrived.
examples.zh: 她到之前，我们从「客房」里搬走了两个箱子。

collocations: spare pillows in the guest room

words.enDefinition: A Swahili question used as a traditional Kwanzaa greeting, answered with the day's principle.

examples.en: The guide used “Habari Gani?” to open a discussion of the day's Kwanzaa principle.
examples.zh: 导览员用「今日有什么消息？」开场，带大家讨论当天的宽扎节原则。

examples.en: I saw “Habari Gani?” printed above an explanation of the greeting at the exhibit.
examples.zh: 展览上，问候语的说明上方写着「今日有什么消息？」。

words.enDefinition: a Nowruz display with at least seven symbolic items whose Persian names begin with the letter sin

examples.en: Our class saw a Haft Sin table at a campus Nowruz celebration that spring.
examples.zh: 那年春天，我们班在校园的诺鲁孜节庆典上看到了「诺鲁孜节七件陈设桌」。

examples.en: My friend explained one object on her family's Haft Sin table before we ate.
examples.zh: 吃饭前，朋友介绍了她家「诺鲁孜节七件陈设桌」上的一件物品。

collocations: set up a Haft Sin table
items on a Haft Sin table

words.enDefinition: a Jewish text read during the seder that recounts the Exodus

examples.en: We passed copies of the Haggadah around the table before the meal started.
examples.zh: 开饭前，我们把几本「逾越节仪式手册」在桌上传了一圈。

examples.en: The library exhibition showed an illustrated Haggadah next to a handwritten family note.
examples.zh: 图书馆的展览在一张家庭手写留言旁展示了一册插图版「逾越节仪式手册」。

words.enDefinition: the October holiday often celebrated with costumes and treats

examples.en: Our neighbours put paper bats in their windows for Halloween every year.
examples.zh: 邻居每年都会为「万圣节前夜」在窗户上贴纸蝙蝠。

examples.en: I'd never celebrated Halloween before moving into the residence hall here.
examples.zh: 我搬进这里的宿舍以前，从来没有过「万圣节前夜」。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement of objects used to decorate a place for Halloween

examples.en: The library's Halloween display included pumpkins painted by first-year students last week.
examples.zh: 图书馆的「万圣节主题布景」里有大一学生上周涂绘的南瓜。

examples.en: We stopped to take pictures of a Halloween display across the street.
examples.zh: 我们停下来，给街对面的「万圣节主题布景」拍了几张照片。

words.enDefinition: the evening when people celebrate Halloween with events and activities

examples.en: On Halloween night, we watched old films in our residence lounge.
examples.zh: 「万圣节之夜」，我们在宿舍休息室里看老电影。

examples.en: The students put out lanterns on Halloween night just before supper.
examples.zh: 「万圣节之夜」，同学们在晚饭前摆出了灯笼。

words.enDefinition: the Japanese custom of gathering to view blossoms, especially cherry blossoms

examples.en: Some exchange students invited me to hanami under cherry trees beside their campus.
examples.zh: 几位交换生邀请我到他们校园旁的樱花树下体验「日本赏樱习俗」。

examples.en: The Japan society explained hanami before its spring picnic in the botanical garden.
examples.zh: 日本文化社在植物园办春季野餐前，先介绍了「日本赏樱习俗」。

words.enDefinition: Traditional Korean clothing worn on special occasions such as Seollal.

examples.en: The campus exhibit displayed hanbok beside photographs of Korean families celebrating the new year.
examples.zh: 校园展览把「韩服」摆在韩国各家庭庆祝新年的照片旁。

examples.en: A classmate showed us the hanbok her aunt had worn at their Seollal gathering.
examples.zh: 有位同学给我们看了她姨妈在韩国农历新年聚会时穿的「韩服」。

words.enDefinition: to stay behind instead of approaching or taking part right away

examples.en: I decided to hang back until someone introduced me to the group.
examples.zh: 我决定先「留在后面观望」，等有人把我介绍给大家。

examples.en: She chose to hang back at first and watch the others play.
examples.zh: 她决定先「留在后面观望」，看看其他人怎么玩。

words.enDefinition: An eight-day Jewish festival observed with lights and a range of household traditions.

examples.en: A classmate told us how her family celebrates Hanukkah when our seminar discussed winter festivals.
examples.zh: 研讨课谈到冬季节日时，一位同学讲了她家怎么过「光明节」。

examples.en: The student center listed a public event for Hanukkah alongside several other December activities.
examples.zh: 学生活动中心公布了几项十二月活动，其中有一场面向公众的「光明节」活动。

words.enDefinition: Candles used in the traditional Hanukkah lamp or candleholder during the festival.

examples.en: We noticed a box of Hanukkah candles beside the holiday books in the campus shop.
examples.zh: 我们在校园商店节日图书旁看到一盒「光明节蜡烛」。

examples.en: The display showed several kinds of Hanukkah candles next to a picture of a lamp.
examples.zh: 展览在一张烛台图片旁摆出了几种「光明节蜡烛」。

words.enDefinition: Money traditionally given at Hanukkah, often to children in the family.

examples.en: My flatmate said her grandparents used to give her Hanukkah gelt when she was little.
examples.zh: 室友说，她小时候祖父母会给她「光明节零钱」。

examples.en: A student presentation mentioned Hanukkah gelt alongside other traditions that vary from family to family.
examples.zh: 同学做展示时提到了「光明节零钱」，还讲了其他因家庭而异的习俗。

words.enDefinition: A nine-branched lamp or candleholder used during Hanukkah.

examples.en: We saw a Hanukkah menorah in the window while walking back from our tutorial.
examples.zh: 辅导课下课走回去时，我们在一扇窗户里看到一座「光明节九枝烛台」。

examples.en: The museum guide compared a modern Hanukkah menorah with an older metal example from its collection.
examples.zh: 博物馆导览员把一座现代「光明节九枝烛台」和馆藏的一座旧金属烛台作了对照。

collocations: a Hanukkah menorah in the window
a Hanukkah menorah in the exhibition

words.enDefinition: a greeting wishing someone well during the Easter holiday

examples.en: My neighbour said “Happy Easter” as we walked past her garden on Sunday.
examples.zh: 周日我们经过邻居的花园，她说：“「复活节快乐」。”

examples.en: I wrote “Happy Easter” on the card for my friend's family that weekend.
examples.zh: 那个周末，我在给朋友家人的卡片上写了“「复活节快乐」”。

words.enDefinition: A greeting offering good wishes to someone observing Hanukkah.

examples.en: I wrote “Happy Hanukkah” in a note for my flatmate before she went home.
examples.zh: 室友回家之前，我给她留了张纸条，写着「光明节快乐」。

examples.en: The banner said “Happy Hanukkah” above a table with books about the Jewish festival.
examples.zh: 摆放犹太节日书籍的桌子上方，横幅写着「光明节快乐」。

collocations: write Happy Hanukkah in a card

words.enDefinition: a friendly greeting for people celebrating Holi

examples.en: My friend wrote “Happy Holi” in the group chat before the campus celebration started.
examples.zh: 校园庆典开始之前，朋友在群里写道“「胡里节快乐」”。

examples.en: I heard someone say “Happy Holi” as we approached the music stage together.
examples.zh: 我们一起走近音乐舞台时，我听见有人说“「胡里节快乐」”。

words.enDefinition: A greeting that offers good wishes during the holiday season without naming one holiday.

examples.en: Our tutor said “Happy holidays” after our final seminar before the winter break began.
examples.zh: 寒假前最后一节研讨课结束后，导师祝我们「节日快乐」。

examples.en: I wrote “Happy holidays” in the group chat before everyone left campus for their break.
examples.zh: 大家离校休假前，我在群聊里写了句「节日快乐」。

words.enDefinition: A greeting offering good wishes to someone celebrating Kwanzaa.

examples.en: A greeting card on the community table said “Happy Kwanzaa” in three bright colors.
examples.zh: 社区活动桌上的一张贺卡用三种亮色写着「宽扎节快乐」。

examples.en: The volunteer said “Happy Kwanzaa” as she greeted families arriving for the evening program.
examples.zh: 志愿者迎接来参加晚间活动的家庭时，和他们说「宽扎节快乐」。

words.enDefinition: A greeting for someone celebrating the start of a new year in a lunisolar calendar.

examples.en: The library put up a banner reading “Happy Lunar New Year” beside the information desk.
examples.zh: 图书馆在咨询台旁挂了条写着「农历新年快乐」的横幅。

examples.en: Our tutor wrote “Happy Lunar New Year” at the end of the weekly class email.
examples.zh: 导师在每周课程邮件末尾写了「农历新年快乐」。

collocations: wish someone a Happy Lunar New Year
a banner reading Happy Lunar New Year

words.enDefinition: A greeting wishing someone a happy start to a new year.

examples.en: Our friends called out “Happy New Year” when the clock in the lounge reached midnight.
examples.zh: 休息室里的钟走到午夜时，朋友们喊起了「新年快乐」。

examples.en: I sent “Happy New Year” to my flatmate after she got home for the break.
examples.zh: 室友回家过假期后，我给她发了句「新年快乐」。

collocations: wish someone a Happy New Year
a message reading Happy New Year

words.enDefinition: a greeting wishing someone well during the Jewish holiday of Passover

examples.en: I wrote “Happy Passover” to my friend before she went home on the train.
examples.zh: 朋友坐火车回家前，我给她写了句“「逾越节快乐」”。

examples.en: The student society wished members “Happy Passover” in its message announcing the shared dinner.
examples.zh: 学生社团在公布聚餐的消息里祝成员“「逾越节快乐」”。

words.enDefinition: an event celebrating the gathering of seasonal crops

examples.en: The harvest festival had a stall where growers talked about their crops.
examples.zh: 「丰收庆典」上有个摊位，种植户在那里介绍自家的作物。

examples.en: Students helped hang banners for the community harvest festival on Saturday.
examples.zh: 周六，同学们帮忙为社区的「丰收庆典」挂横幅。

collocations: take part in a harvest festival

words.enDefinition: the time of year when crops are gathered from fields

examples.en: The campus garden held a picnic near the end of harvest season.
examples.zh: 「收获季」快结束时，校园菜园办了一场野餐。

examples.en: Our campus farm ran extra walking tours during harvest season that year.
examples.zh: 那年「收获季」，校园农场加开了几次步行参观。

words.enDefinition: a shared evening meal celebrating the end of a harvest

examples.en: The community garden hosted a harvest supper using vegetables from its plots.
examples.zh: 社区菜园用自家地块种的菜办了一场「丰收聚餐」。

examples.en: I helped put chairs out for the harvest supper in the hall.
examples.zh: 我帮忙给礼堂里举行的「丰收聚餐」摆椅子。

words.enDefinition: a hayride with staged scary scenes along the route

examples.en: I liked the silly costumes on the haunted hayride more than the scares.
examples.zh: 比起「惊吓主题干草车游览」上吓人的环节，我更喜欢那些搞怪的化装服。

examples.en: Our group booked a haunted hayride after hearing about it in class.
examples.zh: 我们组在课堂上听人提起「惊吓主题干草车游览」，随后订了票。

words.enDefinition: a walk-through attraction designed to make visitors feel frightened

examples.en: We took our classmates to a haunted house run by the theatre club.
examples.zh: 我们带同学去了戏剧社办的「鬼屋」。

examples.en: The haunted house used funny sound effects instead of anything too scary.
examples.zh: 「鬼屋」用了些好笑的音效，整体也没布置得太吓人。

words.enDefinition: to feel strongly attracted to someone, often without telling them

examples.en: I used to have a crush on someone who sat beside me in lectures.
examples.zh: 我以前「对一个上大课时坐在我旁边的人心动过」。

examples.en: You can have a crush on a friend and still want to take things slowly.
examples.zh: 你可能「对一个朋友心动」，同时仍想慢慢发展关系。

collocations: have a crush on a classmate
admit you have a crush on someone

words.enDefinition: to have fun with others by joking or laughing together

examples.en: We managed to have a laugh about getting lost on our first day.
examples.zh: 聊起第一天迷路的事，我们痛痛快快地「笑了一场」。

examples.en: I was glad we could have a laugh about our matching school bags.
examples.zh: 我们的书包一模一样，还能一起拿这事「开开心心笑一场」，我挺高兴。

words.enDefinition: to get the wrong idea about each other's words or intentions

examples.en: Friends sometimes have a misunderstanding when they talk about serious things by text.
examples.zh: 朋友用文字聊严肃事情时，有时会「彼此产生误会」。

examples.en: I thought we might have a misunderstanding, so I asked what she meant.
examples.zh: 我想我们可能「彼此产生误会」了，就问她是什么意思。

collocations: have a misunderstanding with a friend

words.expression: have a seat wherever you like
words.lemma: have a seat wherever you like
words.enDefinition: invites a guest to sit anywhere they prefer
acceptedEnVariants: have a seat wherever you like

examples.en: Have a seat wherever you like while I go and find another mug for you.
examples.zh: 「想坐哪儿都行」，我去再给你找个杯子。

examples.en: Our host said, "Have a seat wherever you like," and pointed to the chairs by the window.
examples.zh: 主人指着窗边的椅子说：「想坐哪儿都行」。

collocations: please have a seat wherever you like
come in and have a seat wherever you like
go ahead and have a seat wherever you like

words.enDefinition: to feel a natural romantic attraction or connection with each other

examples.en: They have chemistry, judging by the way they laugh at the same jokes.
examples.zh: 看他们被同样的玩笑逗笑的样子，两人确实「彼此来电」。

examples.en: You can have chemistry with someone even if your lives are quite different.
examples.zh: 即使生活方式很不同，两个人也可能「彼此来电」。

collocations: have chemistry on a first date

words.enDefinition: to be willing to protect or support one another when needed

examples.en: We try to have each other's backs when either of us has a hard week.
examples.zh: 我们中间谁遇到难熬的一周，都会尽量「彼此照应」。

examples.en: They have each other's backs and take turns helping when one of them is busy.
examples.zh: 两人「彼此照应」，谁忙不过来，另一个就帮忙。

collocations: promise to have each other's backs
friends who have each other's backs

words.enDefinition: to feel romantic affection towards a particular person

examples.en: I knew I might have feelings for him when I missed our Sunday walks.
examples.zh: 我开始想念周日一起散步时，就意识到自己可能「对他有爱慕之情」。

examples.en: She asked what to do if you have feelings for a close friend from class.
examples.zh: 她问，如果「对一位关系很好的同学有爱慕之情」，该怎么办。

collocations: admit you have feelings for someone

words.expression: have no one to talk to
words.lemma: have no one to talk to
words.enDefinition: to be without anyone available to chat with
acceptedEnVariants: have no one to talk to

examples.en: It's difficult to have no one to talk to during your first lunch on campus.
examples.zh: 在学校第一天吃午餐时「没人可以说话」，挺难受的。

examples.en: I thought I'd have no one to talk to until two new students sat beside me.
examples.zh: 我以为自己会「没人可以说话」，直到两个新同学坐到我旁边。

collocations: feel like you have no one to talk to
realise you have no one to talk to
have no one to talk to at lunch

words.enDefinition: to receive one or more people as guests in your home

examples.en: I love to have people over when our flat is free on Sundays.
examples.zh: 周日公寓空着的时候，我喜欢「请人来家里做客」。

examples.en: We can't usually have people over when everyone has exams the next week.
examples.zh: 要是大家下周都要考试，我们通常不方便「请人来家里做客」。

words.enDefinition: to share a similar interest, experience, or personal trait

examples.en: It turned out we did have something in common besides taking the same class.
examples.zh: 原来，除了上同一门课，我们也「有共同点」。

examples.en: I asked about volunteering to see if we might have something in common.
examples.zh: 我问对方做过什么志愿活动，想看看我们是不是「有共同点」。

collocations: find that you have something in common
realise you have something in common
discover that you have something in common

words.enDefinition: asks if you and another person have met previously

examples.en: Have we met before? I remember someone with the same yellow notebook from orientation.
examples.zh: 「我们以前见过吗」？我记得迎新时有个人也拿着这种黄色笔记本。

examples.en: The student asked, "Have we met before? I think we both know Sam."
examples.zh: 那位同学问：「我们以前见过吗」？我记得咱俩都认识山姆。

collocations: have we met before on campus
have we met before at a workshop

words.enDefinition: asks whether someone arrived at this place a long time ago

examples.en: Have you been here long, or are you still getting used to all the buses?
examples.zh: 「你来这里多久了」？还是还在熟悉这儿的公交线路？

examples.en: My neighbour asked, "Have you been here long? I hadn't seen you before Monday."
examples.zh: 邻居问：「你来这里多久了」？周一以前我没见过你。

collocations: so have you been here long
have you been here long or just moved
ask whether someone has been here long

words.enDefinition: dried grass packed tightly into a block or round bundle

examples.en: I sat on a hay bale while my friends picked their pumpkins.
examples.zh: 朋友选南瓜时，我坐在一个「干草捆」上。

examples.en: The volunteers put a hay bale beside the entrance for photographs.
examples.zh: 志愿者在入口旁放了一个「干草捆」，供大家拍照。

words.enDefinition: a recreational ride in a wagon carrying straw or hay

examples.en: Our hayride ended at a field full of small orange pumpkins.
examples.zh: 我们「乘干草车游览」的终点是一块长满橙色小南瓜的地。

examples.en: We took a hayride with students from the hall next door.
examples.zh: 我们和隔壁宿舍楼的同学一起「乘干草车游览」。

words.enDefinition: To go to the agreed meeting place with other people rather than separately.

examples.en: We can head over together once you put your notebook back in your room.
examples.zh: 你把笔记本放回房间后，我们可以「一起过去」。

examples.en: I asked if they wanted to head over together after the seminar finished at noon.
examples.zh: 我问他们中午研讨课结束后要不要「一起过去」。

words.enDefinition: to receive a message or other contact from a friend from the past

examples.en: It's always nice to hear from an old friend when a long term ends.
examples.zh: 漫长的一个学期结束时，「收到老朋友的消息」总让人开心。

examples.en: I didn't expect to hear from an old friend the week after our class reunion.
examples.zh: 我没想到同学聚会后一周就会「收到老朋友的消息」。

collocations: be glad to hear from an old friend
hope to hear from an old friend
surprised to hear from an old friend

words.enDefinition: gives a visitor permission to get a drink for themselves

examples.en: Help yourself to a drink while I finish helping the neighbours with their bags.
examples.zh: 「想喝什么自己拿」，我先帮邻居把包拿完。

examples.en: My friend said, "Help yourself to a drink. The cold glasses are in the fridge."
examples.zh: 朋友说：「想喝什么自己拿」。冰过的杯子在冰箱里。

collocations: please help yourself to a drink
go ahead and help yourself to a drink
feel free to help yourself to a drink

words.enDefinition: invites someone to take another serving when they want one

examples.en: You can help yourself to seconds once everyone has had their first serving.
examples.zh: 等大家都盛过第一份，「想再吃可以自己添」。

examples.en: My host said, "Help yourself to seconds," when she saw me looking at the potatoes.
examples.zh: 主人看我望着土豆，说：「想再吃可以自己添」。

collocations: feel free to help yourself to seconds
tell guests to help themselves to seconds
you can help yourself to seconds

words.enDefinition: a family or community language passed down where another language is dominant

examples.en: She takes weekend classes to keep learning her heritage language while studying abroad.
examples.zh: 留学期间，她周末上课继续学自己的「传承语」。

examples.en: I heard my heritage language at the community market near the student residence.
examples.zh: 我在学生宿舍附近的社区市场听到了自己的「传承语」。

words.enDefinition: someone raised with a family or community language in a different dominant language setting

examples.en: The workshop welcomed each heritage speaker to talk about what they could already do.
examples.zh: 工作坊请每位「传承语使用者」说说自己已经能用这门语言做些什么。

examples.en: My friend identifies as a heritage speaker even though he reads slowly.
examples.zh: 朋友虽然读得比较慢，还是认同自己是「传承语使用者」。

words.enDefinition: The Scottish name for New Year's Eve and its celebrations.

examples.en: My classmate told us about Hogmanay when we met at her room for tea.
examples.zh: 我去同学房间喝茶时，她给我们讲了「苏格兰除夕庆典」。

examples.en: The university notice advertised a Hogmanay gathering for students staying in town during the break.
examples.zh: 大学的告示为放假留在城里的学生宣传了一场「苏格兰除夕庆典」。

words.zhGloss: 帮我们留着排队的位置
words.enDefinition: To keep the group's place in a queue while some people step away briefly.
acceptedZhAnswers: 帮我们留着排队的位置
acceptedEnVariants: hold our place in the queue

examples.en: Could you hold our place in line while we check which screening is starting first?
examples.zh: 我们去看看哪场放映先开始，你能「帮我们留着排队的位置」吗？

examples.en: Maya offered to hold our place in line while we moved our bikes off the path.
examples.zh: 我们去把自行车从通道上挪走时，玛雅主动「帮我们留着排队的位置」。

collocations: ask someone to hold our place in line
hold our place in line for a minute
offer to hold our place in line

words.enDefinition: to wait for an appropriate point before applauding

examples.en: “Hold your applause until all the names are read,” the host reminded us.
examples.zh: 主持人提醒大家「先不要鼓掌」，等所有名字念完。

examples.en: The notice read “Hold your applause” at the start of the performance.
examples.zh: 演出开始时，提示写着「先不要鼓掌」。

collocations: hold your applause until the end
a request to hold your applause

words.enDefinition: a Hindu spring festival widely associated with celebrations using coloured powders

examples.en: Several students volunteered at the campus Holi celebration in the park near residence.
examples.zh: 几名学生在宿舍附近公园举办的校园「胡里节」活动中做了志愿者。

examples.en: I learned about Holi from a classmate whose family celebrated it every spring.
examples.zh: 我从一位同学那里了解了「胡里节」，他们家每年春天都会过。

words.enDefinition: the times or places where services will close because of a holiday

examples.en: The residence app listed holiday closures for the library and sports centre that weekend.
examples.zh: 宿舍应用列出了那个周末图书馆和体育中心的「假日停业安排」。

examples.en: I checked the holiday closures before planning to study on campus with my classmates.
examples.zh: 安排和同学在校园学习前，我查了「假日停业安排」。

words.enDefinition: the opening hours that a business uses during a holiday

examples.en: The campus shop posted its holiday hours on the door before Thanksgiving.
examples.zh: 感恩节前，校园商店把「节日营业时间」贴在了门上。

examples.en: I checked the holiday hours because I needed to buy groceries before dinner.
examples.zh: 我晚饭前得买些食品杂货，所以查了一下「节日营业时间」。

words.enDefinition: a package of ingredients or food for preparing a holiday meal

examples.en: A few students helped pack a holiday meal kit for each registered household.
examples.zh: 几位同学帮忙给每户报名的家庭打包一份「节日餐食包」。

examples.en: I picked up a holiday meal kit from the organisation hosting the dinner.
examples.zh: 我从负责晚餐的机构那里领了一份「节日餐食包」。

collocations: hand out a holiday meal kit

words.enDefinition: a series of organised activities offered during a school or public holiday

examples.en: The community centre posted its holiday programme on the door near the bus stop.
examples.zh: 社区中心在公交站旁的门上贴出了「假期系列活动」信息。

examples.en: I signed up to help at the holiday programme before leaving campus for summer.
examples.zh: 暑假离校前，我报名协助「假期系列活动」。

words.enDefinition: The part of the year around several late-year holidays, especially in North American usage.

examples.en: The student center stayed open on selected days during the holiday season for residents.
examples.zh: 「年末节庆时段」，学生活动中心选了几天对住户开放。

examples.en: My roommate worked extra shifts at the campus bookstore during the holiday season.
examples.zh: 「年末节庆时段」，室友在校园书店多上了几个班。

collocations: the start of the holiday season

words.enDefinition: a public transport schedule used for a holiday instead of the usual weekday schedule

examples.en: The station used its holiday timetable on Monday, so we left home earlier.
examples.zh: 车站周一用的是「假日班次时刻表」，所以我们早一点出了门。

examples.en: Our last bus was at nine on the holiday timetable printed near the door.
examples.zh: 门边贴的「假日班次时刻表」显示，我们的末班车是九点。

words.enDefinition: road traffic affected or increased by travel for a holiday

examples.en: We left after lunch to avoid the worst holiday traffic near the city centre.
examples.zh: 我们午饭后出发，避开市中心附近最拥堵的「节假日车流」。

examples.en: The coach driver warned that holiday traffic could slow us down near the coast.
examples.zh: 大巴司机提醒，沿海一带的「节假日车流」可能会让我们开得慢一些。

words.enDefinition: the week immediately before Easter in many Christian traditions

examples.en: One of the students gave a short talk on traditions during Holy Week in Spain.
examples.zh: 一名学生做了个简短介绍，讲西班牙「圣周」期间的传统。

examples.en: The small church published a separate calendar for Holy Week beside its usual schedule.
examples.zh: 小教堂在常规安排旁，另贴了一份「圣周」日程。

words.enDefinition: Describes someone spending the holiday period at home, often with family.

examples.en: I decided to go home for the holidays after my final exam ended early.
examples.zh: 最后一场考试提前结束，我决定「回家过节」。

examples.en: My roommate planned to be home for the holidays but return before classes started again.
examples.zh: 室友计划「回家过节」，开课前再回来。

words.enDefinition: a language a person or family regularly uses at home

examples.en: My cousin and I switched to our home language when we called.
examples.zh: 我和表亲打电话时换回了「家中使用的语言」。

examples.en: The project let each student read a short passage in their home language.
examples.zh: 这个项目让每个同学用「家中使用的语言」朗读一小段。

words.enDefinition: an outfit someone makes for a character or theme

examples.en: The homemade costume looked like a paper lantern from across the room.
examples.zh: 从房间另一头看，那件「自制化装服」像一盏纸灯笼。

examples.en: I wore a homemade costume made from an old pillowcase and ribbon.
examples.zh: 我穿了件用旧枕套和丝带做的「自制化装服」。

words.enDefinition: sweet snacks or similar small foods someone makes at home

examples.en: I brought some homemade treats as a thank-you for the weekend visit.
examples.zh: 我带了些「自制的小点心」，谢谢他们周末的招待。

examples.en: My host set out the homemade treats I had brought from home.
examples.zh: 主人把我从家里带来的「自制小点心」摆了出来。

words.enDefinition: a title used with a name to show respect

examples.en: The form let each speaker choose an honorific for the printed programme.
examples.zh: 表格让每位发言者为印制的活动手册挑选一个「姓名前的敬称」。

examples.en: I checked which honorific the guest used before writing the name on the card.
examples.zh: 在卡片上写名字前，我查了来宾使用哪个「敬称」。

collocations: use an honorific before a name

words.enDefinition: Expresses a wish that the person can attend a planned gathering.

examples.en: Hope you can make it to our picnic once your afternoon class is over.
examples.zh: 下午下课后，「希望你能来」参加我们的野餐。

examples.en: I added “Hope you can make it” when I sent my roommate the updated plan.
examples.zh: 把更新后的安排发给室友时，我加了句「希望你能来」。

collocations: add hope you can make it
say hope you can make it
write hope you can make it

words.enDefinition: friendly treatment or care offered to guests or visitors

examples.en: I was grateful for the hospitality my classmate's family showed me.
examples.zh: 我很感激同学一家对我的「热情款待」。

examples.en: She always remembers the hospitality she received during her first term.
examples.zh: 她一直记得自己第一学期受到的「热情款待」。

words.enDefinition: a small present brought to thank someone for hosting

examples.en: I picked up some local biscuits as a host gift before dinner.
examples.zh: 晚餐前，我买了些本地饼干，作「拜访时给主人的礼物」。

examples.en: My roommate brought a host gift when she stayed with my family.
examples.zh: 室友来我家住时，带了份「给主人的礼物」。

words.enDefinition: warm apple juice, often spiced, served as a seasonal drink

examples.en: The farm shop served hot apple cider next to the entrance to the maze.
examples.zh: 那家农场店在迷宫入口旁供应「热苹果汁」。

examples.en: We drank hot apple cider outside while our friends picked out a pumpkin.
examples.zh: 朋友选南瓜时，我们在外面喝着「热苹果汁」。

words.enDefinition: a lightly spiced sweet bun marked with a cross, traditionally associated with Easter

examples.en: My flatmate brought me a hot cross bun from the bakery before class.
examples.zh: 上课前，室友从面包店给我带了一个「十字面包」。

examples.en: I bought a hot cross bun to try after seeing them in several Easter displays.
examples.zh: 我在几个复活节展台见过，就买了一个「十字面包」尝尝。

words.enDefinition: someone staying temporarily as a visitor in another person's home

examples.en: My roommate made up the sofa for our houseguest that evening.
examples.zh: 那天晚上，室友把沙发铺好给我们「留宿的客人」睡。

examples.en: I was a houseguest at a friend's flat during the reading break.
examples.zh: 阅读周假期，我是朋友公寓里的「留宿客人」。

collocations: have a houseguest for the weekend

words.enDefinition: asks how comfortable someone is becoming in a new place

examples.en: My new neighbour asked, "How are you settling in after your first week on campus?"
examples.zh: 在学校待了一星期后，新邻居问我：“「你适应得怎么样」？”

examples.en: How are you settling in now that you've moved from the temporary room upstairs?
examples.zh: 从楼上的临时房间搬出来以后，「你适应得怎么样」？

collocations: so how are you settling in
how are you settling in so far
ask how someone is settling in

words.zhGloss: 这个传统是怎么开始的
words.enDefinition: a question about the origins of a particular practice
acceptedZhAnswers: 这个传统是怎么开始的

examples.en: “How did that tradition start?” I asked after hearing about my friend's school.
examples.zh: 听朋友说起以前的学校后，我问「这个传统是怎么开始的？」

examples.en: The volunteer pointed to an old photograph and asked, “How did that tradition start?”
examples.zh: 志愿者指着一张老照片问「这个传统是怎么开始的？」

collocations: “How did that tradition start at your school?”
“How did that tradition start in your family?”

words.expression: how do you know each other
words.lemma: how do you know each other
words.enDefinition: asks how two people first became acquainted or connected
acceptedEnVariants: how do you know each other

examples.en: At the first lunch, someone asked, "How do you know each other? Were you roommates last year?"
examples.zh: 第一次一起午餐时，有人问：「你们是怎么认识的」？去年是室友吗？

examples.en: My new flatmate asked, "How do you know each other? I keep seeing you two together."
examples.zh: 新室友问：「你们是怎么认识的」？我老是看到你俩在一起。

collocations: ask how two people know each other
so how do you know each other
how do you know each other again

words.expression: how do you take your tea
words.lemma: how do you take your tea
words.enDefinition: asks how someone likes their tea, including milk or sugar
acceptedEnVariants: how do you take your tea

examples.en: My classmate asked, "How do you take your tea? I've got a little milk left."
examples.zh: 同学问：「你喝茶加些什么」？我还有一点牛奶。

examples.en: How do you take your tea at home? I can bring the sugar over if you like.
examples.zh: 你在家「喝茶加些什么」？你要是想加糖，我可以拿过来。

collocations: how do you take your tea again
so how do you take your tea
ask how someone takes their tea

words.enDefinition: A question asking how far someone is from where you plan to meet.

examples.en: Kai asked “How far away are you?” when the doors opened five minutes early.
examples.zh: 门提前五分钟开了，凯就问「你离这儿还有多远」？

examples.en: I asked “How far away are you?” so we could decide whether to order yet.
examples.zh: 我问「你离这儿还有多远」，好决定现在要不要点单。

collocations: text how far away are you
ask how far away are you
how far away are you now

words.expression: how much do I owe you
words.lemma: how much do i owe you
words.enDefinition: A question asking how much to pay back to someone who covered a shared expense.
acceptedEnVariants: how much do I owe you

examples.en: How much do I owe you for the two tickets you bought for us yesterday?
examples.zh: 昨天你帮我们买了两张票，「我该给你多少钱」？

examples.en: How much do I owe you for my share of the picnic supplies today?
examples.zh: 今天野餐用品我该出的那一份，「我该给你多少钱」？

collocations: ask how much do I owe you
how much do I owe you for the tickets
text how much do I owe you

words.enDefinition: asks how someone's initial week in a new place is going

examples.en: How's your first week going since you moved into the residence hall on Sunday?
examples.zh: 周日搬进宿舍之后，「你第一周过得怎么样」？

examples.en: My lab partner turned around and said, "How's your first week going now classes have started?"
examples.zh: 我的实验搭档转过身问：「你第一周过得怎么样」？课已经开始上了。

collocations: so how's your first week going
how's your first week going so far
ask how someone's first week is going

words.zhGloss: 幽默换种语言不一定奏效
words.enDefinition: a comment that jokes may not work in another language or setting
acceptedZhAnswers: 幽默换种语言不一定奏效

examples.en: “Humour doesn't always translate,” my classmate said after trying to explain the pun.
examples.zh: 同学试着解释完双关后说「幽默换种语言不一定奏效」。

examples.en: I said, “Humour doesn't always translate,” when the punchline sounded flat in English.
examples.zh: 笑点译成英语显得平淡时，我说「幽默换种语言不一定奏效」。

words.enDefinition: a conversation held quietly enough not to disturb other people

examples.en: We had a hushed conversation in the corridor while the speaker answered questions.
examples.zh: 发言者回答提问时，我们在走廊里「低声交谈」。

examples.en: I heard a hushed conversation behind me while the library film was playing.
examples.zh: 图书馆放电影时，我听见身后有人「低声交谈」。

collocations: a hushed conversation in the corridor

words.enDefinition: A reply saying that you have another arrangement for that time.

examples.en: I already have plans for Saturday, but I can join the picnic on Sunday.
examples.zh: 星期六「我已经有安排了」，但星期天可以参加野餐。

examples.en: I said “I already have plans” when they asked me to come out after class.
examples.zh: 他们问我下课后要不要一起出去，我说「我已经有安排了」。

collocations: I already have plans for that evening

words.enDefinition: Introduces a time by which the speaker can get to the meeting place.

examples.en: I can be there by seven if I take the bus right after class.
examples.zh: 如果下课后马上坐公交，「我最晚七点能到」。

examples.en: I can be there by the start of the film even if I miss the first bus.
examples.zh: 即使错过第一趟公交，「我最晚也能在电影开场时到」。

collocations: I can be there by seven
tell the group I can be there by
I can be there by the break

words.expression: I can come for a bit
words.lemma: i can come for a bit
words.enDefinition: A reply saying you can join an event for only part of it.
acceptedEnVariants: I can come for a bit

examples.en: I can come for a bit before heading back to campus for my evening class.
examples.zh: 晚课前我得回学校，不过「我能来待一小会儿」。

examples.en: Tell Mina I can come for a bit if the picnic starts before my shift.
examples.zh: 告诉米娜，如果野餐在我上班前开始，「我能来待一小会儿」。

collocations: I can come for a bit after work
say I can come for a bit
reply I can come for a bit

words.enDefinition: tells the host they need not accompany you to the exit

examples.en: I can show myself out. You can stay here and finish talking to your guests.
examples.zh: 「我自己出去就行」。你可以留在这儿继续跟客人聊。

examples.en: I said, "I can show myself out," and put my coat on in the hallway.
examples.zh: 我说：「我自己出去就行」，在走廊里穿上了外套。

collocations: don't get up, I can show myself out
thanks, I can show myself out
no need to come, I can show myself out

words.enDefinition: Introduces the time up to which someone can remain at an event.

examples.en: I can stay until eight, when I need to catch my last bus home.
examples.zh: 「我可以待到八点」，之后得去赶回家的末班公交车。

examples.en: I can stay until the film ends if we start before seven this evening.
examples.zh: 如果今晚七点前开始，「我可以待到电影结束」。

collocations: I can stay until the end

words.expression: I can't see this going anywhere
words.lemma: i can't see this going anywhere
words.zhGloss: 我看不到这段关系的未来
words.enDefinition: a phrase saying you do not expect the relationship to develop further
acceptedZhAnswers: 我看不到这段关系的未来
acceptedEnVariants: I can't see this going anywhere
I cannot see this going anywhere

examples.en: “I can't see this going anywhere,” he wrote after their conversation about next year.
examples.zh: 谈过明年的计划后，他写道：“「我看不到这段关系的未来」。”

examples.en: I finally said, “I can't see this going anywhere,” during our walk back to campus.
examples.zh: 走回学校的路上，我终于说：“「我看不到这段关系的未来」。”

collocations: honestly, I can't see this going anywhere
I can't see this going anywhere right now
I can't see this going anywhere long term

words.expression: I can't speak for my whole country
words.lemma: i can't speak for my whole country
words.zhGloss: 我不能代表整个国家的人
words.enDefinition: a statement limiting what you say to your own experience
acceptedZhAnswers: 我不能代表整个国家的人
acceptedEnVariants: I can't speak for my whole country

examples.en: I can't speak for my whole country, but my neighbours didn't do that.
examples.zh: 「我不能代表整个国家的人」，不过我以前的邻居不这么做。

examples.en: “I can't speak for my whole country,” she said before describing her own experience.
examples.zh: 她介绍自己的经历前说「我不能代表整个国家的人」。

collocations: say “I can't speak for my whole country”
“I can't speak for my whole country, only my family”
“I can't speak for my whole country on that”

words.expression: I'd like to see you again
words.lemma: i'd like to see you again
words.enDefinition: a direct way to say you would enjoy another meeting or date
acceptedEnVariants: I'd like to see you again
I would like to see you again

examples.en: “I'd like to see you again,” he said as we walked to the bus stop.
examples.zh: 走去公交站时他说：“「我想再和你见面」。”

examples.en: I wrote, “I'd like to see you again if you're also free next week.”
examples.zh: 我写道：“如果你下周也有空，「我想再和你见面」。”

collocations: I'd like to see you again sometime
I'd like to see you again next week
I'd like to see you again if you're interested

words.enDefinition: a polite way to decline to share information

examples.en: “I'd rather not say,” I told my classmate when they asked about my marks.
examples.zh: 有同学问我成绩，我说「我不太想说」。

examples.en: She said, “I'd rather not say,” when asked why she had changed rooms.
examples.zh: 有人问她为什么换房间，她说「我不太想说」。

collocations: “I'd rather not say in front of everyone”

words.enDefinition: introduces the name a person normally wants others to use

examples.en: My full name is Amara, but I go by Amy during class.
examples.zh: 我的全名是阿玛拉，但在班里我「平时叫」艾米。

examples.en: I go by Lou, which is easier for my new classmates to remember.
examples.zh: 我「平时叫」卢，新同学更容易记住这个称呼。

collocations: I go by my middle name
I go by a shortened name

words.enDefinition: a friendly way to say you enjoyed an outing with someone

examples.en: I texted, “I had a lovely time at the exhibition, thanks for asking me.”
examples.zh: 我发消息说：“看展时「我玩得很开心」，谢谢你约我。”

examples.en: “I had a lovely time tonight,” she said before heading back to her residence.
examples.zh: 回宿舍前她说：“今晚「我玩得很开心」。”

collocations: I had a lovely time tonight
I had a lovely time with you
I had a lovely time at dinner

words.enDefinition: expresses a wish that the recipient enjoys the gift

examples.en: I hope you like it. I wasn't sure which cover design you would go for.
examples.zh: 「希望你喜欢」。我拿不准你会喜欢哪款封面。

examples.en: As I handed over the drawing, I said, "I hope you like it. It's handmade."
examples.zh: 我递过那幅画时说：「希望你喜欢」。是我自己画的。

collocations: I really hope you like it
I hope you like it as much as I did
anyway, I hope you like it

words.enDefinition: A message reporting that you arrived at the meeting place a moment ago.

examples.en: I just got here, and the queue outside the cinema is already around the corner.
examples.zh: 「我刚到」，电影院外的队伍已经排到拐角了。

examples.en: I just got here, but I can't see anyone from our class in the lobby.
examples.zh: 「我刚到」，不过在大厅没看见咱们班的人。

collocations: tell them I just got here

words.enDefinition: signals understanding based on a shared or similar experience

examples.en: I know what you mean. My first week was also full of wrong turns and detours.
examples.zh: 「我懂你的意思」。我第一周也总拐错弯、走冤枉路。

examples.en: She said, "I know what you mean," when I described eating lunch alone on Monday.
examples.zh: 我说起周一独自吃午饭，她说：「我懂你的意思」。

collocations: say I know what you mean
I know what you mean about that
I know what you mean there

words.expression: I'll get a lot of use out of it
words.lemma: i'll get a lot of use out of it
words.enDefinition: says that a present will be useful repeatedly over time
acceptedEnVariants: I'll get a lot of use out of it

examples.en: I'll get a lot of use out of it, especially since the handle fits my hand so well.
examples.zh: 「这东西我会经常用」，尤其是这个手柄握着特别合手。

examples.en: I turned to her and said, "I'll get a lot of use out of it. Thank you."
examples.zh: 我转向她说：「这东西我会经常用」。谢谢。

collocations: I'm sure I'll get a lot of use out of it
I know I'll get a lot of use out of it
honestly, I'll get a lot of use out of it

words.enDefinition: offers to open the door when someone is waiting outside

examples.en: I'll get the door while you finish pouring the tea for our other guests.
examples.zh: 「我去开门」，你继续给其他客人倒茶吧。

examples.en: When the bell rang, I said, "I'll get the door. You can stay seated."
examples.zh: 门铃响时，我说：「我去开门」，你坐着就好。

collocations: don't worry, I'll get the door
I'll get the door this time
stay there, I'll get the door

words.expression: I'll keep it here for you
words.lemma: i'll keep it here for you
words.enDefinition: an offer to look after something until its owner can collect it
acceptedEnVariants: I'll keep it here for you

examples.en: “I'll keep it here for you,” my host wrote after finding the blue scarf.
examples.zh: 主人找到那条蓝围巾后写道：“「我先替你收着」。”

examples.en: “I'll keep it here for you until next weekend,” my friend said at the door.
examples.zh: 朋友在门边说：“下周末前，「我先替你收着」。”

collocations: don't worry, I'll keep it here for you
I'll keep it here for you until Friday
I'll keep it here for you until you return

words.enDefinition: gives a visitor time alone to get comfortable after arriving

examples.en: I'll let you get settled upstairs before I call everyone down for something to eat.
examples.zh: 「你先在楼上安顿一下」，再喊大家下楼吃点东西。

examples.en: My neighbour said, "I'll let you get settled," and brought my suitcase to the room.
examples.zh: 邻居说：「你先安顿一下」，然后把行李箱送到房间。

collocations: I'll let you get settled first
I'll let you get settled in your room
I'll let you get settled before dinner

words.enDefinition: promises to tell another person that someone has thanked them

examples.en: I'll pass on your thanks when I see my parents at their place tomorrow.
examples.zh: 我明天去看父母时，「会转达你的谢意」。

examples.en: My friend replied, "I'll pass on your thanks. My sister loved having everyone over."
examples.zh: 朋友回复：「我会转达你的谢意」。我妹妹特别喜欢大家来做客。

collocations: don't worry, I'll pass on your thanks
of course I'll pass on your thanks
I'll pass on your thanks when I see her

words.enDefinition: a casual goodbye suggesting you may meet again nearby

examples.en: I said, "I'll see you around," when we parted at the library steps.
examples.zh: 在图书馆台阶处分开时，我说了声「回头见」。

examples.en: She waved and said, "I'll see you around," before heading to her next class.
examples.zh: 她挥挥手说了声「回头见」，然后去上下一节课了。

collocations: I guess I'll see you around

words.expression: I'll show you where everything is
words.lemma: i'll show you where everything is
words.enDefinition: offers to tell a visitor where they can find useful things
acceptedEnVariants: I'll show you where everything is

examples.en: I'll show you where everything is so you won't have to wake us up tomorrow morning.
examples.zh: 「我带你看看东西在哪」，这样明早你就不用叫醒我们了。

examples.en: My friend said, "I'll show you where everything is," and opened the cupboard with the clean towels.
examples.zh: 朋友说：「我带你看看东西在哪」，打开了放干净毛巾的柜门。

collocations: come with me and I'll show you where everything is
first I'll show you where everything is
I'll show you where everything is when you arrive

words.expression: I'll walk you to the bus stop
words.lemma: i'll walk you to the bus stop
words.enDefinition: offers to accompany a departing visitor as far as their stop
acceptedEnVariants: I'll walk you to the bus stop

examples.en: I'll walk you to the bus stop so you don't have to find it in the dark.
examples.zh: 「我陪你走到公交站」，免得你天黑了还得自己找。

examples.en: My friend said, "I'll walk you to the bus stop," before she went to find her jacket.
examples.zh: 朋友去找夹克前说：「我陪你走到公交站」。

collocations: wait and I'll walk you to the bus stop
come on, I'll walk you to the bus stop
if you like, I'll walk you to the bus stop

words.enDefinition: a statement that someone feels content without a romantic relationship

examples.en: “I'm happy being single,” my flatmate said when we asked about the dating event.
examples.zh: 我们问起单身交友活动时，室友说：“「我享受单身生活」。”

examples.en: I told her, “I'm happy being single while I get used to living here.”
examples.zh: 我告诉她：“我还在适应这里的生活，「我享受单身生活」。”

collocations: I'm happy being single right now
I'm happy being single while I finish my degree

words.expression: I'm not looking for a relationship
words.lemma: i'm not looking for a relationship
words.enDefinition: a direct way to say you are not seeking a romantic commitment
acceptedEnVariants: I'm not looking for a relationship
I am not looking for a relationship

examples.en: “I'm not looking for a relationship right now,” she said after they finished coffee.
examples.zh: 喝完咖啡后，她说：“「我现在不想谈恋爱」。”

examples.en: I said, “I'm not looking for a relationship while I'm finishing my degree.”
examples.zh: 我说：“完成学位之前，「我现在不想谈恋爱」。”

collocations: I'm not looking for a relationship right now
I'm not looking for a relationship at the moment
I'm not looking for a relationship this year

words.expression: I only see you as a friend
words.lemma: i only see you as a friend
words.enDefinition: a kind but direct way to say you do not feel romantic interest
acceptedEnVariants: I only see you as a friend

examples.en: “I only see you as a friend,” she said when he asked about another date.
examples.zh: 他问要不要再约一次，她说：“「我只把你当朋友」。”

examples.en: I told him, “I only see you as a friend, and I didn't want to pretend.”
examples.zh: 我告诉他：“「我只把你当朋友」，我不想假装有别的感情。”

collocations: I only see you as a friend right now
honestly, I only see you as a friend
I think I only see you as a friend

words.enDefinition: explains that a remembered preference influenced what the giver chose

examples.en: I remembered you liked orange tea, so I brought you some from my hometown.
examples.zh: 「我记得你喜欢」橙味茶，所以从家乡给你带了点。

examples.en: I said, "I remembered you liked this artist," and gave my friend the print.
examples.zh: 我说：「我记得你喜欢」这位画家，就把那幅印刷画送给了朋友。

collocations: I remembered you liked this author
I remembered you liked that kind
tell her I remembered you liked it

words.expression: I think I've seen you around
words.lemma: i think i've seen you around
words.enDefinition: suggests you recognise someone from seeing them nearby before
acceptedEnVariants: I think I've seen you around

examples.en: I think I've seen you around campus, usually at the library around the same time.
examples.zh: 「我好像在学校见过你」，通常是在差不多的时间去图书馆时。

examples.en: The student said, "I think I've seen you around the building, but we've never spoken."
examples.zh: 那位同学说：「我好像在这栋楼附近见过你」，但咱们还没说过话。

collocations: I think I've seen you around campus
I think I've seen you around here
I think I've seen you around the gym

words.expression: I thought of you when I saw it
words.lemma: i thought of you when i saw it
words.enDefinition: explains that an item immediately reminded you of the recipient
acceptedEnVariants: I thought of you when I saw it

examples.en: I thought of you when I saw it at the book fair. You mentioned this author last month.
examples.zh: 我在书展上「一看到就想到你」。你上个月提过这个作者。

examples.en: My friend said, "I thought of you when I saw it," when she gave me the mug.
examples.zh: 朋友把马克杯送给我时说：「我一看到就想到你」。

collocations: I thought of you when I saw it on display
I thought of you when I saw it in the window
I thought of you when I saw it at the fair

words.enDefinition: Introduces the time or place that someone remembers agreeing to earlier.

examples.en: I thought we said six, but the message from Mina said half past five.
examples.zh: 「我以为咱们说好的是六点」，但米娜的消息写的是五点半。

examples.en: I thought we said the main gate rather than the entrance beside the sports hall.
examples.zh: 「我以为咱们说好的是正门」，不是体育馆旁的入口。

collocations: I thought we said the main gate

words.enDefinition: an informal assurance that you will support someone when they need you

examples.en: “I've got your back,” she said when I told her about my difficult meeting.
examples.zh: 我告诉她那场会议不好应付，她说：“「我会支持你」。”

examples.en: He texted, “I've got your back if you need help after the concert.”
examples.zh: 他发消息说：“音乐会结束后要帮忙的话，「我会支持你」。”

collocations: don't worry, I've got your back
I've got your back if anything changes
I've got your back on this

words.expression: I was just about to say that
words.lemma: i was just about to say that
words.enDefinition: says you were about to make the same point
acceptedEnVariants: I was just about to say that

examples.en: I was just about to say that. Walking through the park is quicker than waiting for that bus.
examples.zh: 「我正想说这句」。穿过公园比等那班公交快。

examples.en: She laughed and said, "I was just about to say that," after I mentioned the loud clocks.
examples.zh: 我提到那几只钟走得很响，她笑着说：「我正想说这句」。

collocations: funny, I was just about to say that
I was just about to say that myself
I was just about to say that as well

words.enDefinition: An artwork carved or shaped from ice, often displayed at winter festivals.

examples.en: A large ice sculpture stood near the entrance to the winter festival by campus.
examples.zh: 校园附近的冬季节庆活动入口旁摆了一座大型「冰雕」。

examples.en: My classmate snapped a photo of the ice sculpture shaped like an open book.
examples.zh: 同学拍下了那座形状像一本打开的书的「冰雕」。

collocations: an ice sculpture at a winter festival

words.enDefinition: A friendly way to decline or qualify an invitation by giving a reason.

examples.en: I'd love to, but I promised to help my roommate move her desk this evening.
examples.zh: 「我很想去，不过」我答应了今晚帮室友搬书桌。

examples.en: I'd love to, but my shift ends too late for me to catch the film.
examples.zh: 「我很想去，不过」我下班太晚，赶不上电影。

collocations: I'd love to, but I have class
I'd love to, but I'm working

words.enDefinition: A condition meaning that the weather needs to remain suitable for a planned activity.

examples.en: We'll eat on the lawn if the weather holds until the end of class.
examples.zh: 「如果天气一直不错」到下课，我们就去草坪上吃。

examples.en: If the weather holds, we can leave our coats at home for the walk.
examples.zh: 「如果天气一直不错」，咱们散步时就可以把外套留在家里。

collocations: meet outside if the weather holds
go ahead if the weather holds
eat on the lawn if the weather holds

words.enDefinition: An informal condition used when inviting someone who may be nearby and available.

examples.en: We are getting coffee near the library after class if you're around this afternoon.
examples.zh: 下课后我们要去图书馆附近喝咖啡，「如果你下午在附近有空」可以一起来。

examples.en: You can still join us for a walk by the river if you're around after class.
examples.zh: 「如果你下课后在附近有空」，还可以和我们一起去河边走走。

collocations: stop for coffee if you're around

words.enDefinition: A promise to bring one more of something for a group activity.

examples.en: I'll bring an extra blanket because the bench might be wet at the park.
examples.zh: 公园的长椅可能是湿的，「我会多带一条毯子」。

examples.en: I'll bring an extra chair if your roommate decides to join us for the screening.
examples.zh: 如果你室友决定来一起看电影，「我会多带一把椅子」。

collocations: tell the group I'll bring an extra

words.enDefinition: A message confirming you will go separately and see the other person at the destination.

examples.en: I'll meet you there after I return these books to the library across the road.
examples.zh: 我把这些书还到马路对面的图书馆后，「在那儿跟你碰头」。

examples.en: I'll meet you there because I need to go back for my jacket before the film.
examples.zh: 电影开始前，我得回去拿夹克，所以「我在那儿跟你碰头」。

collocations: I'll meet you there after class

words.enDefinition: A firm reply accepting an invitation when people are counting possible attendees.

examples.en: I'm a definite yes for Friday now that someone has agreed to cover my shift.
examples.zh: 已经有人答应帮我代班了，星期五的活动「我确定参加」。

examples.en: Tell Maya I'm a definite yes before she books the seats for the outdoor film.
examples.zh: 玛雅订露天电影的座位之前，告诉她「我确定参加」。

collocations: I'm a definite yes for Friday
tell the group I'm a definite yes

words.enDefinition: A message estimating you will reach the meeting place in about ten minutes.

examples.en: I'm about ten minutes away, so you can start picking out a spot on the lawn.
examples.zh: 「我大概还有十分钟到」，你们可以先在草坪上挑个地方。

examples.en: I sent “I'm about ten minutes away” as the bus left the stop outside campus.
examples.zh: 公交车离开校园外的站点时，我发消息说「我大概还有十分钟到」。

collocations: text I'm about ten minutes away
tell the group I'm about ten minutes away
say I'm about ten minutes away

words.enDefinition: A message saying you are at an entrance other than the one your group agreed on.

examples.en: I think I'm at the wrong entrance because I can only see the car park.
examples.zh: 我只能看见停车场，可能「我走错入口了」。

examples.en: I texted “I'm at the wrong entrance” after seeing the sign for the staff offices.
examples.zh: 看见员工办公室的指示牌后，我发消息说「我走错入口了」。

collocations: say I'm at the wrong entrance
text I'm at the wrong entrance
tell your friends I'm at the wrong entrance

words.enDefinition: A reply saying the speaker can adjust to the time other people choose.

examples.en: I'm flexible on the time because my only Saturday class was canceled this week.
examples.zh: 我星期六唯一一节课这周取消了，「时间我可以配合」。

examples.en: I'm flexible on the time if you want to wait for Mina's shift to end.
examples.zh: 如果你们想等米娜下班，「时间我可以配合」。

collocations: say I'm flexible on the time
tell the group I'm flexible on the time
I'm flexible on the time this weekend

words.enDefinition: An informal reply saying you want to take part in a suggested activity.

examples.en: I replied “I'm up for it” as soon as they suggested a walk by the river.
examples.zh: 他们一提议去河边散步，我就回了句「我愿意参加」。

examples.en: Maya wrote “I'm up for it” under my message about meeting for coffee on Sunday.
examples.zh: 玛雅在我约大家星期天喝咖啡的消息下说「我愿意参加」。

collocations: a message reading I'm up for it

words.enDefinition: a message suggested indirectly by the way something is expressed

examples.en: I couldn't tell the implied meaning until my friend explained the situation.
examples.zh: 朋友解释当时的情形后，我才听懂「言外之意」。

examples.en: We compared the implied meaning of the same reply in two different conversations.
examples.zh: 我们对比了同一句回复在两段不同对话里的「言外之意」。

words.enDefinition: A social event that comes together without much planning in advance.

examples.en: Our coffee break turned into an impromptu gathering when two other classmates walked past.
examples.zh: 另外两位同学路过后，我们喝咖啡的休息时间变成了一次「临时聚会」。

examples.en: We had an impromptu gathering in the courtyard after the afternoon seminar was canceled.
examples.zh: 下午的研讨课取消后，我们在庭院里搞了场「临时聚会」。

words.enDefinition: a joke whose meaning is shared by a particular group

examples.en: I didn't get the in-joke until another student explained the story.
examples.zh: 另一位同学说了来龙去脉，我才听懂那个「圈内人才懂的玩笑」。

examples.en: The mistake on our first worksheet soon became an in-joke among us.
examples.zh: 第一张练习纸上的那个错，很快变成了我们「圈内人才懂的玩笑」。

words.enDefinition: indicates that something else is requested instead of presents

examples.en: My friend asked for library donations in lieu of gifts this year.
examples.zh: 朋友请大家今年向图书馆捐款「代替送礼」。

examples.en: The family collected donations in lieu of gifts at their celebration last weekend.
examples.zh: 上周末庆祝活动上，这家人收取捐款「代替送礼」。

collocations: give a donation in lieu of gifts
collect books in lieu of gifts
ask for something in lieu of gifts

words.enDefinition: an introduction limiting a practice to what one's family normally does

examples.en: In my family, we usually save a small piece of cake for anyone absent.
examples.zh: 「我们家一般会」给没到场的人留一小块蛋糕。

examples.en: In my family, we usually make the cards ourselves before a reunion.
examples.zh: 「我们家一般会」在聚会前自己做卡片。

collocations: “In my family, we usually make it together”
“In my family, we usually keep it simple”
“In my family, we usually celebrate at home”

words.enDefinition: likely to offend or upset people because it shows poor judgment

examples.en: I thought the comment was in poor taste after our friend had left.
examples.zh: 朋友走后，我觉得那条评论「不得体」。

examples.en: The group agreed that the caption was in poor taste for a public poster.
examples.zh: 大家一致觉得，把那句话放在公开海报上「不得体」。

words.enDefinition: attending the same lessons as another person

examples.en: I thought we were in the same class before she mentioned the afternoon section.
examples.zh: 在她提到下午的班以前，我以为我们「在同一个班」。

examples.en: We discovered that we were in the same class when we compared our timetables.
examples.zh: 我们看了下彼此的课表，发现「在同一个班」。

collocations: find out you're in the same class
meet someone in the same class

words.enDefinition: to give each person in a group a place in an activity or decision

examples.en: We tried to include everyone when we made plans around people's different class schedules.
examples.zh: 安排活动时，我们考虑了不同课表，尽量「把每个人都包括进来」。

examples.en: They wanted to include everyone in the photo before people left for the station.
examples.zh: 在有人去车站前，他们想把「每个人都拍进」照片里。

collocations: find a way to include everyone

words.zhGloss: 包容不同参与者的活动
words.enDefinition: an event planned so people with varied needs or backgrounds can participate
acceptedZhAnswers: 包容不同参与者的活动

examples.en: We wanted an inclusive event where students could bring different parts of themselves.
examples.zh: 我们想办一场「包容不同参与者的活动」，让同学们能自在展现自己的不同面向。

examples.en: The group asked attendees what would make it feel like an inclusive event.
examples.zh: 小组问出席者，怎样才会让他们觉得这是一场「包容不同参与者的活动」。

collocations: help make an inclusive event welcoming

words.enDefinition: the US holiday on July fourth marking the country's declaration of independence

examples.en: My host family invited me to a picnic on Independence Day near the river.
examples.zh: 寄宿家庭邀请我在「美国独立日」当天到河边野餐。

examples.en: The city announced extra train service for its Independence Day events that evening.
examples.zh: 市里宣布为当晚的「美国独立日」活动增开列车。

words.enDefinition: a request expressed through a hint rather than a direct instruction

examples.en: I didn't realise her comment about the window was an indirect request.
examples.zh: 我没意识到她提起窗户是在「委婉提出请求」。

examples.en: The tutor asked which line in the dialogue sounded like an indirect request.
examples.zh: 导师问对话中哪一句听起来像「委婉请求」。

words.enDefinition: sweets with a separate wrapper around each piece or serving

examples.en: The residence volunteers brought individually wrapped candy to share outside the common room.
examples.zh: 宿舍志愿者带了些「独立包装的糖果」，在公共休息室外分享。

examples.en: The bag of individually wrapped candy made it easy to refill our bowl.
examples.zh: 有了这一袋「独立包装的糖果」，往碗里添糖很方便。

words.enDefinition: a small group of the people someone trusts or spends most time with

examples.en: Only her inner circle knew she was thinking of changing universities that year.
examples.zh: 只有她「最亲近的小圈子」里的人知道，她那年在考虑转学。

examples.en: He invited his inner circle to a small lunch before leaving for his placement.
examples.zh: 动身去实习前，他请「最亲近的小圈子」一起简单吃了顿午饭。

words.enDefinition: a conversation in which people with different cultural backgrounds learn from each other

examples.en: Our club held an intercultural dialogue about how students mark the end of term.
examples.zh: 我们社团组织了一场「跨文化对话」，交流同学们怎样纪念学期结束。

examples.en: The intercultural dialogue brought together students who had never taken a class together.
examples.zh: 这场「跨文化对话」让从没一起上过课的同学聚到了一起。

words.enDefinition: a practical session for exploring different cultural perspectives or practices

examples.en: Our intercultural workshop began with two students showing how their families made tea.
examples.zh: 我们的「跨文化工作坊」一开始，两名同学演示了各自家里怎么泡茶。

examples.en: I brought an object from home to the intercultural workshop on Thursday.
examples.zh: 周四去「跨文化工作坊」时，我带了一件从家里拿来的物品。

words.enDefinition: conversation among people with different religious or nonreligious beliefs

examples.en: The student society organised an interfaith dialogue about what people do in difficult times.
examples.zh: 学生社团组织了一场「不同信仰间的对话」，聊遇到难事时各自会怎么做。

examples.en: I attended an interfaith dialogue and listened to experiences different from my own.
examples.zh: 我参加了「不同信仰间的对话」，听到一些和我不同的经历。

collocations: take part in an interfaith dialogue

words.enDefinition: to decide what a movement used for communicating is meant to imply

examples.en: I didn't know how to interpret a gesture my classmate made at supper.
examples.zh: 吃晚饭时，同学比了个手势，我不知道怎么「理解它的含义」。

examples.en: Our group discussed whether to interpret a gesture differently when the setting changes.
examples.zh: 我们小组讨论了换个场合是否要用不同方式「理解手势的含义」。

collocations: ask how to interpret a gesture

words.enDefinition: to present a newcomer to several people who are together

examples.en: It helps to introduce someone to the group before everyone splits off into smaller conversations.
examples.zh: 大家分头聊天前，「把新来的人介绍给大家」会有帮助。

examples.en: The mentor always offers to introduce someone to the group when they arrive a little late.
examples.zh: 有人稍晚一点到时，学长总会主动「把这人介绍给大家」。

collocations: offer to introduce someone to the group
ask a host to introduce someone to the group
remember to introduce someone to the group

words.enDefinition: to tell new people your name and basic information

examples.en: Our orientation leader asked everyone to introduce yourself to the person beside them.
examples.zh: 迎新带队的同学请大家向旁边的人「自我介绍」。

examples.en: You can introduce yourself with just your name if the group is large.
examples.zh: 如果人很多，你可以只报个名字来「自我介绍」。

words.enDefinition: a question that asks for more private information than is appropriate

examples.en: I changed the subject after someone asked an intrusive question about my income.
examples.zh: 有人问了一个「贸然打探我收入的问题」，我就换了话题。

examples.en: My classmate explained why the request sounded like an intrusive question to her.
examples.zh: 同学解释了为什么在她听来，那是一个「贸然打探私事的问题」。

words.enDefinition: Restricted to people who have been personally invited.

examples.en: The screening was invite-only because our friends were borrowing a very small room for it.
examples.zh: 这次放映「仅限受邀者参加」，因为朋友们借用的房间很小。

examples.en: I checked whether the picnic was invite-only before telling my new roommate about it.
examples.zh: 我先问野餐是否「仅限受邀者参加」，才把消息告诉新室友。

words.enDefinition: dance forms from Irish tradition, including both solo and group styles

examples.en: The festival programme listed Irish dancing on the outdoor stage just after lunch.
examples.zh: 节庆节目单写着，午饭过后露天舞台会表演「爱尔兰舞」。

examples.en: My cousin took classes in Irish dancing and performed at the community centre.
examples.zh: 表亲上过「爱尔兰舞」课，还在社区中心表演过。

words.enDefinition: ancestry or cultural traditions passed on from Ireland or Irish communities

examples.en: The library put together a display about Irish heritage in our town that spring.
examples.zh: 那年春天，图书馆做了一个介绍当地「爱尔兰文化传承」的展览。

examples.en: My classmate gave a short talk about her family's Irish heritage before the concert.
examples.zh: 音乐会前，同学简短介绍了她家的「爱尔兰文化传承」。

words.expression: is it warm enough in here
words.lemma: is it warm enough in here
words.enDefinition: checks whether the temperature of a room is comfortable
acceptedEnVariants: is it warm enough in here

examples.en: Is it warm enough in here, or would you like me to turn the heating up?
examples.zh: 「屋里够暖和吗」？要不要我把暖气调高一点？

examples.en: My host asked, "Is it warm enough in here?" when I kept my sweater on indoors.
examples.zh: 我进屋没脱毛衣，主人问：「屋里够暖和吗」？

collocations: so is it warm enough in here
is it warm enough in here for you
ask if it's warm enough in here

words.enDefinition: checks whether water from the tap is acceptable to a guest

examples.en: My host asked, "Is tap water okay?" before filling a jug for the table.
examples.zh: 主人往餐桌上的水壶装水之前问：「喝自来水可以吗」？

examples.en: Is tap water okay, or would you rather have something warm on a cold day?
examples.zh: 「喝自来水可以吗」？还是天冷，你想来点热的？

collocations: ask if tap water is okay
is tap water okay for you
is tap water okay with dinner

words.enDefinition: a question asking whether a practice is particular to someone's family

examples.en: “Is that a family tradition?” I asked about the meal she had described.
examples.zh: 她描述那顿饭后，我问「那是你家的传统吗？」

examples.en: My roommate asked, “Is that a family tradition?” after hearing about our song.
examples.zh: 听我讲完我们唱的那首歌后，室友问「那是你家的传统吗？」

collocations: “Is that a family tradition for birthdays?”
“Is that a family tradition or something newer?”

words.expression: is there somewhere I can change
words.lemma: is there somewhere i can change
words.enDefinition: asks whether a private place is available to change clothes
acceptedEnVariants: is there somewhere I can change

examples.en: Is there somewhere I can change? My jeans got soaked on the walk from the bus.
examples.zh: 「有地方让我换衣服吗」？从公交站走过来时，我的牛仔裤湿透了。

examples.en: Is there somewhere I can change before we leave for the concert? I brought another shirt.
examples.zh: 去听音乐会之前，「有地方让我换衣服吗」？我带了另一件衬衫。

collocations: is there somewhere I can change first
is there somewhere I can change before dinner
ask if there's somewhere I can change

words.expression: is this the end of the line
words.lemma: is this the end of the line
words.enDefinition: a question checking where people should join a queue
acceptedEnVariants: is this the end of the line

examples.en: The queue curved around the corner, so I asked, “Is this the end of the line?”
examples.zh: 队伍拐过了街角，我就问「这里是队尾吗？」

examples.en: “Is this the end of the line?” my friend asked outside the hall.
examples.zh: 朋友在礼堂外问「这里是队尾吗？」

collocations: ask “Is this the end of the line?”
“Excuse me, is this the end of the line?”
“Is this the end of the line for the talk?”

words.enDefinition: an informal expression saying a long time has passed since something happened

examples.en: “It's been ages since we last saw each other,” she said outside the library.
examples.zh: 在图书馆外她说：“我们上次见面到现在「已经好久了」。”

examples.en: I smiled and said, “It's been ages,” when my old classmate sat beside me.
examples.zh: 老同学在我旁边坐下时，我笑着说：“「好久没见了」。”

collocations: it's been ages since we met
it's been ages since we spoke

words.enDefinition: tells a giver that their gift matches what you wanted

examples.en: It's exactly what I wanted. I kept looking at the same mug in the shop.
examples.zh: 「这正是我想要的」。我在店里反复看了同一个马克杯。

examples.en: I opened the parcel and said, "It's exactly what I wanted. Thank you for remembering."
examples.zh: 我打开包裹说：「这正是我想要的」。谢谢你还记得。

collocations: wow, it's exactly what I wanted
honestly, it's exactly what I wanted
I can't believe it's exactly what I wanted

words.enDefinition: says the kindness behind a gesture matters more than the gift

examples.en: It's the thought that counts, and I'm glad you remembered the colour I like.
examples.zh: 「心意最重要」，而且你记得我喜欢什么颜色，我很高兴。

examples.en: When I worried about the cost, she said, "It's the thought that counts. I love it."
examples.zh: 我担心礼物的价钱时，她说：「心意最重要」。我喜欢。

collocations: remember, it's the thought that counts
don't worry, it's the thought that counts
in the end, it's the thought that counts

words.enDefinition: Introduces the time a class ends when explaining when you can meet.

examples.en: I've got class until six, so can we get coffee a little later today?
examples.zh: 「我的课要上到六点」，今天能晚一点再喝咖啡吗？

examples.en: I've got class until lunchtime, but I can meet you after your library shift.
examples.zh: 「我的课要上到午饭时间」，但你在图书馆下班后我可以见你。

words.enDefinition: a pumpkin cut into a face or design and lit inside

examples.en: Our jack-o'-lantern had a crooked smile, but everyone liked it.
examples.zh: 我们的「南瓜灯」笑得有点歪，但大家都很喜欢。

examples.en: A glowing jack-o'-lantern stood on the steps outside my friend's apartment.
examples.zh: 朋友公寓门外的台阶上摆着一个发亮的「南瓜灯」。

words.expression: join in at your own pace
words.lemma: join in at your own pace
words.enDefinition: to start participating gradually as you become comfortable
acceptedEnVariants: join in at your own pace

examples.en: The workshop host said you could join in at your own pace.
examples.zh: 工作坊主持人说，大家可以「按自己的节奏参与」。

examples.en: “You can join in at your own pace,” my neighbour said during the game.
examples.zh: 邻居告诉我，玩游戏时可以「按自己的节奏参与」。

collocations: be free to join in at your own pace
feel welcome to join in at your own pace
leave room to join in at your own pace

words.enDefinition: a temporary space at a fair where judges evaluate competition entries

examples.en: The pumpkin exhibits stood outside the judging tent before the fair opened that morning.
examples.zh: 那天上午集市开放前，参展南瓜摆在「展品评比帐篷」外。

examples.en: My host family showed me the judging tent after taking me around the fair.
examples.zh: 寄宿家庭带我逛了一圈集市，又带我看了「展品评比帐篷」。

words.enDefinition: a sudden moment intended to make people jump in fright

examples.en: I spilled popcorn during a jump scare at the Halloween film screening.
examples.zh: 万圣节电影放到一个「突然惊吓的桥段」，我把爆米花都洒了。

examples.en: My friend warned me about the jump scare just before the music stopped.
examples.zh: 音乐停下来之前，朋友就提醒我有个「突然惊吓的桥段」。

collocations: warn someone about a jump scare

words.zhGloss: 美国六月十九日解放纪念日
words.enDefinition: a US holiday commemorating the announcement of emancipation in Galveston, Texas, on June nineteenth, 1865
acceptedZhAnswers: 美国六月十九日解放纪念日

examples.en: The campus museum organised a public history event for Juneteenth in its courtyard.
examples.zh: 校园博物馆在庭院里为「美国六月十九日解放纪念日」办了一场公众历史活动。

examples.en: I went to a talk about Juneteenth with people from my summer class.
examples.zh: 我和夏季课程的同学去听了一场关于「美国六月十九日解放纪念日」的讲座。

words.enDefinition: easily reachable by telephone whenever someone needs you

examples.en: My sister said she was just a phone call away during my first semester.
examples.zh: 姐姐说，我第一学期有事「打个电话就能联系到她」。

examples.en: It helped to know that my old roommate was still just a phone call away.
examples.zh: 知道以前的室友仍然「打个电话就能联系到」，让我安心。

collocations: remember I'm just a phone call away
always just a phone call away

words.enDefinition: a phrase asking that something said remain private between the people talking

examples.en: “This is just between us for now,” he said before sharing his news.
examples.zh: 他先说“这事目前「只限咱俩知道」”，才讲了自己的消息。

examples.en: I hoped the conversation would stay just between us until I had spoken to everyone.
examples.zh: 我希望在跟每个人都说过之前，这段谈话「只限咱俩知道」。

words.enDefinition: says that someone has recently come to live in this place

examples.en: I just moved here from another town and still use the map every day.
examples.zh: 我从外地「刚搬到这儿」，现在还是每天要看地图。

examples.en: Two of us had just moved here and needed directions to the bus stop.
examples.zh: 我们有两个人「刚搬到这儿」，还得问怎么去公交站。

collocations: tell someone you've just moved here
just moved here from another city

words.enDefinition: A communal feast held as part of Kwanzaa observances.

examples.en: My neighbor invited two students to a Karamu at the community center across the road.
examples.zh: 邻居邀请两位同学去马路对面的社区中心参加「宽扎节团聚宴」。

examples.en: The program listed a Karamu after the afternoon readings and performances in the main hall.
examples.zh: 节目单上写着，大厅下午的朗读和表演之后有一场「宽扎节团聚宴」。

words.expression: keep a date in the diary
