words.lemma: keep a date in the diary
words.enDefinition: to leave an agreed meeting on the calendar despite changing plans
acceptedEnVariants: keep a date in the diary

examples.en: We managed to keep a date in the diary through our busiest exam weeks.
examples.zh: 即使最忙的考试周，我们也设法「让约定留在日程上」。

examples.en: To keep a date in the diary, we picked one evening everyone could protect.
examples.zh: 为了「让约定留在日程上」，我们选了一个大家都能留空的晚上。

collocations: try to keep a date in the diary
agree to keep a date in the diary
find a way to keep a date in the diary

words.enDefinition: to avoid telling others information that someone wants to remain private

examples.en: My roommate asked whether I could keep a secret about her new job offer.
examples.zh: 室友问我能不能为她新拿到的工作机会「保守秘密」。

examples.en: I knew she could keep a secret, so I told her before our classmates.
examples.zh: 我知道她能「保守秘密」，就先告诉了她，没先告诉其他同学。

collocations: ask someone to keep a secret
be able to keep a secret

words.enDefinition: to continue a custom so it is not forgotten

examples.en: The students wanted to keep a tradition alive by teaching their friends the game.
examples.zh: 同学们想把这个游戏教给朋友，「让传统延续下去」。

examples.en: My aunt records old songs to help keep a tradition alive for our family.
examples.zh: 我姨妈录下老歌，帮助「让家里的传统延续下去」。

collocations: work to keep a tradition alive
aim to keep a tradition alive

words.enDefinition: to avoid making a conversation serious or uncomfortable

examples.en: I tried to keep it light by asking about her favourite campus lunch.
examples.zh: 我想「保持话题轻松」，就问她喜欢学校哪种午餐。

examples.en: We decided to keep it light while everyone was still getting to know each other.
examples.zh: 大家还在彼此熟悉的阶段，我们决定「保持话题轻松」。

collocations: keep it light with a joke

words.enDefinition: To keep a gathering relaxed and simple without making it elaborate.

examples.en: We wanted to keep it low-key after exams, so we just met for tea.
examples.zh: 考完试我们想「简单低调地聚一下」，就只约着喝了个茶。

examples.en: Let's keep it low-key this time and play some music in the common room.
examples.zh: 这次「简单低调地办」吧，在公共休息室放点音乐就好。

words.enDefinition: To limit the number of people involved in a gathering.

examples.en: We decided to keep it small because there were only six seats in the lounge.
examples.zh: 休息室只有六个座位，我们决定「办个小规模聚会」。

examples.en: Can we keep it small this time and just invite the people from our seminar?
examples.zh: 这次咱们能不能「就小范围聚一下」，只邀请研讨课上的同学？

words.enDefinition: To speak more quietly as a group so others are not disturbed.

examples.en: Let's keep our voices down because the students next door are studying for exams.
examples.zh: 隔壁同学在复习备考，「咱们说话小声点」吧。

examples.en: We tried to keep our voices down while choosing a film in the shared lounge.
examples.zh: 在共用休息室选电影时，我们尽量「说话小声点」。

collocations: try to keep our voices down
need to keep our voices down
ask everyone to keep their voices down

words.expression: keep personal details out of the chat
words.lemma: keep personal details out of the chat
words.zhGloss: 别把私人信息发到群里
words.enDefinition: to avoid putting private information in a shared conversation
acceptedZhAnswers: 别把私人信息发到群里
acceptedEnVariants: keep personal details out of the chat

examples.en: Our tutor asked us to keep personal details out of the chat during the online briefing.
examples.zh: 线上说明会期间，导师请我们「别把私人信息发到群里」。

examples.en: The moderator reminded the group to keep personal details out of the chat.
examples.zh: 群管理员提醒大家「别把私人信息发到群里」。

collocations: ask people to keep personal details out of the chat
remember to keep personal details out of the chat
agree to keep personal details out of the chat

words.enDefinition: to leave phones elsewhere during a shared meal

examples.en: We agreed to keep phones off the table during the group's dinner.
examples.zh: 我们商量好，小组聚餐时「别把手机放在餐桌上」。

examples.en: The host asked if we could keep phones off the table until dessert.
examples.zh: 主持人问我们在上甜点前能不能「别把手机放在餐桌上」。

collocations: agree to keep phones off the table
ask diners to keep phones off the table
keep phones off the table during the meal

words.enDefinition: to make another person wait longer than expected

examples.en: I didn't want to keep someone waiting while I looked for my coat.
examples.zh: 我找外套时不想「让别人一直等」。

examples.en: Our coordinator said it was easy to keep someone waiting when a message went unread.
examples.zh: 协调员说，消息要是一直没被看到，就容易「让别人一直等」。

collocations: try not to keep someone waiting
feel bad about keeping someone waiting

words.enDefinition: to help people keep talking without the exchange ending

examples.en: I asked about the neighborhood to keep the conversation going while we waited outside.
examples.zh: 我们在外面等的时候，我问起附近的情况，好「让聊天继续下去」。

examples.en: A shared interest in old films helped keep the conversation going well after dinner.
examples.zh: 两人都喜欢老电影，所以晚饭结束好一会儿还能「接着聊下去」。

collocations: ask questions to keep the conversation going
try to keep the conversation going
manage to keep the conversation going

words.enDefinition: to decide not to share personal matters with a wider group of people

examples.en: We chose to keep things private until both of us felt ready to tell friends.
examples.zh: 在两人都准备好告诉朋友之前，我们选择「不公开关系细节」。

examples.en: They agreed to keep things private even after their classmates knew they were dating.
examples.zh: 即使同学知道他们在交往，两人仍同意「不公开关系细节」。

words.enDefinition: to avoid passing the discussion or information beyond a group

examples.en: I asked people to keep this in the group until the schedule was final.
examples.zh: 我请大家在日程确定前「先别把这件事传出群」。

examples.en: The club coordinator wrote, “Please keep this in the group for now.”
examples.zh: 社团协调员写道「请暂时只在群里说这件事」。

collocations: please keep this in the group
ask people to keep this in the group
keep this in the group for now

words.expression: keep up with a fast conversation
words.lemma: keep up with a fast conversation
words.enDefinition: to follow what people say when they speak quickly
acceptedEnVariants: keep up with a fast conversation

examples.en: I couldn't keep up with a fast conversation over lunch that first week.
examples.zh: 第一周午餐时，我没法「跟上语速快的谈话」。

examples.en: It took me a while to keep up with a fast conversation in English.
examples.zh: 过了好一阵，我才能「跟上语速很快的英语谈话」。

collocations: struggle to keep up with a fast conversation
try to keep up with a fast conversation
learn to keep up with a fast conversation

words.enDefinition: to stay informed about what is happening in friends' lives

examples.en: I find it easier to keep up with friends when we send short messages.
examples.zh: 我们发简短的消息时，我更容易「了解朋友的近况」。

examples.en: My summer shifts meant I could only keep up with friends on Sundays.
examples.zh: 暑假排班让我只能在周日「了解朋友的近况」。

collocations: try to keep up with friends
find time to keep up with friends
keep up with friends from home

words.enDefinition: an object someone keeps to remember a person or occasion

examples.en: She gave me the tiny note as a keepsake before leaving.
examples.zh: 离开之前，她把那张小纸条送给我作「纪念」。

examples.en: I still have the keepsake from our first dinner together.
examples.zh: 我还留着第一次一起吃晚饭时收到的「纪念物件」。

words.enDefinition: A cup used in some Kwanzaa observances as a symbol of unity.

examples.en: The campus exhibit labeled the cup as kikombe cha umoja and explained its symbolic meaning.
examples.zh: 校园展览把这只杯子标为「宽扎节团结杯」，还解释了它的象征含义。

examples.en: I asked about the kikombe cha umoja when we looked at the community center's display.
examples.zh: 看社区中心的展览时，我问了问「宽扎节团结杯」。

collocations: learn about the kikombe cha umoja

words.enDefinition: A candleholder with space for seven candles used in Kwanzaa celebrations.

examples.en: A wooden kinara stood on the display table in the student center's winter exhibition.
examples.zh: 学生活动中心的冬季展上，陈列桌上摆着一座木制「宽扎节七枝烛台」。

examples.en: My classmate explained the kinara to visitors who had never seen one before.
examples.zh: 同学向头一次见到「宽扎节七枝烛台」的访客介绍了它。

words.enDefinition: someone with similar interests, attitudes, or feelings to your own

examples.en: I found a kindred spirit in the classmate who loved old maps.
examples.zh: 我发现那个喜欢老地图的同学和我「志趣相投」。

examples.en: She called me a kindred spirit after we compared our reading lists.
examples.zh: 对过各自的书单后，她说我们是「志趣相投的人」。

words.enDefinition: to be thoroughly familiar with someone's character, habits, and reactions

examples.en: You can know someone inside out and still be surprised by their career plans.
examples.zh: 即使「非常了解某人」，也可能对对方的职业计划感到意外。

examples.en: She said you don't need to know someone inside out to notice they're unhappy.
examples.zh: 她说，不用「非常了解某人」，也能注意到对方不开心。

collocations: seem to know someone inside out
feel you know someone inside out
claim to know someone inside out

words.enDefinition: A week-long African American and Pan-African holiday honoring African heritage and community.

examples.en: The library set up a display about Kwanzaa beside its books on winter traditions.
examples.zh: 图书馆在冬季习俗图书旁设置了「宽扎节」展区。

examples.en: A classmate explained how his family celebrates Kwanzaa when we planned a year-end exhibition.
examples.zh: 我们筹划年末展览时，一位同学介绍了他家如何过「宽扎节」。

words.enDefinition: a holiday honouring workers on the first Monday in September in the US and Canada

examples.en: The US community pool changed its opening hours after Labor Day at summer's end.
examples.zh: 夏末的「美加劳动节」过后，美国这家社区泳池更改了开放时间。

examples.en: I took the train home for Labour Day before my first classes in Canada.
examples.zh: 我在「美加劳动节」坐火车回家，之后再回加拿大的学校上开学后的第一批课。

words.enDefinition: how comfortable a person feels using a particular language

examples.en: My language confidence grew once I joined a group that met every Friday.
examples.zh: 加入每周五见面的一个小组后，我「使用这门语言的自信」慢慢增加了。

examples.en: My friend said she gained language confidence by trying short conversations at the market.
examples.zh: 朋友说，在市场试着跟人简单聊几句，提升了她「使用这门语言的自信」。

words.enDefinition: A Chinese festival on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month, associated with lanterns.

examples.en: Students hung lanterns in the common room for their Lantern Festival gathering after class.
examples.zh: 同学们下课后在公共休息室挂灯笼，准备举办「元宵节」聚会。

examples.en: We read about the Lantern Festival in a booklet at the winter culture fair.
examples.zh: 我们在冬季文化集市的一本小册子里读到了「元宵节」。

words.enDefinition: A riddle displayed on a lantern or nearby for people to solve at a celebration.

examples.en: We tried to solve a lantern riddle before my classmate read out the answer.
examples.zh: 同学读出答案前，我们试着猜那道「灯谜」。

examples.en: An exchange student wrote a lantern riddle for the festival table outside the library.
examples.zh: 一位交换生给图书馆外的节日摊位写了一道「灯谜」。

collocations: guess the answer to a lantern riddle

words.enDefinition: a venue's rules for admitting people after an event has begun

examples.en: I checked the late entry policy because my evening class might run over.
examples.zh: 晚课可能拖堂，我就查了「迟到入场规定」。

examples.en: The late entry policy was printed on the back of the concert ticket.
examples.zh: 音乐会门票的背面印着「迟到入场规定」。

collocations: follow the venue's late entry policy

words.enDefinition: a message sent late when the recipient may be resting

examples.en: I saw the late-night message the next morning on my way to class.
examples.zh: 第二天去上课的路上，我才看到那条「深夜消息」。

examples.en: The organiser said a late-night message didn't require an immediate reply from anyone.
examples.zh: 组织者说，收到「深夜消息」谁都不用马上回复。

collocations: wait to answer a late-night message

words.enDefinition: a person who arrives after an activity has already started

examples.en: The usher quietly showed a latecomer to a seat near the door.
examples.zh: 引座员轻声指给一名「迟到的人」门边的座位。

examples.en: The only latecomer at the talk waited until the applause to enter.
examples.zh: 讲座唯一「迟到的人」等到掌声响起才走进来。

collocations: show a latecomer to a seat

words.enDefinition: A fried pancake, commonly made from grated potatoes and associated with Hanukkah.

examples.en: I tried a latke with applesauce at the winter gathering in our residence hall.
examples.zh: 我在宿舍楼的冬季聚会上尝了「犹太式炸土豆饼」配苹果酱。

examples.en: My classmate put a latke on each plate while setting out food for visitors.
examples.zh: 同学为来访的人摆餐时，在每个盘子里放了一块「犹太式炸土豆饼」。

words.enDefinition: to place a wreath somewhere as a gesture of remembrance or respect

examples.en: Two students were invited to lay a wreath during the community's May ceremony.
examples.zh: 两名学生受到邀请，在社区五月的纪念仪式上「敬献花圈」。

examples.en: We watched local volunteers lay a wreath at the memorial before the choir sang.
examples.zh: 合唱团演唱前，我们看着当地志愿者在纪念碑前「敬献花圈」。

collocations: lay a wreath at a memorial
invite someone to lay a wreath
lay a wreath in memory of someone

words.enDefinition: To spread a blanket out so a group can sit on it for a picnic.

examples.en: We went early to lay out a picnic blanket under the trees near campus.
examples.zh: 我们提前去了校园附近的树下，「把野餐毯铺好」。

examples.en: Can you help lay out a picnic blanket while the others bring over the food?
examples.zh: 其他人把食物拿过来时，你能帮忙「把野餐毯铺好」吗？

collocations: help lay out a picnic blanket
lay out a picnic blanket on the lawn
lay out a picnic blanket in the shade

words.enDefinition: to encourage someone to believe you are romantically interested when you are not

examples.en: I didn't want to lead someone on by agreeing to go out again.
examples.zh: 我不想答应再约，「让对方误以为我有意」。

examples.en: You can lead someone on if your actions suggest promises you do not mean.
examples.zh: 如果你的行为暗示了自己无意兑现的承诺，就可能「让对方误以为你对其有意」。

collocations: try not to lead someone on

words.enDefinition: the activity of going to see leaves changing colour in autumn

examples.en: A few of us went leaf peeping after the morning club meeting.
examples.zh: 社团上午开完会后，我们几个人出门「观赏秋叶」。

examples.en: I'd never heard of leaf peeping before my roommate invited me along.
examples.zh: 室友叫我一起去之前，我没听说过「观赏秋叶」这项活动。

words.enDefinition: to learn about a custom by seeing or experiencing it yourself

examples.en: I wanted to learn about a tradition first-hand by watching my friend prepare the meal.
examples.zh: 我想看朋友准备这顿饭，「亲身了解一项传统」。

examples.en: The exhibit let visitors learn about a tradition first-hand from the people who practise it.
examples.zh: 展览让参观者跟践行这一传统的人交流，「亲身了解一项传统」。

collocations: a chance to learn about a tradition first-hand
help people learn about a tradition first-hand
learn about a tradition first-hand from participants

words.enDefinition: to become able to remember what the people present are called

examples.en: The name game helped me learn everyone's names before our first lunch together.
examples.zh: 大家第一次一起吃午饭前，名字游戏帮我「记住了所有人的名字」。

examples.en: I need another tutorial to learn everyone's names in my new group.
examples.zh: 我还得再上一次辅导课，才能「记住新小组所有人的名字」。

words.enDefinition: to go away during a pause rather than while an event continues

examples.en: I asked if I could leave during the break to catch the bus.
examples.zh: 我问能不能「在中场休息时离开」，好去赶公交。

examples.en: We decided to leave during the break so we wouldn't interrupt the lecture.
examples.zh: 我们决定「在中场休息时离开」，这样不会打断讲座。

collocations: plan to leave during the break
ask whether you can leave during the break

words.expression: leave me out of the booking
words.lemma: leave me out of the booking
words.enDefinition: A request not to include the speaker when reserving seats or tickets for the group.
acceptedEnVariants: leave me out of the booking

examples.en: Please leave me out of the booking if you have to pay for everyone today.
examples.zh: 如果今天必须一次性付齐，「预订时别算我」。

examples.en: You can leave me out of the booking because my ticket is already covered.
examples.zh: 我的票已经有了，「预订时别算我」。

collocations: ask them to leave me out of the booking
leave me out of the booking for now
please leave me out of the booking

words.enDefinition: to fail to include someone in a group or shared activity

examples.en: I didn't want to leave someone out when I wrote invitations to our old classmates.
examples.zh: 给老同学写邀请时，我不想「把谁漏掉」。

examples.en: It can hurt to leave someone out of a conversation without noticing it.
examples.zh: 无意中「把某人排除在谈话之外」，也可能伤到对方。

collocations: leave someone out of the conversation

words.enDefinition: to leave a door slightly open without closing it fully

examples.en: Could you leave the door ajar while I carry the mugs into the lounge?
examples.zh: 我把杯子拿到休息室的时候，你能「把门留条缝」吗？

examples.en: We chose to leave the door ajar so Dad could hear us from his chair.
examples.zh: 我们决定「把门留条缝」，这样爸爸坐在椅子上也能听到我们讲话。

collocations: ask someone to leave the door ajar
remember to leave the door ajar
agree to leave the door ajar briefly

words.expression: leave the place as we found it
words.lemma: leave the place as we found it
words.enDefinition: To restore a shared place to the condition it was in before the group used it.
acceptedEnVariants: leave the place as we found it

examples.en: Let's leave the place as we found it by putting all the tables back afterward.
examples.zh: 「咱们把场地恢复原样」吧，结束后把桌子都放回原位。

examples.en: We wanted to leave the place as we found it after borrowing the common room.
examples.zh: 借用公共休息室之后，我们想「把场地恢复原样」。

collocations: make sure we leave the place as we found it
aim to leave the place as we found it
ask everyone to leave the place as we found it

words.enDefinition: to keep the light by the front door switched on

examples.en: We decided to leave the porch light on while we still had candy to give out.
examples.zh: 还有糖果可以分的时候，我们决定「让门廊灯亮着」。

examples.en: My host asked me to leave the porch light on until the kids came home.
examples.zh: 寄宿家庭的主人请我「让门廊灯亮着」，等孩子们回家。

collocations: remember to leave the porch light on
choose to leave the porch light on
leave the porch light on for visitors

words.enDefinition: To avoid agreeing on a specific time until more information is available.

examples.en: We decided to leave the time open until Maya had checked her weekend shifts.
examples.zh: 我们决定「先不定具体时间」，等玛雅查完周末排班再说。

examples.en: Can we leave the time open until everyone has checked their shifts for that weekend?
examples.zh: 能不能「先不定具体时间」，等大家看完那个周末的排班？

collocations: leave the time open for now
decide to leave the time open
leave the time open until Friday

words.enDefinition: to give someone space to continue what they are doing alone

examples.en: I'll leave you to it while you call your family from the spare room.
examples.zh: 你在备用房间给家人打电话，我就不打扰了，「让你自己忙」。

examples.en: I should leave you to it so you can get ready before everyone arrives.
examples.zh: 我先不打扰了，「让你自己忙」，大家到之前你还能准备一下。

collocations: probably best to leave you to it
happy to leave you to it

words.expression: leave your cutlery on the plate
words.lemma: leave your cutlery on the plate
words.zhGloss: 把用过的餐具放在盘里
words.enDefinition: to rest used utensils on the plate when you have finished eating
acceptedZhAnswers: 把用过的餐具放在盘里
acceptedEnVariants: leave your cutlery on the plate

examples.en: The sign said, “Leave your cutlery on the plate when you've finished eating.”
examples.zh: 牌子写着，吃完后请「把用过的餐具放在盘里」。

examples.en: Our host said, “Leave your cutlery on the plate if you're finished.”
examples.zh: 主持人说「要是吃完了，把用过的餐具放在盘里」。

collocations: please leave your cutlery on the plate
remember to leave your cutlery on the plate
leave your cutlery on the plate after eating

words.enDefinition: offers a visitor a place to put their belongings

examples.en: You can leave your things here while we clear a space for dinner.
examples.zh: 我们收拾餐桌准备开饭时，「东西可以放这儿」。

examples.en: My neighbour said, "Leave your things here," and cleared a spot on the bench.
examples.zh: 邻居说：「东西可以放这儿」，腾出了长凳上的一块地方。

collocations: you can leave your things here
feel free to leave your things here
just leave your things here for now

words.enDefinition: to allow a friendship to become weaker through increasingly little contact

examples.en: I didn't want to let a friendship fade just because my timetable became busy.
examples.zh: 我不想只因课表忙起来就「任由友情淡下来」。

examples.en: She wondered whether she had started to let a friendship fade without meaning to.
examples.zh: 她在想，自己是不是已经无意间「任由友情淡下来」。

collocations: decide to let a friendship fade
try not to let a friendship fade
allow yourself to let a friendship fade

words.enDefinition: to agree to stop dwelling on an old disagreement or wrong

examples.en: My former flatmate wanted to let bygones be bygones when we met again downtown.
examples.zh: 又在市中心见面时，原来的室友希望「过去的事就让它过去」。

examples.en: We decided to let bygones be bygones before planning a reunion together that spring.
examples.zh: 那年春天一起筹划聚会前，我们决定「过去的事就让它过去」。

collocations: decide to let bygones be bygones
agree to let bygones be bygones
ready to let bygones be bygones

words.zhGloss: 先让每个人都分到一点
words.enDefinition: to give everyone a portion before anyone takes more
acceptedZhAnswers: 先让每个人都分到一点

examples.en: Our host asked us to let everyone have some first before taking seconds.
examples.zh: 主持人请我们「先让每个人都分到一点」，再添第二份。

examples.en: I decided to let everyone have some first because the bowl was small.
examples.zh: 碗不大，我决定「先让每个人都分到一点」。

collocations: remember to let everyone have some first
ask guests to let everyone have some first
let everyone have some first before going back

words.enDefinition: offers to help two people meet for the first time

examples.en: I said "Let me introduce you to my neighbour" when my classmate joined us.
examples.zh: 同学走过来时，我说：「我来介绍你们认识」，这是我的邻居。

examples.en: When we reached the table, Mei said "Let me introduce you to my lab partner."
examples.zh: 走到桌边时，阿梅说：「我来介绍你们认识」，这是我的实验搭档。

collocations: let me introduce you to my roommate
let me introduce you to the others
come over and let me introduce you

words.expression: let me know how it goes
words.lemma: let me know how it goes
words.enDefinition: a request for someone to share the outcome of something they are doing
acceptedEnVariants: let me know how it goes

examples.en: “Let me know how it goes,” she said as I left for the interview.
examples.zh: 我出发去面试时，她说：“「告诉我后来怎么样」。”

examples.en: I wrote, “Let me know how it goes when you meet your new supervisor.”
examples.zh: 我写道：“见过新导师后，「告诉我后来怎么样」。”

collocations: let me know how it goes tomorrow
please let me know how it goes
let me know how it goes after your appointment

words.enDefinition: to wait for people to leave before you enter

examples.en: I stepped back to let people out first when the lift doors opened.
examples.zh: 电梯门一开，我往后退了退，「先让里面的人出来」。

examples.en: The attendant asked us to let people out first at the hall entrance.
examples.zh: 引座员让我们在礼堂门口「先让里面的人出来」。

collocations: wait and let people out first
let people out first before entering
remember to let people out first

words.expression: let someone go ahead of you
words.lemma: let someone go ahead of you
words.enDefinition: to allow another person to take a turn before you
acceptedEnVariants: let someone go ahead of you

examples.en: You could let someone go ahead of you while you looked for your ticket.
examples.zh: 找票时，你可以「让别人排到你前面」。

examples.en: My friend asked if you could let someone go ahead of you in line here.
examples.zh: 朋友问在这里排队能不能「让别人排到你前面」。

collocations: choose to let someone go ahead of you
let someone go ahead of you in line
offer to let someone go ahead of you

words.expression: let them know you'll be late
words.lemma: let them know you'll be late
words.zhGloss: 提前告诉对方你会迟到
words.enDefinition: to tell the people expecting you that you will arrive late
acceptedZhAnswers: 提前告诉对方你会迟到
acceptedEnVariants: let them know you'll be late

examples.en: “Let them know you'll be late,” my tutor said when class ran over.
examples.zh: 课程拖堂时，导师说「要提前告诉对方你会迟到」。

examples.en: My roommate said, “Let them know you'll be late,” when the bus stopped.
examples.zh: 公交车停下时，室友说「要提前告诉对方你会迟到」。

collocations: remember to let them know you'll be late
let them know you'll be late by text
let them know you'll be late before the start

words.enDefinition: to enter a building without waiting for someone to open it

examples.en: You can let yourself in if I'm still busy with the laundry upstairs.
examples.zh: 要是我还在楼上忙着洗衣服，「你自己进来就好」。

examples.en: My roommate texted, "Let yourself in. We're both on the back porch."
examples.zh: 室友发消息说：「你自己进来就好」，我们俩都在后面的门廊上。

collocations: feel free to let yourself in
text someone to let yourself in
ask if you can let yourself in

words.expression: let's make it a group thing
words.lemma: let's make it a group thing
words.enDefinition: A suggestion to do a proposed activity with more people.
acceptedEnVariants: let's make it a group thing

examples.en: My roommate said “Let's make it a group thing” and suggested inviting our whole floor.
examples.zh: 室友说「咱们约大家一起吧」，提议把我们这层楼的人都约上。

examples.en: Before we buy tickets, let's make it a group thing and ask our seminar friends.
examples.zh: 买票前「咱们约大家一起吧」，先问问研讨课的同学。

collocations: say let's make it a group thing
suggest that we make it a group thing
make it a group thing this time

words.expression: let's stick with the original plan
words.lemma: let's stick with the original plan
words.enDefinition: A suggestion to keep a plan instead of changing to a newly discussed option.
acceptedEnVariants: let's stick with the original plan

examples.en: Let's stick with the original plan since four people have already bought their tickets.
examples.zh: 已经有四个人买票了，「咱们还是按原计划吧」。

examples.en: Let's stick with the original plan while the weather is still looking good for Sunday.
examples.zh: 看起来星期天天气还不错，「咱们还是按原计划吧」。

collocations: say let's stick with the original plan
let's stick with the original plan for now
reply let's stick with the original plan

words.enDefinition: A suggestion to aim to do the activity sometime in the following week.

examples.en: Let's try for next week because both of us have coursework due on Friday.
examples.zh: 咱俩星期五都要交作业，「咱们试试约在下周吧」。

examples.en: Let's try for next week, when the common room should have more free seats.
examples.zh: 「咱们试试约在下周吧」，到时候公共休息室应该有更多空位。

collocations: suggest let's try for next week
say let's try for next week
let's try for next week instead

words.enDefinition: Lucky money given at Tết in Vietnam, often in a red envelope.

examples.en: My flatmate explained lì xì while showing us a red envelope from her family's Tết celebration.
examples.zh: 室友给我们看她家过越南新年的红包时，介绍了「越南新年压岁钱」。

examples.en: The talk described how relatives in one family gave lì xì to their younger cousins.
examples.zh: 分享中讲到，有一家亲戚会给年纪小的表亲发「越南新年压岁钱」。

collocations: a red envelope holding lì xì

words.enDefinition: a brief account of important recent changes in someone's personal life

examples.en: My roommate sent a life update after she moved away for graduate school.
examples.zh: 室友搬去外地读研后，发来了一段「生活近况分享」。

examples.en: We each gave a short life update at the beginning of our monthly call.
examples.zh: 每月电话开始时，我们每个人都简短做了「生活近况分享」。

words.enDefinition: a friend who remains close through much or all of one's life

examples.en: She never expected her neighbour in first-year residence to become a lifelong friend.
examples.zh: 她没想到大一住隔壁的人会成为「一辈子的朋友」。

examples.en: The first person to call after my graduation was a lifelong friend from home.
examples.zh: 毕业后第一个打来电话的是老家一位「一辈子的朋友」。

words.enDefinition: resembling a familiar, shared experience from the past

examples.en: We ended up talking until midnight again, like old times in our first year.
examples.zh: 我们又聊到了半夜，「就像大一时那样」。

examples.en: Walking home together after the lecture felt like old times to both of us.
examples.zh: 听完讲座一起走回家，两人感觉「就像从前一样」。

words.enDefinition: feeling so familiar that a long absence barely seems noticeable

examples.en: Back in the old café, it felt like we never left after that summer.
examples.zh: 回到老咖啡馆时，暑假过后感觉「就像我们没离开过」。

examples.en: We started telling the same jokes again, like we never left the residence hall.
examples.zh: 我们又讲起同样的笑话，「就像我们没离开过」宿舍楼。

collocations: it was like we never left

words.enDefinition: to stand in rows along the sides of streets, often to watch an event

examples.en: People began to line the streets as soon as the parade music started.
examples.zh: 游行音乐一响起，人们就开始「沿街排开围观」。

examples.en: We watched families line the streets around the square before the festival procession.
examples.zh: 庆典队伍经过前，我们看见许多家庭在广场周围「沿街排开围观」。

collocations: line the streets for a parade

words.enDefinition: A traditional performance in which dancers move together inside a lion costume.

examples.en: We heard drums outside the student center shortly before the lion dance began that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午「舞狮」开始前不久，我们听见学生活动中心外传来鼓声。

examples.en: A visiting troupe performed a lion dance beside the community market for the New Year event.
examples.zh: 一个受邀团队在社区集市旁为新年活动表演了「舞狮」。

words.enDefinition: to allow someone to keep speaking while you listen

examples.en: The facilitator asked everyone to listen without interrupting during the opening round.
examples.zh: 第一轮发言时，引导员请大家「听完对方说话，不打断」。

examples.en: I tried to listen without interrupting when my classmate explained why she disagreed.
examples.zh: 同学解释她为什么不同意时，我尽量「听完对方说话，不打断」。

collocations: ask people to listen without interrupting
take time to listen without interrupting

words.enDefinition: the direct meaning of words apart from figurative use or implication

examples.en: The literal meaning made sense, but I didn't understand why it was funny.
examples.zh: 「字面意思」是懂了，可我没明白它为什么好笑。

examples.en: I knew the literal meaning of the phrase but missed the warm tone.
examples.zh: 我知道那个说法的「字面意思」，却没听出语气里的亲切。

words.enDefinition: to have a room or home on the same building level

examples.en: We discovered we live on the same floor when we both headed for the stairs.
examples.zh: 我们都往楼梯走时，发现彼此「住在同一层」。

examples.en: Four people in my lab group live on the same floor as I do.
examples.zh: 实验小组里有四个人和我「住在同一层」。

collocations: happen to live on the same floor
both live on the same floor
live on the same floor in residence

words.enDefinition: having your home somewhere outside the grounds of the university

examples.en: I was living off campus and wanted to meet other people who commuted.
examples.zh: 我「住在校外」，想认识些也需要通勤来上课的人。

examples.en: Some people living off campus came early so they could introduce themselves before class.
examples.zh: 一些「住在校外」的同学来得早，好在上课前互相认识一下。

collocations: get used to living off campus

words.enDefinition: The communal tossing of yusheng to wish for good fortune, especially in Singapore and Malaysia.

examples.en: A classmate from Singapore introduced lo hei at our Lunar New Year gathering on campus.
examples.zh: 一位新加坡同学在我们的校园农历新年聚会上介绍了「新年捞生习俗」。

examples.en: Our neighbor showed us a video of lo hei from her relatives' celebration in Malaysia.
examples.zh: 邻居给我们看了一段视频，里面是她在马来西亚的亲戚过节时「新年捞生」的场景。

words.enDefinition: a word or phrase mainly heard in a particular area

examples.en: My classmate explained the local expression after I heard it at the market.
examples.zh: 我在市场听到那个「当地用语」后，同学给我解释了它。

examples.en: I jotted down a local expression the guide used for the afternoon break.
examples.zh: 我记下了向导称呼下午休息时间时用的一个「当地用语」。

words.enDefinition: To choose a definite time so the arrangement can go ahead.

examples.en: We need to lock in a time before Mina buys all the tickets tonight.
examples.zh: 米娜今晚买齐所有票之前，我们得「把时间敲定」。

examples.en: Could we lock in a time for coffee after everyone checks their class schedule?
examples.zh: 等大家检查完课表，能不能「敲定时间」一起喝咖啡？

collocations: lock in a time for Saturday
lock in a time that works
need to lock in a time

words.enDefinition: a friendship maintained by people who live far apart

examples.en: Our long-distance friendship began when we went to universities in different countries.
examples.zh: 到不同国家读大学后，我们开始维系这段「异地友情」。

examples.en: The long-distance friendship mattered as much to her as the friendships on her course.
examples.zh: 这段「异地友情」对她来说和同一门课上的友情同样重要。

words.enDefinition: a romantic relationship that has lasted or is intended to last a long time

examples.en: He wanted a long-term relationship but hoped to take things slowly at the beginning.
examples.zh: 他想要一段「长期恋爱关系」，不过刚开始希望慢慢来。

examples.en: My roommate talked about maintaining a long-term relationship while finishing a degree abroad.
examples.zh: 室友聊起怎样在国外完成学位时维系「长期恋爱关系」。

words.enDefinition: a weekend extended by one or more days off

examples.en: We spent the long weekend visiting a friend who had moved farther north.
examples.zh: 「连休小长假」期间，我们去看了一位搬到更北边的朋友。

examples.en: The buses will run less often during the long weekend near the end of May.
examples.zh: 五月底的「连休小长假」期间，公交车班次会少一些。

words.enDefinition: a friend someone has known for a long period

examples.en: I stayed with a longtime friend when I went back for a campus reunion.
examples.zh: 我返校参加聚会时，住在一位「相识多年的朋友」家里。

examples.en: A longtime friend sent a postcard from the city where we first studied together.
examples.zh: 一位「相识多年的朋友」从我们最初一起读书的城市寄来了一张明信片。

words.enDefinition: to stop feeling attracted to someone or wanting to continue seeing them

examples.en: He began to lose interest when their conversations became less frequent over the summer.
examples.zh: 暑假里两人聊得越来越少，他开始「不再感兴趣」。

examples.en: They wondered why people sometimes lose interest after a few dates despite getting along well.
examples.zh: 他们想知道，为什么有时几次约会相处得不错，人还是会「不再感兴趣」。

words.enDefinition: no longer conveyed when a message is expressed in another language

examples.en: The wordplay was lost in translation, although the basic message came through.
examples.zh: 基本意思传达到了，但双关的趣味「在翻译中丢失了」。

examples.en: Some of the song's warmth was lost in translation for my flatmate.
examples.zh: 室友听了译文后，觉得歌里一部分温暖的感觉「在翻译中丢失了」。

words.enDefinition: a brief period when people talking together become quiet

examples.en: I used a lull in the conversation to introduce myself to the person beside me.
examples.zh: 我趁着「聊天间隙」向旁边的人做了自我介绍。

examples.en: Someone brought more tea during a lull in the conversation, and we started talking again.
examples.zh: 有人趁着「聊天间隙」又端来些茶，我们就接着聊了。

collocations: a brief lull in the conversation
fill a lull in the conversation
speak during a lull in the conversation

words.enDefinition: The beginning of a lunisolar year, celebrated in a number of East and Southeast Asian traditions.

examples.en: Our student center hosted a Lunar New Year event with displays on several different traditions.
examples.zh: 学生活动中心办了「农历新年」活动，展示了几种不同的习俗。

examples.en: Some of my classmates mark Lunar New Year at home, while others go to local gatherings.
examples.zh: 有些同学在家庆祝「农历新年」，有些会去参加当地的聚会。

collocations: travel home for Lunar New Year

words.enDefinition: A seasonal market selling festive plants and decorations, held in places such as Hong Kong.

examples.en: My flatmate showed us photos from a Lunar New Year flower market in Hong Kong.
examples.zh: 室友给我们看了她在香港「农历新年花市」拍的照片。

examples.en: The culture club's display featured a stall sign from a Lunar New Year flower market.
examples.zh: 文化社的展览中有一块从「农历新年花市」来的摊位招牌。

collocations: visit a Lunar New Year flower market
browse a Lunar New Year flower market
a stall at a Lunar New Year flower market

words.enDefinition: A public procession marking Lunar New Year with performances or decorated displays.

examples.en: My roommate and I watched the Lunar New Year parade near our usual bus stop.
examples.zh: 我和室友在常去的公交站旁看了「农历新年巡游」。

examples.en: The student band was invited to play in the Lunar New Year parade downtown this winter.
examples.zh: 学生乐队受邀在这个冬天的市中心「农历新年巡游」上演出。

collocations: watch a Lunar New Year parade
take part in a Lunar New Year parade
a route for the Lunar New Year parade

words.enDefinition: The last evening or day before the new year begins in a lunisolar calendar.

examples.en: We called our relatives on Lunar New Year's Eve before joining our roommates for dinner.
examples.zh: 「农历新年前夕」，我们先给亲戚打了电话，再和室友一起吃饭。

examples.en: On Lunar New Year's Eve, my classmate video-called her relatives in Vietnam from our lounge.
examples.zh: 「农历新年前夕」，同学在休息室和越南的亲戚打了视频电话。

collocations: a Lunar New Year's Eve dinner
gather on Lunar New Year's Eve

words.enDefinition: A calendar that uses lunar months and keeps the year aligned with the seasons.

examples.en: Our lecturer explained the lunisolar calendar when someone asked why the festival's date moves.
examples.zh: 有人问节日日期为什么会变，老师就讲了「阴阳历」。

examples.en: The exhibition compared a lunisolar calendar with the calendar on our campus noticeboard to illustrate the difference.
examples.zh: 展览用一种「阴阳历」和校园公告栏上的日历作对照，来说明二者的差别。

words.enDefinition: to continue a friendship through sustained contact or shared effort

examples.en: It took more effort to maintain a friendship once we stopped sharing a timetable.
examples.zh: 不再共用一份课表后，「维系一段友情」要花更多心思。

examples.en: They found it easy to maintain a friendship even while studying in separate cities.
examples.zh: 即使在不同城市读书，他们也觉得「维系一段友情」并不难。

words.enDefinition: to give a person unusually attentive or affectionate treatment

examples.en: You don't have to make a fuss over someone just because they're visiting for dinner.
examples.zh: 别人来吃顿饭，你用不着「对人家格外上心」。

examples.en: My friend said she didn't want us to make a fuss over someone on her birthday.
examples.zh: 朋友说，她生日那天不想我们「对她格外上心」。

collocations: tend to make a fuss over someone
try not to make a fuss over someone
make a fuss over someone who is visiting

words.expression: make a joke at someone's expense
words.lemma: make a joke at someone's expense
words.enDefinition: to make a joke that makes someone else look foolish
acceptedEnVariants: make a joke at someone's expense

examples.en: I didn't want to make a joke at someone's expense during the introductions.
examples.zh: 我不想在介绍环节「拿别人开玩笑」。

examples.en: The club's moderator asked us not to make a joke at someone's expense.
examples.zh: 社团主持人请我们不要「拿别人开玩笑」。

collocations: try not to make a joke at someone's expense
choose not to make a joke at someone's expense
be careful not to make a joke at someone's expense

words.enDefinition: to say something about a person's appearance, habits or character

examples.en: I try not to make a personal remark when commenting on someone's work.
examples.zh: 我对别人的作品发表意见时，尽量不「对别人作私人评价」。

examples.en: The moderator asked us not to make a personal remark about any speaker.
examples.zh: 主持人请我们不要「对发言者作私人评价」。

collocations: try not to make a personal remark
make a personal remark about someone's appearance
be tempted to make a personal remark

words.zhGloss: 让新地方带上自己的印记
words.enDefinition: to give a place a personal feel through familiar touches and routines
acceptedZhAnswers: 让新地方带上自己的印记

examples.en: The speaker described how to make a place your own after moving abroad.
examples.zh: 发言者讲了移居国外后，怎样「让新地方带上自己的印记」。

examples.en: Small things can help you make a place your own, like arranging your favourite books.
examples.zh: 收拾摆放自己喜欢的书之类的小事，能「让新地方带上自己的印记」。

collocations: find ways to make a place your own
help someone make a place your own
make a place your own over time

words.enDefinition: To agree on what people will do together and when.

examples.en: Can we make a plan now so I know whether to bring my camera tomorrow?
examples.zh: 我们能现在就「商量好安排」吗？这样我就知道明天要不要带相机了。

examples.en: We could make a plan after class once everyone knows when their last exams end.
examples.zh: 等大家都知道各自最后一场考试几点结束，我们可以下课后「商量好安排」。

collocations: make a plan in the chat
make a plan to meet after class

words.enDefinition: to do something to repair the harm caused by a mistake

examples.en: He tried to make amends by inviting everyone he had left out before.
examples.zh: 他邀请了之前被自己漏掉的所有人，试着「做点事弥补过失」。

examples.en: I wanted to make amends after realising my joke had embarrassed a friend.
examples.zh: 意识到自己的玩笑让朋友难堪后，我想「做点事弥补过失」。

words.enDefinition: To turn a planned activity into a longer evening out or celebration.

examples.en: Let's make an evening of it and get dinner together before the outdoor film.
examples.zh: 「咱们安排一整晚的活动」吧，先吃饭再去看露天电影。

examples.en: We decided to make an evening of it after handing in our last assignment.
examples.zh: 交完最后一份作业后，我们决定「安排一整晚的活动」庆祝一下。

collocations: decide to make an evening of it
suggest we make an evening of it
make an evening of it after exams

words.enDefinition: to start doing an enjoyable activity together repeatedly

examples.en: Our walk was so relaxing that we decided to make it a regular thing.
examples.zh: 散步太放松了，我们决定「把它变成固定活动」。

examples.en: “Should we make it a regular thing after class?” I asked over lunch.
examples.zh: 吃午饭时我问：“课后要不要「把它变成固定活动」？”

collocations: decide to make it a regular thing
agree to make it a regular thing
want to make it a regular thing

words.expression: make it back for the reunion
words.lemma: make it back for the reunion
words.enDefinition: to be able to return in time for a gathering with people from your past
acceptedEnVariants: make it back for the reunion

examples.en: I hope you can make it back for the reunion before your work term starts.
examples.zh: 希望你工作学期开始前能「赶回去参加聚会」。

examples.en: My old classmate couldn't make it back for the reunion because her train was cancelled.
examples.zh: 火车取消了，老同学没能「赶回去参加聚会」。

collocations: hope to make it back for the reunion
try to make it back for the reunion
be able to make it back for the reunion

words.enDefinition: to explicitly agree that two people are a couple

examples.en: They decided to make it official after studying together for most of their exchange.
examples.zh: 一起学习了大半个交换期之后，他们决定「正式确定恋爱关系」。

examples.en: I wasn't ready to make it official just because our friends assumed we were dating.
examples.zh: 朋友以为我们在交往，可我还没准备好「正式确定恋爱关系」。

words.enDefinition: to welcome others expressing interpretations different from one's own

examples.en: Our chair tried to make room for different viewpoints during the discussion.
examples.zh: 讨论时，主持人尽量「给不同看法留出空间」。

examples.en: Working in pairs helped us make room for different viewpoints in the session.
examples.zh: 两人分组让我们能在活动中「给不同看法留出空间」。

collocations: try to make room for different viewpoints
learn to make room for different viewpoints
help make room for different viewpoints

words.enDefinition: to clear a place for a visitor to put a coat

examples.en: Give me a second to make room for your coat before you sit down.
examples.zh: 你坐下之前稍等一下，我「给你的外套腾个地方」。

examples.en: My host said she would make room for your coat next to the kitchen door.
examples.zh: 主人说会在厨房门边「给我的外套腾个地方」。

collocations: let me make room for your coat
need to make room for your coat
make room for your coat on the rack

words.enDefinition: to behave in a way that puts a newcomer at ease

examples.en: It doesn't take much to make someone feel welcome on their first day here.
examples.zh: 别人在这里的第一天，花一点心思就能「让对方感到受欢迎」。

examples.en: Offering to introduce them can make someone feel welcome when they arrive on their own.
examples.zh: 对方独自到场时，主动帮忙介绍一下，能「让对方感到受欢迎」。

collocations: try to make someone feel welcome
know how to make someone feel welcome

words.zhGloss: 给少发言的人表达的机会
words.enDefinition: to help people who speak less often contribute to a discussion
acceptedZhAnswers: 给少发言的人表达的机会

examples.en: Our moderator paused after each question to make space for quieter voices.
examples.zh: 主持人每问一个问题后就停一停，「给少发言的人表达的机会」。

examples.en: Writing before sharing helped us make space for quieter voices in our team.
examples.zh: 先写下来再分享，帮我们「给小组里少发言的人表达的机会」。

collocations: try to make space for quieter voices
take time to make space for quieter voices
find ways to make space for quieter voices

words.enDefinition: to be the first to show interest or do something about it

examples.en: I decided to make the first move and ask him about coffee after class.
examples.zh: 我决定「主动迈出第一步」，问他下课后要不要喝咖啡。

examples.en: They each hoped the other would make the first move at the club social.
examples.zh: 在社团聚会上，两人都希望对方「主动迈出第一步」。

collocations: decide to make the first move
wait for someone to make the first move
be willing to make the first move

words.enDefinition: to go around a place visiting several people in succession

examples.en: I wanted to make the rounds before I settled into a long conversation.
examples.zh: 我想先「转一圈逐个打招呼」，然后再找人慢慢聊。

examples.en: We had time to make the rounds and say hello to all three groups.
examples.zh: 我们有时间「转一圈逐个打招呼」，三个小组都问候到了。

collocations: make the rounds at a reception
take time to make the rounds

words.enDefinition: to set aside time to be together despite other duties

examples.en: We try to make time for each other even during the busiest weeks of term.
examples.zh: 即便在学期最忙的几周，我们也尽量「抽时间陪伴彼此」。

examples.en: They found ways to make time for each other while working opposite shifts.
examples.zh: 两人上班时间错开，还是想办法「抽时间陪伴彼此」。

collocations: try to make time for each other
find ways to make time for each other
remember to make time for each other

words.enDefinition: to reserve time to talk with someone about what has happened since you last met

examples.en: We promised to make time to catch up before everyone left for summer.
examples.zh: 大家暑假离开前，我们答应「抽空聊聊近况」。

examples.en: I tried to make time to catch up with my school friends every month.
examples.zh: 我尽量每月和以前上学时的朋友「抽空聊聊近况」。

collocations: try to make time to catch up
promise to make time to catch up
always make time to catch up

words.enDefinition: to prepare a bed with sheets for someone who will sleep there

examples.en: My roommate offered to make up the spare bed while I picked up our visitor.
examples.zh: 我去接客人时，室友主动说会「把备用床铺好」。

examples.en: I just need to make up the spare bed before you bring your bag upstairs.
examples.zh: 你把包拿上楼之前，我只要先「把备用床铺好」。

collocations: offer to make up the spare bed
time to make up the spare bed
make up the spare bed for a guest

words.enDefinition: invites someone to relax in a place where they are a guest

examples.en: Make yourself comfortable while I move the papers from this end of the sofa.
examples.zh: 「怎么舒服怎么来」，我把沙发这头的文件挪开。

examples.en: My friend's mum said, "Make yourself comfortable," and offered me the armchair.
examples.zh: 朋友妈妈说：「怎么舒服怎么来」，把扶手椅让给了我。

collocations: come in and make yourself comfortable
go ahead and make yourself comfortable

words.enDefinition: A traditional Hebrew song sung by many people during Hanukkah.

examples.en: The campus choir included Ma'oz Tzur in its program for the winter music evening.
examples.zh: 校园合唱团把「光明节歌曲《坚固磐石》」列入了冬季音乐会的节目单。

examples.en: My roommate recognized Ma'oz Tzur because she had heard her family sing it at Hanukkah.
examples.zh: 室友认出了「光明节歌曲《坚固磐石》」，因为她听过家人在光明节唱这首歌。

words.enDefinition: the Canadian flag featuring a central red maple leaf

examples.en: Someone hung a maple leaf flag outside the residence office for the July holiday.
examples.zh: 为了庆祝七月的节日，有人在宿管办公室外挂了一面「加拿大枫叶旗」。

examples.en: A large maple leaf flag hung behind the band on the outdoor stage.
examples.zh: 户外舞台上的乐队背后挂着一面大大的「加拿大枫叶旗」。

words.enDefinition: to be connected to another person by a dating app after showing interest

examples.en: I didn't expect to match with someone who went to the same university.
examples.zh: 我没想到会「与同一所大学的人配对成功」。

examples.en: Can you match with someone without seeing their whole profile in this app?
examples.zh: 在这个应用里，不看完整资料也能「与某人配对成功」吗？

collocations: match with someone on a dating app

words.enDefinition: flat bread without leaven, eaten during Passover in Jewish tradition

examples.en: The shop put boxes of matzah on a separate shelf before Passover began.
examples.zh: 逾越节开始前，商店把一盒盒「逾越节无酵饼」放在单独的货架上。

examples.en: I tried matzah for the first time at my friend's family dinner that spring.
examples.zh: 那年春天，我在朋友的家宴上第一次尝了「逾越节无酵饼」。

words.enDefinition: in its spring festival sense, a celebration on May first with local seasonal customs

examples.en: We watched maypole dancing at a May Day celebration in a village near campus.
examples.zh: 我们在校园附近一个村庄的「五月节」庆典上看到了彩带柱舞。

examples.en: I learned about May Day traditions during a weekend visit to my friend's village.
examples.zh: 周末去朋友的村子做客时，我了解了「五月节」的习俗。

words.enDefinition: a tall pole often decorated with ribbons for some European spring celebrations

examples.en: The village had a maypole decorated with ribbons in the centre of the green.
examples.zh: 村里的公共草坪中央立着一根扎满彩带的「五月节彩带柱」。

examples.en: The museum guide showed us an old photograph of the maypole beside the school.
examples.zh: 博物馆讲解员给我们看了一张学校旁「五月节彩带柱」的老照片。

words.enDefinition: traditional dancing around a pole, often with ribbons attached to it

examples.en: The children practised maypole dancing on the grass before their families arrived that morning.
examples.zh: 那天上午家人到来前，孩子们在草地上练习「绕五月节彩带柱跳舞」。

examples.en: I watched maypole dancing for the first time at a fair near the university.
examples.zh: 我在大学附近的市集上第一次看见有人「绕五月节彩带柱跳舞」。

words.enDefinition: The crops or produce displayed during Kwanzaa to symbolize the harvest.

examples.en: The fruit on the exhibit table was labeled mazao, with an explanation about the harvest.
examples.zh: 展桌上的水果标为「宽扎节陈设中的农产」，说明文字提到了收获。

examples.en: We asked what the mazao represented while touring the exhibition with our seminar group.
examples.zh: 随研讨班参观展览时，我们问「宽扎节陈设中的农产」代表什么。

words.enDefinition: shows that something another person has said also applies to you

examples.en: Me too, actually. I moved here last week and only know my roommate.
examples.zh: 「其实我也一样」。我上周才搬来，只认识室友。

examples.en: I said, "Me too, actually," when she mentioned getting lost on the first day.
examples.zh: 她说第一天迷了路，我说：「其实我也一样」。

collocations: me too, actually, I thought I was the only one

words.enDefinition: to be introduced to the people close to one's romantic partner

examples.en: We decided to meet each other's friends at the café after our last exam.
examples.zh: 我们决定最后一门考试后在咖啡馆「见见彼此的朋友」。

examples.en: They thought it would be easier to meet each other's friends at a casual picnic.
examples.zh: 他们觉得轻松的野餐更适合「见见彼此的朋友」。

collocations: be ready to meet each other's friends
plan to meet each other's friends
first time you meet each other's friends

words.enDefinition: to arrange an in-person meeting somewhere open to other people

examples.en: They agreed to meet in a public place near the main campus entrance.
examples.zh: 他们约好「在公共场所见面」，就在主校区入口附近。

examples.en: I suggested we meet in a public place both of us already knew.
examples.zh: 我建议「在两人都熟悉的公共场所见面」。

collocations: agree to meet in a public place
choose to meet in a public place
ask to meet in a public place

words.enDefinition: to be introduced to the parents of the person one is dating

examples.en: She felt ready to meet the parents during their short visit to the city.
examples.zh: 伴侣的父母来城里短住时，她觉得可以「去见对方的父母」了。

examples.en: I packed a spare shirt because I was going to meet the parents after class.
examples.zh: 我下课后要「见伴侣的父母」，就多带了一件衬衫。

collocations: be ready to meet the parents
first time you meet the parents

words.enDefinition: A plan to meet someone outside the front of a building or venue.

examples.en: I'll meet you out front when the library closes so we can go together.
examples.zh: 图书馆关门后，我会「在正门外和你碰头」，这样咱们可以一起走。

examples.en: We can meet you out front before everyone heads into the student center for the film.
examples.zh: 大家进学生活动中心看电影前，我们可以「在正门外和你碰头」。

collocations: meet you out front after class

words.enDefinition: a US holiday honouring people who died in military service

examples.en: The library posted a notice about Memorial Day opening hours before classes ended.
examples.zh: 课程结束前，图书馆张贴了「美国阵亡将士纪念日」的开放时间告示。

examples.en: The town held a quiet ceremony on Memorial Day in the square near campus.
examples.zh: 「美国阵亡将士纪念日」当天，镇上在校园附近广场举办了一场安静的纪念仪式。

words.enDefinition: a gathering held to remember a person or people who have died

examples.en: The university choir sang at the memorial service in the old hall on Monday.
examples.zh: 大学合唱团周一在旧礼堂举行的「追思纪念仪式」上献唱。

examples.en: A friend asked whether the memorial service in the town square was open to visitors.
examples.zh: 朋友问，在镇广场举行的「追思纪念仪式」是否向访客开放。

words.enDefinition: to improve a friendship hurt by conflict, distance, or lost trust

examples.en: It took time to mend a friendship after so much had been left unsaid.
examples.zh: 有那么多事没说开，「修复一段友情」需要时间。

examples.en: She wrote a private note because she wanted to mend a friendship from first year.
examples.zh: 她想「修复一段大一时的友情」，就私下写了张字条。

collocations: find ways to mend a friendship

words.enDefinition: An occasion when the lights on a Hanukkah menorah are lit.

examples.en: We stopped by the public menorah lighting in the square after our evening lecture.
examples.zh: 上完晚课，我们去了广场上面向公众的「光明节烛台点灯仪式」。

examples.en: The campus notice listed the menorah lighting and a short talk by a student group.
examples.zh: 校园告示上列出了「光明节烛台点灯仪式」及一个学生团体的简短分享。

words.enDefinition: A greeting wishing someone an enjoyable Christmas.

examples.en: My neighbor said “Merry Christmas” as he brought in the parcels from the front step.
examples.zh: 邻居把门前台阶上的包裹搬进来时说了声「圣诞快乐」。

examples.en: I wrote “Merry Christmas” on the card for the classmate who invited me over.
examples.zh: 我在写给邀请我去她家做客的同学的卡片上写了「圣诞快乐」。

words.enDefinition: The counting of the last seconds before the clock reaches midnight.

examples.en: We heard the midnight countdown from the courtyard while checking the clock on my phone.
examples.zh: 我在看手机时间，就听见庭院里开始了「午夜倒计时」。

examples.en: Our residence lounge showed the midnight countdown on a screen next to the main window.
examples.zh: 宿舍休息室靠大窗户的屏幕上播放着「午夜倒计时」。

words.enDefinition: A public display of fireworks timed to mark midnight, especially on New Year's Eve.

examples.en: We watched the midnight fireworks from the hill near campus after finishing our board game.
examples.zh: 结束桌游后，我们从校园附近的山坡看了「午夜烟花表演」。

examples.en: The midnight fireworks were visible from several dorm windows across the river that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚，从河对岸的几扇宿舍窗户可以看到「午夜烟花表演」。

collocations: a view of the midnight fireworks
a broadcast of the midnight fireworks

words.enDefinition: A Mass traditionally celebrated at night on Christmas Eve in some Christian churches.

examples.en: My classmate went to midnight Mass with her family after their evening meal at home.
examples.zh: 在家吃完晚饭后，同学跟家人去参加了「圣诞夜子夜弥撒」。

examples.en: The church notice listed midnight Mass separately from its service earlier that same evening.
examples.zh: 教堂告示将「圣诞夜子夜弥撒」和当晚较早的一场礼拜分开列出。

words.enDefinition: A toast made at midnight to mark the start of the new year.

examples.en: We used sparkling apple juice for a midnight toast in the residence lounge that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚，我们在宿舍休息室用苹果气泡饮料「午夜举杯庆祝」。

examples.en: My neighbor made a short midnight toast before everyone called their families back home.
examples.zh: 大家给家人打电话前，邻居在「午夜举杯庆祝」，说了几句祝福。

words.enDefinition: the period around the middle of summer, often near the summer solstice

examples.en: The village held an outdoor concert at midsummer in the park near campus.
examples.zh: 「仲夏时节」，村里在校园附近的公园办了场露天音乐会。

examples.en: We visited friends at midsummer, when their evenings seemed to go on for hours.
examples.zh: 我们在「仲夏时节」拜访朋友，那时当地的傍晚感觉能持续好几个小时。

words.enDefinition: the part of a North American fair with amusement rides, stands, or games

examples.en: My host sister showed me the midway after we finished looking at the displays.
examples.zh: 看完展品后，寄宿家的姐姐带我去看「北美集市游乐区」。

examples.en: We agreed to meet at the far end of the midway before catching the bus.
examples.zh: 我们约定坐公交之前在「北美集市游乐区」的另一端碰头。

words.enDefinition: A small sweet pie usually filled with spiced dried fruit and served at Christmas in Britain.

examples.en: I tried a mince pie at the market after a classmate told me about its sweet filling.
examples.zh: 同学告诉我里面是甜馅后，我在集市尝了一个「圣诞甜果馅饼」。

examples.en: Our British neighbor put a mince pie beside each cup of tea she served.
examples.zh: 英国邻居端茶来时，在每杯茶旁放了一个「圣诞甜果馅饼」。

words.expression: mind if I take the last piece
words.lemma: mind if i take the last piece
words.enDefinition: a question asking if others mind you taking the remaining portion
acceptedEnVariants: mind if I take the last piece

examples.en: “Mind if I take the last piece?” I asked before reaching for the pizza.
examples.zh: 我伸手拿披萨前问「我拿最后一块可以吗？」

examples.en: My friend looked around and asked, “Mind if I take the last piece?”
examples.zh: 朋友环顾大家，问「我拿最后一块可以吗？」

collocations: ask “Mind if I take the last piece?”
“Do you mind if I take the last piece?”
“Mind if I take the last piece of bread?”

words.enDefinition: A casual way to ask whether the group can move to another spot nearby.

examples.en: Mind if we move over to the window where we can hear each other better?
examples.zh: 「介意咱们挪到窗边吗」？那里大家更能听清彼此说话。

examples.en: Mind if we move over a little so the other group can use this bench?
examples.zh: 「介意咱们稍微挪个地方吗」？好让另一组人也能用这条长椅。

collocations: ask mind if we move over
mind if we move over to the window
say mind if we move over

words.enDefinition: to move around and talk to different people at an event

examples.en: There was time to mingle before everyone sat down for dinner.
examples.zh: 大家坐下吃晚饭前，还有时间「四处找人聊天」。

examples.en: The new residents were encouraged to mingle over tea and biscuits.
examples.zh: 组织者鼓励刚入住的人吃饼干喝茶时「四处找人聊天」。

words.enDefinition: The seven candles used in the Kwanzaa candleholder to represent the festival's principles.

examples.en: The poster showed the colors of the mishumaa saba beside a picture of the candleholder.
examples.zh: 海报在烛台图片旁标明了「宽扎节七支蜡烛」的颜色。

examples.en: We learned about the mishumaa saba while helping label the objects in the campus exhibit.
examples.zh: 我们协助给校园展品写标签时，了解了「宽扎节七支蜡烛」。

collocations: the colors of the mishumaa saba

words.enDefinition: to say a person's name with the wrong sounds or stress

examples.en: I didn't want to mispronounce a name during the club's award ceremony.
examples.zh: 我不想在社团颁奖典礼上「读错姓名」。

examples.en: It's easy to mispronounce a name if you've only seen it written down.
examples.zh: 如果只见过书写形式，就容易「读错姓名」。

collocations: try not to mispronounce a name

words.enDefinition: to feel the absence of familiar everyday details

examples.en: I miss the little things, like hearing our neighbours talking in the stairwell.
examples.zh: 我「想念那些小事」，比如听以前的邻居在楼梯间聊天。

examples.en: My classmate said she started to miss the little things after the first month.
examples.zh: 同学说，过了第一个月，她开始「想念那些小事」。

collocations: start to miss the little things
miss the little things about home

words.enDefinition: A plant sometimes hung as a Christmas decoration and associated with a kissing custom.

examples.en: Our guide pointed out mistletoe above the doorway during a tour of the historic house.
examples.zh: 参观历史建筑时，向导指给我们看门口悬挂的「槲寄生」。

examples.en: The craft display used paper mistletoe among its examples of traditional decorations for students.
examples.zh: 手工展览给学生展示传统装饰，其中放了用纸做的「槲寄生」。

words.enDefinition: family origins drawn from more than one cultural or ethnic background

examples.en: The student spoke about her mixed heritage while showing us an old family map.
examples.zh: 那名学生给我们看一张旧家谱地图时，谈到了自己的「多元文化出身」。

examples.en: My friend said one label didn't fully describe his mixed heritage.
examples.zh: 朋友说，用一个标签说不清他的「多元文化出身」。

words.enDefinition: a group whose participants use different languages

examples.en: I joined a mixed-language group to make captions for a local history video.
examples.zh: 我加入了一个「使用不同语言的小组」，给一段地方历史视频做字幕。

examples.en: Our mixed-language group wrote questions in whichever languages we felt comfortable using.
examples.zh: 我们这个「使用不同语言的小组」用各自熟悉的语言写了问题。

collocations: a conversation in a mixed-language group

words.enDefinition: A mat used as the base for the symbolic objects displayed at Kwanzaa.

examples.en: The volunteer laid out a woven mkeka before putting the other objects on the table.
examples.zh: 志愿者先铺好编织的「宽扎节陈设用席垫」，再把其他物品摆上桌。

examples.en: We noticed the mkeka in a photograph accompanying the article for our culture class.
examples.zh: 我们在文化课阅读材料配的一张照片里留意到了「宽扎节陈设用席垫」。

words.enDefinition: a short, shared pause without speaking to show respect

examples.en: The society observed a moment of silence in memory of a former member.
examples.zh: 社团为一位前成员「默哀片刻」。

examples.en: We stood for a moment of silence at the campus remembrance event.
examples.zh: 在校园纪念活动上，我们起立「默哀片刻」。

collocations: ask for a moment of silence
begin with a moment of silence

words.enDefinition: a traditional English folk dance often performed in groups at local events

examples.en: The Morris dancing group performed in front of the library during the spring fair.
examples.zh: 春季市集期间，「英格兰莫里斯舞」团队在图书馆前表演。

examples.en: Our guide mentioned Morris dancing when we asked about events on the village green.
examples.zh: 我们问村里的公共草坪上有什么活动时，导游提到了「英格兰莫里斯舞」。

words.enDefinition: a day honouring mothers and other maternal figures

examples.en: I called my mother on Mother's Day after finishing my afternoon tutorial that year.
examples.zh: 那年「母亲节」，我上完下午的辅导课就给妈妈打了电话。

examples.en: The shop put a table of cards beside the door for Mother's Day.
examples.zh: 商店为了「母亲节」，在门旁摆了一桌卡片。

words.enDefinition: the fourth Sunday of Lent, often observed as Mother's Day in the UK

examples.en: The UK shop had signs for Mothering Sunday beside its spring flower display.
examples.zh: 英国那家店在春季鲜花展台旁放了「英国传统母亲节」的标牌。

examples.en: I asked my host family when they usually exchanged cards for Mothering Sunday.
examples.zh: 我问寄宿家庭，大家通常什么时候为「英国传统母亲节」互送卡片。

words.enDefinition: To change the location of a planned activity from outside to inside.

examples.en: We can move it indoors if the tables outside are still wet after lunch.
examples.zh: 如果午饭后室外桌子还是湿的，我们可以「把活动移到室内」。

examples.en: Mina suggested we move it indoors because the wind kept knocking over the cups.
examples.zh: 风老是把杯子刮倒，米娜建议我们「把活动移到室内」。

collocations: ask whether to move it indoors
move it indoors if it rains

words.enDefinition: A social evening organized around watching a film together.

examples.en: We planned a movie night in the residence lounge after our last exam was over.
examples.zh: 最后一场考试结束后，我们计划在宿舍休息室办个「电影之夜」。

examples.en: Our movie night started later because half the group was coming from a class across campus.
examples.zh: 有一半人要从校园另一边下课后赶来，所以我们的「电影之夜」开始得晚了一点。

collocations: pick a film for movie night

words.enDefinition: a title placed before a man's surname or full name

examples.en: The moderator introduced him as Mr Patel before handing him the microphone.
examples.zh: 主持人把麦克风递给他之前，介绍他是 Patel「先生」。

examples.en: The host wrote Mr Green on the name card beside the lectern.
examples.zh: 主持人在讲台旁的姓名卡上写了 Green「先生」。

words.enDefinition: a title traditionally used before the surname of a married woman

examples.en: The guest asked us to call her Mrs Lewis during the awards ceremony.
examples.zh: 来宾请我们在颁奖典礼上称她为 Lewis「太太」。

examples.en: The speech notes used Mrs Shah, the title she had entered on the form.
examples.zh: 发言稿用了 Shah「太太」，这是她自己在表格上填的称谓。

words.enDefinition: The ears of corn displayed at Kwanzaa to represent children.

examples.en: A student volunteer wrote the label for the muhindi in our winter traditions display.
examples.zh: 一位学生志愿者为我们的冬季习俗展写了介绍「宽扎节陈设中的玉米」的展签。

examples.en: The display placed the muhindi next to a card describing the festival's focus on family.
examples.zh: 展览把「宽扎节陈设中的玉米」放在一张介绍宽扎节重视家庭的卡片旁。

words.enDefinition: A warm apple cider flavored with spices, often served at winter gatherings.

examples.en: We bought mulled cider from a winter market stall before heading back to campus.
examples.zh: 回学校之前，我们在冬季集市的摊位买了「热香料苹果饮」。

examples.en: The student event served nonalcoholic mulled cider with biscuits in the lounge that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚，学生活动在休息室供应无酒精的「热香料苹果饮」和饼干。

words.enDefinition: a calendar showing significant occasions across different faith traditions

examples.en: The club checked the multifaith calendar before choosing its next rehearsal date.
examples.zh: 社团先查了「多种信仰纪念日历」，才定下次排练的日期。

examples.en: I found a multifaith calendar on the noticeboard outside the common room.
examples.zh: 我在公共休息室外的公告板上找到了「多种信仰纪念日历」。

words.enDefinition: a home where different languages are used in everyday life

examples.en: My roommate grew up in a multilingual household and uses three languages with relatives.
examples.zh: 室友在「多语言家庭」长大，跟亲戚交流时用三种语言。

examples.en: In her multilingual household, family games often used words from two different languages.
examples.zh: 她在「多语言家庭」里玩全家游戏时，经常会用到两种语言的词。

collocations: grow up in a multilingual household

words.enDefinition: Candied fruit, roots, or other sweet preserved treats served during Tết.

examples.en: We tried mứt Tết at the culture fair after our class finished for the day.
examples.zh: 当天课程结束后，我们在文化集市尝了「越南新年蜜饯」。

examples.en: My classmate brought a tray of mứt Tết to share with friends in the lounge.
examples.zh: 同学把一盘「越南新年蜜饯」带到休息室跟朋友分享。

words.enDefinition: a feeling of romantic interest that two people share towards each other

examples.en: Their mutual attraction surprised both of them after years on the same course.
examples.zh: 同上一门课多年后，两人发现彼此「相互吸引」，都感到意外。

examples.en: They talked about the mutual attraction only when a friend brought it up.
examples.zh: 朋友提起后，他们才聊到彼此「相互吸引」的事。

words.enDefinition: the end of a relationship agreed to by both partners

examples.en: They described it as a mutual breakup after months of talking about different priorities.
examples.zh: 讨论了几个月彼此不同的优先事项后，他们说这是「双方同意分手」。

examples.en: After the mutual breakup, both of them kept attending their usual weekly film club.
examples.zh: 「双方同意分手」之后，两人还是继续参加原来每周的电影社活动。

collocations: describe it as a mutual breakup

words.enDefinition: a match recorded after two dating app users express interest in each other

examples.en: The app showed a mutual match after they each liked the other's profile.
examples.zh: 两人各自点了对方资料的喜欢后，应用显示「双方互选配对」。

examples.en: I noticed the mutual match notification when I checked my phone between classes.
examples.zh: 两节课之间查手机时，我看到了「双方互选配对」的通知。

words.enDefinition: help that people provide to one another rather than in only one direction

examples.en: Our mutual support made the first weeks at university feel much less overwhelming.
examples.zh: 我们的「相互支持」让刚上大学的那几周轻松了许多。

examples.en: The small friendship group was built on mutual support during a demanding course.
examples.zh: 课程要求很高，那几个朋友靠「相互支持」走到了一起。

words.enDefinition: a title used before a name without indicating gender

examples.en: The speaker had selected Mx on the form, so I used it on their badge.
examples.zh: 发言者在表格上选了「无性别敬称 Mx」，我便把它写在了对方的胸牌上。

examples.en: The staff list gave the volunteer's name as Mx Lane for the welcome session.
examples.zh: 迎新活动的工作人员名单把那位志愿者写作「Mx Lane」。

words.enDefinition: someone whose character or interests appeal to the speaker

examples.en: Anyone who brings biscuits to a study group is my kind of person.
examples.zh: 愿意带饼干来学习小组的人，都是「和我合得来的人」。

examples.en: I knew she was my kind of person when she laughed at my joke.
examples.zh: 她被我的笑话逗笑时，我就知道她是个「和我合得来的人」。

collocations: seem like my kind of person
turn out to be my kind of person

words.enDefinition: an affectionate or humorous way to refer to one's romantic partner

examples.en: I asked my other half whether we still had time for coffee before the film.
examples.zh: 我问「我的另一半」，电影开场前我们还有没有时间喝咖啡。

examples.en: I told the group that my other half would join us once class ended.
examples.zh: 我告诉大家，「我的另一半」下课后会过来和我们会合。

words.enDefinition: a phrase saying someone is mentioned during a conversation

examples.en: His name comes up whenever we talk about our first month in the residence.
examples.zh: 我们一聊起刚住宿舍的第一个月，「就有人提到他的名字」。

examples.en: Her name comes up a lot when the old group gets together for coffee.
examples.zh: 老朋友聚着喝咖啡时，「经常有人提到她的名字」。

collocations: someone's name comes up in conversation
his name comes up at reunions

words.enDefinition: a group game that helps people remember one another's names

examples.en: We played a name game while we waited for the others to arrive.
examples.zh: 我们一边等其他人到，一边玩了个「名字破冰游戏」。

examples.en: A name game helped me remember the people sitting on either side.
examples.zh: 一个「名字破冰游戏」帮我记住了坐在两边的人。

words.enDefinition: a written or recorded aid for saying a name correctly

examples.en: The event organiser sent a name pronunciation guide before our practice introductions.
examples.zh: 我们练习介绍来宾前，活动组织者发来了一份「姓名读音指南」。

examples.en: I listened to the name pronunciation guide while walking to the lecture hall.
examples.zh: 我走去讲堂时听了「姓名读音指南」的录音。

words.enDefinition: an August observance celebrating Acadian culture and heritage in Canada

examples.en: The library display for National Acadian Day included recordings of songs from the region.
examples.zh: 为「加拿大阿卡迪亚人日」布置的图书馆展览收录了当地歌曲的录音。

examples.en: We heard French spoken throughout the community festival for National Acadian Day that summer.
examples.zh: 那年夏天，在庆祝「加拿大阿卡迪亚人日」的社区节庆上，我们到处都能听到法语。

words.enDefinition: a June observance celebrating First Nations, Inuit, and Métis cultures and contributions in Canada

examples.en: The library hosted a public reading on National Indigenous Peoples Day in the main hall.
examples.zh: 「加拿大原住民日」当天，图书馆在大厅办了公开朗读活动。

examples.en: Our class visited a community exhibition for National Indigenous Peoples Day that June.
examples.zh: 那年六月，我们班参观了为「加拿大原住民日」举办的社区展览。

words.enDefinition: A display depicting the birth of Jesus in the Christian Christmas story.

examples.en: The museum displayed a small nativity scene in its exhibition about winter traditions in Europe.
examples.zh: 博物馆在欧洲冬季习俗展中摆了一组小型「耶稣诞生场景」。

examples.en: I saw a handmade nativity scene while visiting the chapel with my history class.
examples.zh: 我跟历史课同学参观礼拜堂时，看到了一组手工制作的「耶稣诞生场景」。

words.enDefinition: conventions for considerate behaviour when communicating online

examples.en: The club discussed netiquette before inviting new members into its online forum.
examples.zh: 社团邀请新成员进线上论坛前，讨论了「网络礼仪」。

examples.en: Our class covered netiquette during the first week of the online project.
examples.zh: 线上项目第一周，我们这门课讲了「网络礼仪」。

words.enDefinition: having only recently arrived at or joined a university community

examples.en: I was new to campus and didn't recognise anyone at the first lunch.
examples.zh: 我「刚来学校」，在第一次午餐时谁都不认识。

examples.en: Several of us were new to campus, so we compared notes about the area.
examples.zh: 我们有好几个人「刚来学校」，于是聊了聊各自对附近的了解。

collocations: students who are new to campus

words.enDefinition: The first day of the new year in the Gregorian calendar.

examples.en: Some classmates met for breakfast on New Year's Day before the library opened again.
examples.zh: 「公历元旦」那天，几位同学在图书馆重新开放前约着吃了早饭。

examples.en: The apartment building was unusually quiet on New Year's Day after the celebrations downtown.
examples.zh: 市中心的庆祝活动过后，公寓楼在「公历元旦」那天格外安静。

collocations: a meal on New Year's Day

words.enDefinition: A public procession held to celebrate the first day of the calendar year.

examples.en: Our student band rehearsed a march before performing in the local New Year's Day parade.
examples.zh: 学生乐队在当地「元旦巡游」演出前排练了一首进行曲。

examples.en: We stood near the campus gate to watch the New Year's Day parade pass by.
examples.zh: 我们站在校门附近，看「元旦巡游」队伍经过。

collocations: watch a New Year's Day parade
a costume for a New Year's Day parade
perform in a New Year's Day parade

words.enDefinition: The last day or evening of the calendar year just before New Year's Day.

examples.en: We planned to spend New Year's Eve in the lounge with a couple of classmates.
examples.zh: 我们打算和几位同学在休息室里过「跨年夜」。

examples.en: My neighbors stayed in on New Year's Eve because they had guests visiting from abroad.
examples.zh: 邻居有客人从国外来访，所以他们「跨年夜」留在家里。

words.enDefinition: A promise or goal that someone sets for the year ahead.

examples.en: My New Year's resolution was to call home more often during busy weeks at university.
examples.zh: 我「新年立下的目标」是，在学校忙的时候也要多给家里打电话。

examples.en: We each wrote a New Year's resolution on a card for our future selves.
examples.zh: 我们每个人都在给未来自己的卡片上写下了一个「新年立下的目标」。

words.enDefinition: The Swahili name for the seven principles celebrated during Kwanzaa.

examples.en: The program listed the Nguzo Saba in Swahili and English beside the event schedule.
examples.zh: 节目单在日程旁用斯瓦希里语和英语列出了「宽扎节七项原则」。

examples.en: Our reading group talked about the Nguzo Saba after visiting the local history museum.
examples.zh: 参观当地历史博物馆后，我们读书小组谈到了「宽扎节七项原则」。

collocations: an exhibit about the Nguzo Saba

words.enDefinition: A rice cake commonly eaten during the Chinese New Year, with many regional varieties.

examples.en: We tried nian gao at the student food table during the Lunar New Year event.
examples.zh: 农历新年活动期间，我们在学生美食摊位尝了「中式年糕」。

examples.en: My neighbor showed me how her family's nian gao differs from the kind at the market.
examples.zh: 邻居给我看她家的「中式年糕」和集市上的那种有什么不同。

words.enDefinition: a period or arrangement in which people do not communicate with each other

examples.en: They agreed to no contact for a while after their relationship ended in spring.
examples.zh: 春天结束恋情后，两人约好一段时间「完全停止联系」。

examples.en: She wanted no contact during exams so she could focus on finishing the term.
examples.zh: 她想在考试期间「完全停止联系」，好专心完成这学期的学业。

words.enDefinition: having no exact match in another language or setting

examples.en: The term has no direct equivalent in English, so I described its use.
examples.zh: 这个词在英语里「没有直接对应的说法」，所以我解释了它的用法。

examples.en: I found no direct equivalent for the nickname in my first language.
examples.zh: 我在自己的第一语言里没有找到这个昵称「直接对应的说法」。

collocations: no direct equivalent in another language

words.enDefinition: asks visitors to attend without bringing a gift

examples.en: My cousin wrote "No gifts, please," so we just brought a card.
examples.zh: 表姐写了「请不要送礼」，所以我们只带了张卡片。

examples.en: The sign said "No gifts, please," and the hosts repeated it at dinner.
examples.zh: 牌子上写着「请不要送礼」，主人在晚餐上又说了一遍。

collocations: write no gifts, please at the bottom

words.enDefinition: a request to greet without hugging the speaker

examples.en: At the reunion I smiled and said, “No hugs, please,” before waving.
examples.zh: 在重聚会上，我笑着说「请不要拥抱我」，然后挥了挥手。

examples.en: My friend said, “No hugs, please,” and offered a wave instead.
examples.zh: 朋友说「请不要拥抱我」，然后挥手打了个招呼。

collocations: “No hugs, please, but I'd love a wave”

words.enDefinition: a phrase reassuring someone that they can answer another time

examples.en: “No need to reply tonight,” I added because my classmate had an early shift.
examples.zh: 同学第二天早班，我就补了一句「今晚不用回复」。

examples.en: The organiser wrote, “No need to reply tonight,” under the message about rehearsals.
examples.zh: 组织者在排练消息下面写着「今晚不用回复」。

collocations: “No need to reply tonight if you're busy”
“No need to reply tonight if you're tired”

words.enDefinition: a sign stating that food from elsewhere is not allowed

examples.en: The screening room had a “No outside food” sign on the door.
examples.zh: 放映室门上有一块「请勿自带食物」的牌子。

examples.en: I saw a notice saying “No outside food” beside the café entrance.
examples.zh: 我在咖啡馆入口旁看见了「请勿自带食物」的通知。

words.enDefinition: a queue rule against keeping a place for someone who is absent

examples.en: A sign said “No place saving” by the queue for student tickets.
examples.zh: 学生票队伍旁的标牌写着「请勿替人占排队位置」。

examples.en: The organiser repeated “No place saving” when the line began to fill.
examples.zh: 队伍开始变长时，组织者又提醒了一次「请勿替人占排队位置」。

words.enDefinition: An invitation phrase saying it is fine to decline or skip the event.

examples.en: No pressure to come if you need the evening to finish your assignment.
examples.zh: 如果你晚上得留时间写完作业，「来不来都没关系」。

examples.en: I added “No pressure to come” because I knew my roommate had an exam tomorrow.
examples.zh: 我知道室友明天有考试，就加了一句「来不来都没关系」。

collocations: tell them there's no pressure to come
a message saying no pressure to come

words.enDefinition: a notice asking people not to make an audio or video recording

examples.en: The sign said “No recording” above the door of the student screening room.
examples.zh: 学生放映室的门上方写着「禁止录音录像」。

examples.en: I saw “No recording” on the first slide of the club's rehearsal.
examples.zh: 社团排练的第一张幻灯片上写着「禁止录音录像」。

words.enDefinition: politely says that you do not want sugar in your drink

examples.en: No sugar for me, please, but could I have a little milk in mine?
examples.zh: 「我这杯不加糖」，不过能加一点牛奶吗？

examples.en: When my host brought out the sugar, I said, "No sugar for me, thanks."
examples.zh: 主人拿糖出来时，我说：「我这杯不加糖」，谢谢。

collocations: just milk and no sugar for me
I said no sugar for me

words.zhGloss: 不是每个人都过这个节
words.enDefinition: a reminder that a celebration is not shared by all people
acceptedZhAnswers: 不是每个人都过这个节

examples.en: “Not everyone celebrates it,” I reminded the club before we made the poster.
examples.zh: 社团做海报之前，我提醒大家「不是每个人都过这个节」。

examples.en: My classmate said, “Not everyone celebrates it,” when asked about our winter break.
examples.zh: 有人问起我们的寒假时，同学说「不是每个人都过这个节」。

words.enDefinition: to have no acquaintances at all in a situation

examples.en: It's hard to walk into a room and not know a soul there.
examples.zh: 走进一间屋子，发现「一个人都不认识」，确实不容易。

examples.en: You can arrive and not know a soul, then leave with three new friends.
examples.zh: 你到场时可能「一个人都不认识」，离开时却交到了三个新朋友。

collocations: realise you do not know a soul
arrive and not know a soul
go somewhere and not know a soul

words.enDefinition: describes a person who usually does not speak very much

examples.en: I'm not much of a talker in a crowd, but I like talking one on one.
examples.zh: 人多时我「话不多」，不过我喜欢一对一聊天。

examples.en: My new neighbour is not much of a talker until we get onto our favourite books.
examples.zh: 我新邻居一般「话不多」，直到聊起我们喜欢的书。

collocations: I'm not much of a talker
she is not much of a talker at first
turn out to be not much of a talker

words.enDefinition: not feeling prepared to start going on romantic dates

examples.en: He said he was not ready to date after ending a long relationship.
examples.zh: 结束一段长期恋情后，他说自己「还没准备好约会」。

examples.en: I told my friend I was not ready to date anyone from our class.
examples.zh: 我告诉朋友，自己「还没准备好和班里的人约会」。

collocations: feel like you're not ready to date
still not ready to date again

words.enDefinition: a spring new year celebrated in Iran and other parts of Asia and beyond

examples.en: A classmate invited me to a Nowruz celebration at the community centre that spring.
examples.zh: 同学邀请我参加那年春天在社区中心举行的「诺鲁孜节」庆典。

examples.en: The museum's Nowruz display showed how some families welcome the return of spring.
examples.zh: 博物馆的「诺鲁孜节」展览展示了有些家庭怎样迎接春天归来。

words.enDefinition: wording saying that the holiday is officially observed on Monday

examples.en: The calendar said the holiday was observed on Monday because it fell on Sunday.
examples.zh: 节日本身在周日，日历标明「节日改在周一举行」。

examples.en: I checked which buses ran after seeing “Observed on Monday” on the notice.
examples.zh: 看到告示写着「节日改在周一举行」后，我查了哪些公交车有班次。

collocations: the date is observed on Monday
closed for the holiday observed on Monday

words.enDefinition: a joke considered indecent or unsuitable for the occasion

examples.en: An off-color joke made the conversation stop for a moment at our table.
examples.zh: 有人讲了个「粗俗的笑话」，我们那桌一时没人说话。

examples.en: The host changed the subject after hearing an off-color joke from the audience.
examples.zh: 听到观众讲了个「粗俗的笑话」后，主持人换了话题。

words.enDefinition: to ask another person whether they want to sit where you are sitting

examples.en: Our tutor said you can offer someone your seat with a simple question.
examples.zh: 导师说，想「给别人让座」，简单问一声就行。

examples.en: It can feel awkward to offer someone your seat in a crowded room.
examples.zh: 房间里很挤时，主动「给别人让座」可能会觉得有点尴尬。

collocations: choose to offer someone your seat
offer someone your seat on the bus

words.enDefinition: someone who used to be in one of your classes

examples.en: I ran into an old classmate outside the library on my way to work.
examples.zh: 上班路上，我在图书馆外碰到了一位「老同学」。

examples.en: An old classmate helped me remember the name of the teacher in that photograph.
examples.zh: 一位「老同学」帮我想起了那张照片里老师的名字。

words.enDefinition: temporarily apart by agreement while deciding about a romantic relationship

examples.en: They were on a break when our class went away for the field trip.
examples.zh: 我们班去实地考察时，他们的「恋爱关系暂时暂停」了。

examples.en: I didn't know we were on a break until we finally spoke about it.
examples.zh: 我们终于聊起这事时，我才知道我们的「恋爱关系暂时暂停」了。

collocations: spend time apart while on a break
agree to be on a break

words.enDefinition: a relationship that repeatedly ends and starts again

examples.en: They had an on-again, off-again relationship while studying for degrees in different cities.
