examples.zh: 在不同城市读书时，他们有一段「分分合合的恋情」。

examples.en: My friend was tired of an on-again, off-again relationship by the end of summer.
examples.zh: 到暑假末，我朋友已经厌倦了那段「分分合合的恋情」。

collocations: be in an on-again, off-again relationship

words.enDefinition: willing to talk to each other after an argument or other difficulty

examples.en: We were still on speaking terms even after our argument over the train tickets.
examples.zh: 即便为火车票吵过，两人也「还愿意彼此说话」。

examples.en: I didn't know they were not on speaking terms when I planned the dinner.
examples.zh: 安排晚餐时，我不知道两人「已经不愿意彼此说话了」。

words.enDefinition: still affected by a recent breakup, especially when starting to date again

examples.en: She wondered whether she was on the rebound when she started dating again that summer.
examples.zh: 那年夏天重新约会时，她怀疑自己是不是「仍受刚分手的影响」。

examples.en: He didn't want to go on another date while he was still on the rebound.
examples.zh: 他不想在「仍受刚分手的影响」时接着去约会。

collocations: meet someone while on the rebound

words.enDefinition: understanding things in a similar way and communicating easily

examples.en: We were on the same wavelength from the moment we started talking about art.
examples.zh: 从一开口聊艺术起，我们就「很合拍」。

examples.en: After one short conversation, I felt we were on the same wavelength already.
examples.zh: 短短聊了一次，我就感觉和对方「很合拍」。

words.enDefinition: a discussion between just two people without a group present

examples.en: I felt more relaxed in a one-on-one conversation than in the group.
examples.zh: 「一对一聊天」让我感觉更放松。

examples.en: I had a one-on-one conversation with her while the others were eating.
examples.zh: 其他人吃东西时，我和她「一对一聊了会儿」。

words.enDefinition: a friendship where only one person makes much effort or provides support

examples.en: She felt it had become a one-sided friendship once she was always making the calls.
examples.zh: 每次都是她打电话，她觉得这成了「一方单向付出的友情」。

examples.en: I wondered whether I was in a one-sided friendship after several ignored invitations.
examples.zh: 几次邀约都没回音后，我怀疑这是不是段「一方单向付出的友情」。

words.enDefinition: meeting potential romantic partners through the internet

examples.en: My roommate tried online dating after moving somewhere she didn't know many people.
examples.zh: 室友搬到没多少熟人的地方后，尝试了「网上交友约会」。

examples.en: We talked about how online dating felt different from meeting someone through our friends.
examples.zh: 我们聊到「网上交友约会」和经朋友介绍认识人的感受有什么不同。

words.enDefinition: a live music event held outdoors

examples.en: We packed a blanket for the open-air concert because seating was on the lawn.
examples.zh: 「露天音乐会」的座位在草坪上，我们就带了条毯子。

examples.en: The local orchestra held an open-air concert for families during the July holiday weekend.
examples.zh: 七月假日周末，当地管弦乐团为家庭观众举办了一场「露天音乐会」。

words.enDefinition: An invitation that anyone in the intended group can accept.

examples.en: It was an open invite, so students from both seminar groups could join us.
examples.zh: 这次是「开放邀请」，所以两个研讨班的学生都可以加入。

examples.en: We posted an open invite for a picnic on the lawn after Friday's classes.
examples.zh: 我们发了「开放邀请」，约大家星期五下课后去草坪野餐。

collocations: an open invite to the picnic

words.enDefinition: tells a recipient that they can choose when to open a gift

examples.en: Open it when you're ready. There's no need to unwrap it in front of everyone.
examples.zh: 「你想打开的时候再拆」。不用当着所有人的面拆。

examples.en: My friend said, "Open it when you're ready," as she handed me the little box.
examples.zh: 朋友把小盒子递给我，说：「你想打开的时候再拆」。

collocations: you can open it when you're ready
please open it when you're ready
feel free to open it when you're ready

words.expression: open to people from all backgrounds
words.lemma: open to people from all backgrounds
words.zhGloss: 欢迎不同背景的人参与
words.enDefinition: welcoming participants regardless of their personal or cultural background
acceptedZhAnswers: 欢迎不同背景的人参与
acceptedEnVariants: open to people from all backgrounds

examples.en: The poster said the story night was open to people from all backgrounds this year.
examples.zh: 海报写着，今年的故事分享夜「欢迎不同背景的人参与」。

examples.en: I joined after learning that the discussion was open to people from all backgrounds.
examples.zh: 我得知这次讨论「欢迎不同背景的人参与」，便加入了。

collocations: an event open to people from all backgrounds
a group open to people from all backgrounds
make an event open to people from all backgrounds

words.enDefinition: to begin sharing private feelings or worries with the person you are dating

examples.en: It can take time to open up to your partner about worries from home.
examples.zh: 要「向伴侣说出有关家里的心里话」，有时需要一点时间。

examples.en: My friend said it helped to open up to your partner when work became stressful.
examples.zh: 朋友说，工作压力变大时，「向伴侣说出心里话」会有帮助。

collocations: find time to open up to your partner
learn to open up to your partner
feel safe to open up to your partner

words.enDefinition: a group of new students assigned to do welcome activities together

examples.en: I recognised her from my orientation group when she sat beside me.
examples.zh: 她坐到我旁边时，我认出她是我「迎新小组」里的同学。

examples.en: Our orientation group had several people who were new to the city.
examples.zh: 我们「迎新小组」里有好几个人是刚来这座城市的。

collocations: be in the same orientation group
recognise someone from your orientation group

words.enDefinition: a gourd grown to be displayed for its shape or colour

examples.en: A striped ornamental gourd sat beside the apples at the farm stand.
examples.zh: 农场小摊的苹果旁摆着一个有条纹的「观赏葫芦」。

examples.en: I bought a tiny ornamental gourd to put on my windowsill.
examples.zh: 我买了个小小的「观赏葫芦」，准备放在窗台上。

words.enDefinition: having no candy left to hand out to visitors

examples.en: We were out of candy by the time my roommate got back from class.
examples.zh: 室友下课回来时，我们的「糖发完了」。

examples.en: The sign said "Out of candy," but the pumpkin was still glowing beside it.
examples.zh: 牌子上写着「糖发完了」，旁边的南瓜灯还亮着。

words.enDefinition: celebratory events held outside, often as part of a larger occasion

examples.en: The town moved the start of the outdoor festivities to later in the afternoon.
examples.zh: 镇上把「户外庆祝活动」的开始时间改到了下午晚一些。

examples.en: We watched the outdoor festivities from the bridge before meeting friends in the square.
examples.zh: 我们先在桥上看了「户外庆祝活动」，再去广场和朋友见面。

words.enDefinition: a platform outside where performers appear before an audience

examples.en: The dance group practised on the outdoor stage before the gates opened.
examples.zh: 大门开放前，舞蹈团在「露天舞台」上排练。

examples.en: We sat on the grass near the outdoor stage for the student performances.
examples.zh: 我们坐在「露天舞台」旁的草地上看学生演出。

words.zhGloss: 因各自成长而不再适合做朋友
words.enDefinition: to change over time until an old friendship no longer suits the people involved
acceptedZhAnswers: 因各自成长而不再适合做朋友

examples.en: She wondered whether people can outgrow a friendship without having a single argument.
examples.zh: 她想知道，两个人没吵过一次架，也会不会「因各自成长而不再适合做朋友」。

examples.en: Sometimes friends outgrow a friendship as their lives take them in different directions.
examples.zh: 有时候朋友走上不同的生活道路，会「因各自成长而不再适合做朋友」。

collocations: feel you may outgrow a friendship

words.enDefinition: to stay longer than a host wants or is comfortable with

examples.en: It's easy to overstay your welcome when you lose track of the time.
examples.zh: 聊得忘了时间，很容易「待得太久惹人嫌」。

examples.en: You might overstay your welcome if you ignore the host's bedtime routine.
examples.zh: 要是不留意主人的睡觉时间，就可能「待得太久惹人嫌」。

collocations: try not to overstay your welcome
worry that you'll overstay your welcome

words.enDefinition: the speed and rhythm of ordinary activities in a place

examples.en: The pace of life felt different after I moved out of halls.
examples.zh: 搬出宿舍后，我觉得「生活节奏」变了。

examples.en: My roommate said she preferred the pace of life in her new neighbourhood.
examples.zh: 室友说，她更喜欢新社区的「生活节奏」。

collocations: get used to the pace of life
enjoy the local pace of life

words.enDefinition: to form groups with two people in each

examples.en: We had to pair off and tell each other about our hometowns.
examples.zh: 我们得「两两结成一组」，互相说说自己的家乡。

examples.en: The mentor asked us to pair off with someone we didn't know.
examples.zh: 带队的学长让我们找个不认识的人「两两结成一组」。

words.enDefinition: the Sunday before Easter, observed in memory of Jesus entering Jerusalem

examples.en: My neighbour invited me to a choir performance on Palm Sunday at her church.
examples.zh: 邻居邀请我去她的教堂看「棕枝主日」的合唱表演。

examples.en: The programme explained why palm branches appear in some Palm Sunday services each year.
examples.zh: 节目单解释了为什么有些「棕枝主日」礼拜每年会用到棕枝。

words.enDefinition: bat shapes cut from paper and used as decorations

examples.en: We taped paper bats around the menu board in the student café.
examples.zh: 我们把「纸蝙蝠」贴在学生咖啡馆菜单板的四周。

examples.en: The club made paper bats from old black posters for the evening.
examples.zh: 社团用废旧的黑色海报做了些「纸蝙蝠」，晚上布置用。

collocations: put paper bats in the window

words.enDefinition: a decorated vehicle that carries people or displays in a procession

examples.en: The art students built a parade float with enormous painted maple leaves.
examples.zh: 美术生做了一辆「游行花车」，上面有巨大的彩绘枫叶。

examples.en: My neighbour waved from a parade float during the Thanksgiving celebration.
examples.zh: 感恩节庆典上，邻居在一辆「游行花车」上向我挥手。

words.enDefinition: the planned order of groups or performers taking part in a parade

examples.en: I checked the parade lineup to see when our university group would appear.
examples.zh: 我查了「游行队伍出场顺序」，看我们学校的队伍什么时候出现。

examples.en: The parade lineup listed the musicians just before the group from our residence.
examples.zh: 「游行队伍出场顺序」把乐手排在我们宿舍的队伍之前。

words.enDefinition: the planned path that a parade follows through an area

examples.en: I checked the parade route before choosing a place to meet my classmate.
examples.zh: 我先查了「游行路线」，再选地方和同学碰头。

examples.en: The map showed the parade route ending outside the main community centre that afternoon.
examples.zh: 地图显示，当天下午的「游行路线」终点在主要的社区中心外。

words.enDefinition: apologises informally because a place looks untidy to a visitor

examples.en: Pardon the mess. I had to finish a project before you came over.
examples.zh: 「屋里有点乱，见谅」。你来之前我得赶完一个项目。

examples.en: My friend said, "Pardon the mess," as she picked up her textbooks.
examples.zh: 朋友一边捡起课本，一边说：「屋里有点乱，见谅」。

collocations: pardon the mess on the table

words.enDefinition: a present given when someone is leaving or saying goodbye

examples.en: My host gave me a parting gift on my last morning there.
examples.zh: 我在那儿待的最后一个早上，主人给了我一份「道别时送的礼物」。

examples.en: We made a parting gift for the classmate who was transferring.
examples.zh: 我们给要转学的同学做了份「道别时送的礼物」。

words.enDefinition: to move a serving dish from person to person so everyone can reach it

examples.en: We took turns helping to pass a dish around the long table.
examples.zh: 我们轮流帮忙，「把一道菜沿着长桌递给大家」。

examples.en: The dinner host showed us how to pass a dish around without reaching across anyone.
examples.zh: 聚餐主持人示范如何不从别人面前伸手，就能「把一道菜递给大家」。

collocations: offer to pass a dish around
pass a dish around the table

words.enDefinition: to teach or give a custom to a younger generation

examples.en: My friend learned how to pass down a tradition by cooking with her aunt.
examples.zh: 朋友跟姨妈学做菜，明白了怎样「把传统传给后辈」。

examples.en: The film showed how people pass down a tradition through songs and stories.
examples.zh: 影片展示了人们怎样用歌和故事「把传统传给后辈」。

collocations: pass down a tradition through storytelling
decide how to pass down a tradition

words.enDefinition: to choose to skip a question instead of answering it

examples.en: The facilitator said we could pass on a question about family experience.
examples.zh: 引导员说，涉及家庭经历的问题，大家可以「选择不回答」。

examples.en: I chose to pass on a question about a lesson from childhood.
examples.zh: 我对那个关于童年经验的问题「选择不作答」。

collocations: feel free to pass on a question
choose to pass on a question
allow participants to pass on a question

words.enDefinition: to hand a large serving plate to someone nearby

examples.en: Could you pass the platter down this way so Maya can try some?
examples.zh: 能不能「把大餐盘递过来」，让玛雅也尝一点？

examples.en: We had to pass the platter carefully because the table was so crowded.
examples.zh: 餐桌上摆得满满当当，我们得小心「把大餐盘递过去」。

collocations: ask someone to pass the platter

words.enDefinition: a Jewish spring holiday commemorating the biblical Exodus from Egypt

examples.en: The campus dining hall posted information for students observing Passover that spring.
examples.zh: 那年春天，学校食堂为过「犹太逾越节」的学生张贴了相关信息。

examples.en: I asked my friend what she usually did with her family during Passover.
examples.zh: 我问朋友，她家过「犹太逾越节」时通常会做些什么。

words.enDefinition: a ritual meal at Passover involving readings, foods, and the story of the Exodus

examples.en: My classmate invited me to a Passover seder at his family's home that evening.
examples.zh: 同学邀请我那晚去他家参加「逾越节家宴仪式」。

examples.en: The campus group explained what visitors could expect at its Passover seder on Friday.
examples.zh: 校园小组向来访者介绍了周五的「逾越节家宴仪式」会有哪些环节。

words.enDefinition: indicates that the leaves are less colourful than at their best

examples.en: The website said the leaves were past peak near the lake.
examples.zh: 网站说，湖边的秋叶「已过最佳观赏期」。

examples.en: The valley was past peak by the time our reading week began.
examples.zh: 我们的阅读周开始时，山谷的秋叶「已过最佳观赏期」。

collocations: report that foliage is past peak

words.enDefinition: to take steps to improve a relationship after a disagreement

examples.en: I hoped we could patch things up before we went back to our seminar.
examples.zh: 我希望回去上研讨课前，我们能「修补彼此的关系」。

examples.en: They met at the library café to patch things up after avoiding each other all week.
examples.zh: 互相躲了一周后，他们在图书馆咖啡馆见面，想「修补彼此的关系」。

words.enDefinition: a saint regarded as a special protector of a place or group

examples.en: The museum display explained why Saint Patrick is considered Ireland's patron saint today.
examples.zh: 博物馆的展览解释了为什么圣帕特里克今天被视为爱尔兰的「守护圣人」。

examples.en: Our guide pointed out a picture of the city's patron saint near the entrance.
examples.zh: 导游指出入口附近一张描绘这座城市「守护圣人」的画。

collocations: feast day of a patron saint

words.enDefinition: the stage when flowering reaches its fullest

examples.en: The park estimated peak bloom for the middle of the following week that spring.
examples.zh: 那年春天，公园预计下一周中段会进入「盛花期」。

examples.en: Our tutor booked the walk during peak bloom so the class could see the trees.
examples.zh: 导师把散步安排在「盛花期」，这样全班都能看到开花的树。

words.enDefinition: the period when autumn leaves display their most vivid colours

examples.en: We didn't reach the park until a week after peak fall color.
examples.zh: 我们到公园时，已经过了「秋叶色彩最盛期」一周。

examples.en: The student outdoors club planned a weekend hike around peak fall color.
examples.zh: 学生户外社选在「秋叶色彩最盛期」前后安排了周末徒步。

words.enDefinition: people who live in the same residence hall as the speaker

examples.en: I saw some people from my hall at the food truck near the library.
examples.zh: 我在图书馆旁边的餐车前看到了几个「我宿舍楼的人」。

examples.en: Two people from my hall turned out to be taking the same history class.
examples.zh: 有两个「我宿舍楼的人」原来也选了同一门历史课。

collocations: eat with people from my hall

words.enDefinition: a limit someone sets to protect their comfort, privacy, or time

examples.en: Keeping their messages private was a personal boundary they discussed before dating seriously.
examples.zh: 不公开聊天记录，是他们认真交往前谈过的一条「个人界限」。

examples.en: My friend told me that Sunday study time was a personal boundary for her.
examples.zh: 朋友告诉我，周日的学习时间是她的一条「个人界限」。

words.enDefinition: the area around someone that they expect people to respect

examples.en: I moved my chair back to give my classmate more personal space.
examples.zh: 我把椅子往后挪了挪，给同学多留一些「个人空间」。

examples.en: My friend said she needed personal space when the room became crowded.
examples.zh: 房间里人一多，朋友就说她需要一点「个人空间」。

words.enDefinition: a present made or changed to suit one particular person

examples.en: We chose a personalized gift with her initials stitched on the front.
examples.zh: 我们选了件「个性化定制礼物」，正面绣着她姓名的首字母。

examples.en: The personalized gift had a drawing of the garden behind his flat.
examples.zh: 那份「个性化定制礼物」上画着他公寓后面的花园。

words.enDefinition: the practice of considering a situation from another person's viewpoint

examples.en: Our class used perspective-taking to discuss why the same invitation sounded different to us.
examples.zh: 我们在课上用「换位理解」讨论，为什么大家对同一份邀请的感受不同。

examples.en: The facilitator described perspective-taking as imagining how the new student understood the exchange.
examples.zh: 引导员举例说，「换位理解」是想象新同学会怎么理解刚才的对话。

words.zhGloss: 可接触动物的小动物园
words.enDefinition: a place where visitors can touch some of the animals
acceptedZhAnswers: 可接触动物的小动物园

examples.en: The farm festival had a petting zoo near the pumpkin field.
examples.zh: 农场庆典在南瓜地旁设了个「可接触动物的小动物园」。

examples.en: My host family's kids wanted to see goats at the petting zoo.
examples.zh: 寄宿家庭的孩子想在「可接触动物的小动物园」看山羊。

words.enDefinition: an area where people are asked not to use phones

examples.en: The entrance sign described the small gallery as a phone-free zone during performances.
examples.zh: 入口标牌上说，演出期间，小展厅是「禁用手机的区域」。

examples.en: Our club made the rehearsal room a phone-free zone for one evening.
examples.zh: 社团把排练室设成了一晚上的「禁用手机的区域」。

collocations: a sign for a phone-free zone

words.enDefinition: permission to take or use a photograph of a person

examples.en: The committee collected photo consent before taking pictures at the welcome event.
examples.zh: 委员会在迎新活动中拍照前，先征求了「拍照许可」。

examples.en: I checked the photo consent section before sharing the club's group picture.
examples.zh: 分享社团合影前，我查了「照片使用同意」一栏。

words.enDefinition: a series of messages where people post and respond to photos

examples.en: Our photo thread started with a picture of the first flat we shared.
examples.zh: 我们的「照片讨论串」从一张以前合住的第一套公寓的照片开始。

examples.en: I found the campus picture in a photo thread my classmates had started.
examples.zh: 我在同学发起的一个「照片讨论串」里找到了那张校园照片。

words.expression: pick a day that suits everyone
words.lemma: pick a day that suits everyone
words.zhGloss: 选个大家都方便的日子
words.enDefinition: To choose a date when all members of the group can attend.
acceptedZhAnswers: 选个大家都方便的日子
acceptedEnVariants: pick a day that suits everyone

examples.en: Let's pick a day that suits everyone before we ask about borrowing the common room.
examples.zh: 打听能不能借用公共休息室之前，先「选个大家都方便的日子」吧。

examples.en: We used the group chat to pick a day that suits everyone for our picnic.
examples.zh: 我们在群聊里为野餐「选了个大家都方便的日子」。

collocations: try to pick a day that suits everyone
pick a day that suits everyone in the group
let's pick a day that suits everyone

words.enDefinition: To choose a place to sit, stand, or gather for an activity.

examples.en: Can you pick a spot in the shade while I get the picnic blanket?
examples.zh: 我去拿野餐毯时，你能「在阴凉处挑个位置」吗？

examples.en: Let's pick a spot near the front so the shorter people can see the stage.
examples.zh: 咱们「在靠前的地方挑个位置」吧，让个子矮一点的人也能看到舞台。

collocations: pick a spot near the front
pick a spot in the shade

words.expression: pick up where we left off
words.lemma: pick up where we left off
words.zhGloss: 从上次停下的地方接下去
words.enDefinition: to continue an earlier activity or conversation from the point it stopped
acceptedZhAnswers: 从上次停下的地方接下去
acceptedEnVariants: pick up where we left off

examples.en: At the reunion, we found we could pick up where we left off.
examples.zh: 重聚时，我们发现自己还能「像从前那样聊下去」。

examples.en: We decided to pick up where we left off after comparing our new class schedules.
examples.zh: 对过新的课表后，我们决定「从上次停下的地方接下去」。

collocations: easily pick up where we left off
agree to pick up where we left off
ready to pick up where we left off

words.enDefinition: a blanket spread on the ground to sit on during a picnic

examples.en: We borrowed a picnic blanket from our neighbour before meeting friends in the park.
examples.zh: 去公园和朋友碰头前，我们向邻居借了一条「野餐毯」。

examples.en: My friend folded the picnic blanket while I gathered the empty cups from the grass.
examples.zh: 我从草地上捡起空杯子时，朋友把「野餐毯」叠了起来。

words.enDefinition: a basket or container fitted for carrying picnic food and utensils

examples.en: We packed the picnic hamper with cups and bread before catching the bus.
examples.zh: 坐公交前，我们把杯子和面包装进「野餐提篮」。

examples.en: My neighbour lent me a picnic hamper for the afternoon at the park.
examples.zh: 邻居借给我一个「野餐提篮」，让我下午去公园用。

words.enDefinition: fallen leaves collected or gathered together in one place

examples.en: My neighbour's children kept running into the pile of leaves in the yard.
examples.zh: 邻居家的孩子不停地跑进院子里那「一堆落叶」里。

examples.en: A gust blew the pile of leaves back onto the freshly cleared path.
examples.zh: 一阵风把那「一堆落叶」又吹到了刚扫干净的小路上。

collocations: jump into a pile of leaves

words.enDefinition: a card marking where a particular guest should sit

examples.en: I found my place card next to a little paper pumpkin.
examples.zh: 我在一个小纸南瓜旁找到了自己的「座位名卡」。

examples.en: One student drew a tiny leaf on every place card before dinner.
examples.zh: 饭前，有个同学在每张「座位名卡」上都画了一片小叶子。

words.enDefinition: the dishes and utensils laid out for one person

examples.en: I laid out one more place setting when a neighbour dropped by.
examples.zh: 有个邻居过来时，我又摆了一套「一人份的餐具」。

examples.en: Each place setting had a handwritten card with the guest's name.
examples.zh: 每套「一人份的摆台餐具」旁都有一张写着客人姓名的手写卡片。

words.enDefinition: a close, affectionate relationship without a sexual element, often a friendship

examples.en: She explained that theirs was a platonic relationship when a classmate assumed they were dating.
examples.zh: 同学以为他们在交往，她解释说，两人是「纯友谊关系」。

examples.en: They had a close platonic relationship and often went to films together after lectures.
examples.zh: 他们是关系很好的「纯友谊关系」，下课后常一起看电影。

collocations: describe it as a platonic relationship

words.enDefinition: to unfairly give certain people more attention or better treatment than others

examples.en: I worried that the organiser might play favourites when choosing who led each activity.
examples.zh: 我担心组织者在选每项活动的带领人时会「偏袒某些人」。

examples.en: She didn't want to play favourites between her two groups of friends at university.
examples.zh: 她不想在大学两群朋友之间「偏袒某些人」。

words.enDefinition: to act as the person who welcomes and looks after visitors

examples.en: It was my turn to play host while my roommates were away.
examples.zh: 我室友都不在，这次轮到我「做东招待」。

examples.en: We offered to play host for three classmates who had just arrived.
examples.zh: 我们主动为刚到的三位同学「做东招待」。

words.enDefinition: To wait and decide what to do as the situation becomes clearer.

examples.en: Let's play it by ear because we won't know whether the courtyard is free until noon.
examples.zh: 我们要到中午才知道庭院能不能用，所以「看情况再定」吧。

examples.en: We can play it by ear until we find out when the exhibition closes.
examples.zh: 先「看情况再定」吧，得等确定展览几点关门。

collocations: decide to play it by ear
play it by ear if it rains

words.enDefinition: to let audio play through a speaker where others can hear it

examples.en: I asked my friend not to play it out loud on the bus.
examples.zh: 我请朋友在公交车上别「把声音外放」。

examples.en: She asked before deciding to play it out loud in the common room.
examples.zh: 她先问了一声，再决定要不要在公共休息室「把声音外放」。

collocations: choose to play it out loud
ask before you play it out loud

words.enDefinition: to try to bring two people together as potential romantic partners

examples.en: Our friends liked to play matchmaker whenever we mentioned someone from the film club.
examples.zh: 我们提到电影社里的人，朋友就爱「当红娘牵线」。

examples.en: I promised not to play matchmaker unless both of them asked for an introduction.
examples.zh: 我答应除非两人都要求介绍，否则不「当红娘牵线」。

words.enDefinition: a joke or effect based on similar sounds or different meanings

examples.en: I missed the play on words because one meaning was new to me.
examples.zh: 我只知道其中一个意思，所以没听懂那个「双关文字游戏」。

examples.en: The tutor explained the play on words in our club's bilingual poster.
examples.zh: 导师解释了社团双语海报上的「双关文字游戏」。

words.expression: please thank your family for me
words.lemma: please thank your family for me
words.enDefinition: asks someone to pass your thanks on to their family
acceptedEnVariants: please thank your family for me

examples.en: Please thank your family for me. I felt very welcome at your house last night.
examples.zh: 「请替我谢谢你家人」。昨晚在你家，我感觉很受欢迎。

examples.en: I texted, "Please thank your family for me," after getting back to my place that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚回到自己住处后，我发消息说：「请替我谢谢你家人」。

collocations: and please thank your family for me
please thank your family for me when you see them
while you're there, please thank your family for me

words.enDefinition: A guest that an invited person is allowed to bring.

examples.en: I asked whether I could bring a plus-one because my sister was visiting that weekend.
examples.zh: 姐姐那个周末要来，我就问这次邀请能不能「多带一位同伴」。

examples.en: My roommate came as my plus-one when our classmates booked a few extra seats.
examples.zh: 同学们多订了几个座位，室友就作为我「多带的那位同伴」一起来了。

words.enDefinition: A plant with colorful upper leaves, commonly used as a Christmas decoration.

examples.en: A potted poinsettia stood beside the sign for the residence hall's December opening hours.
examples.zh: 宿舍楼十二月开放时间的告示旁摆着一盆「一品红」。

examples.en: My flatmate recognized the poinsettia in the window because her family displays one at Christmas.
examples.zh: 室友认出了橱窗里的「一品红」，因为她家圣诞节也会摆一盆。

words.enDefinition: A public cold-water swim often held on New Year's Day in places such as Vancouver.

examples.en: My roommate sent a photo of spectators watching a polar bear swim on New Year's Day.
examples.zh: 室友发来照片，里面是元旦当天围观「新年冬泳活动」的人。

examples.en: The museum displayed an old poster for a polar bear swim beside other New Year traditions.
examples.zh: 博物馆陈列了一张「新年冬泳活动」的旧海报，旁边还有其他新年习俗的展品。

collocations: a poster for a polar bear swim

words.enDefinition: to share a message in the group area meant for its topic

examples.en: Our club moderator reminded us to post in the right channel for announcements.
examples.zh: 社团管理员提醒大家，要把公告「发到对应的频道」。

examples.en: I checked the topic list so I could post in the right channel.
examples.zh: 我查了话题列表，好「发到对应的频道」。

collocations: remember to post in the right channel
ask members to post in the right channel
post in the right channel for your topic

words.enDefinition: a list for recording what guests will bring to a shared meal

examples.en: The club posted a potluck sign-up sheet for anyone bringing food to dinner.
examples.zh: 社团公布了「自带菜报名表」，供准备带食物来吃晚饭的人填写。

examples.en: I checked the potluck sign-up sheet before deciding whether to bring dessert.
examples.zh: 决定要不要带甜点前，我看了看「自带菜报名表」。

collocations: fill in the potluck sign-up sheet
add your dish to the potluck sign-up sheet

words.enDefinition: a living plant that is growing in a container

examples.en: We brought a potted plant for the windowsill in her new flat.
examples.zh: 我们带了盆「盆栽」，给她摆在新公寓的窗台上。

examples.en: The host put the potted plant next to her mug of tea.
examples.zh: 主人把「盆栽」摆在自己那杯茶旁边。

words.enDefinition: a present chosen to be useful in someone's daily life

examples.en: My aunt brought a practical gift for my kitchen when she visited.
examples.zh: 姨妈来做客时，给我的厨房带了件「实用礼物」。

examples.en: I wanted a practical gift my roommate would actually use after moving.
examples.zh: 我想送一件室友搬家后真能用上的「实用礼物」。

words.enDefinition: the name or title someone wants others to use

examples.en: The organiser asked each guest about their preferred form of address before the panel.
examples.zh: 座谈开始前，组织者向每位来宾问了他们「希望别人怎么称呼自己」。

examples.en: I wrote the tutor's preferred form of address on a note by my screen.
examples.zh: 我在屏幕旁的便签上记下了导师「希望使用的称呼」。

collocations: ask about someone's preferred form of address
note the preferred form of address
use someone's preferred form of address

words.enDefinition: to keep asking after someone seems unwilling to say more

examples.en: I chose not to press for details when my classmate grew quiet.
examples.zh: 同学沉默下来后，我决定不再「追问细节」。

examples.en: Our club leader did not press for details after I mentioned a family matter.
examples.zh: 我提到家里的事后，社团负责人没有「追问细节」。

collocations: try not to press for details
press for details about a private matter

words.enDefinition: A meeting or social event meant for a limited invited group.

examples.en: They planned a private gathering for the four classmates who had worked on the exhibition.
examples.zh: 他们为一起做展览的四位同学安排了一场「私人聚会」。

examples.en: The courtyard was booked for a private gathering when we went past it after class.
examples.zh: 我们下课经过庭院时，那里已被预订举办一场「私人聚会」。

words.enDefinition: a question or opening line offered to help someone fill in a profile

examples.en: I chose a profile prompt that let me write about my favourite campus café.
examples.zh: 我选了一道「个人资料回答题」，可以写我最喜欢的校园咖啡馆。

examples.en: Her answer to the profile prompt gave me something specific to ask about.
examples.zh: 她对那道「个人资料回答题」的回答，让我有了一个具体的话题可以问。

words.enDefinition: to say someone's name aloud in a particular way

examples.en: I would rather ask how to pronounce someone's name than quietly avoid using it.
examples.zh: 我宁愿问清楚「怎么念对方的名字」，也不愿悄悄避开这个称呼。

examples.en: It takes practice to pronounce someone's name if the sounds are new to you.
examples.zh: 要是那些发音不熟，「念对方的名字」就得练一练。

collocations: know how to pronounce someone's name

words.enDefinition: an action showing romantic affection that other people in public can see

examples.en: They talked about what counted as a public display of affection near the residence.
examples.zh: 两人聊到，在宿舍附近哪些行为算「公开场合的亲密举动」。

examples.en: A quick hug was the only public display of affection that either felt comfortable with.
examples.zh: 两人都只接受短暂拥抱这类「公开场合的亲密举动」。

collocations: a brief public display of affection
comfortable with a public display of affection
avoid a public display of affection

words.enDefinition: An event anyone can attend under the stated entry conditions.

examples.en: The film screening was a public event, so our neighbors asked if they could join us.
examples.zh: 那场电影放映是「面向公众的活动」，所以邻居问能不能和我们一起去。

examples.en: We chose a public event at the art center because our friends study elsewhere.
examples.zh: 朋友们在别的学校读书，我们就选了艺术中心一场「面向公众的活动」。

words.enDefinition: an officially recognized day on which many people get time off

examples.en: The campus library changed its opening hours because Monday was a public holiday.
examples.zh: 周一是「公众假日」，校园图书馆调整了开放时间。

examples.en: My flatmate checked which shops would open on the public holiday in June.
examples.zh: 室友查了六月的「公众假日」有哪些商店会开门。

words.enDefinition: to move a chair closer so you can sit nearby

examples.en: Our group was still talking, so I asked her to pull up a chair.
examples.zh: 我们那组还在聊天，我就请她「拉把椅子过来坐」。

examples.en: You can pull up a chair and listen if you don't feel like talking yet.
examples.zh: 如果暂时不想说话，你可以「拉把椅子过来坐」着听。

collocations: tell someone to pull up a chair
invite someone to pull up a chair
pull up a chair beside us

words.enDefinition: a competition for the best designs cut into pumpkins

examples.en: My flatmate entered the pumpkin carving contest with a design of our library.
examples.zh: 室友用我们图书馆的图案参加了「南瓜雕刻比赛」。

examples.en: The pumpkin carving contest winners had their pumpkins displayed in the student centre.
examples.zh: 「南瓜雕刻比赛」获奖者的南瓜摆在学生中心展示。

words.enDefinition: the activity of decorating pumpkins by applying paint to the surface

examples.en: The art club put on a pumpkin painting workshop during lunch.
examples.zh: 美术社在午餐时间办了一场「南瓜彩绘」活动。

examples.en: We tried pumpkin painting because we wanted to cover the pumpkins in dots.
examples.zh: 我们想给南瓜画满圆点，所以尝试了「南瓜彩绘」。

words.enDefinition: a field where pumpkins grow, often open for visitors to pick

examples.en: We took the bus to a pumpkin patch just outside town.
examples.zh: 我们坐公交去了镇外的一个「南瓜园」。

examples.en: Our campus group visited a pumpkin patch with a farm stand nearby.
examples.zh: 我们学校的小组去了一家「南瓜园」，附近有一个农场小摊。

collocations: take a trip to a pumpkin patch
choose a pumpkin at a pumpkin patch

words.enDefinition: a sweet baked pie filled with a spiced pumpkin mixture

examples.en: Our host served pumpkin pie after everyone finished sharing their holiday stories.
examples.zh: 大家讲完各自的节日故事后，主人端上了「南瓜派」。

examples.en: I had a slice of pumpkin pie at my first Friendsgiving dinner.
examples.zh: 我第一次参加朋友感恩节聚餐时，吃了一块「南瓜派」。

words.enDefinition: a blend of spices traditionally used to flavour pumpkin pie

examples.en: The café had a sign for drinks flavoured with pumpkin spice this week.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆的牌子上写着，本周有用「南瓜派香料混合物」调味的饮品。

examples.en: One of my classmates brought cookies that smelled like pumpkin spice.
examples.zh: 一位同学带来了饼干，闻起来有「南瓜派香料混合物」的味道。

words.enDefinition: a contest that compares pumpkins to see which is heaviest

examples.en: People crowded around the scale to watch the pumpkin weigh-off on Saturday.
examples.zh: 周六，人们围着秤看「南瓜重量比赛」。

examples.en: My classmate brought his biggest pumpkin to the county fair's pumpkin weigh-off.
examples.zh: 同学把自己最大的南瓜带去参加县集市的「南瓜重量比赛」。

words.enDefinition: to slide the seat back under the table after getting up

examples.en: The notice read, “Push your chair in before you leave the room.”
examples.zh: 通知写着，离开房间前请「把椅子推回桌下」。

examples.en: My roommate said, “Push your chair in,” as we got up after lunch.
examples.zh: 我们午饭后起身时，室友说「把椅子推回桌下」。

collocations: remember to push your chair in
push your chair in when you leave

words.expression: put a face to a name
words.lemma: put a face to a name
words.enDefinition: to learn what someone you know by name looks like
acceptedEnVariants: put a face to a name

examples.en: We'd emailed twice, so it was nice to finally put a face to a name.
examples.zh: 我们发过两次邮件，终于能「把名字和长相对上」了，真好。

examples.en: The video introductions helped me put a face to a name before I moved into housing.
examples.zh: 搬进宿舍前，自我介绍视频帮我「把名字和长相对上」。

collocations: finally put a face to a name
nice to put a face to a name
help put a face to a name

words.enDefinition: to place a towel where a visitor can use it

examples.en: I'll put a towel out so you don't have to look for one.
examples.zh: 我会「拿条毛巾放好」，省得你自己找。

examples.en: My roommate offered to put a towel out for my sister before she arrived.
examples.zh: 妹妹到之前，室友说可以为她「拿条毛巾放好」。

collocations: remember to put a towel out
offer to put a towel out
put a towel out for a guest

words.enDefinition: to develop lasting connections with a place where you live

examples.en: I started to put down roots when I joined the neighbourhood choir.
examples.zh: 加入邻里合唱团后，我开始「在当地扎下根」。

examples.en: After graduation, she wanted to put down roots in the city she knew.
examples.zh: 毕业后，她想「在自己熟悉的城市扎下根」。

collocations: put down roots in a new city

words.enDefinition: to place snacks where people can easily take them

examples.en: I offered to put out some snacks while my roommate went to meet our neighbours.
examples.zh: 室友去接邻居时，我主动说可以「摆点零食出来」。

examples.en: We decided to put out some snacks rather than cook a whole meal that evening.
examples.zh: 那天晚上，我们决定只「摆点零食出来」，不做一整顿饭。

collocations: offer to put out some snacks
put out some snacks for guests
remember to put out some snacks

words.enDefinition: to think carefully about what someone would like or appreciate

examples.en: You can tell they put some thought into it when you see the handwritten note.
examples.zh: 看见手写留言时，就知道他们确实「用心考虑过」。

examples.en: I tried to put some thought into it rather than buying the first thing I saw.
examples.zh: 我尽量「用点心考虑」，不会看见第一件就买。

collocations: you really put some thought into it
glad you put some thought into it
try to put some thought into it

words.enDefinition: to give a visitor somewhere to stay for a short time

examples.en: We could put someone up on the sofa if the buses stopped running.
examples.zh: 如果公交停运，我们能「让人在家留宿」，睡沙发。

examples.en: It's easier to put someone up now that the spare room is cleared.
examples.zh: 现在备用房间收拾出来了，「让人在家留宿」容易多了。

collocations: put someone up for the weekend

words.expression: put your bag on the floor
words.lemma: put your bag on the floor
words.enDefinition: to put your bag down rather than occupy another seat with it
acceptedEnVariants: put your bag on the floor

examples.en: The notice said, “Put your bag on the floor during busy journeys.”
examples.zh: 通知请乘客在车厢拥挤时「把包放地上」。

examples.en: “Put your bag on the floor,” my friend said as another student approached.
examples.zh: 又一位同学走过来时，朋友说「把包放地上吧」。

collocations: please put your bag on the floor
put your bag on the floor by your feet
put your bag on the floor to free a seat

words.expression: put your litter in the bin
words.lemma: put your litter in the bin
words.enDefinition: to drop waste into the container provided rather than leave it behind
acceptedEnVariants: put your litter in the bin

examples.en: The park sign read, “Put your litter in the bin by the exit.”
examples.zh: 公园的标牌写着「请把垃圾扔进出口处的垃圾桶」。

examples.en: The event flyer said, “Put your litter in the bin before you leave.”
examples.zh: 活动传单上写着「离开前把垃圾扔进垃圾桶」。

collocations: please put your litter in the bin
put your litter in the bin before leaving
remember to put your litter in the bin

words.expression: put your napkin on your lap
words.lemma: put your napkin on your lap
words.enDefinition: to place your napkin across your legs while sitting at the table
acceptedEnVariants: put your napkin on your lap

examples.en: The guide said to put your napkin on your lap when you sit down.
examples.zh: 指南写着，坐下后「把餐巾放在腿上」。

examples.en: The host smiled and said, “Put your napkin on your lap if you like.”
examples.zh: 主持人微笑着说「如果你愿意，可以把餐巾放在腿上」。

collocations: remember to put your napkin on your lap
put your napkin on your lap first
put your napkin on your lap after sitting

words.expression: put your own spin on it
words.lemma: put your own spin on it
words.enDefinition: to change something familiar so it reflects your own ideas
acceptedEnVariants: put your own spin on it

examples.en: My aunt said to put your own spin on it when following her recipe.
examples.zh: 姨妈说，照她的菜谱做时也可以「按自己的方式改一改」。

examples.en: The volunteer said, “Put your own spin on it,” and showed us her version.
examples.zh: 志愿者说「按自己的方式改一改」，然后给我们看了她的版本。

collocations: feel free to put your own spin on it
try to put your own spin on it
find a way to put your own spin on it

words.enDefinition: to make an effort to meet people despite feeling shy

examples.en: I had to put yourself out there a little before I met anyone from my course.
examples.zh: 我得稍微「主动去认识别人」，才认识了同专业的同学。

examples.en: It's hard to put yourself out there when you don't know the language well.
examples.zh: 语言还不熟的时候，要「主动去认识别人」挺难的。

collocations: find ways to put yourself out there
hard to put yourself out there
decide to put yourself out there

words.enDefinition: time spent together with attention that helps strengthen a relationship

examples.en: We set aside some quality time after exams and cooked lunch together at home.
examples.zh: 考试后，我们专门留了点「专心相处的时光」，一起在家做午饭。

examples.en: She suggested turning off their phones so they could have some quality time together.
examples.zh: 她建议关掉手机，好有一点「专心相处的时光」。

words.zhGloss: 断章取义地引用别人的话
words.enDefinition: to repeat words without the surrounding information needed to understand them
acceptedZhAnswers: 断章取义地引用别人的话

examples.en: I did not want to quote someone out of context in our club newsletter.
examples.zh: 我不想在社团简报里「断章取义地引用别人的话」。

examples.en: Our editor explained how easy it was to quote someone out of context online.
examples.zh: 编辑解释了在网上多么容易「断章取义地引用别人的话」。

collocations: try not to quote someone out of context
be careful not to quote someone out of context
quote someone out of context in a post

words.enDefinition: a variety in how a group of people pronounce their language

examples.en: Our student radio show included a range of accents from across the campus.
examples.zh: 我们的学生广播节目里能听到校园里的「多种口音」。

examples.en: I heard a range of accents in the audio guide made by volunteers.
examples.zh: 志愿者制作的语音导览里，我听到了「多种口音」。

collocations: a recording with a range of accents

words.enDefinition: to stretch over the table to get something farther away

examples.en: I asked for the bowl so I wouldn't have to reach across the table.
examples.zh: 我请人把碗递过来，这样就不用「伸手越过餐桌」。

examples.en: My sleeve brushed the jug when I tried to reach across the table.
examples.zh: 我想「伸手越过餐桌」时，袖子擦到了水壶。

collocations: try not to reach across the table
reach across the table for the salt
avoid having to reach across the table

words.enDefinition: to initiate contact with a friend, especially to ask or offer support

examples.en: I decided to reach out to a friend after a week of studying alone.
examples.zh: 一个人学了一周后，我决定「主动联系一位朋友」。

examples.en: She made time to reach out to a friend who had just started university.
examples.zh: 她抽时间「主动联系一位刚上大学的朋友」。

collocations: decide to reach out to a friend
remember to reach out to a friend
time to reach out to a friend

words.enDefinition: to notice how others feel and adapt your behaviour accordingly

examples.en: I tried to read the room before making a joke during the discussion.
examples.zh: 讨论时，我先「察看现场气氛」，再决定要不要开玩笑。

examples.en: My teammate stopped halfway through the story and took a moment to read the room.
examples.zh: 队友讲到一半停了停，「察看现场气氛」。

words.enDefinition: to interpret clues in someone's actions to understand their intentions or feelings

examples.en: I tried to read the signs but still couldn't tell how he felt.
examples.zh: 我试着「从迹象作出判断」，还是看不出他怎么想。

examples.en: Rather than read the signs from brief messages, she asked whether he was interested.
examples.zh: 她直接问他有没有兴趣，没再「从几条简短消息里的迹象作判断」。

words.enDefinition: to imagine extra meaning without enough evidence to support it

examples.en: I tried not to read too much into my classmate's short reply.
examples.zh: 同学回复得很简短，我尽量不「过度解读」。

examples.en: It was easy to read too much into the long pause before her answer.
examples.zh: 她回答前停顿了很久，很容易让人「过度解读」。

collocations: try not to read too much into a remark
read too much into a pause
easy to read too much into a short reply

words.zhGloss: 分手后迅速开始的恋情
words.enDefinition: a relationship started soon after a breakup, often before the earlier feelings fade
acceptedZhAnswers: 分手后迅速开始的恋情

examples.en: Her friend asked whether it felt like a rebound relationship after such a short break.
examples.zh: 间隔这么短，朋友问她是否觉得那是段「分手后迅速开始的恋情」。

examples.en: They talked about whether a rebound relationship could turn into something more serious over time.
examples.zh: 他们谈到，「分手后迅速开始的恋情」能否随着时间发展成更认真的关系。

words.enDefinition: to restore the ability to trust someone after it was damaged

examples.en: We knew it would take time to rebuild trust after the message was shared.
examples.zh: 消息被传开后，我们知道「重建信任」要时间。

examples.en: I wanted to rebuild trust by following through on the plans we made together.
examples.zh: 我想兑现一起定下的计划，好「重建信任」。

words.enDefinition: to respond to a kind action, feeling, or effort with one of your own

examples.en: My neighbour brought soup last week, so I wanted to reciprocate with some bread.
examples.zh: 邻居上周送了汤，我想送点面包来「以同样的方式回应」。

examples.en: I noticed how my friends reciprocate when someone checks in after a difficult day.
examples.zh: 有人在他们忙完难熬的一天后发来问候，我留意到朋友会怎样「以同样的方式回应」。

words.enDefinition: to identify a person you have seen in a class

examples.en: It was nice to recognise someone from class when I reached the crowded dining hall.
examples.zh: 进到挤满人的食堂时，能「认出一个上课见过的人」让我很高兴。

examples.en: I thought I might recognise someone from class at the welcome picnic on Friday.
examples.zh: 我想周五迎新野餐时也许能「认出一个上课见过的人」。

collocations: recognise someone from class at lunch
recognise someone from class by their voice

words.zhGloss: 重新亲近自己的文化根脉
words.enDefinition: to renew contact with traditions linked to your family or community history
acceptedZhAnswers: 重新亲近自己的文化根脉

examples.en: The speaker described how you can reconnect with your roots through family recipes.
examples.zh: 发言者讲了怎样通过家传菜谱「重新亲近自己的文化根脉」。

examples.en: The archive offers one way to reconnect with your roots through recorded family stories.
examples.zh: 档案里录下的家庭故事，是「重新亲近自己的文化根脉」的一种途径。

collocations: find ways to reconnect with your roots
use stories to reconnect with your roots
reconnect with your roots through music

words.enDefinition: A small red packet used to give money on occasions such as Lunar New Year.

examples.en: A classmate showed me a red envelope his grandmother had given him for the holiday.
examples.zh: 同学给我看了奶奶过节时给他的一个「红包」。

examples.en: We made a paper red envelope at the library's Lunar New Year activity table.
examples.zh: 我们在图书馆的农历新年活动桌上做了一个纸「红包」。

collocations: a red envelope with lucky money

words.enDefinition: A lantern with a red covering, commonly seen at some Lunar New Year celebrations.

examples.en: We noticed a red lantern hanging above the door of the neighborhood community center.
examples.zh: 我们留意到社区中心门上挂着一只「红灯笼」。

examples.en: The campus craft booth displayed a red lantern made by students for their New Year event.
examples.zh: 校园手工摊位展出了一只同学们为新年活动做的「红灯笼」。

words.enDefinition: a quiet area for personal thought, prayer or contemplation

examples.en: The building map showed a reflection space near the ground-floor meeting rooms.
examples.zh: 建筑导览图标出底层会议室旁有一个「静思空间」。

examples.en: I asked the event organiser whether the reflection space would remain open after lunch.
examples.zh: 我问活动组织者，午饭后「静思空间」是否还开放。

words.zhGloss: 把收到的礼物转送别人
words.enDefinition: to give someone a present you previously received yourself
acceptedZhAnswers: 把收到的礼物转送别人

examples.en: I chose to regift the spare notebook because I already had one.
examples.zh: 我已经有一本笔记本，就把收到的那本「转送给别人」了。

examples.en: My friend said I could regift the mug if I wanted.
examples.zh: 朋友说，我如果愿意，可以「把收到的马克杯转送别人」。

words.enDefinition: a practice especially associated with a particular area

examples.en: We learned about a regional custom from a student who grew up nearby.
examples.zh: 住在附近长大的一位同学给我们讲了一个「地方习俗」。

examples.en: The display described the game as a regional custom with several local versions.
examples.zh: 展板把这个游戏介绍为一种「地方习俗」，各地玩法略有不同。

collocations: explain the history of a regional custom

words.enDefinition: the way language is used in a particular area

examples.en: The dictionary marked the word as an example of regional usage in English.
examples.zh: 词典把这个词标为英语「地区用法」的一个例子。

examples.en: We compared regional usage after hearing two different words for the same bread.
examples.zh: 我们听见同种面包有两种叫法，就比较了「地区用法」。

words.enDefinition: repeated brief contact to ask how someone is doing

examples.en: Our regular check-in made it easier to notice when someone was having a hard week.
examples.zh: 「定期联络问候」让我们更容易留意到谁这周过得比较困难。

examples.en: We had a regular check-in over coffee until my friend moved to another city.
examples.zh: 在朋友搬去另一座城之前，我们一直一起喝咖啡「定期联络问候」。

collocations: make time for a regular check-in

words.enDefinition: to bring back a friendship that has grown weaker or been inactive

examples.en: They used their old film club to rekindle a friendship after years of silence.
examples.zh: 多年没联系后，两人借原来的电影社活动「重新培养一段友情」。

examples.en: I wanted to rekindle a friendship but didn't know how to start the conversation.
examples.zh: 我想「重新培养一段友情」，却不知怎样开口。

collocations: a chance to rekindle a friendship

words.enDefinition: to revive a romantic connection that has weakened or ended

examples.en: They hoped to rekindle a relationship after moving back to the same city for work.
examples.zh: 两人工作后搬回同一座城，希望能「重新培养感情」。

examples.en: She wasn't sure whether to rekindle a relationship with someone she had dated before university.
examples.zh: 她不确定是否要和大学前交往过的人「重新培养感情」。

words.enDefinition: what someone hopes to find or develop in a romantic relationship

examples.en: We talked about relationship goals after realising we wanted different things for next year.
examples.zh: 意识到对明年的期望不同后，我们聊了「期望的恋爱方向」。

examples.en: The profile asked about relationship goals alongside hobbies and places people liked to visit.
examples.zh: 个人资料除了问爱好和喜欢去的地方，还问「期望的恋爱方向」。

words.enDefinition: information about the romantic relationships someone has previously had

examples.en: They didn't discuss relationship history until they knew each other well enough to feel comfortable.
examples.zh: 两人熟到觉得自在后才聊「过往恋爱经历」。

examples.en: I chose to leave my relationship history out of the conversation that evening.
examples.zh: 那天晚上，我选择不在谈话中提到「过往恋爱经历」。

collocations: share part of your relationship history

words.enDefinition: an important event marking a new stage in a romantic relationship

examples.en: Moving into the same city felt like a relationship milestone for both of them.
examples.zh: 搬到同一座城，对他们俩而言是个「恋爱关系的里程碑」。

examples.en: They celebrated a small relationship milestone with dinner at the place they first met.
examples.zh: 他们回第一次见面的地方吃饭，庆祝一个小小的「恋爱关系的里程碑」。

words.enDefinition: the description of whether and how someone is romantically involved

examples.en: I left my relationship status off my profile because I preferred to keep it private.
examples.zh: 我希望这件事保密，所以没把「恋爱关系状态」放在个人资料里。

examples.en: They didn't discuss relationship status until both felt comfortable raising the subject in person.
examples.zh: 两人都觉得可以当面聊起这个话题时，才谈了「恋爱关系状态」。

words.enDefinition: a practice or occasion followed for reasons of faith

examples.en: Our organiser asked whether the rehearsal might overlap with a religious observance.
examples.zh: 组织者问排练时间会不会与某项「宗教礼仪活动」冲突。

examples.en: My friend mentioned a religious observance when we planned the next meeting.
examples.zh: 我们安排下次见面时，朋友提到一项「宗教礼仪活动」。

collocations: take part in a religious observance

words.enDefinition: to continue to have a friendship after the nature of a relationship changes

examples.en: They hoped to remain friends after they both decided the relationship was over.
examples.zh: 两人都决定结束恋情后，希望「仍然做朋友」。

examples.en: It was important for them to remain friends because they shared so many classes.
examples.zh: 两人有很多共同的课，所以「仍然做朋友」对他们很重要。

words.zhGloss: 结束之前请留在座位上
words.enDefinition: to stay in your seat until a performance or activity is over
acceptedZhAnswers: 结束之前请留在座位上

examples.en: The programme asked the audience to remain seated until the end of the performance.
examples.zh: 活动手册请观众「在演出结束之前留在座位上」。

examples.en: I decided to remain seated until the end so I wouldn't block anyone's view.
examples.zh: 我决定「结束之前留在座位上」，免得挡住别人。

collocations: ask people to remain seated until the end
choose to remain seated until the end
please remain seated until the end

words.enDefinition: things that make you remember the place or people you come from

examples.en: The smells from my roommate's kitchen were unexpected reminders of home.
examples.zh: 室友厨房里的香味，意外成了「让人想起家乡的事物」。

examples.en: I kept a few reminders of home on the shelf above my bed.
examples.zh: 我把几样「让人想起家乡的事物」放在床上方的架子上。

words.enDefinition: to think or talk with pleasure about something that happened in the past

examples.en: We stayed at the café to reminisce about the year we lived in residence.
examples.zh: 我们留在咖啡馆，「回味」一起住宿舍的那一年。

examples.en: My former classmates liked to reminisce about the trips we took during spring break.
examples.zh: 以前的同学喜欢「回味」我们春假那几次出游。

collocations: get together to reminisce about something

words.enDefinition: to speak or act on behalf of everyone with a given cultural background

examples.en: Nobody expected me to represent an entire culture when I shared a story.
examples.zh: 我讲自己的故事时，没人指望我「代表整个文化群体」。

examples.en: She explained why one student couldn't represent an entire culture in the discussion.
examples.zh: 她解释了为什么一个学生在讨论中无法「代表整个文化群体」。

collocations: be asked to represent an entire culture
feel pressure to represent an entire culture
expect someone to represent an entire culture

words.enDefinition: to rearrange a planned romantic meeting for a different time

examples.en: We had to reschedule a date when my lab session ran over that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午实验课超时，我们不得不「改约会时间」。

examples.en: I asked whether we could reschedule a date for the following week after exams.
examples.zh: 我问能不能「改约会时间」，放到考完试的下一周。

words.enDefinition: not inclined to show feelings or share much personal information

examples.en: I was quite reserved until the others started talking about films.
examples.zh: 大家开始聊电影之前，我一直「比较内敛」。

examples.en: She seemed reserved the first day, but we talked for hours later.
examples.zh: 第一天她显得「比较内敛」，但后来我们聊了好几个小时。

words.enDefinition: to avoid making other people wait or spend time unnecessarily

examples.en: Our committee tried to respect people's time by ending each meeting as planned.
examples.zh: 委员会尽量「尊重别人的时间」，每次会议都按计划结束。

examples.en: She explained that sticking to our schedule was a way to respect people's time.
examples.zh: 她解释说，按时间表行事是「尊重别人的时间」的一种方式。

collocations: show that you respect people's time
respect people's time by starting promptly

words.enDefinition: to accept the limits another person states for their comfort or privacy

examples.en: Being able to respect someone's boundaries includes giving them the quiet time they ask for.
examples.zh: 对方明确说要独处时，给他们留出那段时间，也是在「尊重对方的界限」。

examples.en: It's important to respect someone's boundaries even when they differ from your own.
examples.zh: 即使对方的界限与你自己的不同，也要「尊重对方的界限」。

words.enDefinition: to accept another person's choice even when you had hoped for a different outcome

examples.en: “I respect your decision,” he said when she told him she wasn't ready to date.
examples.zh: 她说还没做好约会的准备，他答道：“我「尊重你的决定」。”

examples.en: I replied, “I respect your decision to wait until after the exams to talk.”
examples.zh: 我回答：“你决定等考试后再谈，我「尊重你的决定」。”

collocations: I respect your decision about this

words.enDefinition: to do something helpful for someone who previously helped you

examples.en: I offered to return the favour by carrying her books back to the library.
examples.zh: 我提出帮她把书送回图书馆，「回报她的人情」。

examples.en: He wanted to return the favour after we helped him move into the new flat.
examples.zh: 我们帮他搬进新公寓后，他想「回报人情」。

collocations: find a way to return the favour

words.enDefinition: A family meal held to reunite relatives, often on Chinese New Year's Eve.

examples.en: My roommate joined her family's reunion dinner on video while eating with us on campus.
examples.zh: 室友在学校跟我们吃饭时，通过视频参加了家里的「年夜团圆饭」。

examples.en: We invited friends who could not go home to a reunion dinner on Chinese New Year’s Eve.
examples.zh: 中国春节除夕，我们邀请没能回家的朋友一起吃「年夜团圆饭」。

collocations: return home for a reunion dinner

words.enDefinition: a weekend set aside for people who have been apart to meet again

examples.en: We booked our train tickets for the reunion weekend before the cheap seats sold out.
examples.zh: 便宜座位卖光之前，我们订了「聚会周末」的火车票。

examples.en: Our reunion weekend began with a walk through the neighbourhood where we used to live.
examples.zh: 我们在以前住的街区散了个步，拉开了「聚会周末」的序幕。

words.zhGloss: 恢复一项曾中断的传统
words.enDefinition: to start a customary activity again after it stopped for a time
acceptedZhAnswers: 恢复一项曾中断的传统

examples.en: Our society voted to revive a tradition that had lapsed during remote classes.
examples.zh: 社团表决同意「恢复一项线上上课期间中断的传统」。

examples.en: The neighbours decided to revive a tradition from an old community newsletter.
examples.zh: 邻居们决定「恢复一项曾中断的传统」，灵感来自旧的社区通讯。

collocations: revive a tradition after a pause

words.enDefinition: To mark the beginning of the new year with a celebration.

examples.en: We decided to ring in the new year together instead of traveling across town tonight.
examples.zh: 今晚我们决定一起「迎接新年」，不往城另一头跑了。

examples.en: A few students met on campus to ring in the new year with hot drinks.
examples.zh: 几位同学在校园碰面，端着热饮一起「迎接新年」。

collocations: ring in the new year together
ring in the new year with friends
gather to ring in the new year

words.enDefinition: something done to show affection or romantic interest to another person

examples.en: Bringing tea to the library felt like a romantic gesture during the exam period.
examples.zh: 考试期间送茶来图书馆，感觉是个「表达爱意的举动」。

examples.en: He kept the silly postcard because he had understood it as a romantic gesture.
examples.zh: 他留着那张搞怪的明信片，因为觉得那是「表达爱意的举动」。

words.enDefinition: interest in someone as a possible romantic partner

examples.en: I wasn't sure whether the invitation showed romantic interest or just friendly curiosity.
examples.zh: 我不确定那次邀请是出于「恋爱方面的好感」，还是朋友间的好奇。

examples.en: He made his romantic interest clear when he asked her on a proper date.
examples.zh: 他正式约她出去时，把自己的「恋爱方面的好感」表达清楚了。

words.enDefinition: available space inside a refrigerator for something to be stored

examples.en: Is there room in the fridge for the drink I brought with me?
examples.zh: 「冰箱里有空位」放我带来的饮料吗？

examples.en: My friend found room in the fridge for the dessert I had made.
examples.zh: 朋友在「冰箱里找到空位」，放我做的甜点。

collocations: check whether there's room in the fridge
leave some room in the fridge

words.enDefinition: to support someone and hope they do well, chiefly in North American English

examples.en: We went to the student debate to root for someone from our residence hall.
examples.zh: 我们去看学生辩论，为同宿舍楼的人「打气」。

examples.en: It's easy to root for someone who has worked so hard on a project.
examples.zh: 看到对方为项目这么努力，很自然就想「为这个人打气」。

collocations: root for someone on the team

words.enDefinition: an expression with a similar meaning without being an exact match

examples.en: My roommate offered a rough equivalent so I could understand the saying.
examples.zh: 为了让我听懂那句俗语，室友举了个「大致对应的说法」。

examples.en: The tutor asked for a rough equivalent in another language we knew.
examples.zh: 导师请我们用自己会的另一种语言举一个「大致对应的说法」。

words.enDefinition: To gather the people taking part in the shared activity.

examples.en: Could you round up the group while I check whether our seats are ready?
examples.zh: 我去看看座位有没有准备好，你能「把大家叫到一起」吗？

examples.en: We need to round up the group for a photo before everyone starts leaving.
examples.zh: 大家陆续离开之前，我们得「把大家叫到一起」拍张照。

collocations: try to round up the group
round up the group for a photo

words.enDefinition: To tell the person inviting you whether you will attend.

examples.en: The message asked us to RSVP before Friday so they could reserve enough seats.
examples.zh: 消息请我们在星期五之前「回复是否出席」，这样他们能留够座位。

examples.en: I forgot to RSVP for the picnic even though I had already saved the date.
examples.zh: 虽然我已经把那天腾出来了，还是忘了为野餐「回复是否出席」。

words.enDefinition: to spend time among the same groups of people

examples.en: We seem to run in the same circles even though we study different subjects.
examples.zh: 虽然学的是不同专业，我们好像「常接触同一批人」。

examples.en: Two neighbours realised they run in the same circles and knew several of the same people.
examples.zh: 两位邻居发现自己「常接触同一批人」，都认识其中几位。

collocations: tend to run in the same circles
happen to run in the same circles
still run in the same circles

words.enDefinition: a joke or humorous idea repeated over time among the same people

examples.en: The missing umbrella became a running joke during the rest of our exchange year.
examples.zh: 丢掉的那把伞成了后来整个交换学年「反复被提起的玩笑」。

examples.en: We had a running joke about always choosing the wrong door at the library.
examples.zh: 我们老是选错图书馆的门，这事成了「反复被提起的玩笑」。

words.enDefinition: A polite Korean greeting wishing someone much good fortune in the new year.

examples.en: My classmate practiced saying “Saehae bok mani badeuseyo” before calling her grandparents for Seollal.
examples.zh: 同学在给祖父母打电话拜年之前，练习说「韩语的新年多福」。

examples.en: A sign at the Korean club's table read “Saehae bok mani badeuseyo” above its translation.
examples.zh: 韩国文化社的桌上摆着牌子，译文上方写的是「韩语的新年多福」。

collocations: a card reading Saehae bok mani badeuseyo

words.enDefinition: a subject unlikely to cause tension or make people uncomfortable

examples.en: The campus bus was a safe topic when nobody knew each other yet.
examples.zh: 大家还不认识的时候，校园公交是个「稳妥的话题」。

examples.en: I went with a safe topic and asked about the new student café.
examples.zh: 我选了个「稳妥的话题」，问起新开的学生咖啡馆。

words.enDefinition: a June celebration of Francophone culture that is Quebec's national holiday

examples.en: Our French teacher explained why the town held special events for Saint-Jean-Baptiste Day.
examples.zh: 法语老师解释了镇上为什么会为「圣让巴蒂斯特节」安排特别活动。

examples.en: I joined friends at an outdoor concert on Saint-Jean-Baptiste Day during my Quebec exchange.
examples.zh: 在魁北克交换期间，我在「圣让巴蒂斯特节」那天和朋友去看了户外音乐会。

words.enDefinition: A suggestion or confirmation to meet again at the same time the following week.

examples.en: Same time next week, or will some of you be preparing for the exhibition?
examples.zh: 「下周同一时间」见，还是你们有人要为展览做准备？

examples.en: We agreed on the same time next week before anyone packed up their board games.
examples.zh: 大家收起桌游之前，我们约好了「下周同一时间」见。

collocations: meet at the same time next week
plan for the same time next week

words.enDefinition: students at the same stage in their course or schooling

examples.en: Two of the people I met were in the same year group as me.
examples.zh: 我认识的两个人和我在「同一年级」。

examples.en: We shared some lectures because we were in the same year group at college.
examples.zh: 我们在大学读「同一年级」，有几门大课一起上。

collocations: be in the same year group
people in the same year group
friends from the same year group

words.enDefinition: A traditional Christmas character said to bring gifts to children.

examples.en: A volunteer dressed as Santa Claus handed out stickers at the library's family event.
examples.zh: 图书馆办家庭活动时，一位扮成「圣诞老人」的志愿者发了贴纸。

examples.en: The museum label compared several drawings of Santa Claus from different countries and time periods.
examples.zh: 博物馆的展签对比了不同国家、不同时期画的几幅「圣诞老人」画像。

words.enDefinition: to keep a seat free until another person arrives

examples.en: I asked whether I could save a seat for someone during the talk.
examples.zh: 我问讲座期间能不能「替别人留座」。

examples.en: The usher said we could save a seat for someone until the play started.
examples.zh: 引座员说，开演前我们可以「替别人留座」。

collocations: offer to save a seat for someone
ask if you can save a seat for someone
save a seat for someone near the aisle

words.enDefinition: to keep a gift unopened until a more convenient time

examples.en: Can I save it for later so I can open it with my family?
examples.zh: 我可以「留到之后再打开」吗？我想和家人一起拆。

examples.en: My neighbour told me to save it for later if I was in a hurry.
examples.zh: 邻居说，如果我赶时间，就「留到之后再打开」。

collocations: ask if you can save it for later
decide to save it for later
feel free to save it for later

words.enDefinition: to eat less at first so you can have dessert later

examples.en: We tried to save room for dessert because three people had brought something sweet.
examples.zh: 三个人都带了甜食，所以我们尽量「留点肚子吃甜点」。

examples.en: My roommate reminded everyone to save room for dessert before passing around the rolls.
examples.zh: 室友把面包卷传给大家之前，提醒大家「留点肚子吃甜点」。

collocations: try to save room for dessert
remember to save room for dessert
tell guests to save room for dessert

words.enDefinition: to keep part of the shared food for people who haven't eaten yet

examples.en: We agreed to save some for others who were coming from the lab.
examples.zh: 我们商量好「给其他人留一点」，他们还在实验室。

examples.en: The note asked us to save some for others at the evening session.
examples.zh: 便条请我们「给别人留一点」，他们要晚上才来参加活动。

collocations: ask people to save some for others
remember to save some for others
save some for others who are arriving later

words.enDefinition: To keep a particular date free for an event that will happen later.

examples.en: Can you save the date for the picnic even if we haven't chosen a park yet?
examples.zh: 虽然我们还没选好公园，你能先「预留这个日期」参加野餐吗？

examples.en: Maya asked us to save the date before she shared the rest of the details.
examples.zh: 玛雅先请我们「预留这个日期」，之后才发其他细节。

collocations: ask friends to save the date
send a save the date message
save the date for a picnic

words.enDefinition: to store your phone number in a device's contacts

examples.en: Let me save your number before my phone runs out of battery again.
examples.zh: 我先「存一下你的号码」，免得手机又没电了。

examples.en: Can I save your number so I know it's you when you call?
examples.zh: 我能「存一下你的号码」吗？你打来时我就知道是你了。

words.enDefinition: to part from someone while expecting to see or speak to them again

examples.en: We stopped by the old café to say goodbye for now before her train.
examples.zh: 她坐火车前，我们顺路去老咖啡馆「先道个别」。

examples.en: I knew we'd have to say goodbye for now after the final reunion lunch.
examples.zh: 我知道重聚的最后一顿午饭结束后，我们得「先道个别」。

collocations: come to say goodbye for now
take a moment to say goodbye for now
wave and say goodbye for now

words.enDefinition: to say a short prayer before starting a meal

examples.en: My host asked if we could wait while they say grace.
examples.zh: 主人问，我们能否等一下，让他们「作饭前祷告」。

examples.en: The family chose to say grace quietly before bringing the dishes around.
examples.zh: 这家人先安静地「作饭前祷告」，再把菜传给大家。

words.enDefinition: an informal request to pass your greeting to someone else

examples.en: “Say hi for me if you see Mei at the library,” he said.
examples.zh: 他说：“如果在图书馆看到小梅，「替我打声招呼」。”

examples.en: “Say hi for me when you visit our old neighbours next weekend,” I said.
examples.zh: 我说：“下周末去看以前的邻居时，「替我打声招呼」。”

collocations: say hi for me when you see them
say hi for me next time

words.enDefinition: to greet someone briefly when you walk past or happen to meet

examples.en: At first we would only say hi in passing on our way to class.
examples.zh: 起初，我们只在去上课途中「碰见时顺口打招呼」。

examples.en: I used to say hi in passing before I learned he lived upstairs.
examples.zh: 还不知道他住楼上时，我过去只是「碰见时顺口打招呼」。

collocations: say hi in passing on campus

words.enDefinition: to tell others what good things you appreciate

examples.en: The card said, "Say what you're thankful for if you'd like to share something."
examples.zh: 卡片上写着，如果愿意分享，可以「说说你感激什么」。

examples.en: Before dinner our host said, "Say what you're thankful for in one short sentence."
examples.zh: 晚饭前，主人说：「说说你感激什么」，简短一句话就好。

collocations: take a moment to say what you're thankful for
if you'd like to say what you're thankful for
go around the table and say what you're thankful for

words.enDefinition: a human-shaped figure used in fields or as a decoration

examples.en: Our class built a scarecrow for the fall festival at the farm.
examples.zh: 我们班做了个「稻草人」，放在农场的秋季庆典上。

examples.en: The scarecrow near the corn maze wore a faded university sweatshirt.
examples.zh: 玉米地迷宫附近的「稻草人」穿着件褪了色的大学卫衣。

words.enDefinition: someone you became friends with when you attended school together

examples.en: A school friend came to visit me during my last week on campus.
examples.zh: 在学校的最后一周，一位「上学时认识的朋友」来看我。

examples.en: I shared the wedding photo with a school friend who still knew both families.
examples.zh: 我把婚礼照片发给一位「上学时认识的朋友」，对方至今还认识两家人。

words.enDefinition: to remove seeds from the inside of something using a scoop

examples.en: My roommate volunteered to scoop out the seeds while I chose a pumpkin design.
examples.zh: 我选南瓜图案时，室友主动帮忙「舀出里面的籽」。

examples.en: We each had a bowl to use when we helped scoop out the seeds.
examples.zh: 我们每人都有一个碗，供帮忙「舀出里面的籽」时用。

collocations: use a spoon to scoop out the seeds

words.enDefinition: To move sideways a short distance, usually to make room for someone.

examples.en: Can you scoot over a little so Mina can sit with us on this bench?
examples.zh: 你能「往旁边挪一下」吗？这样米娜也能坐到这条长椅上。

examples.en: I asked my roommate to scoot over when our friends arrived with their coffee.
examples.zh: 朋友们拿着咖啡到了，我请室友「往旁边挪一下」。

words.enDefinition: A written greeting offering good wishes during the year-end holidays.

examples.en: The library email ended with “Season's greetings” and a note about December opening hours.
examples.zh: 图书馆的邮件以「致以节日问候」结尾，还附上了十二月的开放时间。

examples.en: A card reading “Season's greetings” stood on the counter beside the residence front desk.
examples.zh: 宿舍前台旁的柜台上立着一张写有「致以节日问候」的卡片。

words.enDefinition: the planned positions of where different people will sit

examples.en: We changed the seating arrangement so everyone could reach the long table.
examples.zh: 我们改了「座位安排」，这样大家都能坐到长桌旁。

examples.en: Our host kept the seating arrangement informal so guests could move around.
examples.zh: 做东的人把「座位安排」得比较随意，方便客人走动。

words.enDefinition: A formal bow to elders traditionally made during the Korean Lunar New Year.

examples.en: A student described sebae during our class discussion of Korean Lunar New Year customs.
examples.zh: 课堂讨论韩国农历新年习俗时，有位同学介绍了「韩国新年向长辈行礼」。

examples.en: My neighbor explained sebae while showing us photographs from her family's celebration of Seollal.
examples.zh: 邻居给我们看她家过韩国农历新年的照片时，讲了「韩国新年向长辈行礼」。

words.enDefinition: Money some Korean elders give younger relatives after receiving a New Year bow.

examples.en: My classmate talked about receiving sebaetdon during Seollal visits to her grandparents when she was younger.
examples.zh: 同学讲了她小时候过韩国农历新年去看祖父母时领到「韩国新年压岁钱」的经历。

examples.en: The family traditions display mentioned sebaetdon alongside photographs of several generations celebrating Seollal together.
examples.zh: 家庭习俗展介绍了「韩国新年压岁钱」，旁边配有几代人同庆韩国农历新年的照片。

words.zhGloss: 匿名交换圣诞礼物活动
words.enDefinition: A gift exchange in which each participant secretly gives a present to one assigned person.
acceptedZhAnswers: 匿名交换圣诞礼物活动

examples.en: Our floor organized a Secret Santa and agreed on a small spending limit in advance.
examples.zh: 我们楼层办了「匿名交换圣诞礼物活动」，提前说好不要花太多钱。

examples.en: I signed up for Secret Santa before the deadline because I would still be on campus.
examples.zh: 截止前我报名了「匿名交换圣诞礼物活动」，因为到时候我还会留在学校。

collocations: draw a name for Secret Santa

words.enDefinition: a plate holding symbolic foods used during a Passover seder

examples.en: The museum displayed an old seder plate beside photos from several different families.
examples.zh: 博物馆在几个家庭的照片旁展示了一个旧的「逾越节仪式餐盘」。

examples.en: My friend's grandmother explained one of the foods on the seder plate before dinner.
examples.zh: 晚饭前，朋友的奶奶介绍了「逾越节仪式餐盘」上其中一种食物。

words.enDefinition: To find out whether people are interested in a proposed social activity.

examples.en: I'll put the picnic idea in our class chat to see if anyone's interested.
examples.zh: 我会把野餐的想法发到班级群里，「问问有没有人想参加」。

examples.en: We wanted to see if anyone's interested before booking a larger room for the film.
examples.zh: 我们打算先「问问有没有人想参加」，再订一间更大的房间看电影。

collocations: ask in the chat to see if anyone's interested
see if anyone's interested in the picnic
check first to see if anyone's interested

words.enDefinition: to walk with a departing guest as far as the door

examples.en: My host always gets up to see someone to the door when the evening ends.
examples.zh: 晚上的活动结束时，主人总会站起来「送客人到门口」。

examples.en: I went to see someone to the door and nearly forgot to return their umbrella.
examples.zh: 我去「送人到门口」，差点忘了把雨伞还给对方。

collocations: offer to see someone to the door
go to see someone to the door
get up to see someone to the door

words.enDefinition: to continue without deciding in advance how a relationship will develop

examples.en: We agreed to see where things go after getting coffee a couple of times.
examples.zh: 喝了几次咖啡后，我们同意先「看看关系会怎么发展」。

examples.en: I wanted to see where things go before calling it a serious relationship.
examples.zh: 我想先「看看关系会怎么发展」，再把它称为认真的恋爱关系。

collocations: take it easy and see where things go
agree to see where things go
want to see where things go

words.enDefinition: to mail a card with a picture and a short written message

examples.en: I promised to send a postcard from the city where I was studying abroad.
examples.zh: 我答应从自己留学的城市「寄一张明信片」。

examples.en: She wanted to send a postcard instead of only sharing photos in the chat.
examples.zh: 她想「寄一张明信片」，不只在群聊里分享照片。

collocations: send a postcard to a friend

words.enDefinition: to behave in ways that suggest conflicting levels of interest or intention

examples.en: I didn't want to send mixed signals by accepting another date out of politeness.
examples.zh: 我不想出于礼貌接受下次约会，给对方「发出矛盾信号」。

examples.en: She thought he might send mixed signals without realising how she read his messages.
examples.zh: 她觉得，他可能无意中「发出矛盾信号」，不知道她会怎样理解这些消息。

collocations: send mixed signals about a relationship
try not to send mixed signals

words.enDefinition: To distribute invitations to the people you would like to attend.

examples.en: We waited to send out invitations until we knew the courtyard would be available.
examples.zh: 我们等确认庭院可以用之后，才「发出邀请」。

examples.en: I offered to send out invitations while my roommate asked how many chairs we could borrow.
examples.zh: 我主动提出「发出邀请」，室友则去问能借到多少把椅子。

collocations: send out invitations a week early
send out invitations for the picnic

words.enDefinition: to initiate a conversation by sending the first written message

examples.en: I wasn't sure whether to send the first message after we matched yesterday.
examples.zh: 昨天配对后，我一时拿不准要不要「先发消息搭话」。

examples.en: She suggested I send the first message about something we'd both put in our profiles.
examples.zh: 她建议我「先发消息搭话」，说说我们资料里都提到的一个事。

collocations: decide to send the first message
feel ready to send the first message
ask who should send the first message

words.enDefinition: a present valued for the personal memories or feelings it evokes

examples.en: The old photo was a sentimental gift for my roommate before graduation.
examples.zh: 毕业前，我把那张旧照片送给室友，是份「寄托感情的礼物」。

examples.en: I kept the sentimental gift because it reminded me of our first flat.
examples.zh: 我留着那份「寄托感情的礼物」，因为它让我想起我们的第一间合租公寓。

words.enDefinition: The Korean Lunar New Year holiday, often marked by family gatherings or visits.

examples.en: The campus Korean society invited students to a Seollal event in the common room.
examples.zh: 校园韩国文化社邀请同学们到公共休息室参加「韩国农历新年」活动。

examples.en: My roommate called her family in Korea for Seollal while we were studying abroad.
examples.zh: 我们在海外留学时，室友为过「韩国农历新年」给韩国的家人打了电话。

words.enDefinition: to offer shared dishes from which diners serve themselves

examples.en: We chose to serve family-style so people could try what others had brought.
examples.zh: 我们决定「把菜放中间一起夹」，这样大家都能尝尝别人带来的菜。

examples.en: The hosts decided to serve family-style instead of filling plates in the kitchen.
examples.zh: 主人决定「把菜放中间一起夹」，省得在厨房里逐盘给大家盛好。

words.enDefinition: a large spoon for putting food onto someone else's plate

examples.en: I put a serving spoon beside the dish my roommate had brought.
examples.zh: 我在室友带来的那盘菜旁放了一把「公用盛菜勺」。

examples.en: Someone fetched another serving spoon when the guests opened the second dish.
examples.zh: 客人打开第二盘菜时，有人又拿来一把「公用盛菜勺」。

words.enDefinition: To agree on the calendar date when an event will take place.

examples.en: We wanted to set a date for the picnic before people booked their trains home.
examples.zh: 我们想在大家订好回家的火车票之前，把野餐的「日期定下来」。

examples.en: Could we set a date after our last exam so more people can come along?
examples.zh: 我们能不能把「日期定在」最后一场考试之后，好让更多人来？

collocations: set a date for the picnic
set a date that works for everyone

words.enDefinition: to prepare an additional seat with dishes and utensils for a meal

examples.en: Could you set another place for my roommate before we start dinner tonight?
examples.zh: 今晚开饭前，你能给我室友「再摆一套餐具」吗？

examples.en: We had to set another place when a friend stopped by unexpectedly.
examples.zh: 有位朋友没提前打招呼就来了，我们得「再摆一套餐具」。

collocations: ask someone to set another place
set another place for a guest

words.enDefinition: to explain openly what you expect so that the other person understands

examples.en: They decided to set clear expectations about how often they would see each other.
examples.zh: 两人决定「说清各自的期待」，说明希望多久见一次。

examples.en: It helped to set clear expectations before they planned a holiday together in June.
examples.zh: 六月一起安排假期前，「说清各自的期待」让事情更顺利。

collocations: set clear expectations about a relationship

words.enDefinition: to arrange for a person to meet someone who might become their partner

examples.en: My sister loves to set someone up whenever two people in her club get along.
examples.zh: 姐姐社团里只要有两个人合得来，她就喜欢「给人介绍约会对象」。

examples.en: Would you set someone up if you knew both people wanted to meet?
examples.zh: 如果知道两人都想认识对方，你会「给人介绍约会对象」吗？

collocations: set a friend up with someone

words.enDefinition: to correct a misunderstanding about what really happened

examples.en: I wrote to set the record straight after hearing a different story from classmates.
examples.zh: 从同学那里听到另一种说法后，我发消息想「把事实澄清」。

examples.en: She asked for a moment to set the record straight before the group finished talking.
examples.zh: 大家还没聊完，她就希望占用一点时间「把事实澄清」。

collocations: want to set the record straight
take time to set the record straight
try to set the record straight

words.enDefinition: to make your phone vibrate rather than ring for notifications

examples.en: The host said, “Set your phone to vibrate if you need it on.”
examples.zh: 主持人说，如果手机要开着，就「把它设成振动」。

examples.en: The notice said to set your phone to vibrate before entering the studio.
examples.zh: 通知说，进工作室之前先「把手机设成振动」。

collocations: please set your phone to vibrate
remember to set your phone to vibrate
set your phone to vibrate during the event

words.enDefinition: to become comfortable with a repeated pattern of daily activities

examples.en: It took me a few weeks to settle into a routine after moving overseas.
examples.zh: 搬到国外后，我过了几周才「逐渐适应新的日常」。

examples.en: Volunteering on Thursdays helped me settle into a routine during my first term.
examples.zh: 第一学期，每周四做志愿服务帮我「逐渐适应了新的日常」。

collocations: begin to settle into a routine
help someone settle into a routine
settle into a routine after moving

words.expression: shall I put the kettle on
words.lemma: shall i put the kettle on
words.enDefinition: offers to heat water for tea or another hot drink
acceptedEnVariants: shall I put the kettle on

examples.en: It was cold outside, so I asked, "Shall I put the kettle on for tea?"
examples.zh: 外面挺冷，我就问：「我来烧点水泡茶吧」？

examples.en: Shall I put the kettle on while you show Lina where to hang her coat downstairs?
examples.zh: 你带莉娜去楼下挂外套时，「我来烧点水吧」？

collocations: say shall I put the kettle on
shall I put the kettle on for tea
shall I put the kettle on now

words.expression: shall I take my shoes off
words.lemma: shall i take my shoes off
words.enDefinition: asks whether the host would prefer you to remove your shoes
acceptedEnVariants: shall I take my shoes off

examples.en: Shall I take my shoes off before walking on the rug in your living room?
examples.zh: 踩到你客厅的地毯之前，「我要脱鞋吗」？

examples.en: I looked down at the entrance mat and asked, "Shall I take my shoes off here?"
examples.zh: 我低头看看入口的门垫，问：「我在这儿要脱鞋吗」？

collocations: shall I take my shoes off here
shall I take my shoes off first
ask if I should take my shoes off

words.enDefinition: A casual suggestion to enter a venue now.

examples.en: Shall we head in before the film starts and all the seats fill up?
examples.zh: 「咱们要进去吗」？电影快开场了，座位说不定很快就坐满。

examples.en: Shall we head in now that everyone has found their ticket on their phone?
examples.zh: 大家都在手机上找到各自的票了，「咱们要进去吗」？

collocations: shall we head in before the rain

words.enDefinition: A conversational phrase used to suggest a particular time or place for a plan.

examples.en: Shall we say six so everyone has time to get there after the afternoon class?
examples.zh: 「要不定在六点」，这样大家下午下课后都来得及赶到？

examples.en: Shall we say the main entrance because there are three doors facing the courtyard?
examples.zh: 朝庭院的门有三扇，「要不定在正门」？

collocations: ask shall we say half past
shall we say the main entrance

words.enDefinition: The helper light used to light the other lights on a Hanukkah menorah.

examples.en: My classmate pointed out the shamash in a photograph of her family's Hanukkah menorah.
examples.zh: 同学在她家光明节烛台的照片里指给我看哪一支是「光明节引火烛」。

examples.en: The museum label explained why the shamash had a separate place on the lamp.
examples.zh: 博物馆展签说明了「光明节引火烛」为什么在烛台上有单独的位置。

words.enDefinition: a three-leaved plant used as a symbol of Ireland

examples.en: The student drew a shamrock in the corner of the poster for the parade.
examples.zh: 那名学生在游行海报的角落画了一个「爱尔兰三叶草」。

examples.en: A small shamrock was printed on the card my Irish classmate gave me.
examples.zh: 我的爱尔兰同学送我的卡片上印了一个小小的「爱尔兰三叶草」。

words.enDefinition: to eat one portion or dish together with at least one other person

examples.en: We decided to share a dish rather than each buy a full meal.
examples.zh: 我们决定「分着吃一道菜」，不用每个人都买一整份饭。

examples.en: My roommate asked if I wanted to share a dish at lunch.
examples.zh: 室友问我午餐时想不想「分着吃一道菜」。

collocations: share a dish with a friend
