words.enDefinition: To travel back in the same car with another person or group.

examples.en: Can we share a ride back to campus after the film ends this evening?
examples.zh: 今晚电影结束后，我们能「一起搭车回校园」吗？

examples.en: We decided to share a ride back after finding out the last bus had left.
examples.zh: 得知末班公交已经开走了，我们决定「一起搭车回去」。

collocations: decide to share a ride back
ask if we can share a ride back
share a ride back to campus

words.enDefinition: to tell someone new information about your own life

examples.en: We used the call to share personal news before talking about our university work.
examples.zh: 我们先借电话「分享个人近况」，再聊学校里的事。

examples.en: She chose to share personal news privately instead of posting it for everyone to see.
examples.zh: 她选择私下「分享个人近况」，没有发给所有人看。

collocations: decide where to share personal news
feel ready to share personal news

words.zhGloss: 在不同代之间分享故事
words.enDefinition: to tell and listen to accounts among people of different ages
acceptedZhAnswers: 在不同代之间分享故事

examples.en: The library invited families to share stories across generations for its audio archive.
examples.zh: 图书馆请各个家庭「在不同代之间分享故事」，录音会收入档案。

examples.en: The student group used interviews to share stories across generations in their neighbourhood.
examples.zh: 学生小组通过访谈「在社区的不同代之间分享故事」。

collocations: invite people to share stories across generations
a chance to share stories across generations
share stories across generations through interviews

words.enDefinition: to make space for a neighbour to use the same armrest

examples.en: We managed to share the armrest once we had settled into our seats.
examples.zh: 我们坐定后，顺利地「共用了座椅扶手」。

examples.en: I tried to share the armrest without nudging the person beside me.
examples.zh: 我想不碰到旁边的人，跟对方「共用那个座椅扶手」。

collocations: share the armrest with the person next to you

words.enDefinition: plans or hopes for the life two people might have together

examples.en: They imagined a shared future after finding work in the same part of town.
examples.zh: 在城里同一区域找到工作后，两人想象起了「共同的未来」。

examples.en: We talked about a shared future while walking home from the graduation reception.
examples.zh: 毕业招待会后走回家的路上，我们聊到「共同的未来」。

words.enDefinition: past experiences that people know about because they lived through them together

examples.en: Our shared history made it easy to talk after so many years apart.
examples.zh: 分开那么多年后，「共同经历过的往事」让我们很自然地聊了起来。

examples.en: The photos reminded us of the shared history behind our old university friendships.
examples.zh: 照片让我们想起了大学友情背后那些「共同经历过的往事」。

words.enDefinition: an activity or subject that several people enjoy or value

examples.en: A shared interest in photography got us talking outside the lecture hall.
examples.zh: 我们在阶梯教室外聊了起来，因为摄影是我们的「共同爱好」。

examples.en: I asked what shared interest brought the two friends to the club.
examples.zh: 我问是什么「共同爱好」让这两个朋友加入了社团。

words.enDefinition: a collection of photos several people are allowed to view or add to

examples.en: We made a shared photo album after the last trip of our exchange year.
examples.zh: 交换学年最后一次出游后，我们建了一个「共享相册」。

examples.en: A former classmate added an old picnic photo to our shared photo album.
examples.zh: 一位老同学往「共享相册」里加了一张以前野餐的照片。

collocations: add to a shared photo album
invite someone to a shared photo album

words.enDefinition: A list of songs that several people can listen to or add to.

examples.en: We made a shared playlist so each friend could suggest songs for the picnic.
examples.zh: 我们做了个「共享播放列表」，让每位朋友都能为野餐推荐歌曲。

examples.en: Kai put on the shared playlist while we waited for everyone to finish their coffee.
examples.zh: 我们等大家喝完咖啡时，凯播放了「共享播放列表」。

collocations: add a song to a shared playlist

words.enDefinition: an interpretation or agreement that people have reached together

examples.en: We reached a shared understanding of the joke after each person explained their reaction.
examples.zh: 每个人解释了自己的反应后，我们对那个笑话「形成了共同理解」。

examples.en: The team developed a shared understanding of why the phrase felt too formal.
examples.zh: 小组对那个说法为什么显得太正式「形成了共同理解」。

words.enDefinition: beliefs or principles that two people consider important in similar ways

examples.en: They talked about shared values before deciding where to live after university graduation.
examples.zh: 他们先谈了「共同的价值观」，再决定大学毕业后住在哪里。

examples.en: We agreed that shared values mattered more to us than liking the same films.
examples.zh: 我们一致觉得，「共同的价值观」比喜欢同样的电影更重要。

words.enDefinition: a household request to remove shoes at the entrance

examples.en: The sign said "Shoes off at the door," so we left our boots on the mat.
examples.zh: 牌子上写着「进门脱鞋」，我们就把靴子留在门垫上。

examples.en: My flatmate asked for shoes off at the door because the floor was freshly cleaned.
examples.zh: 地板刚清洁过，室友请大家「进门脱鞋」。

collocations: we prefer shoes off at the door
sign saying shoes off at the door
ask for shoes off at the door

words.zhGloss: 愿意倾听和安慰你的人
words.enDefinition: a person who offers comfort when someone is sad or upset
acceptedZhAnswers: 愿意倾听和安慰你的人

examples.en: My roommate was a shoulder to cry on after I got some disappointing news.
examples.zh: 我收到让人失望的消息后，室友就是那个「愿意倾听和安慰我的人」。

examples.en: He said he could offer a shoulder to cry on after the difficult conversation.
examples.zh: 那次不好开口的谈话结束后，他说他「愿意听我诉苦并安慰我」。

collocations: need a shoulder to cry on
offer a shoulder to cry on
be a shoulder to cry on

words.enDefinition: to make your fondness or care for someone visible through words or actions

examples.en: They had different ways to show affection when they were around their classmates.
examples.zh: 在同学面前，两人「表达亲近和喜爱」的方式不同。

examples.en: I learned that he liked to show affection by remembering small details I mentioned.
examples.zh: 我知道了，他喜欢记住我提到的小事来「表达亲近和喜爱」。

words.expression: show me how your family does it
words.lemma: show me how your family does it
words.zhGloss: 给我看看你家是怎么做的
words.enDefinition: a request to demonstrate one's particular family version of an activity
acceptedZhAnswers: 给我看看你家是怎么做的
acceptedEnVariants: show me how your family does it

examples.en: “Could you show me how your family does it?” I asked during the workshop.
examples.zh: 工作坊里，我问「能给我看看你家是怎么做的吗？」

examples.en: I said, “Show me how your family does it,” when she offered a demonstration.
examples.zh: 她提出做示范时，我说「给我看看你家是怎么做的」。

collocations: could you show me how your family does it
please show me how your family does it
ask someone to show me how your family does it

words.enDefinition: to be present or make an effort when a friend needs support

examples.en: Sometimes the best way to show up for a friend is to listen quietly.
examples.zh: 有时「在朋友需要时出现」，只要安静地听对方说就好。

examples.en: She taught me what it meant to show up for a friend during exam week.
examples.zh: 考试那周，她让我明白了什么叫「在朋友需要时出现」。

collocations: find ways to show up for a friend
make time to show up for a friend
decide to show up for a friend

words.enDefinition: a person's established romantic partner, including a spouse

examples.en: The invitation said I could bring my significant other to the end-of-term dinner.
examples.zh: 邀请函上说，我可以带「亲密伴侣」参加学期末聚餐。

examples.en: Her significant other helped her pack the books before she moved for graduate school.
examples.zh: 她去外地读研前，「亲密伴侣」帮她把书装了起来。

words.enDefinition: not in a relationship because you prefer to remain single

examples.en: She described herself as single by choice while finishing the final year of her degree.
examples.zh: 她在读学位最后一年时，说自己是「主动选择单身」。

examples.en: My roommate was single by choice and enjoyed meeting people as friends through clubs.
examples.zh: 室友「主动选择单身」，喜欢通过社团结交朋友。

collocations: describe yourself as single by choice

words.enDefinition: a social event intended for people who are not currently in a relationship

examples.en: We heard about the singles event when we passed the café near campus.
examples.zh: 经过校园附近那家咖啡馆时，我们听说了那场「单身交友活动」。

examples.en: My friend agreed to come to the singles event so I wouldn't arrive alone.
examples.zh: 朋友答应一起去「单身交友活动」，这样我就不用一个人到场。

words.enDefinition: To choose not to take part in this particular shared activity.

examples.en: I think I'll sit this one out because I have an early class tomorrow.
examples.zh: 我明天有早课，想「这次先不参加」。

examples.en: Mina said she'd sit this one out and join us for the picnic next week.
examples.zh: 米娜说她「这次先不参加」，下周再来和我们一起野餐。

collocations: decide to sit this one out
have to sit this one out
sit this one out for now

words.zhGloss: 没有明确关系的暧昧交往
words.enDefinition: an informal term for romantic involvement without a clearly defined relationship or commitment
acceptedZhAnswers: 没有明确关系的暧昧交往

examples.en: My friend described their situationship as somewhere between friendship and a committed relationship.
examples.zh: 朋友说，两人的「没有明确关系的暧昧交往」介于友情和正式恋爱之间。

examples.en: She wanted to understand where the situationship was going before making plans for next year.
examples.zh: 安排明年的计划前，她想弄清这段「没有明确关系的暧昧交往」接下来会怎样。

words.enDefinition: an ornament made to resemble a skeleton, often for Halloween

examples.en: The skeleton decoration kept falling off the student lounge door that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，学生休息室门上的「骷髅装饰」总往下掉。

examples.en: We tied a scarf around the skeleton decoration during the costume competition.
examples.zh: 化装比赛时，我们给「骷髅装饰」围了条围巾。

words.enDefinition: to leave out the title when using someone's name

examples.en: My tutor said I could skip the title when writing to her directly.
examples.zh: 导师说，直接给她写信时「不用加头衔」。

examples.en: The guest asked me to skip the title on their informal name badge.
examples.zh: 来宾请我在非正式活动的胸牌上「不用加头衔」。

collocations: ask someone to skip the title
feel free to skip the title

words.enDefinition: to smile at someone who has smiled at you

examples.en: I tried to smile back before I asked if she knew Maya.
examples.zh: 我先试着「回以微笑」，再问她认不认识玛雅。

examples.en: It felt natural to smile back when I recognised her from orientation.
examples.zh: 认出她是迎新时见过的人，我很自然地「回以微笑」。

collocations: take a moment to smile back

words.enDefinition: someone who moves easily between groups and enjoys meeting people

examples.en: My roommate is a social butterfly and already knows half the floor.
examples.zh: 室友在「各种社交场合都很活跃」，已经认识半层楼的人了。

examples.en: I'm no social butterfly, but I did introduce myself to two people.
examples.zh: 我「在社交场合没那么活跃」，不过还是向两个人做了自我介绍。

words.enDefinition: a word, expression or action suggesting how to respond in company

examples.en: I missed the social cue when my classmate glanced toward the door.
examples.zh: 同学往门口瞥了一眼，我没看懂那个「社交信号」。

examples.en: Her pause was a social cue I didn't recognise until we talked afterwards.
examples.zh: 她的停顿是个「社交信号」，后来我们聊过我才明白。

words.enDefinition: conventions for behaving considerately in interactions with other people

examples.en: Our orientation included a short discussion about social etiquette in shared study spaces.
examples.zh: 迎新活动简短讨论了共享自习空间里的「社交礼仪」。

examples.en: The club's social etiquette handout suggested asking before sharing photos of other members.
examples.zh: 社团的「社交礼仪」资料建议，分享其他成员的照片前先问一声。

collocations: social etiquette in a shared space

words.enDefinition: in informal social media usage, to hint at a romance without fully announcing it

examples.en: They decided to soft-launch a relationship by posting a photo of two coffees on campus.
examples.zh: 两人决定发一张校园里两杯咖啡的照片，「在网上低调透露恋情」。

examples.en: I didn't want to soft-launch a relationship before we'd even told our friends.
examples.zh: 我们还没告诉朋友，所以我不想「在网上低调透露恋情」。

collocations: soft-launch a relationship on social media

words.enDefinition: having a gentle, quiet way of speaking

examples.en: A soft-spoken student asked if I wanted help finding the room.
examples.zh: 一个「说话轻声细语」的同学问我要不要帮忙找教室。

examples.en: My new neighbour is soft-spoken, so I moved closer to hear.
examples.zh: 新邻居「说话声音轻」，于是我走近一点听。

words.enDefinition: a person who gives you emotional or practical support when needed

examples.en: My old roommate was someone to lean on during the first difficult month abroad.
examples.zh: 刚出国最难的那个月，原来的室友是我「可以依靠的人」。

examples.en: It helped to have someone to lean on while I sorted out my university paperwork.
examples.zh: 处理学校手续时，有个「可以依靠的人」让我好过些。

words.enDefinition: expresses regret that your group has to leave a visit soon

examples.en: Sorry we can't stay longer. I've got to meet my lab partner before the last bus.
examples.zh: 「抱歉我们不能多待」。我得在末班车前见一下实验搭档。

examples.en: I said, "Sorry we can't stay longer," as my sister and I put on our coats.
examples.zh: 妹妹和我穿外套时，我说：「抱歉我们不能多待」。

collocations: really sorry we can't stay longer
sorry we can't stay longer today
we're sorry we can't stay longer

words.enDefinition: to resolve problems or confusion through discussion or action

examples.en: We met for coffee to sort things out after the group chat became confusing.
examples.zh: 群聊说不清楚后，我们见面喝咖啡，好「把问题处理妥当」。

examples.en: The two friends needed time to sort things out after the summer plans changed.
examples.zh: 暑假计划改变后，那两位朋友需要时间「把问题处理妥当」。

words.zhGloss: 帮忙听取想法并给反馈的人
words.enDefinition: a person who listens to your ideas and offers feedback before you decide
acceptedZhAnswers: 帮忙听取想法并给反馈的人

examples.en: My old roommate became a sounding board when I considered switching to another degree.
examples.zh: 我考虑转读另一个学位时，以前的室友「听了我的想法并给了反馈」。

examples.en: I needed a sounding board before I sent that long message to our group.
examples.zh: 给我们小组发那条长消息前，我需要「有人听听我的想法并给些反馈」。

collocations: use someone as a sounding board

words.enDefinition: an extra set of indoor shoes kept for possible use

examples.en: There is a spare pair of slippers by the mat if your feet are cold.
examples.zh: 要是脚冷，门垫旁有一双「备用拖鞋」。

examples.en: The host brought a spare pair of slippers over from the shoe rack.
examples.zh: 主人从鞋架拿来了一双「备用拖鞋」。

collocations: offer a spare pair of slippers
lend a spare pair of slippers
keep a spare pair of slippers for guests

words.enDefinition: an extra toothbrush kept in case someone needs one

examples.en: My friend offered me a spare toothbrush because I hadn't planned to stay.
examples.zh: 我本来没打算留宿，朋友就给了我一支「备用牙刷」。

examples.en: There's a spare toothbrush in this drawer if you forgot to pack yours.
examples.zh: 如果你忘了带牙刷，这个抽屉里有支「备用牙刷」。

collocations: have a spare toothbrush for guests

words.enDefinition: an event where people have several short meetings with possible partners

examples.en: The student union advertised speed dating as part of an evening of social events.
examples.zh: 学生会宣传晚间社交活动时，把「快速轮换式约会」列为其中一项。

examples.en: I tried speed dating once and met someone from a course I'd considered taking.
examples.zh: 我试过一次「快速轮换式约会」，遇到了一位读我考虑过的课程的人。

words.enDefinition: to write the letters of a person's name in the correct order

examples.en: I checked the list to spell a name correctly on the group card.
examples.zh: 我核对了名单，好在联名卡片上「把姓名拼对」。

examples.en: The coordinator reminded us to spell a name correctly on every certificate we printed.
examples.zh: 协调员提醒我们，打印证书时都要「把姓名拼对」。

collocations: check that you spell a name correctly
learn to spell a name correctly
make sure you spell a name correctly

words.enDefinition: slightly frightening because something seems strange or ghostly

examples.en: We put on some spooky music for the student film screening.
examples.zh: 学生电影放映时，我们放了点「让人觉得阴森」的音乐。

examples.en: The spooky paper shadows looked funny once we turned on the lights.
examples.zh: 灯一开，那些本来「阴森森的」纸影子看起来挺好笑的。

words.enDefinition: the weeks around Halloween when spooky themes become popular

examples.en: Our film club picked three funny horror movies for spooky season this year.
examples.zh: 今年「万圣节前后的节庆季」，电影社挑了三部搞笑恐怖片。

examples.en: The students were already hanging bats in the lounge for spooky season.
examples.zh: 为了迎接「万圣节前后的节庆季」，同学们已经在休息室挂起蝙蝠装饰了。

words.enDefinition: a UK bank holiday usually observed near the end of May

examples.en: The office moved our meeting because it would close for the spring bank holiday.
examples.zh: 办公室因「英国春季公众假日」要关闭，于是把我们的会议改期了。

examples.en: We booked the coast trip for the spring bank holiday after comparing train times.
examples.zh: 比过火车时刻后，我们把沿海旅行定在「英国春季公众假日」。

collocations: closed for the spring bank holiday

words.enDefinition: the time in spring when day and night are nearly equal in length

examples.en: The student society planned a talk about the spring equinox and seasonal traditions.
examples.zh: 学生社团安排了一场关于「春分」和时令习俗的讲座。

examples.en: We met near the garden around the spring equinox, when it stayed light later.
examples.zh: 「春分」前后，我们在花园附近见面，那时天黑得晚一些了。

words.enDefinition: an event in spring with stalls, games, or items for sale

examples.en: I bought a plant at the spring fair after my last lecture on Friday.
examples.zh: 周五最后一节课结束后，我在「春季市集」买了一株植物。

examples.en: The residence hall ran a stall at the spring fair to raise money locally.
examples.zh: 宿舍楼在「春季市集」摆摊，为本地项目筹款。

words.enDefinition: the Chinese celebration marking the new year in the traditional Chinese lunisolar calendar

examples.en: I went to a Spring Festival performance in town with friends from my language class.
examples.zh: 我和语言课的朋友去城里看了「春节」演出。

examples.en: My roommate showed us photos of her family preparing for the Spring Festival back home.
examples.zh: 室友给我们看了她家人在家乡准备过「春节」的照片。

collocations: travel home for the Spring Festival

words.enDefinition: A pair of matching lines with festive wishes displayed at Chinese New Year.

examples.en: We read a Spring Festival couplet with help from the students at the calligraphy table.
examples.zh: 书法桌旁的同学帮我们读了一副「春联」。

examples.en: My classmate photographed a Spring Festival couplet beside her family's doorway before returning to campus.
examples.zh: 返校前，同学拍下了家门边的一副「春联」。

collocations: a Spring Festival couplet on red paper

words.enDefinition: an Irish holiday honouring Saint Patrick and widely celebrated as an occasion for Irish culture

examples.en: The campus society held an Irish music session for St Patrick's Day after class.
examples.zh: 下课后，校园社团为「圣帕特里克节」办了一场爱尔兰音乐活动。

examples.en: We watched the St Patrick's Day parade with friends from our exchange programme downtown.
examples.zh: 我们和交换项目的朋友一起在市中心看了「圣帕特里克节」游行。

words.enDefinition: to put plates on top of one another for collection

examples.en: We helped stack the plates after the club's lunch in the common room.
examples.zh: 社团在公共休息室吃完午饭后，我们帮着「把盘子叠起来」。

examples.en: I asked whether to stack the plates or leave them where they were.
examples.zh: 我问是要「把盘子叠起来」，还是留在原处。

collocations: ask people to stack the plates

words.enDefinition: to stand one person behind another in one line

examples.en: We were asked to stand in single file near the coat check.
examples.zh: 工作人员请我们在衣帽间旁「排成一列站好」。

examples.en: The volunteer pointed to the marker and asked us to stand in single file.
examples.zh: 志愿者指着标记，请我们「排成一列站好」。

collocations: ask people to stand in single file
stand in single file near the entrance
remember to stand in single file

words.enDefinition: to stand nearer to someone than they are comfortable with

examples.en: I tried not to stand too close while we waited for the lift.
examples.zh: 我们等电梯时，我尽量别「站得太近」。

examples.en: It's easy to stand too close when you cannot hear the person speaking.
examples.zh: 听不清对方讲话时，很容易「站得太近」。

collocations: try not to stand too close

words.enDefinition: a plan that remains in place without being arranged again each time

examples.en: We had a standing plan to meet for coffee on the first Friday of each month.
examples.zh: 我们有个「长期固定的约定」，每月第一个周五见面喝咖啡。

examples.en: I kept the standing plan in my calendar after my timetable changed in spring.
examples.zh: 春天课表调整后，我还是把「长期固定的约定」留在日历里。

words.enDefinition: asks other people to begin eating before your group arrives

examples.en: I texted "Start without us," because our bus was running nearly half an hour late.
examples.zh: 公交要晚到将近半小时，我就发消息说「不用等我们，先开饭」。

examples.en: Please start without us if the rest of the class is ready to eat.
examples.zh: 如果班里其他人都准备好了，「不用等我们，先开饭」吧。

collocations: tell them to start without us
go ahead and start without us

words.enDefinition: a holiday formally established by law in a particular jurisdiction

examples.en: The Canadian campus calendar showed which Monday was a statutory holiday in our province.
examples.zh: 加拿大这所学校的校历标出了我们省哪一个周一是「法定假日」。

examples.en: My employer sent a reminder about opening hours on the next statutory holiday.
examples.zh: 雇主发了提醒，告知下一个「法定假日」的营业时间。

words.enDefinition: to keep a strong personal connection even as circumstances change

examples.en: We managed to stay close after we moved to opposite sides of the city.
examples.zh: 我们搬到城里相隔很远的两头后，关系还是「保持亲近」。

examples.en: She wanted to stay close to her old friends while making new ones abroad.
examples.zh: 她在国外交新朋友，也想和老朋友「继续保持亲近」。

words.enDefinition: to maintain contact with the people or customs of where you come from

examples.en: Playing the songs my cousin sends helps me stay connected to home.
examples.zh: 听表亲发来的歌，能帮我「保持与家乡的联系」。

examples.en: Sharing recipes was how our flatmates chose to stay connected to home.
examples.zh: 室友们选择互相分享菜谱，「保持与家乡的联系」。

collocations: find ways to stay connected to home
help someone stay connected to home
stay connected to home while abroad

words.enDefinition: To remain a little longer to take part in another round of a game.

examples.en: Can you stay for one more round before you have to catch the bus?
examples.zh: 你去赶公交之前能「留下来再玩一轮」吗？

examples.en: We agreed to stay for one more round because Kai had only just joined us.
examples.zh: 凯刚加入，我们说好「留下来再玩一轮」。

collocations: want to stay for one more round
ask people to stay for one more round
decide to stay for one more round

words.enDefinition: to maintain a friendly or civil relationship after a change or disagreement

examples.en: They managed to stay on good terms after they stopped seeing each other.
examples.zh: 两人不再交往后，还是能「保持客气友好的关系」。

examples.en: I hoped we could stay on good terms and greet each other in the lab.
examples.zh: 我希望我们能「保持客气友好的关系」，在实验室见面可以打个招呼。

collocations: manage to stay on good terms
want to stay on good terms
stay on good terms with someone

words.enDefinition: to sleep somewhere away from your own home for one night

examples.en: My sister decided to stay the night after we talked until midnight.
examples.zh: 我和妹妹聊到半夜，她决定「留宿一晚」。

examples.en: There's a spare bed if you'd rather stay the night and leave tomorrow.
examples.zh: 如果你想「留宿一晚」明天再走，这儿有张备用床。

collocations: offer to let someone stay the night

words.enDefinition: To leave a room briefly to get fresh air outside.

examples.en: Do you want to step outside for some air before we start the next film?
examples.zh: 开始放下一部电影前，你想「出去透透气」吗？

examples.en: I said I would step outside for some air while everyone chose another game.
examples.zh: 大家在选下一轮玩什么时，我说要「出去透透气」。

collocations: want to step outside for some air
let's step outside for some air
offer to step outside for some air

words.zhGloss: 只和认识的人待在一起
words.enDefinition: to stay around familiar people instead of meeting new ones
acceptedZhAnswers: 只和认识的人待在一起

examples.en: It's easy to stick with people you know when you're new and the room is crowded.
examples.zh: 刚来时，一屋子都是人，很容易「只和认识的人待在一起」。

examples.en: You can stick with people you know at first while you get used to the group.
examples.zh: 你可以先「和认识的人待在一起」，等适应这个群体再说。

collocations: tend to stick with people you know
feel safer when you stick with people you know
easy to stick with people you know

words.enDefinition: indicating that a person is learning how to navigate a place

examples.en: I'm still finding my way around, so I sometimes take the long path to class.
examples.zh: 我「还在熟悉这儿的路」，所以有时会上课绕远。

examples.en: I said I was still finding my way around, and she offered to walk with me.
examples.zh: 我说自己「还在熟悉这儿的路」，她就说陪我一起走。

collocations: I'm still finding my way around
still finding my way around campus
still finding my way around the building

words.enDefinition: A small gift intended to go inside a Christmas stocking.

examples.en: My flatmate used a tiny notebook as a stocking stuffer for her younger brother.
examples.zh: 室友把一本迷你笔记本当作「塞进圣诞袜的小礼物」送给弟弟。

examples.en: A stall at the market sold small soaps and described each as a stocking stuffer.
examples.zh: 集市有个摊位卖小块香皂，称每块都适合当「塞进圣诞袜的小礼物」。

collocations: use something as a stocking stuffer

words.enDefinition: a group meeting where people take turns sharing their own stories

examples.en: I spoke about moving overseas during a story circle at the library.
examples.zh: 我在图书馆的「围坐分享故事的小组」里讲了移居国外的经历。

examples.en: The story circle let everyone choose whether to tell a story or listen.
examples.zh: 这个「围坐分享故事的小组」让每个人自己选，可以讲故事，也可以听别人讲。

collocations: take part in a story circle

words.enDefinition: to put pressure on a friendship so it becomes harder to get along

examples.en: A series of missed calls can strain a friendship when both people are busy.
examples.zh: 两个人都忙时，一连串没接到的电话可能会「让友情变得紧张」。

examples.en: I didn't want the disagreement to strain a friendship that mattered to both of us.
examples.zh: 这段友情对我们俩都很重要，我不想分歧「让友情变得紧张」。

collocations: be enough to strain a friendship
avoid doing things that strain a friendship

words.enDefinition: a public event with stalls or performances set up along a street

examples.en: I stopped at the street fair on my way back from the bus station.
examples.zh: 从公交总站回来的路上，我在「街头集市」停了一下。

examples.en: The street fair had a stall selling handmade notebooks from a nearby student cooperative.
examples.zh: 「街头集市」有个摊位，卖附近学生合作社做的手工笔记本。

words.enDefinition: a public procession through streets organized to celebrate or mark an event

examples.en: The street parade passed our bus stop just as we arrived for the festival.
examples.zh: 我们刚到庆典会场，「街头游行」就经过了公交站。

examples.en: My friend brought a camera to the street parade because her sister was taking part.
examples.zh: 朋友的姐姐要参加「街头游行」，于是朋友带上了相机。

collocations: take part in a street parade

words.enDefinition: a celebration held in a street, often closed to traffic for the occasion

examples.en: The road was closed for a street party hosted by several local community groups.
examples.zh: 为几家社区团体合办的「封街联欢活动」，这条路临时封闭了。

examples.en: Our friends joined the street party after helping set up tables near the library.
examples.zh: 帮忙在图书馆附近摆好桌子后，朋友们参加了「封街联欢活动」。

words.enDefinition: To reach twelve at night and mark the time with a clock's sound.

examples.en: Some classmates waited to hear the clock strike midnight from the top of the hill.
examples.zh: 几位同学在山顶等着听「敲钟报午夜」。

examples.en: The host waited for the clock to strike midnight before greeting viewers on camera.
examples.zh: 主持人等到钟「敲响午夜」后才对着镜头和观众打招呼。

collocations: wait for the clock to strike midnight

words.enDefinition: to start talking to someone without a prior arrangement

examples.en: I wanted to strike up a conversation with someone while waiting for the bus.
examples.zh: 等公交的时候，我想找个人「主动聊上几句」。

examples.en: It was easy to strike up a conversation because we recognised each other's course books.
examples.zh: 我们认出了彼此的课本，所以很容易就「攀谈起来」。

collocations: strike up a conversation with a stranger
strike up a conversation in line
easy to strike up a conversation

words.enDefinition: students who start or study a program as one group

examples.en: The welcome event was the first time our student cohort met in person.
examples.zh: 那场迎新活动是我们「这批学生」第一次线下见面。

examples.en: She recognised a few people from her student cohort in the dining hall.
examples.zh: 她在食堂认出了几位「同批学生」。

collocations: part of the same student cohort

words.enDefinition: students with varied personal, social or cultural experiences

examples.en: The project paired students from different backgrounds to prepare a short audio guide.
examples.zh: 项目让「不同背景的学生」两人一组，制作简短的语音导览。

examples.en: We asked students from different backgrounds which examples belonged in the display.
examples.zh: 我们问了几位「不同背景的学生」，哪些例子适合放到展板上。

collocations: bring together students from different backgrounds
hear from students from different backgrounds

words.enDefinition: a weekday designated as a holiday in place of the usual date, especially in the UK

examples.en: The UK campus calendar said Monday was a substitute day for the bank holiday.
examples.zh: 英国这所大学的校历写着，周一是这次公众假日的「补假日」。

examples.en: The receptionist said the office would reopen on Tuesday after the substitute day.
examples.zh: 前台工作人员说，办事处过完「补假日」会在周二重新开放。

words.enDefinition: Jelly-filled doughnuts traditionally eaten at Hanukkah, particularly in Israel.

examples.en: Our neighbor brought a box of sufganiyot when she came to the winter craft evening.
examples.zh: 邻居晚上来参加冬季手工活动时，带来一盒「光明节果酱甜甜圈」。

examples.en: A card next to the sufganiyot explained their connection with Hanukkah at the student fair.
examples.zh: 学生集市上，「光明节果酱甜甜圈」旁的卡片说明了它们和光明节的关系。

words.enDefinition: a bank holiday in August whose usual date differs within the UK

examples.en: My student job had shorter opening hours on the summer bank holiday that year.
examples.zh: 那年「英国夏季公众假日」，我打学生工的地方缩短了营业时间。

examples.en: We compared the dates of the summer bank holiday in Scotland and in Wales.
examples.zh: 我们比较了苏格兰和威尔士的「英国夏季公众假日」日期。

collocations: closed for the summer bank holiday

words.enDefinition: an outdoor or seasonal market operating during the summer

examples.en: We bought fresh fruit at the summer market after walking through the campus garden.
examples.zh: 穿过校园花园后，我们在「夏季集市」买了新鲜水果。

examples.en: My flatmate sold handmade bookmarks at the summer market on several weekends that year.
examples.zh: 那年有几个周末，室友在「夏季集市」卖手工书签。

words.enDefinition: the time of year with the longest period of daylight in one hemisphere

examples.en: Some students watched the sunset together on the summer solstice by the river.
examples.zh: 一些学生在「夏至」那天一起到河边看日落。

examples.en: A museum guide explained why the summer solstice mattered to some farming communities.
examples.zh: 博物馆的讲解员解释了为什么一些农业社区重视「夏至」。

collocations: the day of the summer solstice

words.enDefinition: with a family name written or spoken before given names

examples.en: The attendance sheet listed her surname first, but the name badge didn't.
examples.zh: 签到表上她的「姓氏在前」，胸牌上却不是。

examples.en: I kept the surname first because that was the order he'd given me.
examples.zh: 我保留了「姓氏在前」的顺序，因为这是他交给我的写法。

words.enDefinition: to give each other your phone numbers

examples.en: We decided to swap numbers after realising we took the same bus.
examples.zh: 发现我们坐同一班公交之后，我们决定「互留电话号码」。

examples.en: Would you like to swap numbers before everyone leaves for the afternoon?
examples.zh: 大家下午散场前，你愿意「互留电话号码」吗？

words.enDefinition: to exchange the seats two people are using

examples.en: We decided to swap seats so she could hear the speaker more easily.
examples.zh: 我们决定「换一下座位」，这样她就更容易听清发言。

examples.en: I asked whether we could swap seats at the end of the table.
examples.zh: 我问能不能在餐桌那头「和别人换座位」。

words.enDefinition: to send brief recorded messages to one another instead of talking live

examples.en: We started to swap voice notes because our schedules rarely lined up after graduation.
examples.zh: 毕业后时间很少对得上，我们就开始「互发语音消息」。

examples.en: My old school friends swap voice notes when someone has news we want to hear.
examples.zh: 有人有大家想听的消息时，以前的同学就会「互发语音消息」。

collocations: swap voice notes instead of calling

words.enDefinition: on some dating apps, to move a profile left to pass over it

examples.en: I didn't mean to swipe left before reading the rest of the profile.
examples.zh: 我本想看完剩下的资料，不是故意「向左划表示不感兴趣」。

examples.en: The app instructions showed how to swipe left when you want to skip a profile.
examples.zh: 应用说明演示了想跳过一份资料时怎样「向左划表示不感兴趣」。

words.enDefinition: on some dating apps, to move a profile right to show interest

examples.en: My flatmate told me what swipe right meant when I first tried the app.
examples.zh: 我第一次用这个应用时，室友告诉了我「向右划表示感兴趣」的意思。

examples.en: I decided to swipe right after seeing that we both loved old films.
examples.zh: 看见我们都爱老电影后，我决定「向右划表示感兴趣」。

words.enDefinition: a decoration placed prominently in the middle of a table

examples.en: We used painted gourds and a small vase as our table centerpiece.
examples.zh: 我们用彩绘葫芦和一个小花瓶做「餐桌中央的装饰」。

examples.en: The table centerpiece was so tall that I couldn't see across the table.
examples.zh: 「餐桌中央的装饰」太高了，我都看不见桌对面。

words.enDefinition: ways of behaving considerately while eating with others

examples.en: We talked about table manners while setting up for the club dinner.
examples.zh: 准备社团聚餐时，我们聊到了「餐桌礼仪」。

examples.en: The student guide covered table manners at the formal awards dinner that evening.
examples.zh: 学生指南介绍了当晚正式颁奖晚宴上的「餐桌礼仪」。

words.enDefinition: to mention all group members so they may receive a notification

examples.en: We agreed to tag everyone only when the rehearsal time changed suddenly.
examples.zh: 我们约好，只有排练时间突然变动时才「@群内所有人」。

examples.en: I chose not to tag everyone when sharing a link to a café.
examples.zh: 我分享咖啡馆链接时，决定不「@群内所有人」。

words.enDefinition: invites someone to sit beside or near the speaker's group

examples.en: You can take a seat with us if you don't see anyone from your class.
examples.zh: 要是没看到班里的同学，可以「来跟我们一起坐」。

examples.en: The student by the door said I could take a seat with us if I wanted.
examples.zh: 门边的同学说我要是愿意，可以「来跟我们一起坐」。

collocations: come and take a seat with us
you can take a seat with us
feel free to take a seat with us

words.enDefinition: to serve yourself a small amount rather than a large helping

examples.en: I decided to take a small portion so everyone could try the dish.
examples.zh: 我决定「先取少量食物」，让大家都能尝尝这道菜。

examples.en: The volunteer suggested we take a small portion before going back for more.
examples.zh: 志愿者建议大家「先取少量食物」，吃完再回来添。

collocations: decide to take a small portion
take a small portion at first
ask diners to take a small portion

words.expression: take a trip down memory lane
words.lemma: take a trip down memory lane
words.enDefinition: to remember or talk about events from the past with pleasure
acceptedEnVariants: take a trip down memory lane

examples.en: We opened our old group photos to take a trip down memory lane after dinner.
examples.zh: 晚饭后，我们翻出小组旧照「一起回忆往事」。

examples.en: Some old classmates wanted to take a trip down memory lane before the reunion ended.
examples.zh: 聚会结束前，几位老同学想「一起回忆往事」。

collocations: take a trip down memory lane with friends
invite someone to take a trip down memory lane
take a trip down memory lane together

words.enDefinition: to do something when it becomes your chance to participate

examples.en: Each of us got to take a turn sharing something about the city.
examples.zh: 大家「轮到自己时」都说了一件和这座城市有关的事。

examples.en: The leader let everyone take a turn so the quieter students could speak.
examples.zh: 带队的同学让大家「轮着说」，这样平时话少的同学也能开口。

words.expression: take a while to feel settled
words.lemma: take a while to feel settled
words.zhGloss: 过一阵才觉得安顿下来
words.enDefinition: to need some time before feeling comfortable in a new place
acceptedZhAnswers: 过一阵才觉得安顿下来
acceptedEnVariants: take a while to feel settled

examples.en: My roommate said it might take a while to feel settled after the move.
examples.zh: 室友说，搬家后可能「要过一阵才觉得安顿下来」。

examples.en: I told the new student it can take a while to feel settled.
examples.zh: 我告诉新同学，有时「要过一阵才觉得安顿下来」。

collocations: expect it to take a while to feel settled
it may take a while to feel settled
take a while to feel settled after moving

words.expression: take it to a private chat
words.lemma: take it to a private chat
words.enDefinition: to move a discussion away from a public or group conversation
acceptedEnVariants: take it to a private chat

examples.en: I suggested we take it to a private chat when names came up.
examples.zh: 谈到具体人员的姓名时，我建议「转到私聊去说」。

examples.en: The group moderator asked us to take it to a private chat.
examples.zh: 群管理员请我们「转到私聊去说」。

collocations: suggest taking a topic to a private chat
ask people to take it to a private chat
agree to take it to a private chat

words.enDefinition: to bring home food that remains after a shared meal

examples.en: We asked who wanted to take leftovers home before clearing the table.
examples.zh: 收拾餐桌前，我们先问了谁想「把剩菜带回家」。

examples.en: I didn't plan to take leftovers home, but my neighbour insisted I take some.
examples.zh: 我原本没打算「把剩菜带回家」，但邻居执意让我带一些。

collocations: offer to let guests take leftovers home
ask if you can take leftovers home

words.enDefinition: to feel insulted by something another person says or does

examples.en: I could see why someone might take offence at that joke in class.
examples.zh: 我能理解，有人听到课堂上那个玩笑可能会「感觉被冒犯」。

examples.en: My friend didn't take offence when I asked her to repeat my name.
examples.zh: 我请朋友再叫一遍我的名字，她并没有「感觉被冒犯」。

words.enDefinition: asks each person to pick up only one item

examples.en: The note by the bowl read "Take one, please" in big letters.
examples.zh: 碗旁的纸条上用大字写着：「请只拿一个」。

examples.en: My roommate put "Take one per person" on the candy table sign.
examples.zh: 室友在糖果桌的牌子上写着「每人请只拿一个」。

collocations: bowl with a take one sign

words.enDefinition: to participate using a way besides speaking aloud

examples.en: We could take part without speaking by pointing to pictures on our cards.
examples.zh: 我们可以指卡片上的图，「不用发言也能参与」。

examples.en: I was glad I could take part without speaking during the first meeting.
examples.zh: 第一次开会时，我很高兴可以「不用发言也能参与」。

collocations: choose to take part without speaking
let visitors take part without speaking

words.enDefinition: to spend a period away from each other to consider a relationship

examples.en: They agreed to take some time apart before deciding whether to move in together.
examples.zh: 两人同意先「暂时各自冷静一段」，再决定是否一起住。

examples.en: We decided to take some time apart after struggling to balance travel and exams.
examples.zh: 因为在出行和考试之间难以兼顾，我们决定「暂时各自冷静一段」。

collocations: decide to take some time apart
agree to take some time apart
choose to take some time apart

words.enDefinition: to invite and accompany another person on a romantic outing

examples.en: I had never wanted to take someone on a date until we met at the films.
examples.zh: 直到在电影放映时遇见对方，我才第一次想「带个人去约会」。

examples.en: Where would you take someone on a date if you both liked quiet places?
examples.zh: 如果两个人都喜欢安静的地方，你会「带对方去哪里约会」？

collocations: take someone on a date downtown
offer to take someone on a date
take someone on a date to the cinema

words.enDefinition: to step outside to handle a phone call without disturbing others

examples.en: I offered to take the call outside when my phone started buzzing.
examples.zh: 手机开始振动时，我说可以「出去接电话」。

examples.en: My classmate chose to take the call outside before our study session began.
examples.zh: 自习开始前，同学决定「出去接电话」。

collocations: decide to take the call outside
ask someone to take the call outside
step out to take the call outside

words.enDefinition: to understand a suggestion that was not spoken directly

examples.en: I hoped he would take the hint when I moved back a little.
examples.zh: 我往后挪了挪，希望他能「领会我的暗示」。

examples.en: My friend did not take the hint when I changed the subject twice.
examples.zh: 我两次换话题，朋友还是没「领会我的暗示」。

collocations: hope someone will take the hint

words.enDefinition: to move forward to a more committed stage of a relationship

examples.en: They wanted to take the next step after finding work in the same city.
examples.zh: 在同一座城找到工作后，两人想「让关系更进一步」。

examples.en: I asked what it would mean to take the next step in our relationship.
examples.zh: 我问在我们的恋爱里，「让关系更进一步」意味着什么。

collocations: be ready to take the next step
decide to take the next step
want to take the next step

words.enDefinition: to study the same unit of a university degree

examples.en: I was surprised we could take the same module with such different degree plans.
examples.zh: 我们的修读计划差别很大，居然能「选同一门课」，我很意外。

examples.en: We decided to take the same module after we learned it included field trips.
examples.zh: 听说要出校考察后，我们决定「选同一门课」。

collocations: decide to take the same module
happen to take the same module
plan to take the same module

words.enDefinition: to let a romantic relationship develop without rushing decisions or commitments

examples.en: I said I wanted to take things slowly because we had only just met.
examples.zh: 我说想「慢慢发展关系」，因为我们刚认识。

examples.en: They agreed to take things slowly while settling into life on a new campus.
examples.zh: 他们同意在适应新校园生活的同时「慢慢发展关系」。

words.enDefinition: to alternate responsibility for staying in contact or asking how people are

examples.en: We agreed to take turns checking in while both of us were studying abroad.
examples.zh: 我们约好两人都在国外读书的时候，「轮流主动联系问候」。

examples.en: It felt fairer to take turns checking in instead of leaving it to one friend.
examples.zh: 「轮流主动联系问候」感觉更公平，免得只靠一个朋友张罗。

collocations: decide to take turns checking in
agree to take turns checking in
remember to take turns checking in

words.enDefinition: to alternate translating what people say during a conversation

examples.en: Our bilingual volunteers agreed to take turns interpreting during the informal game.
examples.zh: 双语志愿者约好，在这场非正式游戏中「轮流做口译」。

examples.en: We decided to take turns interpreting while our relatives shared memories on a call.
examples.zh: 亲戚们在通话中分享回忆时，我们决定「轮流做口译」。

collocations: ask volunteers to take turns interpreting
take turns interpreting during an exchange

words.enDefinition: To alternate who gets to choose something for a group.
acceptedEnVariants: take it in turns to pick

examples.en: We take turns picking films so everyone gets to show the group something they like.
examples.zh: 我们「轮流挑选」电影，让每个人都能放一部自己喜欢的片子给大家看。

examples.en: Could we take turns picking the music while we wait for the others to arrive?
examples.zh: 等其他人过来的时候，咱们能「轮流挑选」音乐吗？

words.enDefinition: to talk about work or study with others in that field

examples.en: My lab partner and I tend to talk shop whenever we meet.
examples.zh: 我和实验搭档每次见面，往往都会「聊本行的事」。

examples.en: Our new friends promised not to talk shop during dinner this time.
examples.zh: 新朋友答应这次吃晚饭时不「聊本行的事」。

words.enDefinition: to discuss a situation in detail to understand it or decide what to do

examples.en: We went for a walk to talk things through before making a decision.
examples.zh: 我们出去走了走，先「把事情谈清楚」再做决定。

examples.en: He asked if there was time to talk things through after her evening class.
examples.zh: 他问她晚课后有没有时间「把事情谈清楚」。

collocations: take time to talk things through

words.enDefinition: to discuss a concern with someone you believe will handle it with care

examples.en: It can help to talk to someone you trust after a difficult week away from home.
examples.zh: 离家在外遇到难熬的一周，「找信任的人聊一聊」可能有帮助。

examples.en: She told me to talk to someone you trust if the situation got confusing.
examples.zh: 她对我说，如果事情变得让人摸不着头脑，可以「找信任的人聊一聊」。

collocations: take time to talk to someone you trust
try to talk to someone you trust
find a chance to talk to someone you trust

words.enDefinition: to speak while there is food still in your mouth

examples.en: My friend laughed and said, “You don't have to talk with your mouth full.”
examples.zh: 朋友笑着说「你不用嘴里含着食物说话」。

examples.en: “When you talk with your mouth full, I can't hear you clearly,” my friend said.
examples.zh: 朋友说，你「嘴里含着食物说话」，我听不清。

collocations: try not to talk with your mouth full
avoid having to talk with your mouth full
don't talk with your mouth full

words.enDefinition: Glutinous rice balls often served at the Chinese Lantern Festival, commonly with sweet fillings or syrup.

examples.en: My classmate brought a bowl of tangyuan to our small Lantern Festival gathering on campus.
examples.zh: 同学带来一碗「汤圆」，参加我们在学校办的小型元宵聚会。

examples.en: The cafe's handwritten menu listed tangyuan as a dessert during the winter culture fair.
examples.zh: 冬季文化集市期间，咖啡馆的手写菜单把「汤圆」列为一道甜点。

words.enDefinition: offers a choice between two common hot drinks

examples.en: Would you like tea or coffee while you wait for the others?
examples.zh: 等其他人的时候，你「喝茶还是喝咖啡」？

examples.en: My host asked, "Tea or coffee?" as she took down two mugs.
examples.zh: 主人一边拿下两个马克杯，一边问：「喝茶还是喝咖啡」？

collocations: would you like tea or coffee

words.enDefinition: to share a short account of something that happened

examples.en: She decided to tell a quick story about finding her room on the first day.
examples.zh: 她决定「简单讲个小故事」，说说第一天是怎么找到宿舍房间的。

examples.en: We each got to tell a quick story before choosing a new table.
examples.zh: 在换桌之前，我们每个人都「简单讲了个小故事」。

collocations: offer to tell a quick story
tell a quick story about home
ask someone to tell a quick story

words.enDefinition: to share your feelings openly with the person they concern

examples.en: It takes courage to tell someone how you feel before you know their response.
examples.zh: 不知道对方会怎么答时，「把感受告诉对方」需要勇气。

examples.en: My friend said it's easier to tell someone how you feel somewhere quiet and familiar.
examples.zh: 朋友说，在安静熟悉的地方更容易「把感受告诉对方」。

collocations: want to tell someone how you feel
decide to tell someone how you feel
find time to tell someone how you feel

words.enDefinition: An arrangement that has been suggested but is still subject to change.

examples.en: We have a tentative plan for Saturday, but two people still need to check their shifts.
examples.zh: 我们星期六有个「暂定安排」，不过还有两个人要看排班。

examples.en: I shared a tentative plan before anyone spent money on tickets for the outdoor screening.
examples.zh: 趁大家都还没花钱买露天放映的票，我先发了一个「暂定安排」。

collocations: share a tentative plan with friends

words.enDefinition: The Vietnamese Lunar New Year holiday, often marked by family visits and seasonal foods.

examples.en: Our Vietnamese classmate brought photos from her family's Tết celebrations to share with the seminar.
examples.zh: 越南同学带了她家过「越南农历新年」的照片，跟研讨班分享。

examples.en: The student society offered a short talk about Tết before lunch in the common room.
examples.zh: 学生社团在公共休息室开午饭前，安排了一场关于「越南农历新年」的简短分享。

words.expression: text me when you get here
words.lemma: text me when you get here
words.enDefinition: A request for someone to send a message when they reach the meeting place.
acceptedEnVariants: text me when you get here

examples.en: Text me when you get here and I'll come downstairs to meet you outside.
examples.zh: 「你到了给我发消息」，我就下楼到外面接你。

examples.en: Just text me when you get here because the doorbell in our lounge is broken.
examples.zh: 我们休息室的门铃坏了，「你到了给我发消息」就行。

collocations: say text me when you get here
please text me when you get here
just text me when you get here

words.expression: text me when you get home
words.lemma: text me when you get home
words.enDefinition: asks a departing person to message you once they arrive home
acceptedEnVariants: text me when you get home

examples.en: Text me when you get home so I know you caught the last train okay.
examples.zh: 「到家给我发消息」，好让我知道你顺利坐上了末班车。

examples.en: My friend said, "Text me when you get home," just before I got on the bus.
examples.zh: 就在我上公交车前，朋友说：「到家给我发消息」。

collocations: remember to text me when you get home
just text me when you get home
can you text me when you get home

words.enDefinition: a written card thanking the person who looked after you

examples.en: We left a thank-you card for the host on the table before catching our train.
examples.zh: 我们去坐火车之前，在桌上留了张「写给主人的感谢卡」。

examples.en: Everyone signed a thank-you card for the host after the group stayed at her place.
examples.zh: 一行人借住在她家后，每个人都在「写给主人的感谢卡」上签了名。

collocations: write a thank-you card for the host
leave a thank-you card for the host
sign a thank-you card for the host

words.enDefinition: repeats your thanks to someone who gave you a meal

examples.en: Thanks again for dinner and for making sure I got to the station.
examples.zh: 「再次谢谢你请我吃饭」，还特意照应我到车站。

examples.en: I wrote, "Thanks again for dinner," under the photo my friend took at her flat.
examples.zh: 我在朋友家拍的照片下面写了句「再次谢谢你请我吃饭」。

collocations: by the way, thanks again for dinner
thanks again for dinner last night

words.enDefinition: thanks someone for letting you stay in their home

examples.en: Thanks for putting me up. Otherwise I would have missed the morning lecture.
examples.zh: 「谢谢你让我留宿」。不然我肯定赶不上早上的大课。

examples.en: I sent her a message saying, "Thanks for putting me up," after the early train.
examples.zh: 我坐早班火车离开后，给她发了条消息：「谢谢你让我留宿」。

collocations: and thanks for putting me up
thanks for putting me up last night
thanks for putting me up at such short notice

words.enDefinition: an autumn holiday for giving thanks in North America

examples.en: Some of us spent Thanksgiving on campus and shared a meal.
examples.zh: 我们几个留在学校过「感恩节」，一起吃了顿饭。

examples.en: I called my family on Thanksgiving before joining friends for dinner.
examples.zh: 「感恩节」那天，我先给家人打了电话，再和朋友吃晚饭。

words.enDefinition: a break in classes around the Thanksgiving holiday

examples.en: I took the train home for Thanksgiving break and saw my sister.
examples.zh: 我坐火车回家过「感恩节假期」，见到了妹妹。

examples.en: My advisor asked what I planned to do during Thanksgiving break this November.
examples.zh: 导师问我，十一月的「感恩节假期」打算做什么。

collocations: stay on campus over Thanksgiving break

words.enDefinition: a procession held on the day of Thanksgiving

examples.en: A few of us watched the Thanksgiving Day parade while everyone prepared dinner.
examples.zh: 大家忙着准备晚饭时，我们几个人看了「感恩节游行」。

examples.en: We heard drums from the Thanksgiving Day parade before we reached the main street.
examples.zh: 还没走到大街，我们就听到了「感恩节游行」的鼓声。

words.enDefinition: a special meal shared with others to celebrate Thanksgiving

examples.en: We joined my roommate's family for Thanksgiving dinner at their apartment.
examples.zh: 我们去了室友家的公寓，和他们一家一起吃「感恩节晚餐」。

examples.en: The students took a group picture before Thanksgiving dinner in the lounge.
examples.zh: 同学们在休息室吃「感恩节晚餐」前拍了张合影。

words.enDefinition: an American football game played around the holiday of Thanksgiving

examples.en: My roommate's family watched a Thanksgiving football game after they finished lunch.
examples.zh: 室友一家吃完午饭后，看了一场「感恩节美式橄榄球赛」。

examples.en: Some students came early to watch the Thanksgiving football game in the lounge.
examples.zh: 一些同学早点来了，在休息室看「感恩节美式橄榄球赛」。

words.enDefinition: a period when many people travel around the Thanksgiving holiday

examples.en: I left a little early to avoid the Thanksgiving travel rush that week.
examples.zh: 那周我稍微早一点出发，避开「感恩节出行高峰」。

examples.en: The station felt busier than usual during the Thanksgiving travel rush last November.
examples.zh: 去年十一月的「感恩节出行高峰」期间，车站感觉比平时更忙。

collocations: ahead of the Thanksgiving travel rush

words.enDefinition: the weekend around the date of Thanksgiving

examples.en: We spent Thanksgiving weekend with a classmate's family just outside Montreal.
examples.zh: 我们在蒙特利尔城外和同学的家人一起过了「感恩节周末」。

examples.en: The club plans to go hiking over Thanksgiving weekend if it stays dry.
examples.zh: 如果不下雨，社团打算在「感恩节周末」去徒步。

words.enDefinition: a response signalling that a question touches on a private matter

examples.en: “That's a bit personal,” I said when someone asked about my family's income.
examples.zh: 有人问我家里的收入时，我说「这个问题有点私人」。

examples.en: My friend answered, “That's a bit personal,” before moving to another topic.
examples.zh: 朋友答道「这个问题有点私人」，然后换了个话题。

words.enDefinition: a statement limiting a familiar practice to one's place of origin

examples.en: “That's specific to my hometown,” I said when someone asked about our procession.
examples.zh: 有人问起我们的游行活动时，我说「那是我家乡才有的」。

examples.en: She explained, “That's specific to my hometown,” after we asked about the lanterns.
examples.zh: 我们问起那些灯笼后，她解释道「那是我家乡才有的」。

collocations: “I think that's specific to my hometown”
“That's specific to my hometown as far as I know”

words.expression: that varies from family to family
words.lemma: that varies from family to family
words.enDefinition: a response saying a practice differs between households
acceptedEnVariants: that varies from family to family

examples.en: “That varies from family to family,” I said when asked who usually cooked.
examples.zh: 有人问一般由谁来做饭，我说「各家做法不太一样」。

examples.en: My classmate said, “That varies from family to family,” while discussing birthday meals.
examples.zh: 聊到生日那顿饭时，同学说「各家做法不太一样」。

collocations: say “That varies from family to family”
“I think that varies from family to family”
“That varies from family to family here”

words.expression: the bathroom is down the hall
words.lemma: the bathroom is down the hall
words.enDefinition: tells someone the bathroom is farther along a hallway
acceptedEnVariants: the bathroom is down the hall

examples.en: The bathroom is down the hall, just past the little shelf with everyone's shoes on it.
examples.zh: 「洗手间在走廊那头」，过了大家放鞋的小架子就是。

examples.en: My friend said, "The bathroom is down the hall, and the light switch is inside."
examples.zh: 朋友说：「洗手间在走廊那头」，灯的开关在里面。

collocations: the bathroom is down the hall on the left
the bathroom is down the hall from here
I think the bathroom is down the hall

words.enDefinition: says that leaves are changing colour as autumn arrives

examples.en: Our neighbour said the leaves are turning already along the footpath near her house.
examples.zh: 邻居说，她家附近那条小路旁的「树叶已经开始变色了」。

examples.en: The leaves are turning near the river, so we might take a walk tomorrow.
examples.zh: 河边的「树叶开始变色了」，所以我们明天可能会去散步。

collocations: see that the leaves are turning

words.enDefinition: A friendly response saying additional people are welcome to join.

examples.en: I said “The more the merrier” when my roommate asked about inviting our neighbors.
examples.zh: 室友问能不能约上邻居，我说「人越多越热闹」。

examples.en: The more the merrier was our motto for the afternoon picnic in the courtyard.
examples.zh: 「人越多越热闹」是我们下午在庭院野餐的口号。

collocations: tell them the more the merrier

words.enDefinition: A place where the same people regularly meet.

examples.en: Shall we meet at the usual place before heading to the craft market together?
examples.zh: 咱们要不要先在「老地方」碰头，再一起去手工艺集市？

examples.en: I'll be at the usual place after class with the books I borrowed from you.
examples.zh: 下课后我会带着跟你借的书去「老地方」。

collocations: go to the usual place after class

words.expression: the version I grew up with
words.lemma: the version i grew up with
words.zhGloss: 我从小熟悉的那个版本
words.enDefinition: the form of a story or practice familiar from childhood
acceptedZhAnswers: 我从小熟悉的那个版本
acceptedEnVariants: the version I grew up with

examples.en: The version I grew up with ends with everyone helping the youngest child.
examples.zh: 「我从小熟悉的那个版本」结尾是大家一起帮助最小的孩子。

examples.en: I learned that the version I grew up with differed from my roommate's.
examples.zh: 我发现，「我从小熟悉的那个版本」和室友知道的不一样。

collocations: tell the version I grew up with
show the version I grew up with
remember the version I grew up with

words.enDefinition: tells a guest that a spare blanket is available if needed

examples.en: There's an extra blanket on the chair if the room gets cold at night.
examples.zh: 要是晚上屋里冷，椅子上「还有一条备用毯子」。

examples.en: My friend said, "There's an extra blanket," and pointed to the bottom drawer.
examples.zh: 朋友指着最下面的抽屉说：「还有一条备用毯子」。

collocations: there's an extra blanket in the cupboard
there's an extra blanket if you need it
don't forget there's an extra blanket

words.expression: there's no one way to do it
words.lemma: there's no one way to do it
words.enDefinition: a comment recognising that a practice has more than one valid form
acceptedEnVariants: there's no one way to do it

examples.en: “There's no one way to do it,” my friend said during the recipe swap.
examples.zh: 大家交换菜谱时，朋友说「做法不止一种」。

examples.en: The tutor wrote, “There's no one way to do it,” beside the examples.
examples.zh: 导师在这些例子旁写着「做法不止一种」。

collocations: say “There's no one way to do it”
“There's no one way to do it here”
“Remember, there's no one way to do it”

words.enDefinition: lets someone know you are giving them a present

examples.en: This is for you. I remembered what you said about liking this kind of tea.
examples.zh: 「这个是给你的」。我记得你说过喜欢这种茶。

examples.en: My neighbour said, "This is for you," and handed me a small paper parcel.
examples.zh: 邻居说：「这个是给你的」，递给我一个小纸包。

collocations: this is for you from all of us
this is for you to keep

words.enDefinition: says something seems especially suited to someone's personality or taste

examples.en: This is so you. You always carry three books around without a proper bag.
examples.zh: 「这太适合你了」。你总带三本书，却没有个合适的包。

examples.en: My roommate said, "This is so you," when she gave me the purple teapot.
examples.zh: 室友把紫色茶壶送给我时说：「这太适合你了」。

collocations: I thought this is so you
look at this, this is so you

words.enDefinition: a present chosen with attention to what someone would appreciate

examples.en: The signed book was a thoughtful gift because I loved the author's work.
examples.zh: 我很喜欢那位作者的作品，所以这本签名书是份「用心挑选的礼物」。

examples.en: I was surprised by the thoughtful gift my flatmates chose for me.
examples.zh: 室友们给我选了这么「用心的礼物」，我很惊喜。

words.enDefinition: Thin, shiny strips used as festive decoration, especially on Christmas trees.

examples.en: There was silver tinsel around the window of the cafe where our study group met.
examples.zh: 我们自习小组碰面的咖啡馆在窗户边上围了银色的「圣诞装饰亮丝」。

examples.en: My roommate saved the tinsel in a paper bag for next year's holiday decorations.
examples.zh: 室友把「圣诞装饰亮丝」收在纸袋里，留着明年过节再用。

words.enDefinition: a respectful way of referring to someone using both elements

examples.en: I used her title and surname when addressing her in the public session.
examples.zh: 我在公开活动上称呼她时用了「头衔加姓氏」。

examples.en: The organiser printed each guest's title and surname on the reserved seat card.
examples.zh: 组织者在预留座位的卡片上印了每位来宾的「头衔加姓氏」。

collocations: address someone by their title and surname

words.enDefinition: a small gift that shows you are grateful for something

examples.en: I left a token of appreciation for the neighbours who had hosted us.
examples.zh: 我给招待过我们的邻居留了一件「聊表谢意的礼物」。

examples.en: We sent a token of appreciation to my cousin after staying with her.
examples.zh: 我们在表姐家住过之后，给她寄了份「聊表谢意的礼物」。

words.enDefinition: said playfully although it sounds serious at first

examples.en: I thought she was serious until I realised the comment was tongue-in-cheek.
examples.zh: 我起初以为她是认真的，后来才明白那句话是「故作认真地开玩笑」。

examples.en: Our group rewrote the tongue-in-cheek caption after a visitor misunderstood the poster.
examples.zh: 访客误会了海报，我们就改了那句「故作认真、实则开玩笑」配文。

words.enDefinition: to pour more of a drink into a partly filled glass

examples.en: Shall I top up your glass while I've still got the jug here?
examples.zh: 水壶还在我手边，要不要我「给你续杯」？

examples.en: Let me top up your glass before I put the juice away.
examples.zh: 我先「给你续杯」，再把果汁收起来。

collocations: offer to top up your glass
shall I top up your glass
let me top up your glass

words.enDefinition: to mentally convert between languages while listening or preparing to speak

examples.en: I still translate in my head when I hear an unfamiliar expression.
examples.zh: 听到不熟悉的说法时，我还是会「在心里先翻译」。

examples.en: “Do you translate in your head?” my classmate asked after the discussion.
examples.zh: 讨论结束后，同学问「你会在心里先翻译吗？」

collocations: tend to translate in your head
no longer need to translate in your head
translate in your head while listening

words.enDefinition: to preserve the original words closely in another language

examples.en: I tried not to translate literally when explaining the joke to my roommate.
examples.zh: 给室友解释笑话时，我尽量不「逐字直译」。

examples.en: The expression sounds harsher if you translate literally from the original message.
examples.zh: 原消息里的那个说法，要是「逐字直译」会显得更尖锐。

collocations: a phrase that's hard to translate literally

words.enDefinition: to convey the meaning even if the original wording changes

examples.en: I chose to translate the idea rather than keep every word in order.
examples.zh: 我选择「把原意转达出来」，没有按原来的词序逐个词照搬。

examples.en: My friend helped me translate the idea in a way our group understood.
examples.zh: 朋友帮我用小组都听得懂的方式「把原意转达出来」。

collocations: translate the idea into everyday language

words.enDefinition: event information rewritten in another language for participants

examples.en: The committee made translated event materials available at the welcome desk.
examples.zh: 委员会把「翻译后的活动资料」放在了迎宾台。

examples.en: I helped a visitor find the translated event materials on the shared site.
examples.zh: 我帮一位访客在共享网站上找到了「翻译后的活动资料」。

collocations: offer translated event materials in several languages

words.enDefinition: a small bag used to hold candy or other treats

examples.en: One of the children dropped a treat bag beside the mailbox.
examples.zh: 一个小孩把「装节日糖果的袋子」掉在了信箱旁边。

examples.en: The student café put one cookie in each treat bag before closing.
examples.zh: 学生咖啡馆关门前，往每个「装节日糖果的袋子」里放了一块曲奇。

words.zhGloss: 把每个人看作独立个体
words.enDefinition: to respond to the person rather than assume they represent a group
acceptedZhAnswers: 把每个人看作独立个体

examples.en: The tutor encouraged us to treat people as individuals in our interview project.
examples.zh: 导师鼓励我们，在访谈项目里「把每个人看作独立个体」。

examples.en: The meeting was easier once we tried to treat people as individuals.
examples.zh: 我们试着「把每个人看作独立个体」后，会议聊得顺畅多了。

collocations: remember to treat people as individuals
try to treat people as individuals
learn to treat people as individuals

words.enDefinition: to pay for another person's dinner as a kind gesture

examples.en: I'd like to treat you to dinner after we finish our last group project.
examples.zh: 最后一个小组项目做完后，我想「请你吃晚饭」。

examples.en: Can I treat you to dinner at the noodle place after your evening lab?
examples.zh: 你晚上的实验课结束后，我能在那家面馆「请你吃晚饭」吗？

collocations: offer to treat someone to dinner
treat you to dinner this weekend

words.enDefinition: A decorative cloth spread around the base of a Christmas tree.

examples.en: The library volunteers placed a green tree skirt around the base of their small display.
examples.zh: 图书馆志愿者在小型展示树的底部围了一块绿色的「圣诞树底围布」。

examples.en: We borrowed a tree skirt from my flatmate to hide the stand in the lounge.
examples.zh: 我们向室友借了块「圣诞树底围布」，遮住休息室里圣诞树的支架。

collocations: a tree skirt around the stand

words.enDefinition: A decorative object placed at the top of a Christmas tree.

examples.en: The art students made a paper star to use as the tree topper this year.
examples.zh: 美术专业的同学做了一颗纸星星，作为今年的「圣诞树顶饰」。

examples.en: Our tree topper was so light that it leaned over when someone opened the window.
examples.zh: 我们的「圣诞树顶饰」很轻，有人一开窗它就歪了。

words.enDefinition: the traditional greeting children say when asking for Halloween candy

examples.en: Kids shouted "Trick or treat!" when my roommate answered the door that evening.
examples.zh: 那天晚上，室友一开门，孩子们就喊：「不给糖就捣蛋」！

examples.en: We heard "Trick or treat!" from the front steps before the doorbell rang.
examples.zh: 门铃响之前，我们就听见门前台阶上有人喊「不给糖就捣蛋」。

collocations: knock and say trick or treat

words.enDefinition: someone who visits houses to ask for Halloween candy

examples.en: The first trick-or-treater at our door wore a cardboard robot costume.
examples.zh: 第一个到门口的「万圣节讨糖人」穿着纸板机器人装。

examples.en: I put an extra piece of candy aside for the last trick-or-treater.
examples.zh: 我给最后一个「万圣节讨糖的人」多留了一颗糖。

words.enDefinition: an event where children collect treats at decorated parked cars

examples.en: My student club decorated a car for the campus trunk-or-treat.
examples.zh: 我们学生社团给一辆车做了装饰，准备参加校园的「汽车后备箱讨糖活动」。

examples.en: Families started lining up early at the trunk-or-treat by the library.
examples.zh: 来参加图书馆旁「汽车后备箱讨糖活动」的家庭很早就排起了队。

words.enDefinition: to experience something you do not already know

examples.en: A friend encouraged me to try something unfamiliar at the student food fair.
examples.zh: 朋友鼓励我在学生美食节上「尝试不熟悉的食物」。

examples.en: I decided to try something unfamiliar and asked how the game worked.
examples.zh: 我决定「尝试不熟悉的事物」，便问这个游戏怎么玩。

collocations: be willing to try something unfamiliar
have a chance to try something unfamiliar

words.enDefinition: Korean soup with sliced rice cakes, often served during Seollal.

examples.en: We tried tteokguk with friends at an event organized by the campus Korean society.
examples.zh: 我们在校园韩国文化社举办的活动上和朋友一起尝了「韩国年糕汤」。

examples.en: My flatmate shared photos of tteokguk that her relatives had made during the holiday.
examples.zh: 室友分享了亲戚在过节时做的「韩国年糕汤」照片。

words.enDefinition: an event celebrating tulips in bloom, often with public gardens and activities

examples.en: We walked to the tulip festival after our friend finished her weekend shift.
examples.zh: 朋友周末下班后，我们步行去了「郁金香节」。

examples.en: The tulip festival map showed which flower beds were open to visit that morning.
examples.zh: 「郁金香节」地图标出了那天上午哪些花坛开放参观。

words.enDefinition: an event where people can get a turkey without paying

examples.en: The student volunteers helped families check in for the turkey giveaway.
examples.zh: 学生志愿者协助各家到「免费发放火鸡活动」签到。

examples.en: Our neighbour told us about a turkey giveaway at the community centre.
examples.zh: 邻居告诉我们，社区中心有一场「免费发放火鸡活动」。

words.enDefinition: a community running or walking event around Thanksgiving, especially in America

examples.en: My friend signed up for a Turkey Trot near her campus in Illinois.
examples.zh: 朋友报名参加了伊利诺伊州校园附近的「感恩节趣味跑」。

examples.en: We walked most of the Turkey Trot and met other students there.
examples.zh: 「感恩节趣味跑」的大部分路程我们都是走的，还在那里认识了别的同学。

collocations: sign up for a Turkey Trot

words.enDefinition: to say no to an invitation to go on a date

examples.en: She decided to turn down a date because she wasn't interested in meeting that way.
examples.zh: 她对这种见面方式没有兴趣，决定「谢绝约会邀请」。

examples.en: I felt awkward when I had to turn down a date with someone from class.
examples.zh: 我不得不「谢绝同班同学的约会邀请」时，觉得有些尴尬。

collocations: turn down a date with someone
decide to turn down a date

words.expression: turn to the person next to you
words.lemma: turn to the person next to you
words.enDefinition: to face the person beside you to speak with them
acceptedEnVariants: turn to the person next to you

examples.en: Before we started the game, she said to turn to the person next to you and introduce yourself.
examples.zh: 游戏开始前，她请大家「转向旁边的人」，做个自我介绍。

examples.en: The leader said, "Turn to the person next to you and ask their name before we begin."
examples.zh: 带队的同学说：「转向你旁边的人」，先问问对方的名字，我们再开始。

collocations: please turn to the person next to you
first turn to the person next to you
turn to the person next to you and say hello

words.enDefinition: a game of guessing which of three personal statements is false

examples.en: We played two truths and a lie to learn something unexpected about our new neighbours.
examples.zh: 我们玩了「两真一假破冰游戏」，了解了新邻居们不为人知的一面。

examples.en: My group played two truths and a lie while we waited for the pizza delivery.
examples.zh: 等披萨送到的时候，我们组玩了「两真一假破冰游戏」。

collocations: play two truths and a lie
a round of two truths and a lie
use two truths and a lie as an icebreaker

words.enDefinition: an orchard where visitors can pick their own fruit

examples.en: We bought the apples by weight at the U-pick orchard near town.
examples.zh: 我们在镇附近的「自摘果园」按重量买了苹果。

examples.en: The U-pick orchard kept a board showing which varieties were ready.
examples.zh: 「自摘果园」立了块牌子，写着哪些品种已经可以采摘。

words.enDefinition: A deliberately gaudy or humorous sweater worn for Christmas festivities.

examples.en: My roommate borrowed an ugly Christmas sweater for the gathering in our residence lounge.
examples.zh: 室友借了件「搞怪圣诞毛衣」，准备参加宿舍休息室的聚会。

examples.en: The campus shop displayed an ugly Christmas sweater with a giant snowman on the front.
examples.zh: 校园商店展出了一件「搞怪圣诞毛衣」，正面印着个大雪人。

words.enDefinition: a friend made at university, especially in informal British and Australian English

examples.en: I met a uni friend for lunch while I was visiting Bristol again.
examples.zh: 又去布里斯托那次，我和一位「大学里认识的朋友」一起吃了午饭。

examples.en: A uni friend in Sydney offered me a place to stay after the reunion.
examples.zh: 聚会结束后，一位在悉尼「大学里认识的朋友」主动让我在他那儿留宿。

collocations: meet up with a uni friend

words.enDefinition: romantic love that the other person does not return

examples.en: The campus play told a funny story about unrequited love between two old friends.
examples.zh: 校园戏剧讲了两个老朋友之间「得不到回应的爱」，故事很有趣。

examples.en: He used to write songs about unrequited love when he first moved here.
examples.zh: 他刚搬来的时候，经常写关于「得不到回应的爱」的歌。

words.enDefinition: a convention people generally follow without seeing it formally stated

examples.en: One unwritten rule in our study group was to let the speaker finish.
examples.zh: 我们学习小组有条「不成文的规矩」，就是让发言的人把话说完。

examples.en: Our club had an unwritten rule about leaving the front row for guests.
examples.zh: 我们社团有条「不成文的规矩」，把第一排留给来宾。

collocations: an unwritten rule in a group

words.enDefinition: to share new information with the members of a group

examples.en: I offered to update the group after hearing from our friend about her flight.
examples.zh: 听到朋友的航班消息后，我主动提出「把进展告诉群里的人」。

examples.en: Will you update the group once you have spoken to our old classmate today?
examples.zh: 你今天和老同学谈过后，会「把进展告诉群里的人」吗？

collocations: send a message to update the group

words.enDefinition: a student who has already completed the first year

examples.en: An upper-year student at the café told us which buses run late.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆里一位「高年级学生」告诉我们哪几路公交收车晚。

examples.en: I asked an upper-year student how they had met people outside class.
examples.zh: 我问一位「高年级学生」平时怎么在课堂外认识别人的。

collocations: seek advice from an upper-year student

words.enDefinition: to put a mat under a drink to protect the surface

examples.en: My flatmate asked me to use a coaster on the shared coffee table.
examples.zh: 室友请我在公用的茶几上「用杯垫」。

examples.en: The library room sign asked visitors to use a coaster under every mug.
examples.zh: 图书馆房间里的标牌请来客在每个马克杯下面「用杯垫」。

collocations: use a coaster under your mug
ask people to use a coaster

words.enDefinition: to speak at a quieter level appropriate for an indoor space

examples.en: My friend smiled and asked me to use an indoor voice in the café.
examples.zh: 朋友笑着请我在咖啡馆「在室内小声说话」。

examples.en: The volunteer reminded the visiting children to use an indoor voice near the library.
examples.zh: 志愿者提醒来参观的孩子在图书馆附近「小声说话」。

collocations: remember to use an indoor voice
ask someone to use an indoor voice

words.enDefinition: to listen through headphones to avoid playing sound into a shared space

examples.en: I chose to use headphones so my music wouldn't bother the people studying.
examples.zh: 我选择「戴耳机听」，免得音乐打扰正在自习的人。

examples.en: The train announcement asked passengers to use headphones for their own videos.
examples.zh: 车上广播请乘客看自己的视频时「戴耳机听」。

words.enDefinition: to take food with the spoon provided for the shared dish

examples.en: Our club coordinator asked us to use the serving spoon for the salad.
examples.zh: 社团协调员请大家夹取沙拉时「用公用分餐勺」。

examples.en: The card by the shared bowl read, “Please use the serving spoon.”
examples.zh: 公用碗旁的卡片写着「请用公用分餐勺」。

collocations: ask everyone to use the serving spoon
use the serving spoon for salad

words.enDefinition: pointed false teeth worn as part of a vampire costume

examples.en: I took out my vampire fangs before trying to eat the cookies.
examples.zh: 我先摘下「吸血鬼假尖牙」，再试着吃曲奇。

examples.en: Her vampire fangs made it hard to smile in the group photo.
examples.zh: 她戴着「吸血鬼假尖牙」，拍合影时很难露出笑容。

words.enDefinition: differences among people or settings within a shared cultural background

examples.en: The film showed variation within a culture by following three different households.
examples.zh: 影片拍了三个不同家庭，展示了「同一文化内部的差异」。

examples.en: Our discussion focused on variation within a culture rather than broad national comparisons.
examples.zh: 我们的讨论主要关注「同一文化内部的差异」，少做宽泛的国别比较。

words.enDefinition: a Canadian holiday in May associated with the monarch's official birthday

examples.en: I used the Victoria Day weekend to visit a friend at another Canadian university.
examples.zh: 我利用「加拿大维多利亚日」长周末去看了在加拿大另一所大学读书的朋友。

examples.en: Our supervisor posted the museum's Victoria Day hours before we finished work on Friday.
examples.zh: 我们周五下班前，主管张贴了博物馆「加拿大维多利亚日」当天的开放时间。

words.enDefinition: a designated public space for watching part of an event

examples.en: Staff directed families to the viewing area beside the main path through the park.
examples.zh: 工作人员把家庭观众引到公园主路旁的「观看区」。

examples.en: We reached the viewing area early enough to find seats together near the front.
examples.zh: 我们很早就到了「观看区」，在前面找到了挨在一起的座位。

words.enDefinition: a village event with stalls, games, and entertainment, especially in Britain

examples.en: My neighbour baked cakes for the village fête that raised money for the hall.
examples.zh: 邻居给为村礼堂筹款的「乡村游园会」烤了蛋糕。

examples.en: I took the bus to the village fête with a friend from my course.
examples.zh: 我和同一门课的朋友一起坐公交去「乡村游园会」。

words.enDefinition: a grassy public space in a village, often used for gathering

examples.en: The summer fair occupied the village green across the road from the post office.
examples.zh: 夏季市集在邮局对面的「村庄公共草坪」上举行。

examples.en: We sat on the village green with some classmates after the local concert.
examples.zh: 当地音乐会结束后，我们和几个同学坐在「村庄公共草坪」上。

words.enDefinition: To choose a film by asking the group to vote for its preference.

examples.en: Can we vote on a film before I go to buy anything for the evening?
examples.zh: 我去买晚上用的东西前，咱们能先「投票选一部电影」吗？

examples.en: We decided to vote on a film because nobody had agreed on a comedy yet.
examples.zh: 大家还没选定要看的喜剧，我们决定「投票选一部电影」。

collocations: ask everyone to vote on a film
vote on a film in the chat
vote on a film for Friday

words.enDefinition: A request for someone to wait outdoors near the agreed place.

examples.en: Can you wait for me outside while I return these books at the library desk?
examples.zh: 我去图书馆柜台还这些书时，你能「在外面等我」吗？

examples.en: Please wait for me outside because I forgot my jacket in the common room.
examples.zh: 我把夹克忘在公共休息室了，请「在外面等我」。

collocations: ask you to wait for me outside
can you wait for me outside

words.expression: wait for someone to offer their hand
words.lemma: wait for someone to offer their hand
words.enDefinition: to let another person choose whether to offer a handshake first
acceptedEnVariants: wait for someone to offer their hand

examples.en: I decided to wait for someone to offer their hand at the reception.
examples.zh: 在招待会上，我决定「等对方先伸手」。

examples.en: Our guide suggested we wait for someone to offer their hand during the introductions.
examples.zh: 向导建议，在介绍环节「等对方先伸手」。

collocations: choose to wait for someone to offer their hand
prefer to wait for someone to offer their hand
wait for someone to offer their hand before shaking

words.enDefinition: To delay starting an activity until the rest of the group arrives.

examples.en: Let's wait for the others before starting the game because we're still missing two players.
examples.zh: 还有两位玩家没到，咱们「等其他人到了再开始」玩吧。

examples.en: We chose to wait for the others before ordering drinks at the cafe near campus.
examples.zh: 在校园附近的咖啡馆，我们决定「等其他人都到了再点饮料」。

collocations: decide to wait for the others
ask if we should wait for the others
wait for the others before starting

words.zhGloss: 等所有人都有菜再开始
words.enDefinition: to delay eating until all diners have received their food
acceptedZhAnswers: 等所有人都有菜再开始

examples.en: The host said to wait until everyone is served before we started eating.
examples.zh: 主持人请我们「等所有人都有菜再开始」。

examples.en: A volunteer reminded us to wait until everyone is served at the banquet.
examples.zh: 宴会上，志愿者提醒我们「等所有人都有菜再开始」。

collocations: please wait until everyone is served
ask diners to wait until everyone is served
remind people to wait until everyone is served

words.enDefinition: To return on foot to campus or another place with the rest of the group.

examples.en: We can walk back together once the film ends and the lights come up.
examples.zh: 电影结束、灯亮起来后，我们可以「一起走回去」。

examples.en: My roommate asked if we could walk back together after the picnic in the park.
examples.zh: 室友问，公园的野餐结束后我们能不能「一起走回去」。

collocations: walk back together after the film
ask if we can walk back together

words.enDefinition: someone who stays quietly apart from others at social events

examples.en: I felt like a wallflower until her friends waved me over.
examples.zh: 她的朋友招手叫我过去之前，我感觉自己「在聚会上一直独处，没怎么说话」。

examples.en: He was a wallflower at first, then joined the card game.
examples.zh: 他一开始「在聚会上坐在一旁，没怎么说话」，后来加入了牌局。

collocations: be a wallflower at a party

words.enDefinition: An informal invitation to take part in an activity with the speaker's group.

examples.en: We are getting coffee after the workshop, so do you want to join us?
examples.zh: 研讨活动结束后我们要去喝咖啡，你「想加入我们吗」？

examples.en: We have an extra ticket for the screening tonight if you want to join us.
examples.zh: 我们今晚的放映活动多了一张票，你「想加入我们」的话可以一起来。

collocations: want to join us for coffee
want to join us after class
want to join us on Saturday

words.enDefinition: A gathering where people watch an event or program together as it is shown.

examples.en: My friend invited me to a watch party for the final in the student lounge.
examples.zh: 朋友邀请我去学生休息室参加决赛的「集体观看活动」。

examples.en: We moved the watch party to another flat because its living room had more seats.
examples.zh: 另一套公寓客厅的座位更多，我们就把「集体观看活动」搬到了那里。

collocations: a watch party for the final

words.enDefinition: a circular mark left by a wet glass or cup

examples.en: I spotted a water ring where someone had put a cold drink.
examples.zh: 有人放冷饮的地方，我看到一个「杯底水圈印」。

examples.en: We wiped the water ring off the meeting table before leaving.
examples.zh: 我们离开前，把会议桌上的「杯底水圈印」擦掉了。

collocations: notice a water ring on a table

words.enDefinition: signals that you and another person have not met before

examples.en: I said, "We haven't met before. I'm Nia from the floor upstairs."
examples.zh: 我说：「我们以前还没见过」。我是楼上的尼娅。

examples.en: My neighbour smiled and said, "We haven't met yet. I just moved in."
examples.zh: 邻居笑着说：「我们还没见过」。我刚搬进来。

collocations: I'm pretty sure we haven't met

words.expression: we haven't seen each other in years
words.lemma: we haven't seen each other in years
words.enDefinition: a phrase saying two people have gone several years without meeting
acceptedEnVariants: we haven't seen each other in years

examples.en: She said, “We haven't seen each other in years,” when I arrived at the station.
examples.zh: 我到车站时，她说：“「我们好多年没见了」。”

examples.en: “We haven't seen each other in years, but we still talk every month online.”
examples.zh: “「我们好多年没见了」，不过每月还是在线上聊天。”

collocations: we haven't seen each other in years but still text
realise we haven't seen each other in years
we haven't seen each other in years now

words.expression: we should do this more often
words.lemma: we should do this more often
words.enDefinition: an expression suggesting that a shared activity should happen more frequently
acceptedEnVariants: we should do this more often

examples.en: “We should do this more often,” she said after our walk through the park.
examples.zh: 在公园散步后，她说：“「我们应该多这样聚聚」。”

examples.en: As lunch ended, he laughed and said, “We should do this more often.”
examples.zh: 午饭吃完时，他笑着说：“「我们应该多这样聚聚」。”

collocations: I think we should do this more often
we should do this more often next term
honestly, we should do this more often

words.expression: we should let you get some rest
words.lemma: we should let you get some rest
words.enDefinition: signals you are about to leave so someone can rest
acceptedEnVariants: we should let you get some rest

examples.en: We should let you get some rest. You've been taking care of everyone all evening.
examples.zh: 「我们该让你休息了」。你一晚上都在照顾大家。

examples.en: When our host said she was tired, I said, "We should let you get some rest."
examples.zh: 主人说累了，我就说：「我们该让你休息了」。

collocations: I think we should let you get some rest
right, we should let you get some rest
maybe we should let you get some rest

words.enDefinition: a phrase saying two people have different hopes for their lives or relationship

examples.en: “We want different things,” she said after they compared their plans for next year.
examples.zh: 比过明年的计划后，她说：“「我们想要的不一样」。”

examples.en: I told a friend that we want different things and had decided to stop dating.
examples.zh: 我告诉朋友，「我们想要的不一样」，已经决定不再交往。

collocations: we want different things in life
we want different things right now
I think we want different things

words.enDefinition: to dress in green, a common custom at some Saint Patrick's Day events

examples.en: My flatmate said she planned to wear green at the Irish society's evening concert.
